l4_steps.pain_point: Proposal templates are maintained outside Salesforce; manual formatting increases turnaround time and introduces inconsistency across sales reps

l4_steps.name: Negotiate charter terms and revise pricing if needed
l4_steps.input: Client counter-proposal or revision request against issued proposal
l4_steps.output: Revised proposal within approved negotiation band or escalation to RM for exception
l4_steps.kpi: Negotiation rounds ≤3 before agreement or rejection; average deal close time ≤5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Negotiation iterations not tracked in CRM opportunity stages; pricing concessions granted below floor price without RM visibility due to lack of automated guardrails

l4_steps.name: Generate charter contract from approved terms
l4_steps.input: Agreed pricing, route, date, pax count, service level, and penalty clauses
l4_steps.output: Executed charter contract with digital signatures from airline and client
l4_steps.kpi: Contract execution within 24 hours of verbal agreement; contract error rate <2%
l4_steps.pain_point: DocuSign not integrated with Salesforce CRM; contract data entry is manual, risking discrepancies between CRM opportunity record and signed contract terms

l4_steps.name: Collect deposit payment and record in receivables
l4_steps.input: Executed contract with deposit amount and due date
l4_steps.output: Deposit receipt posted to charter receivables ledger; booking confirmed in CRM
l4_steps.kpi: Deposit received within 5 business days of contract execution; deposit collection rate ≥95%
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated dunning workflow for charter deposit collection in SAP; manual follow-up required, and overdue deposits are not automatically flagged in Salesforce CRM

l4_steps.name: Apply for overflight and landing permits
l4_steps.input: Confirmed route, registration, date, and flight number from executed contract
l4_steps.output: Permit applications submitted to relevant CAAs and overflight authorities
l4_steps.kpi: Permit applications filed ≥10 days before departure for international routes; permit clearance rate ≥98%
l4_steps.pain_point: Permit processing times vary by country (24 hours to 10+ days); no centralised permit tracking system — status monitored via email chains with handling agents, risking missed deadlines

l4_steps.name: File flight plan and request airport slots
l4_steps.input: Approved permits, route, and aircraft registration
l4_steps.output: Confirmed slot times at origin and destination airports; SSIM slot entry in SkyWORKS
l4_steps.kpi: Slot confirmed ≥5 days before departure; slot change rate <10% post-confirmation
l4_steps.pain_point: Charter flights at slot-coordinated airports (IATA Level 3) compete with scheduled carriers; last-minute charter requests are often rejected, requiring costly alternative routing

l4_steps.name: Assign crew pairing and verify duty-time compliance
l4_steps.input: Confirmed flight date, departure time, route, and block hours
l4_steps.output: Crew pairing with duty-time compliance verification per FAR Part 117
l4_steps.kpi: Crew assigned ≥72 hours before departure; FAR Part 117 violation rate = 0%
l4_steps.pain_point: Charter dates often conflict with scheduled crew pairings; Jeppesen requires manual pairing creation for ad-hoc charters, and duty-time buffers may be exhausted if schedule disruptions precede the charter

l4_steps.name: Coordinate fuel uplift, catering, and ground handling
l4_steps.input: Aircraft type, pax count, catering specification, and station identifiers
l4_steps.output: Ground services order confirmation at origin and destination stations
l4_steps.kpi: Ground handling confirmed ≥48 hours before departure; catering order accuracy ≥98%
l4_steps.pain_point: Charter stations may be uncontracted airports; negotiating ad-hoc fuel and handling rates increases cost unpredictability and erodes the charter margin estimated in Phase 2

l4_steps.name: Execute charter flight and record departure/arrival actuals
l4_steps.input: Confirmed crew pairing, flight plan, slot time, and pax manifest
l4_steps.output: Actual departure/arrival times, block hours flown, and pax count recorded
l4_steps.kpi: Charter on-time departure (D0) ≥85%; pax manifest discrepancy rate <0.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Charter pax manifests are often finalised late by clients; last-minute pax additions or removals require real-time weight & balance recalculations, delaying departure

l4_steps.name: Capture actual costs and reconcile against estimate
l4_steps.input: Actual fuel receipts, handling invoices, permit fees, and crew actuals
l4_steps.output: Variance report: actual cost vs pre-flight estimate with margin impact
l4_steps.kpi: Cost reconciliation completed within 5 business days of flight; cost variance ≤8% of estimate
l4_steps.pain_point: Fuel and handling invoices from ad-hoc stations arrive weeks after the flight; SAP posting cutoffs create accrual uncertainty, requiring manual re-opening of periods for charter settlements

l4_steps.name: Issue final invoice and collect balance payment
l4_steps.input: Actual cost report, contract price, deposit received, and any agreed extras
l4_steps.output: Final tax invoice issued; balance payment collected and posted to charter revenue account
l4_steps.kpi: Final invoice issued within 7 business days of flight; payment collected within contract terms (net 14 days); DSO for charter ≤21 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Client disputes over fuel surcharges or extras delay final payment; no automated dispute escalation workflow in SAP, requiring manual intervention by Finance and Sales teams

l4_steps.name: Conduct post-charter debrief and update client record
l4_steps.input: Client satisfaction feedback, operations debrief notes, and final financial result
l4_steps.output: Closed opportunity record with win/loss analysis, margin achieved, and repeat-sale flag
l4_steps.kpi: Debrief completed within 10 business days of flight; repeat charter conversion rate ≥30%
l4_steps.pain_point: Post-charter learnings (pricing accuracy, permit delays, ground handling issues) are not systematically fed back into pricing models or permit planning checklists, causing repeated errors

l4_steps.name: Define commission tier structure by agency segment
l4_steps.input: Historical agency booking data, competitive intelligence, budget guidance
l4_steps.output: Draft commission tier matrix segmented by agency type and channel
l4_steps.kpi: Commission cost as % of total distribution revenue ≤3.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Legacy GDS commission structures limit dynamic per-segment tier adjustments; IATA Resolution 818 constrains net-rate transparency, reducing ability to differentiate incentive rates by booking window or route

l4_steps.name: Model financial impact of proposed commission rates
l4_steps.input: Draft commission tier matrix, O&D revenue data from Amadeus NRM
l4_steps.output: Financial impact model with revenue-at-risk analysis and break-even volumes
l4_steps.kpi: Commission ROI ≥4:1 incremental revenue per dollar paid
l4_steps.pain_point: Incomplete NDC booking attribution in data lake distorts channel profitability calculations — NDC and GDS bookings not tagged consistently in Redshift, leading to underestimation of NDC cost savings

l4_steps.name: File commission schedules in ATPCO CAT 35
l4_steps.input: Approved commission tier matrix from budget sign-off
l4_steps.output: Published ATPCO CAT 35 commission schedules distributed to all GDS platforms
l4_steps.kpi: Filing cycle completed ≤2 business days from policy approval; zero GDS distribution failures
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO CAT 35 supports net fares rather than explicit commission rates, requiring workaround constructions that reduce transparency for agency partners and complicate audits under IATA Resolution 850

l4_steps.name: Validate IATA/ARC accreditation for new agency
l4_steps.input: New agency onboarding request with IATA/ARC number
l4_steps.output: Accreditation verification record; agency status confirmed as current and bonded
l4_steps.kpi: Onboarding validation completed within 3 business days of request submission
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA accreditation lapses and bond failures are not automatically propagated to GDS agency profiles — risk of continuing commission payments to deaccredited agencies discovered only at BSP settlement

l4_steps.name: Configure commission parameters in GDS platforms
l4_steps.input: Validated accreditation record, approved commission tier assignment
l4_steps.output: Agency commission profile active and consistent across Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus GDS
l4_steps.kpi: Configuration accuracy 100%; zero commission miscalculation incidents per quarter across all three GDS platforms
l4_steps.pain_point: Managing parallel commission configurations across Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus requires manual triple-entry with no centralised commission API — errors typically discovered only at monthly BSP/ARC settlement, creating retroactive adjustment workload

l4_steps.name: Enroll agency in NDC incentive programme
l4_steps.input: Agency NDC API certification status, signed NDC incentive agreement
l4_steps.output: Agency NDC incentive profile active; incremental booking targets and incentive rates configured
l4_steps.kpi: NDC share of enrolled agency bookings ≥15% within 90 days of enrolment
l4_steps.pain_point: Many TMCs and leisure agencies lack technical capability for full NDC API integration; incentive uptake is constrained by agency IT readiness rather than demand, reducing the effectiveness of shift-to-NDC distribution strategy

l4_steps.name: Extract historical agency performance data
l4_steps.input: 24-month GDS MIDT data, NDC booking events, agency tier classification history
l4_steps.output: Agency performance scorecards: revenue contribution, yield, load factor uplift by route
l4_steps.kpi: Data extraction latency ≤4 hours for full 24-month dataset; completeness ≥99% of expected agency records
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS MIDT data arrives with 24–48hr delay and does not distinguish flown versus unflown bookings at ingestion — performance scorecards overstate agency contribution until cancellation netting is applied in a separate downstream process

l4_steps.name: Set incentive thresholds and tier boundaries
l4_steps.input: Agency performance scorecards, annual incentive budget allocation from Finance
l4_steps.output: Incentive programme terms sheet: booking thresholds, earning rates, measurement period, eligible routes
l4_steps.kpi: Target incentive budget utilisation ≥85% by end of programme period; zero over-budget accruals
l4_steps.pain_point: Revenue Management incentive budget inputs are static annual figures — no dynamic recalculation when O&D demand shifts mid-year, causing misalignment between incentive thresholds and actual revenue opportunity by quarter

l4_steps.name: Approve override rates for strategic partner accounts
l4_steps.input: Incentive terms sheet, strategic partner account plans, revenue policy guardrail limits
l4_steps.output: Signed incentive agreement with approved override commission rates; uploaded to SAP contract management
l4_steps.kpi: Override approval cycle ≤5 business days of proposal submission; 100% of overrides documented with ROI justification
l4_steps.pain_point: Override approvals require VP-level sign-off but historically tracked in email threads with no structured workflow — creates audit exposure under IATA Resolution 850 and SOX internal controls for airline revenue contracts

l4_steps.name: Ingest daily booking volumes from GDS and NDC
l4_steps.input: Sabre MIDT, Amadeus MIDT, Travelport MIDT feeds, NDC API booking event stream
l4_steps.output: Daily agency booking volume dashboard; commission accrual staging table updated
l4_steps.kpi: MIDT ingestion completeness ≥98% of expected records per day; ingestion pipeline latency ≤6 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: MIDT data does not distinguish flown versus unflown bookings at time of ingestion — commission accruals include no-show and subsequently cancelled bookings that must net out at BSP settlement, creating transient overstatement of liability

l4_steps.name: Calculate commission accruals against tier thresholds
l4_steps.input: Daily booking volume data, approved tier thresholds and override rate agreements
l4_steps.output: Commission accrual journal entries posted to SAP GL; agency tier status report
l4_steps.kpi: Accrual calculation cycle completed within 2 hours of MIDT ingestion; accrual variance to final settlement ≤1%
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP accrual entries require manual journal adjustment when an agency crosses a tier boundary mid-month — automated tier-crossing triggers not yet configured, exposing the process to under-accrual risk and period-end restatements

l4_steps.name: Flag agencies approaching performance thresholds
l4_steps.input: Daily accrual report, tier threshold proximity rules (within 10% of next tier)
l4_steps.output: Account management action list; proactive outreach triggers for agents within reach of next incentive tier
l4_steps.kpi: ≥90% of threshold-proximity alerts actioned within 48 hours; conversion rate of nudged agencies reaching next tier ≥35%
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated CRM integration between Tableau alerts and account management workflows — alerts require manual transfer, causing follow-up delays that reduce the effectiveness of incentive tier nudging as a revenue acceleration tactic

l4_steps.name: Generate commission billing statement via BSP/ARC
l4_steps.input: Final monthly accrual report, confirmed flown-only booking data after cancellation netting
l4_steps.output: Commission billing statement; BSP debit memo or ARC IAR report
l4_steps.kpi: BSP/ARC billing statement issued within 5 business days of month-end close; billing accuracy vs accruals within ±2% tolerance
l4_steps.pain_point: BSP remittance data format (IATA Resolution 850) does not map directly to SAP GL coding — manual field-by-field rekeying required, creating a 2–3 day reconciliation lag and introducing transcription error risk at scale

l4_steps.name: Post commission payables to SAP AP
l4_steps.input: Validated BSP/ARC billing statement reconciled to accruals
l4_steps.output: Posted AP invoice; payment run scheduled in SAP; GL entries aligned to accrual period
l4_steps.kpi: AP posting completed within 2 business days of billing statement validation; on-time payment rate ≥98%
l4_steps.pain_point: Multi-currency commission payments (USD, EUR, GBP) require FX conversion at time of AP posting — exchange rate movement between accrual date and payment date creates untracked P&L exposure not captured in current distribution cost reporting

l4_steps.name: Process and resolve agency dispute claims
l4_steps.input: Agency dispute submission referencing original booking data and billing statement line items
l4_steps.output: Dispute resolution decision; adjusted credit note issued via BSP Link if claim upheld
l4_steps.kpi: Dispute resolution cycle ≤15 business days; dispute rate ≤2% of total monthly invoices by value
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA BSP dispute window is 12 months — historical disputes can surface against already-closed SAP accounting periods, requiring prior-period adjustment journals that breach internal month-end close policies and trigger external audit queries

l4_steps.name: Analyse commission ROI by channel and agency segment
l4_steps.input: Full-year commission payments from SAP, channel revenue data from Amadeus NRM, per-booking cost by channel
l4_steps.output: Commission effectiveness report with channel ROI ranking, cost-per-booking comparison GDS vs NDC, and under/over-performing agency list
l4_steps.kpi: Incremental revenue per £1 commission paid ≥4:1; NDC cost-per-booking ≤60% of equivalent GDS cost
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC and GDS bookings are not comparable on a per-booking-cost basis without blended modelling spanning GDS segment fees, NDC API development costs, and commission payments — data lives across Redshift, SAP FI, and GDS billing portals with no single unified view

l4_steps.name: Revise commission tier structure for next programme cycle
l4_steps.input: Commission effectiveness report, Finance budget guidance for next period, Legal sign-off on rate changes
l4_steps.output: Revised commission tier matrix approved; ATPCO CAT 35 filing initiated for next programme period
l4_steps.kpi: Policy revision cycle completed ≤30 days before new programme period start; zero ATPCO filing errors on submission
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO filing lead time for commission changes is 7–14 days — late budget approvals from Finance regularly compress the filing window, risking programme launch delays that disrupt agency booking behaviour during high-demand booking periods

l4_steps.name: Validate Interline Ticketing Agreement status
l4_steps.input: Partner carrier IATA code, agreement reference number
l4_steps.output: ITA validity confirmation and billing currency code
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of active partners with valid ITA before ticket issuance enabled
l4_steps.pain_point: MITA agreements lapse without automated renewal alerts — expired ITAs cause ticket rejection at GDS, creating passenger disruption and manual escalation to partner airline's commercial team

l4_steps.name: Load partner carrier tariff and fare rules
l4_steps.input: Partner carrier tariff filing, IATA fare construction rules
l4_steps.output: Loaded fare table with combinability and routing rules
l4_steps.kpi: Tariff load completed within 24 hours of ATPCO effective date
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO batch updates publish at 00:01 EST — late-night automation failures leave stale fare rules in production until manual intervention, causing mispriced interline itineraries

l4_steps.name: Configure MITA SSR message formats in PSS
l4_steps.input: Partner carrier EDIFACT profile, SSR/OSI message templates
l4_steps.output: Configured interline messaging profiles in Altéa
l4_steps.kpi: SSR message delivery success rate ≥99.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: EDIFACT PADIS message version mismatches between carriers require manual mapping tables — each new partner requires 2–4 weeks of IT configuration, delaying commercial go-live

l4_steps.name: Register codeshare flight designator in Amadeus Altéa
l4_steps.input: Operating carrier flight schedule, codeshare agreement terms
l4_steps.output: Codeshare flight records in SSIM format, loaded to Altéa inventory
l4_steps.kpi: Codeshare schedule loaded ≥90 days before first departure date
l4_steps.pain_point: Operating carrier schedule changes propagate with latency — SkyWORKS SSIM refresh cycle is 24 hours, meaning same-day schedule swaps create ghost codeshare flights visible in GDS

l4_steps.name: Sync partner inventory blocks via EDIFACT SSR/ACK
l4_steps.input: Codeshare seat block allocation from operating carrier
l4_steps.output: Confirmed inventory allocation in Altéa booking classes
l4_steps.kpi: Inventory sync acknowledgement (ACK) received within 15 minutes of block request
l4_steps.pain_point: Dual inventory control (marketing vs operating carrier) creates overbooking risk — NRM cannot directly query operating carrier's live seat map, relying on asynchronous SSR messages with no guaranteed delivery SLA

l4_steps.name: File codeshare fares via ATPCO and validate combinability
l4_steps.input: Agreed codeshare fare levels, routing restrictions, booking class mapping
l4_steps.output: Published codeshare fare filing with combinability Cat 10/11 rules
l4_steps.kpi: Zero misfiled combinability rules causing GDS pricing errors at launch
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO Category 10 combinability rules are complex — errors in end-on-end fare construction go undetected until passengers receive incorrect fares at booking, requiring mass repricing and IROPS-level agent intervention

l4_steps.name: Receive interline booking request from GDS or NDC
l4_steps.input: Agent PNR with multi-carrier itinerary, passenger name, fare basis
l4_steps.output: Interline booking record with all carrier segments confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: GDS booking response time ≤3 seconds for interline itineraries
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC-sourced interline bookings lack standardised offer/order IDs compatible with legacy EDIFACT settlement — carriers without full NDC back-office integration cannot receive or settle NDC-issued interline tickets

l4_steps.name: Perform fare construction combinability check
l4_steps.input: Multi-carrier itinerary, fare basis codes, routing
l4_steps.output: Approved fare construction or rejected itinerary with reason code
l4_steps.kpi: Fare construction error rate ≤0.5% of all interline transactions
l4_steps.pain_point: Half-round-trip (HRT) and end-on-end combination logic in Altéa pricing engine has known edge cases for 3+ carrier itineraries — manual audit required for itineraries crossing IATA traffic conference areas

l4_steps.name: Issue interline e-ticket via BSP or ARC
l4_steps.input: Approved fare construction, PNR, passenger data, payment details
l4_steps.output: Interline e-ticket (ET) with all coupons, transmitted to BSP/ARC
l4_steps.kpi: Ticket issuance success rate ≥99.8%; time-to-issue ≤60 seconds
l4_steps.pain_point: BSP settlement reporting requires per-coupon carrier code validation — system-generated document check digit errors in Altéa have caused bulk ticket voids requiring 48-hour manual reissue queues

l4_steps.name: Transmit PNR and coupon data to operating carrier
l4_steps.input: Issued e-ticket coupons, booking class, SSR elements
l4_steps.output: EDIFACT PNRGOV / IATCI message delivered to partner carrier PSS
l4_steps.kpi: PNR transmission to operating carrier within 5 minutes of ticket issuance; delivery confirmation ≥99%
l4_steps.pain_point: IATCI (Interline Through Check-In) handoff failures occur when operating carrier's PSS is on a different version of the EDIFACT PADIS standard — passengers arrive at operating carrier's check-in counter with no booking record

l4_steps.name: Calculate revenue proration using IATA Proration rules
l4_steps.input: Issued ticket coupons, fare basis, mileage/unit proration method
l4_steps.output: Proration memo per carrier with amounts in billing currency
l4_steps.kpi: Proration calculation completed within T+1 business day of travel date
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA Proration Rules Manual (PRM) updates twice yearly — revenue accounting system requires manual rule table updates, and delayed updates cause incorrect proration splits that take months to detect via interline billing reconciliation

l4_steps.name: Generate and submit interline billing memo via IATA CASS
l4_steps.system: IATA CASS (Cargo Accounts Settlement System) / ICH
l4_steps.input: Proration memos, coupon usage data, billing period cutoff
l4_steps.output: Interline billing memo (IBM) submitted to IATA Clearing House
l4_steps.kpi: Billing memo submission before monthly IATA ICH cutoff (25th of month); dispute rate ≤2%
l4_steps.pain_point: ICH submission deadlines are fixed — revenue accounting system outages during the last 3 business days of the month result in missed cutoffs, deferring settlement by a full month and creating cash flow exposure

l4_steps.name: Reconcile and approve interline billing statements
l4_steps.input: Partner carrier billing memos, internal proration calculations
l4_steps.output: Reconciled statement with approved, disputed, and pending items
l4_steps.kpi: Reconciliation completed within 10 business days of billing statement receipt; dispute resolution ≤30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Coupon usage data gaps (e.g., missing lift coupons from operating carrier) prevent automated matching — manual reconciliation for unmatched coupons exceeds 200 hours/month at mid-size carriers

l4_steps.name: Post approved proration revenue to general ledger
l4_steps.input: Approved interline billing statement, GL account mapping
l4_steps.output: Revenue journal entries posted to SAP GL with interline partner cost centre
l4_steps.kpi: GL posting completed within 2 business days of billing approval; zero unposted items at month-end close
l4_steps.pain_point: Interline revenue accounting system integration with SAP FI relies on nightly batch file transfer — intra-month adjustments require manual journal entries, increasing month-end close effort and audit trail risk

l4_steps.name: Detect schedule disruption affecting interline itinerary
l4_steps.input: IROPS alert from operating carrier, flight cancellation or delay >3 hours
l4_steps.output: Affected interline PNR list flagged for rebooking action
l4_steps.kpi: Disruption notification to marketing carrier within 30 minutes of operating carrier declaring IROPS
l4_steps.pain_point: Operating carrier IROPS notifications arrive via unstructured email or telephone — no automated EDIFACT OC (Other Communication) message standard exists, meaning marketing carrier agents learn of disruptions reactively when passengers call

l4_steps.name: Reroute passenger on alternate interline or codeshare flight
l4_steps.input: Disrupted PNR, alternate routing options, IATA Resolution 735d rebooking rules
l4_steps.output: Reprotected PNR on new itinerary, updated coupons transmitted to operating carrier
l4_steps.kpi: Passenger reprotection offer presented within 60 minutes of IROPS declaration; acceptance rate ≥85%
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA Resolution 735d mandates specific rebooking rules for involuntary rerouting — agents are not always trained on which rules apply to each interline agreement, leading to incorrect fare differences being charged or waived

l4_steps.name: Process interline ticket reissue or refund
l4_steps.input: Original e-ticket coupons, rerouting decision, applicable waiver code
l4_steps.output: Reissued ticket or refund application submitted to BSP with ADM/ACM if required
l4_steps.kpi: Reissue or refund processing completed within 24 hours of passenger request; ADM dispute rate ≤1%
l4_steps.pain_point: BSP Agent Debit Memos (ADMs) for incorrectly waived change fees create disputes lasting 6–12 months — interline reissue waiver codes are not standardised across carriers, causing downstream billing errors that inflate interline dispute volumes

l4_steps.name: Extract GDS/NDC ticket sales data
l4_steps.input: Daily GDS ticket transaction files from Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus GDS; NDC booking records
l4_steps.output: Raw daily sales extract (tickets issued, voided, refunded) in BSP standard format
l4_steps.kpi: Sales extract completeness ≥99.9% of all ticketed transactions captured within 2hr of BSP cut-off
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC direct-connect bookings are not automatically included in legacy BSP extract jobs — manual intervention required to merge NDC settlement files, creating reconciliation gaps and delayed reporting

l4_steps.name: Validate ticket stock vs. IATA BSP allocation
l4_steps.input: Raw sales extract; IATA BSP ticket stock allocation records
l4_steps.output: Validated ticket list with orphan/duplicate flags
l4_steps.kpi: Ticket validation error rate <0.1% of transactions per BSP billing period
l4_steps.pain_point: Ticket number ranges allocated across multiple GDS channels can overlap when PSS configuration changes; BSPlink does not auto-detect cross-channel duplicates, requiring manual range-conflict queries

l4_steps.name: Decision: Completeness check — missing records?
l4_steps.input: Validated ticket list; expected transaction count from GDS settlement reports
l4_steps.output: Go/No-Go decision; missing-record exception report if No-Go
l4_steps.kpi: Data completeness gate passed first attempt ≥95% of BSP periods
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS settlement files arrive up to 6 hours after cut-off due to Travelport file delivery SLA gaps, causing repeated re-ingestion cycles and risk of missing the BSP submission window

l4_steps.name: Aggregate sales by agent and BSP billing period
l4_steps.input: Validated ticket transaction file; IATA BSP agent master and billing period calendar
l4_steps.output: Per-agent sales summary with fare, tax, commission, and net remittance amounts
l4_steps.kpi: Aggregation processing completed ≤4hr after data validation; <50 manual corrections per billing period
l4_steps.pain_point: Sub-agents consolidated under a parent IATA code are not disaggregated in Amadeus Revenue Accounting, requiring custom SQL extracts to identify high-risk individual agents for ADM targeting

l4_steps.name: Calculate commissions, taxes, and surcharges
l4_steps.input: Per-agent sales summary; ATPCO fare and tax rule tables; commission schedule from SAP Ariba contracts
l4_steps.output: Itemised billing breakdown per ticket: base fare, YQ/YR surcharges, government taxes, agent commission
l4_steps.kpi: Tax calculation accuracy ≥99.95%; surcharge variance vs. ATPCO published rules <0.05%
l4_steps.pain_point: YQ/YR fuel surcharges filed in ATPCO are updated bi-weekly; Revenue Accounting must manually trigger ATPCO feed refresh — stale surcharge tables cause systematic billing errors affecting hundreds of transactions per period

l4_steps.name: Generate Agency Debit Memos (ADMs) for discrepancies
l4_steps.input: Itemised billing breakdown; expected fare/tax amounts from ATPCO; waiver/authorisation log from Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Draft ADMs for agents with fare undercharges, invalid discounts, or missing taxes
l4_steps.kpi: ADM issuance rate within 30 days of ticket issue date; ADM dispute rate <15% of issued ADMs
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA Resolution 850 ADM deadlines (within 9 months of ticket issue) are frequently missed due to backlog in Amadeus Revenue Accounting audit queues — expired ADMs result in unrecoverable revenue leakage

l4_steps.name: Decision: Discrepancy amount exceeds $500 threshold?
l4_steps.input: Draft ADM list with per-agent discrepancy amounts
l4_steps.output: Approved ADMs forwarded to IATA submission; sub-threshold items flagged for batch review
l4_steps.kpi: Threshold review completed within 1 business day; 100% of ADMs >$500 reviewed by manager before submission
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated threshold alerting in BSPlink — manager must manually filter ADM queue; sub-$500 items often accumulate to material amounts across an agent portfolio and are not escalated

l4_steps.name: Submit BSP billing file to IATA via BSPlink
l4_steps.input: Finalised billing file; approved ADMs; BSP billing period calendar
l4_steps.output: BSP submission receipt and IATA confirmation number
l4_steps.kpi: Submission on-time rate ≥99% of billing periods; file rejection rate <0.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: BSPlink file format requirements (IATA Type A/Type B formats) change with each IATA resolution cycle; failure to update Revenue Accounting export templates before cut-off causes submission rejections with no same-day correction window

l4_steps.name: Receive and validate BSP settlement advice
l4_steps.input: IATA BSP settlement advice document; submitted billing file
l4_steps.output: Validated settlement advice with line-item variance analysis
l4_steps.kpi: Settlement advice received within 3 business days of submission; variance analysis completed same day as receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA settlement advice arrives as a non-machine-readable PDF in some BSP country plans; manual re-keying into Amadeus Revenue Accounting introduces transcription errors and delays the bank reconciliation cycle

l4_steps.name: Decision: Settlement amount matches billing submission?
l4_steps.input: Settlement advice; original billing file totals; ADM/ACM adjustments
l4_steps.output: Confirmed match → proceed; variance → raise IATA billing query
l4_steps.kpi: Settlement match rate ≥98% first-pass; queries resolved within 5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA BSP applies country-specific rounding rules for multi-currency settlements that differ from airline accounting system rounding — persistent $0.01–$0.05 per-ticket variances aggregate to thousands of dollars per period and are difficult to auto-clear

l4_steps.name: Confirm clearing bank receipt from IATA BSP
l4_steps.input: BSP settlement advice; bank statement from IATA-appointed clearing bank
l4_steps.output: Confirmed bank receipt entry in SAP cash management
l4_steps.kpi: Bank confirmation posted within 1 business day of settlement value date; 100% of expected receipts matched
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA uses country-specific clearing banks (e.g., Citi for US BSP, Barclays for UK BSP); different value date conventions and SWIFT message formats require manual mapping to SAP bank accounts, slowing auto-matching

l4_steps.name: Post BSP settlement to airline AR accounts
l4_steps.input: Confirmed bank receipt; per-agent billing summary; SAP AR account mapping
l4_steps.output: SAP AR postings clearing agent receivable balances; BSP period journal entry
l4_steps.kpi: AR posting completed within 2 business days of settlement; open AR items from BSP <3% of total AR at month-end
l4_steps.pain_point: Agent IATA codes in BSPlink are not always 1:1 mapped to SAP customer master records — new agents or consolidated GSA accounts require manual SAP FI configuration before postings can clear, causing AR aging issues

l4_steps.name: Decision: Settlement received within BSP calendar deadline?
l4_steps.input: Bank receipt date; BSP settlement calendar (IATA-published); SAP open item report
l4_steps.output: On-time: proceed to reconciliation; Late: escalate to IATA BSP country manager and initiate default agent process
l4_steps.kpi: Zero late settlements from airline side; agent default escalations initiated within 24hr of missed deadline
l4_steps.pain_point: BSP settlement calendars differ by country and are updated annually by IATA — treasury teams using stale calendar files have missed escalation windows, resulting in unsecured exposure to financially distressed agents

l4_steps.name: Review agent disputes on issued ADMs
l4_steps.input: Agent dispute notification via BSPlink; original ADM with supporting fare calculation
l4_steps.output: Dispute case record with initial validity assessment
l4_steps.kpi: Dispute acknowledgement within 5 business days per IATA Resolution 850; dispute queue cleared within 30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Agents submit bulk disputes at the 9-month IATA deadline, creating a volume spike that overwhelms the Revenue Accounting team — no automated triage in BSPlink means all disputes require manual review regardless of amount

l4_steps.name: Investigate disputed ADM with fare/booking evidence
l4_steps.input: Dispute case record; original booking and ticketing data from Amadeus Altéa PSS; ATPCO fare rules
l4_steps.output: Investigation outcome: uphold or reverse ADM with documented evidence
l4_steps.kpi: Investigation completed within 15 business days; <5% of ADMs reversed due to airline data errors
l4_steps.pain_point: Historical booking records in Amadeus Altéa PSS are purged after 13 months, making it impossible to reconstruct fare basis for ADMs near the 9-month dispute deadline — leading to unwinnable disputes and revenue write-offs

l4_steps.name: Decision: ADM dispute upheld by airline?
l4_steps.input: Investigation outcome with fare evidence; IATA dispute arbitration guidelines
l4_steps.output: Upheld: agent notified, ADM stands; Reversed: ACM issued to agent via BSPlink
l4_steps.kpi: Decision communicated within 30 days of dispute receipt; ACMs issued within 5 business days of reversal decision
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA dispute arbitration (if agent escalates to IATA) typically rules against the airline when documentation is incomplete — inadequate ADM issuance evidence (missing ATPCO fare snapshots at ticketing date) is the leading cause of lost arbitrations

l4_steps.name: Reconcile BSP settlements with revenue GL accounts
l4_steps.input: SAP AR postings; BSP settlement totals by period; revenue recognition entries from Amadeus Revenue Accounting
l4_steps.output: Reconciled trial balance; variance report flagging unmatched items
l4_steps.kpi: Month-end BSP reconciliation completed by day 5 close; unreconciled items <0.1% of gross BSP settlement value
l4_steps.pain_point: Timing differences between Amadeus Revenue Accounting (accrual at ticket lift) and SAP FI (cash at BSP settlement) create persistent reconciling items that are difficult to clear during month-end close under tight finance calendar deadlines

l4_steps.name: Generate IATA compliance and audit reports
l4_steps.input: Reconciled BSP data; IATA audit requirements (IATA Resolution 854); SAP FI closed-period data
l4_steps.output: IATA BSP compliance pack: settlement summary, ADM/ACM register, dispute log, defalcation report
l4_steps.kpi: Compliance pack delivered within 10 business days of period close; zero IATA audit findings classed as material
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA Resolution 854 compliance reporting requires data from both BSPlink and Amadeus Revenue Accounting in a specific format — no native export combining both sources forces manual assembly in Excel, introducing version control and audit-trail risks

l4_steps.name: Close BSP period and archive transaction records
l4_steps.input: IATA compliance pack; cleared AR items in SAP; resolved dispute log
l4_steps.output: Locked BSP period in BSPlink; archived transaction files in AWS S3 data lake per IATA 7-year retention policy
l4_steps.kpi: Period closed within 15 business days of settlement date; 100% of records archived with retention metadata
l4_steps.pain_point: BSPlink does not provide a programmatic archive export API — records must be manually downloaded and uploaded to AWS S3, creating a labour-intensive process that is frequently deprioritised, resulting in gaps in the audit archive

l4_steps.name: Evaluate OTA partnership opportunities
l4_steps.input: Market share data, OTA volume reports, channel performance benchmarks
l4_steps.output: OTA partnership shortlist with commercial rationale
l4_steps.kpi: OTA channel revenue contribution ≥25% of total passenger revenue
l4_steps.pain_point: OTA market consolidation (Expedia/Booking.com duopoly) limits airline negotiating leverage on commission rates and parity terms

l4_steps.name: Negotiate OTA commercial agreement terms
l4_steps.input: OTA partnership shortlist, competitive commission benchmarks, IATA Resolution 818g standards
l4_steps.output: Draft commercial term sheet (commission rate, override tiers, content parity requirements)
l4_steps.kpi: Commission rate negotiated ≤12% of ticket value; override incentive thresholds agreed within 45 days
l4_steps.pain_point: OTAs demand last-look pricing rights and rate parity clauses that directly conflict with airline direct channel strategy and dynamic pricing

l4_steps.name: Execute OTA distribution agreement
l4_steps.input: Negotiated term sheet, legal review checklist, EU Package Travel Directive and US DOT transparency requirements
l4_steps.output: Signed OTA distribution agreement with SLA annexures
l4_steps.kpi: Contract execution cycle ≤45 days from term sheet agreement
l4_steps.pain_point: Jurisdictional complexity across markets (EU Package Travel Directive 2015/2302, US DOT full-fare advertising rule 14 CFR Part 399) extends legal review and requires market-specific agreement variants

l4_steps.name: Configure OTA technical connectivity
l4_steps.input: Signed agreement, OTA technical specifications (IATA NDC Level 4 or GDS EDIFACT)
l4_steps.output: Validated API or GDS connection in test environment; go-live approval
l4_steps.kpi: API connectivity test pass rate 100% before go-live; integration delivery ≤30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: OTA NDC adoption remains below 40% industry-wide; most connections still use legacy GDS EDIFACT, limiting ancillary upsell capability and real-time inventory access

l4_steps.name: File fares and fare rules to ATPCO
l4_steps.input: Approved fare structure, seasonal pricing calendar, OTA-specific fare product requirements
l4_steps.output: Published fares and fare rules in ATPCO database distributed to GDS channels
l4_steps.kpi: Fare filing lead time ≥72h before sale date per ATPCO SOTI schedule; filing error rate ≤0.1%
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO filing windows create pricing latency vs. direct channel dynamic pricing; competitors using NDC bypass ATPCO for OTA-specific private offers, gaining speed-to-market advantage

l4_steps.name: Configure OTA channel fare availability in PSS
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS / Amadeus Revenue Management (NRM)
l4_steps.input: Published ATPCO fares, RM inventory allocation decisions, OTA booking class mapping
l4_steps.output: OTA booking class availability configured and active in Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.kpi: Fare availability accuracy ≥99.5% vs. ATPCO published fares; inventory update latency ≤15 minutes
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa inventory caching can lag up to 15 minutes on high-demand routes during peak booking windows, causing OTA booking failures, GDS error messages, and lost revenue on price-sensitive leisure routes

l4_steps.name: Distribute ancillary content to OTA channels
l4_steps.input: Ancillary product catalogue (bags, seats, meals, lounge), OTA NDC capability certification status
l4_steps.output: Structured ancillary offers available on OTA storefront for NDC-connected partners
l4_steps.kpi: Ancillary attach rate via OTA ≥18% of bookings; NDC ancillary revenue per booking ≥$22
l4_steps.pain_point: Non-NDC OTAs cannot render structured ancillary offers; EDIFACT-connected OTAs display ancillaries as free-text remarks only, reducing attach rate to <5% and suppressing ancillary revenue on high-volume OTA channels

l4_steps.name: Monitor OTA content parity compliance
l4_steps.input: Live OTA storefront pricing scraped across 50+ routes, direct channel published fares
l4_steps.output: Content parity compliance report; violation alerts triggered for OTA account management
l4_steps.kpi: Price parity violations ≤0.5% of sampled OTA fares per weekly audit cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: OTAs apply opaque loyalty discounts, packaging, and credit card rewards to undercut direct channel pricing, remaining technically parity-compliant while effectively bypassing parity agreements and eroding direct channel value proposition

l4_steps.name: Process OTA-originated bookings in PSS
l4_steps.input: OTA booking request via GDS sell message or NDC OrderCreate API
l4_steps.output: Confirmed PNR with OTA agency IATA number and pseudo-city code tagged
l4_steps.kpi: OTA booking acceptance rate ≥99.8%; booking confirmation latency ≤3 seconds via GDS, ≤1.5 seconds via NDC
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS booking surcharge of $3–$7 per segment raises airline cost of distribution vs. direct channel; carriers absorb cost to maintain OTA relationship but margin erodes on low-yield leisure itineraries

l4_steps.name: Validate OTA ticket issuance and EMD generation
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS / IATA BSP Link
l4_steps.input: Confirmed PNR, OTA ticketing time limit, ancillary EMD requirements
l4_steps.output: Issued e-ticket (ET) and Electronic Miscellaneous Documents (EMDs) for all ancillary charges
l4_steps.kpi: Ticket issuance within BSP ticketing time limit 100%; EMD issuance error rate ≤0.2%
l4_steps.pain_point: OTA back-office systems frequently breach ticketing time limits due to payment processing delays, triggering automatic PNR cancellation in Altéa without customer notification — generating rebooking costs, customer complaints, and CSAT impact

l4_steps.name: Handle OTA booking modifications and cancellations
l4_steps.input: OTA-submitted modification or cancellation request via GDS or NDC OrderChange API
l4_steps.output: Updated or cancelled PNR; refund amount or credit voucher calculated and confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: OTA modification fulfilment rate ≥98%; refund processing ≤5 business days per IATA Resolution 824
l4_steps.pain_point: Non-NDC OTAs cannot submit structured order changes via API; refund workflows are manual when OTA uses EDIFACT, creating backlogs of 10,000+ cases during irregular operations (IROPS) events such as severe weather or ATC strikes

l4_steps.name: Reconcile OTA bookings against flown revenue
l4_steps.input: BSP/ARC settlement files, Amadeus Altéa PNR extract, OTA monthly booking reports
l4_steps.output: Revenue recognition journal entries; OTA revenue reconciliation report with variance analysis
l4_steps.kpi: Reconciliation completion within 3 business days of month close; revenue variance ≤0.1% of OTA channel revenue
l4_steps.pain_point: OTA booking data arrives in multiple formats — BSP XML, ARC ACH files, and direct NDC API logs — requiring manual transformation and mapping before SAP ingestion, extending the month-close cycle by 1–2 days

l4_steps.name: Process BSP/ARC settlement for OTA bookings
l4_steps.system: IATA BSP Link / ARC (Airlines Reporting Corporation)
l4_steps.input: Validated OTA sales data, BSP billing memoranda, ARC weekly transaction reports
l4_steps.output: Settled BSP payment received; ARC remittance filed and confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: BSP settlement on-time rate 100%; settlement discrepancy rate ≤0.05% of billed amount
l4_steps.pain_point: OTA agents with multiple IATA numbers split bookings across sub-entities to stay below BSP credit limits, creating reconciliation gaps, default risk exposure, and triggering IATA credit management review processes

l4_steps.name: Audit and pay OTA commission and override incentives
l4_steps.input: OTA quarterly sales performance report, commission rate schedule, override tier thresholds from contract
l4_steps.output: Commission payment instruction processed; override incentive credit note issued
l4_steps.kpi: Commission payment accuracy ≥99.9%; override incentive payment within 30 days of quarter close
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual commission calculation for multi-tier OTA override structures (base + volume override + market development funds) is error-prone; disputes with large OTAs (Expedia, Booking.com) over override eligibility can delay payments 60+ days and damage commercial relationships

l4_steps.name: Analyse OTA channel performance vs. targets
l4_steps.input: OTA booking volumes, revenue by route, ancillary attach rates, cost-of-sale per ticket by channel
l4_steps.output: OTA channel performance dashboard; monthly KPI scorecard distributed to VP Distribution
l4_steps.kpi: OTA revenue contribution vs. plan ±5%; cost of distribution per ticket ≤$15 including GDS fees and commissions
l4_steps.pain_point: OTA data-sharing agreements vary significantly — major OTAs withhold passenger-level booking data citing GDPR and commercial confidentiality, preventing complete channel profitability analysis and obscuring true margin contribution by OTA partner

l4_steps.name: Review OTA contract performance and renewal decision
l4_steps.input: OTA channel KPI scorecard, contracted volume commitments, competitive distribution benchmarks
l4_steps.output: OTA contract renewal recommendation; renegotiation mandate or termination notice issued ≥90 days before expiry
l4_steps.kpi: OTA contracts reviewed annually; renewal or renegotiation decision finalised ≥90 days before expiry date
l4_steps.pain_point: Bilateral OTA contracts frequently lack performance clawback provisions; underperforming OTAs retain preferred commission rates and override eligibility without meeting volume commitments, reducing airline's ability to redirect inventory to higher-yield channels

l4_steps.name: Execute metasearch partner agreement & API onboarding
l4_steps.input: Signed commercial agreement with metasearch partner (Google Flights, Kayak, Skyscanner)
l4_steps.output: API credentials, endpoint URLs, CPC rate card
l4_steps.kpi: Partner onboarding lead time ≤30 days from contract signature
l4_steps.pain_point: Each metasearch partner requires bespoke API configurations; NDC schema versioning mismatches between partners cause silent feed failures with no error surfaced to airline

l4_steps.name: Configure fare & schedule feed for metasearch ingestion
l4_steps.input: API credentials, ATPCO fare filing rules, schedule data from Amadeus SkyWORKS
l4_steps.output: Configured fare feed in OTA Schema or NDC 21.3 format
l4_steps.kpi: Feed configuration accuracy ≥99% (zero critical field mappings missing)
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO filing propagation latency (up to 24h) means published fares lag dynamic pricing changes in Amadeus NRM, creating an arbitrage window exploited by OTAs

l4_steps.name: Validate feed quality & schema compliance
l4_steps.system: NDC API Gateway / Postman API Testing Suite
l4_steps.input: Test feed response from metasearch sandbox environment
l4_steps.output: Validation report; go/no-go decision for production activation
l4_steps.kpi: Zero critical schema errors before go-live; feed round-trip response ≤2s (p95)
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC 21.3 vs 17.2 schema incompatibility across metasearch partners; several comparison sites (Momondo, Kayak) accept only legacy EDIFACT/GDS feeds, forcing dual-channel maintenance

l4_steps.name: Publish fare cache to metasearch price index
l4_steps.input: Current fare inventory from Amadeus Altéa PSS booking class availability
l4_steps.output: Fare cache updated on metasearch price index
l4_steps.kpi: Fare cache refresh latency ≤15 minutes; stale fare rate <2%
l4_steps.pain_point: Fare cache staleness causes price disparity between metasearch display price and booking engine checkout; leads to consumer complaints and potential EU261/ATPCO fare filing violations

l4_steps.name: Sync real-time seat availability via NDC/GDS
l4_steps.input: Live inventory status from Altéa booking classes (Y, B, M, H, Q, etc.)
l4_steps.output: Real-time availability displayed on metasearch for each fare bucket
l4_steps.kpi: Availability accuracy ≥98.5% vs Altéa live booking class status
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS RBD (Reservation Booking Designator) mapping inconsistencies between Altéa and Sabre GDS cause availability discrepancies; sold-out fare classes displayed as available on Skyscanner, generating 'sorry, fare unavailable' errors at checkout

l4_steps.name: Perform fare parity audit across distribution channels
l4_steps.input: Published fares scraped from metasearch, GDS, and airline.com for same O&D/date
l4_steps.output: Fare parity compliance report; exception list of breached routes
l4_steps.kpi: Fare parity compliance ≥95% across monitored routes; exception resolution ≤4 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Dynamic pricing adjustments in Amadeus NRM create unintentional fare disparities across channels; corporate/negotiated fares inadvertently surfaced on public metasearch breach TMC contract confidentiality clauses

l4_steps.name: Define CPC bid strategy by route and market segment
l4_steps.system: Google Flights Hotel Ads Console / Kayak Partner Portal
l4_steps.input: Historical CTR data, route revenue targets from Amadeus NRM, seasonal demand forecast
l4_steps.output: CPC bid schedule per route, date range, and cabin class
l4_steps.kpi: Target CPC ≤$0.45 domestic routes; ≤$1.20 international routes
l4_steps.pain_point: Metasearch auction dynamics require continuous bid optimisation; static bid tables lose price competitiveness within hours during peak booking windows (holiday periods, fare sales)

l4_steps.name: Monitor click-through rates and impression share
l4_steps.system: Google Flights Ads Console / AWS Redshift
l4_steps.input: Live metasearch impression and click data feed from partner APIs
l4_steps.output: Daily CTR dashboard; impression share report by route
l4_steps.kpi: CTR ≥1.8% on primary routes; impression share ≥40% for top 20 O&D markets
l4_steps.pain_point: Metasearch partner APIs throttle reporting data refresh to 6-hour intervals; bid adjustments based on stale data reduce campaign ROI during intraday demand spikes

l4_steps.name: Adjust bids using demand signals and competitor fares
l4_steps.system: Google Flights Ads Console / PROS RM
l4_steps.input: Competitor fare monitoring signals, demand forecast from Amadeus SkyCAST
l4_steps.output: Updated bid schedule; exception report for routes with bid floor violations
l4_steps.kpi: ROAS (return on ad spend) ≥4.5x on metasearch channel; bid update turnaround ≤2 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: PROS RM demand signals are not natively integrated with Google Flights bid management console; manual data transfer introduces 24-hour lag, blunting competitive responsiveness

l4_steps.name: Generate deep-link redirect URL to booking engine
l4_steps.system: NDC API Gateway / Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Metasearch user click event with fare parameters (O&D, date, cabin class, fare basis)
l4_steps.output: Deep-link URL to airline booking engine pre-populated with selected itinerary
l4_steps.kpi: Deep-link generation latency ≤800ms (p95); link validity ≥99.9%
l4_steps.pain_point: Session parameter passing between metasearch redirect and booking engine breaks on Safari/iOS mobile browsers due to ITP cookie restrictions; causes booking abandonment rate >35% on mobile

l4_steps.name: Track metasearch click-to-confirmed-booking conversion
l4_steps.input: Click event from metasearch partner; booking confirmation event from Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Conversion rate report per metasearch partner, route, and device type
l4_steps.kpi: Metasearch-to-booking conversion ≥2.5%; cart abandonment ≤65%
l4_steps.pain_point: Cross-domain tracking gaps between metasearch redirect and airline.com booking funnel cause 20–30% attribution loss; inflates apparent cost-per-booking and understates true metasearch channel value

l4_steps.name: Aggregate metasearch channel performance data
l4_steps.input: Click, impression, conversion, and revenue data from all metasearch partner APIs
l4_steps.output: Consolidated metasearch performance dashboard covering all partners
l4_steps.kpi: Data pipeline freshness ≤4 hours; dashboard availability ≥99.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Each metasearch partner (Google Flights, Kayak, Skyscanner, Momondo) exposes proprietary reporting APIs with incompatible schemas; ETL pipeline maintenance requires dedicated engineering resource

l4_steps.name: Calculate cost-per-booking and channel contribution margin
l4_steps.input: Metasearch ad spend from CPC invoices; booking revenue from Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Channel P&L report; cost-per-booking by partner and route
l4_steps.kpi: Metasearch cost-per-booking ≤$8.50 domestic; ≤$18.00 international
l4_steps.pain_point: Attribution of ancillary revenue (checked bags, seat upgrades, travel insurance) to the originating metasearch channel is inconsistent across reporting systems, systematically understating true channel margin contribution

l4_steps.name: Reconcile metasearch partner click invoices vs tracked clicks
l4_steps.input: Monthly CPC invoice from metasearch partner; internal click tracking logs from AWS Redshift
l4_steps.output: Reconciliation report; dispute list for unmatched or bot-classified clicks
l4_steps.kpi: Invoice match rate ≥97%; dispute raised within 10 business days of invoice receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: Discrepancies between partner-reported clicks and airline-side tracking arise from differing bot/invalid-traffic filtering rules; Google Flights click audit process takes 45–90 days, creating cash flow exposure on disputed amounts

l4_steps.name: Raise formal dispute with metasearch partner for excess clicks
l4_steps.input: Reconciliation exception list; internal click evidence from AWS Redshift logs
l4_steps.output: Formal dispute submission; credit note or adjusted invoice from partner
l4_steps.kpi: Dispute resolution ≤30 days; credit recovery rate ≥90% of disputed amount
l4_steps.pain_point: Absence of a neutral click audit standard across metasearch platforms means dispute outcomes depend on partner goodwill; airlines with low traffic volume have limited negotiating leverage

l4_steps.name: Process approved metasearch invoices for payment
l4_steps.input: Approved reconciliation report; vendor invoice cleared of disputes
l4_steps.output: Payment instruction executed in SAP; cleared invoice posted to GL
l4_steps.kpi: Payment processed within contract terms (Net 30/Net 45); zero late payment penalties
l4_steps.pain_point: Multi-currency CPC invoices (USD, EUR, GBP) require FX rate alignment between SAP FI and partner billing systems; rate discrepancies >0.5% trigger re-approval workflows, delaying payment and risking vendor relationship

l4_steps.name: Extract sales transactions from PSS and GDS feeds
l4_steps.input: Daily booking, ticketing, and revenue transactions from Altéa
l4_steps.output: Raw sales transaction file (PNR, fare basis, channel, O&D)
l4_steps.kpi: Data extraction completeness ≥99.5% of daily transactions
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa feed latency can delay T+1 reporting; GDS interline sales require separate reconciliation from Sabre and Travelport settlement files

l4_steps.name: Ingest GDS booking and yield data via settlement files
l4_steps.input: Sabre PRISM BSP settlement files and Travelport agency booking reports
l4_steps.output: Consolidated GDS channel dataset with agency, fare, and yield fields
l4_steps.kpi: GDS data ingestion within 4 hours of BSP file receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: Sabre PRISM and Travelport use different file formats requiring dual ETL pipelines; mismatched PNR cross-references cause ~2% of records to fail automatic join

l4_steps.name: Validate data quality and apply cleansing rules
l4_steps.input: Raw PSS and GDS transaction datasets
l4_steps.output: Quality-scored dataset; rejected records quarantine file
l4_steps.kpi: Data quality score ≥98% (nulls, duplicates, invalid fare codes <2%)
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO fare basis code changes not always reflected in Altéa within same reporting cycle, causing mis-classification of fare families

l4_steps.name: Load cleansed data to analytics data warehouse
l4_steps.input: Validated and cleansed sales transaction dataset
l4_steps.output: Populated sales_fact and channel_dim tables in Redshift
l4_steps.kpi: Load completion within 2 hours of data quality sign-off; zero load failures
l4_steps.pain_point: Redshift cluster contention during concurrent ETL and BI query windows causes load job timeouts; workload management (WLM) tuning needed per reporting cycle

l4_steps.name: Configure KPI targets and alert thresholds in BI platform
l4_steps.input: Annual commercial plan targets (revenue, load factor, yield by route/channel)
l4_steps.output: Configured KPI thresholds and RAG alert rules in Tableau
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of approved KPI targets loaded before reporting cycle open
l4_steps.pain_point: Mid-year target revisions require manual threshold updates across multiple Tableau workbooks; no automated sync from SAP S/4HANA budget module

l4_steps.name: Build channel and revenue performance dashboards
l4_steps.input: Redshift sales_fact tables; KPI threshold configuration
l4_steps.output: Channel performance dashboard (GDS, NDC, direct, corporate) and revenue dashboard
l4_steps.kpi: Dashboard refresh latency ≤15 minutes from data load completion
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC API Gateway booking data lacks full itinerary detail compared to GDS PNRs, creating reporting asymmetry between channels that distorts yield comparisons

l4_steps.name: Validate dashboard figures against source system totals
l4_steps.input: Tableau dashboard revenue totals; SAP AR revenue recognition ledger
l4_steps.output: Reconciliation sign-off report; variance log if delta >0.5%
l4_steps.kpi: Dashboard-to-SAP revenue variance ≤0.5% before stakeholder distribution
l4_steps.pain_point: BSP settlement timing differences mean Altéa ticketing revenue and SAP AR recognised revenue diverge by up to 3 days, complicating same-day reconciliation

l4_steps.name: Analyse GDS channel yield and cost-per-booking
l4_steps.input: GDS segment dataset; published GDS booking fee schedule
l4_steps.output: Cost-per-booking report by GDS (Sabre / Travelport / Amadeus) and market
l4_steps.kpi: GDS net yield ≥$0.08/RPM after distribution cost deduction
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS incentive overrides negotiated per agency are not always reflected in PRISM reporting, causing under-reporting of true distribution cost by up to 12%

l4_steps.name: Assess NDC and direct channel conversion rates
l4_steps.input: NDC API search-to-book funnel data; direct website booking data
l4_steps.output: NDC/direct conversion funnel report with drop-off analysis
l4_steps.kpi: NDC channel conversion rate ≥2.8%; direct web conversion ≥4.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC API Gateway does not expose abandoned search data uniformly across aggregators, making full-funnel attribution incomplete for ~30% of NDC traffic

l4_steps.name: Review corporate and TMC account performance vs contract
l4_steps.input: Sabre PRISM corporate account booking volumes; contracted revenue commitments
l4_steps.output: Corporate account scorecard; list of accounts below commitment threshold
l4_steps.kpi: ≥90% of corporate accounts at or above 80% of contracted volume target
l4_steps.pain_point: PRISM reporting lag of 48–72 hours means corporate account shortfalls are identified too late in the quarter for proactive remediation conversations with TMCs

l4_steps.name: Analyse fare class mix and RASK by route and market
l4_steps.input: Closed booking data by fare basis and O&D from Altéa NRM
l4_steps.output: Fare mix report: premium vs discount share, RASK by route
l4_steps.kpi: Average RASK ≥$0.145; premium fare class share ≥22% of total revenue
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM O&D attribution for multi-segment itineraries uses pro-rate allocation that diverges from finance segment-level revenue, creating dual versions of RASK truth

l4_steps.name: Monitor load factor and yield trends vs prior year
l4_steps.input: Current period and prior year sales_fact data from Redshift
l4_steps.output: Load factor and yield trend report; YoY variance by route, season, and channel
l4_steps.kpi: Load factor ≥83%; yield variance to prior year within ±5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Seasonal schedule changes (IATA SSIM S/W schedule swaps) cause route-level YoY comparisons to be distorted when new routes replace discontinued ones mid-period

l4_steps.name: Identify routes and segments below revenue performance target
l4_steps.input: RASK and load factor report; network revenue target thresholds from commercial plan
l4_steps.output: Underperformance flag list: routes with RASK <target for ≥2 consecutive periods
l4_steps.kpi: Zero routes with RASK <80% of target unaddressed beyond two consecutive reporting cycles
l4_steps.pain_point: Thin O&D markets with <10 daily passengers produce statistically unreliable RASK readings; automated flags generate false positives requiring manual analyst review

l4_steps.name: Produce budget variance and forecast deviation analysis
l4_steps.input: Actuals from SAP AR; approved budget and rolling forecast from SAP CO
l4_steps.output: Variance analysis pack: actual vs budget vs forecast by revenue line
l4_steps.kpi: Variance commentary complete for all lines deviating >±3% from budget
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP CO rolling forecast is updated monthly while sales actuals close weekly, creating a structural lag that makes mid-month variance analysis unreliable for operational decisions

l4_steps.name: Compile executive management reporting pack
l4_steps.input: Channel performance, fare mix, RASK, load factor, and variance reports
l4_steps.output: Monthly sales performance deck with KPI scorecards and narrative commentary
l4_steps.kpi: Management pack distributed by business day 5 of the following month
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual consolidation from multiple source reports (Tableau, SAP, PRISM) into a single Power BI pack introduces transcription risk and is a single-point-of-failure if the analyst is absent

l4_steps.name: Assess exceptions and determine escalation requirement
l4_steps.input: Management reporting pack; KPI RAG status from Tableau
l4_steps.output: Escalation decision: confirmed exception list for board or commercial committee
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of Red-rated KPIs reviewed within 24 hours of report distribution
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated linkage between Tableau RAG alerts and calendar invites or escalation workflows; exception follow-through depends on manual distribution list hygiene

l4_steps.name: Distribute reports and archive reporting cycle artefacts
l4_steps.input: Final approved management pack and all source reports
l4_steps.output: Reports distributed to stakeholders; artefacts archived in S3 with version tag
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of reports archived within 1 business day; distribution list accuracy ≥99%
l4_steps.pain_point: No single authoritative distribution list; stale email groups cause reports to reach departed employees or miss new regional sales directors after org changes

l4_steps.name: Extract channel cost data from PSS and finance
l4_steps.input: Monthly GDS booking fee invoices from Sabre, Travelport, Amadeus; Altéa PSS transaction logs
l4_steps.output: Channel cost report segmented by GDS, NDC, and direct booking source
l4_steps.kpi: Cost extraction completeness ≥99% of bookings reconciled per period
l4_steps.pain_point: Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus each use different invoice formats and fee codes; reconciliation against Altéa PSS PNRs requires manual mapping that introduces errors in ~2–3% of bookings

l4_steps.name: Allocate GDS booking fees to route and O&D level
l4_steps.input: Channel cost report, Altéa PSS O&D booking data
l4_steps.output: Per-segment distribution cost dataset by route, O&D, and booking class
l4_steps.kpi: GDS cost per booking reconciled within ±$0.05 vs. invoiced totals
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS booking records must be joined to SAP cost data at different granularities; PNR format mismatches between GDS sources and PSS cause join failures requiring manual resolution

l4_steps.name: Validate and approve cost allocation baseline
l4_steps.input: Per-segment distribution cost dataset from AWS Redshift
l4_steps.output: Approved distribution cost baseline dashboard with channel-level unit economics
l4_steps.kpi: Baseline approved and published within 5 business days of period close
l4_steps.pain_point: Disputed cost allocations between Finance and Commercial teams delay sign-off; no single P&L owner for distribution costs creates accountability gaps that slow the optimization cycle

l4_steps.name: Benchmark distribution cost vs. industry peers
l4_steps.input: Approved cost baseline, IATA Distribution Cost Study, OAG channel share data
l4_steps.output: Competitive gap analysis: cost per booking vs. peer carriers by channel
l4_steps.kpi: Distribution cost per booking target ≤$11.00 (vs. IATA industry average of $14–18)
l4_steps.pain_point: Industry peer benchmarks are self-reported and often exclude hidden indirect costs such as agency incentive overrides; benchmarking accuracy is limited and results may misstate true competitive position

l4_steps.name: Set channel-specific cost reduction targets
l4_steps.input: Competitive gap analysis, annual revenue and margin plan
l4_steps.output: Approved cost reduction targets by channel (GDS, NDC, direct) for the planning year
l4_steps.kpi: Target: 15% reduction in blended distribution cost per booking year-on-year
l4_steps.pain_point: Commercial teams may resist aggressive NDC shift targets when GDS volume is contractually linked to incentive tiers or corporate travel agreements that cannot be restructured mid-year

l4_steps.name: Identify high-cost booking segments and routes
l4_steps.input: Cost baseline, channel mix data from Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Priority route and channel matrix: top 20% routes by distribution cost contributing ≥40% of GDS spend
l4_steps.kpi: Top-20% high-cost routes identified and validated within 3 business days of baseline approval
l4_steps.pain_point: High-yield corporate routes are typically the highest GDS-cost segments; reducing GDS dependency on these routes risks losing managed travel bookings routed through Sabre PRISM by TMC partners

l4_steps.name: Assess NDC API capability and agency readiness
l4_steps.input: NDC adoption tracker, agency certification status list, OBT compatibility matrix
l4_steps.output: Agency NDC readiness scorecard ranked by booking volume
l4_steps.kpi: ≥60% of top-50 agencies NDC-certified within 6 months of programme launch
l4_steps.pain_point: Mid-market agencies lack NDC-capable booking tools; OBTs such as SAP Concur require separate NDC plug-ins with additional integration fees, creating adoption friction outside the top-10 agency pool

l4_steps.name: Design NDC incentive and GDS surcharge structure
l4_steps.input: Agency NDC readiness scorecard, current commission and override schedule
l4_steps.output: NDC incentive tier schedule and GDS surcharge policy filed via ATPCO
l4_steps.kpi: NDC incentive cost per shifted booking ≤50% of the GDS fee saving on the same booking
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO filing of channel-differentiated pricing is restricted by fare parity clauses in certain GDS full-content agreements and by regulatory price-parity rules in EU and select APAC markets; legal review adds 4–6 weeks per market

l4_steps.name: Negotiate NDC adoption agreements with top agencies
l4_steps.input: NDC incentive tier schedule, agency booking volume data from Sabre PRISM
l4_steps.output: Signed NDC adoption agreements covering milestone targets and incentive conditions
l4_steps.kpi: NDC adoption agreements signed with agencies covering ≥40% of total indirect booking volume
l4_steps.pain_point: Large TMCs (BCD Travel, CWT, Amex GBT) negotiate distribution terms as blocs; failure to reach agreement risks losing the entire managed travel segment, which may represent 25–35% of revenue on key business routes

l4_steps.name: Activate NDC channel and monitor booking shift
l4_steps.input: Signed adoption agreements, NDC API go-live checklist, Amadeus Altéa PSS integration confirmation
l4_steps.output: NDC booking volume report; channel shift metrics vs. GDS baseline
l4_steps.kpi: NDC share of indirect bookings ≥20% within 12 months of channel activation
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC API stability issues — including rate limit breaches, error code ambiguity, and mid-session session token failures — cause booking failures that agents attribute to the airline, risking channel abandonment and reversion to GDS

l4_steps.name: Audit GDS full-content agreement compliance
l4_steps.input: GDS full-content contracts (Sabre, Travelport, Amadeus), booking volume reports from Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Full-content compliance audit report by GDS and market
l4_steps.kpi: GDS contract compliance rate ≥98%; zero penalty clauses triggered
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS full-content clauses require all published fares to be available in GDS, creating direct tension with NDC-exclusive offer strategies; legal interpretation of content parity varies by GDS provider and jurisdiction, increasing compliance risk

l4_steps.name: Renegotiate GDS booking fee and incentive terms
l4_steps.input: Full-content compliance audit, multi-year volume forecast, peer airline benchmark data
l4_steps.output: Renegotiated GDS agreement with revised booking fee tiers and volume-based incentive schedule
l4_steps.kpi: GDS booking fee reduction ≥10% vs. current contracted rate across all three GDS providers
l4_steps.pain_point: Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus maintain strong negotiating leverage; airlines with less than 5% regional GDS market share have limited bargaining power, and fee concessions often require multi-year volume commitments that constrain future NDC migration

l4_steps.name: Restructure agency override commission schedule
l4_steps.input: Renegotiated GDS terms, agency performance data from Sabre PRISM
l4_steps.output: Updated performance-linked agency incentive schedule with NDC migration milestones
l4_steps.kpi: Agency incentive cost as % of total revenue ≤2.5% (down from industry average ~3.5%)
l4_steps.pain_point: Legacy override commission structures in Sabre PRISM are deeply embedded in agency workflows; unilateral reductions risk booking withdrawal by top-producing agencies during the renegotiation window, creating a short-term revenue gap

l4_steps.name: Track blended distribution cost per booking weekly
l4_steps.input: Weekly GDS fee invoices from Sabre, Travelport, Amadeus; NDC booking data; direct booking revenue data from Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Weekly distribution cost dashboard with channel-level unit cost and trend vs. target
l4_steps.kpi: Blended distribution cost per booking ≤$11.50; dashboard published within T+2 business days of week close
l4_steps.pain_point: Weekly GDS invoice data from Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus arrives on different billing cycles (weekly, bi-weekly, monthly), creating inconsistent data availability and lag in blended cost visibility

l4_steps.name: Identify cost leakage and wrong-channel bookings
l4_steps.input: Weekly distribution cost dashboard, PNR source data from Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Cost leakage report: high-cost outlier bookings, NDC-enrolled agencies still booking via GDS
l4_steps.kpi: Cost leakage identified and escalated within 5 business days; leakage <2% of total distribution cost
l4_steps.pain_point: Wrong-channel bookings — NDC-enrolled agencies reverting to GDS — are difficult to detect without real-time PNR source tracking; Altéa PSS booking source flags are inconsistently populated by some GDS-connected OBTs

l4_steps.name: Report cost performance to leadership and plan next cycle
l4_steps.input: Cost leakage report, monthly blended distribution cost summary, YoY trend data
l4_steps.output: Executive distribution cost report; updated channel optimization action plan for next quarter
l4_steps.kpi: Monthly report delivered within 5 business days of period close; YoY cost reduction trajectory on track vs. 15% annual target
l4_steps.pain_point: Executive reporting requires attribution of cost changes to specific initiatives (NDC shift, GDS renegotiation, incentive restructure), but the multi-year lag in GDS contract cycles and NDC adoption curves makes causal attribution difficult without a controlled test-and-learn design

l4_steps.name: Ingest corporate lead from partner referral
l4_steps.input: Lead referral from GDS TMC partner, NDC API inquiry, or inbound web form
l4_steps.output: New lead record created in Salesforce with source, contact, and estimated spend
l4_steps.kpi: Lead response time ≤4 hours; lead conversion rate ≥25%
l4_steps.pain_point: Leads arriving via multiple channels (Sabre PRISM, direct email, NDC API) have no unified ingestion point — manual entry causes data gaps and delayed response

l4_steps.name: Score and qualify lead by spend threshold
l4_steps.input: Lead record with estimated annual air spend and company size
l4_steps.output: Qualified or disqualified lead; assigned lead score (0–100)
l4_steps.kpi: Lead qualification accuracy ≥80%; disqualification rate ≤40%
l4_steps.pain_point: Salesforce lead scoring models are not calibrated against actual ticket revenue data from Amadeus Altéa PSS, resulting in mis-scoring of high-value accounts

l4_steps.name: Assign qualified lead to regional sales rep
l4_steps.input: Qualified lead record with territory and vertical segment
l4_steps.output: Lead assigned to named sales rep with SLA clock started
l4_steps.kpi: Assignment turnaround ≤2 hours; SLA acknowledgement by rep ≤24 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Territory alignment rules in Salesforce are manually maintained and lag behind network route changes, causing mis-assignment of accounts near new city-pair launches

l4_steps.name: Create opportunity record and discovery call
l4_steps.input: Assigned lead record; initial client discovery meeting notes
l4_steps.output: Salesforce opportunity with Stage = Discovery, estimated ARR, and travel policy details
l4_steps.kpi: Discovery-to-proposal cycle time ≤5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Sales reps manually key in travel volume data from client spreadsheets; no API integration with SAP Concur or Egencia to import actual managed travel spend

l4_steps.name: Model fare & volume proposal with RM inputs
l4_steps.input: Client O&D mix, estimated annual seat volume, preferred travel windows
l4_steps.output: Draft corporate fare proposal with negotiated discount tiers and volume thresholds
l4_steps.kpi: Proposal margin ≥ target contribution per O&D; average corporate discount ≤14% off published fare
l4_steps.pain_point: Revenue Management team must be consulted manually for each proposal; no self-service fare modelling tool for sales reps, causing bottlenecks when RM team is capacity-constrained

l4_steps.name: Submit proposal for RM and pricing approval
l4_steps.input: Draft fare proposal; RM contribution model output
l4_steps.output: Approved or rejected proposal with RM sign-off recorded in Salesforce opportunity
l4_steps.kpi: RM approval turnaround ≤48 hours; approval rate on first submission ≥70%
l4_steps.pain_point: Approval workflow is email-based with no SLA enforcement; pricing decisions are lost outside Salesforce audit trail, creating compliance risk under ATPCO corporate fare filing rules

l4_steps.name: Submit approved proposal to corporate client
l4_steps.input: RM-approved fare proposal; client contact details
l4_steps.output: Formal proposal document sent to client; opportunity stage updated to Proposal Submitted
l4_steps.kpi: Proposal acceptance rate ≥55%; time-to-response from client ≤7 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Proposal documents are generated from Word templates rather than CRM-native output, leading to version mismatches and unapproved fare terms being quoted

l4_steps.name: Negotiate corporate agreement terms with client
l4_steps.input: Submitted proposal; client counter-proposal or negotiation notes
l4_steps.output: Revised term sheet with agreed discount levels, volume commitments, and bonus triggers
l4_steps.kpi: Negotiation cycle time ≤10 business days; concession rate (additional discount) ≤3%
l4_steps.pain_point: Negotiation concessions (extra discount, waived change fees) are granted ad hoc without systematic tracking, eroding yield across the corporate portfolio without visibility to Finance

l4_steps.name: Execute contract and record in CRM
l4_steps.input: Agreed term sheet; legal corporate agreement template
l4_steps.output: Executed contract stored in Salesforce; opportunity stage = Closed Won
l4_steps.kpi: Contract execution time ≤3 business days post-agreement; 100% of contracts stored in Salesforce with expiry date populated
l4_steps.pain_point: DocuSign / e-signature integration with Salesforce is not enforced; some reps email PDF contracts outside CRM, breaking the audit trail and renewal reminder automation

l4_steps.name: Load negotiated fares into PSS and GDS channels
l4_steps.input: Executed contract with agreed fare levels, booking codes, and validity dates
l4_steps.output: Corporate fare records loaded in Altéa and filed to Sabre GDS, Travelport GDS, and Amadeus GDS via ATPCO
l4_steps.kpi: Fare load accuracy 100%; time from contract execution to fare availability ≤2 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual fare loading into Altéa and ATPCO filing are separate processes with no automated handoff from Salesforce contract record, creating a window where the corporate account is active but fares are not yet bookable

l4_steps.name: Configure corporate account in booking tool and TMC
l4_steps.input: Corporate account ID, negotiated fare codes, TMC contact details
l4_steps.output: Account configured in Sabre PRISM with correct preferred fare hierarchy; TMC notified
l4_steps.kpi: Configuration accuracy rate ≥99%; TMC test booking success rate 100% before go-live
l4_steps.pain_point: Sabre PRISM configuration must be done separately from Altéa PSS fare loading; mismatches between the two systems cause TMC booking failures that are only discovered by the corporate traveller

l4_steps.name: Activate corporate account and confirm with client
