l4_steps.input: Confirmation from Distribution Ops that fares are live and booking tool is configured
l4_steps.output: Account activation confirmation email to client; Salesforce account status = Active
l4_steps.kpi: Time from contract execution to account activation ≤3 business days; activation CSAT ≥4.2/5
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated trigger from Altéa or Sabre PRISM back to Salesforce to confirm fare go-live; sales reps manually chase Distribution Ops, delaying client communication and eroding trust in the onboarding process

l4_steps.name: Track corporate booking volume against contract targets
l4_steps.input: Booking data from Amadeus Altéa PSS; contract volume commitments from Salesforce
l4_steps.output: Monthly account scorecard showing actual vs target volume by O&D and booking class
l4_steps.kpi: Volume attainment ≥90% of contracted threshold; on-time scorecard delivery by 5th of each month
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa booking data is not directly piped into Salesforce opportunity tracking; reporting requires manual extracts and reconciliation in Tableau, introducing a 5–7 day data lag that slows account intervention

l4_steps.name: Conduct quarterly business review with corporate client
l4_steps.input: Account scorecard; market share data from Sabre PRISM; competitive benchmarks from OAG
l4_steps.output: QBR presentation delivered; action items logged in Salesforce; contract amendment flags raised if needed
l4_steps.kpi: QBR completion rate 100% for accounts >$500K ARR; action item close rate ≥80% within 30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: OAG market share data and Sabre PRISM share-of-wallet reports are not integrated into Salesforce, requiring manual assembly of QBR materials and reducing time available for strategic client discussion

l4_steps.name: Assess contract renewal or renegotiation trigger
l4_steps.input: Contract expiry date alert; YTD volume attainment; competitive win/loss signals
l4_steps.output: Renewal decision: auto-renew, renegotiate, or let expire; opportunity stage updated accordingly
l4_steps.kpi: Renewal rate ≥85% for accounts meeting volume thresholds; renewal initiated ≥90 days before expiry
l4_steps.pain_point: Salesforce contract expiry alerts are often suppressed or ignored; accounts have lapsed without renewal, forcing expensive re-acquisition through GDS channels at higher distribution cost

l4_steps.name: Capture new member application data
l4_steps.input: New member sign-up form via web, mobile app, or in-flight registration
l4_steps.output: Pending member profile record with email, name, contact details
l4_steps.kpi: Enrollment completion rate ≥97%; form abandonment rate <3%
l4_steps.pain_point: Members signing up through multiple channels (web, mobile, GDS booking) without email deduplication create duplicate records that inflate reported membership figures by up to 8%

l4_steps.name: Validate identity and deduplicate profile
l4_steps.input: Pending member profile record
l4_steps.output: Verified, deduplicated member record or merge notification
l4_steps.kpi: Duplicate member rate <0.5% of active member base
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS-sourced bookings frequently lack email address, producing orphaned accounts that cannot be auto-merged; manual resolution queues exceed 5,000 records per month at large carriers

l4_steps.name: Assign base tier and post welcome bonus miles
l4_steps.input: Verified member record
l4_steps.output: Active member account with base tier, welcome bonus posted
l4_steps.kpi: Welcome bonus posting accuracy 100%; account activation within 24 hours of enrollment
l4_steps.pain_point: Tier assignment rules not synchronised in real time between Comarch and Amadeus Altéa PSS; boarding pass may display incorrect tier for first flight taken within hours of enrollment

l4_steps.name: Ingest flight segment data from PSS
l4_steps.input: Completed flight manifest and boarded-passenger segment records
l4_steps.output: Raw accrual transaction records staged in Comarch queue
l4_steps.kpi: Post-flight accrual data ingestion SLA ≤72 hours; segment match rate ≥99%
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa segment data may arrive with codeshare operating-carrier code mismatch, causing failed accrual lookups for interline and partner flights; exception queue can spike after irregular operations

l4_steps.name: Calculate eligible miles per booking class
l4_steps.input: Raw accrual transaction + fare class accrual rate table
l4_steps.output: Calculated mile award amount per segment
l4_steps.kpi: Accrual calculation accuracy ≥99.8%; rules table refresh within 4 hours of fare class change
l4_steps.pain_point: Complex earning multipliers for co-brand card holders are not reflected in real time if card-link data lags from bank partner API by 24–48 hours; members earn base miles then must request adjustment

l4_steps.name: Post miles to member account
l4_steps.input: Validated calculated mile award
l4_steps.output: Posted transaction on member account ledger; balance updated
l4_steps.kpi: Miles posting success rate ≥99.9%; failed posting retry resolution within 4 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: API timeout during peak post-travel periods (Monday 06:00–09:00 local) causes transaction queuing; backlog can delay posting beyond the 72-hour SLA, generating member service contacts

l4_steps.name: Process retro-credit claim for missing miles
l4_steps.input: Member-submitted missing miles claim with booking reference and boarding pass
l4_steps.output: Approved retro-credit posting or rejection notification
l4_steps.kpi: Retro-claim resolution ≤5 business days; auto-approval rate for flight claims ≥70%
l4_steps.pain_point: Partner hotel and car-rental claims require manual verification due to absence of real-time partner transaction feeds; average handle time for partner retro-claims is 3× that of flight claims

l4_steps.name: Aggregate qualifying activity for tier review
l4_steps.input: 12-month rolling transaction history from Comarch Loyalty Management
l4_steps.output: Tier qualification summary per member (qualifying miles, segments, spend)
l4_steps.kpi: Tier calculation batch processing time <4 hours for membership base ≥1M; completed by 02:00 local on qualification date
l4_steps.pain_point: Year-end tier rollover processing creates Comarch database contention; programmes with >2M active members have experienced rollover jobs exceeding the maintenance window, delaying tier notifications by up to 48 hours

l4_steps.name: Evaluate tier upgrade or downgrade eligibility
l4_steps.input: Tier qualification summary per member
l4_steps.output: Tier change decision (upgrade, downgrade, maintain) per member record
l4_steps.kpi: Tier assignment accuracy rate 100%; exception case resolution ≤2 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Tier criteria differ between earned-status and status-match members; exceptions are managed via manual spreadsheet outside Comarch, creating audit trail gaps and occasional erroneous downgrades that drive high-value member complaints

l4_steps.name: Notify member of tier change and updated benefits
l4_steps.input: Tier change decision from Comarch Loyalty Management
l4_steps.output: Personalised tier upgrade or downgrade notification email
l4_steps.kpi: Email open rate ≥35% for tier upgrade notifications; send within 2 hours of tier change
l4_steps.pain_point: Salesforce Marketing Cloud integration with Comarch runs on nightly batch; real-time tier changes (e.g., reached Gold at midnight) are not reflected in communications until the following morning, delaying member recognition

l4_steps.name: Provision tier benefits and flags in PSS
l4_steps.input: New tier assignment from Comarch Loyalty Management
l4_steps.output: Updated member profile in Altéa with lounge access, priority boarding, and SSR flags
l4_steps.kpi: Benefit provisioning SLA ≤2 hours post-tier assignment; SSR flag accuracy 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa profile update does not propagate to codeshare or interline partner carrier systems; lounge access flags may be absent on partner-operated flights, requiring manual override at airport — a top-5 elite member complaint driver

l4_steps.name: Search and display award flight availability
l4_steps.input: Member redemption request with desired origin, destination, and dates
l4_steps.output: Award availability display with applicable mile costs by fare bucket
l4_steps.kpi: Award availability search response time ≤3 seconds; award seat availability ≥5% of cabin capacity on operated flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Award seat inventory is managed in a separate Altéa RM bucket from revenue inventory; RM team allocation rules are not always aligned with redemption demand, resulting in sub-optimal award availability that pushes members to competitors

l4_steps.name: Validate member miles balance and expiry status
l4_steps.input: Member account query triggered by redemption request
l4_steps.output: Confirmed available balance and expiry date; warning if miles expire within 90 days
l4_steps.kpi: Balance check API response time ≤1 second; expiry warning accuracy 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Miles expiry rules differ by programme tier and earning source; expired-miles disputes are consistently in the top-3 contact centre drivers, each requiring manual audit of the 24-month transaction ledger

l4_steps.name: Process award booking and deduct miles
l4_steps.input: Confirmed award selection and validated miles balance from Comarch
l4_steps.output: Award PNR in Altéa and corresponding miles deduction transaction in Comarch
l4_steps.kpi: Redemption processing success rate ≥99.5%; dual-system transaction completion within 60 seconds
l4_steps.pain_point: Dual-system transaction (Altéa PNR creation + Comarch deduction) has no atomic rollback; if Altéa confirms the PNR but Comarch times out, miles are not deducted, creating liability; or vice versa creating orphaned PNRs

l4_steps.name: Issue award ticket via GDS or NDC channel
l4_steps.input: Confirmed award PNR
l4_steps.output: Issued award e-ticket with ATPCO award fare code
l4_steps.kpi: Award ticket issuance within 15 minutes of booking confirmation; ticketing failure rate <0.3%
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO award fare filing delays can cause ticketing failures when a carrier updates its award chart mid-season without providing adequate lead time; agents must manually override fare basis codes, increasing error risk

l4_steps.name: Ingest partner earn transactions via SFTP or API
l4_steps.input: Partner transaction data files (hotel, car rental, retail) via SFTP or REST API
l4_steps.output: Staged partner transaction records in data lake for Comarch processing
l4_steps.kpi: Partner file ingestion within 24 hours of transaction; data completeness rate ≥98%
l4_steps.pain_point: Partner data formats are inconsistent across up to 15 active earn partners; each non-standard SFTP feed requires a bespoke ETL transform in AWS, with schema changes by partners breaking pipelines and delaying member mile postings

l4_steps.name: Reconcile co-brand card spend accruals with bank
l4_steps.input: Co-brand card transaction data from bank partner API and Comarch accrual ledger
l4_steps.output: Reconciled mile liability journal entry; variance report for disputes
l4_steps.kpi: Reconciliation completion within 3 business days of month-end; variance rate <0.1% of total miles issued
l4_steps.pain_point: Bank API transaction data is typically 24–48 hours delayed; real-time card spend accrual SLA commitments made to co-brand cardholders are not achievable with batch feeds, requiring liability provisioning estimates that create month-end restatements

l4_steps.name: Invoice partner for mile liability and settle AR
l4_steps.input: Reconciled mile liability from co-brand and earn partner transactions
l4_steps.output: Partner invoice (AR document) and settlement confirmation
l4_steps.kpi: Invoice issued within 5 business days of month-end; DSO on partner invoices ≤30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Mile valuation disputes with hotel and retail partners are a recurring AR collection risk; no contractual SLA governs partner dispute resolution timelines, and unresolved disputes can age beyond 90 days before escalation

l4_steps.name: Segment members by engagement and lifetime value
l4_steps.input: Full member transaction, redemption, and flight history
l4_steps.output: Member segments: active, at-risk, lapsed, high-value
l4_steps.kpi: Segmentation model refresh ≤weekly; at-risk identification lead time ≥30 days before predicted churn
l4_steps.pain_point: Member lifetime value model is not updated in real time; at-risk interventions may lag by up to 7 days after engagement drops, reducing campaign effectiveness for time-sensitive retention windows

l4_steps.name: Design and launch targeted retention campaign
l4_steps.input: At-risk and lapsed member segment lists from AWS Redshift
l4_steps.output: Deployed retention campaign (miles bonus, status extension offer, or upgrade voucher)
l4_steps.kpi: Campaign redemption rate ≥8% for re-engagement offers; unsubscribe rate <0.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: GDPR and CCPA consent management in Salesforce Marketing Cloud is not always synchronised with Comarch consent flags; sending campaigns to members who have opted out in Comarch but not yet in SFMC creates regulatory exposure and potential fines

l4_steps.name: Measure programme ROI and report to leadership
l4_steps.input: Campaign results, financial data from SAP S/4HANA, and booking attribution data
l4_steps.output: Monthly programme ROI dashboard and executive summary
l4_steps.kpi: Monthly ROI report delivered by day 5 of following month; programme break-even mile cost ≤$0.012 per mile issued
l4_steps.pain_point: Revenue attribution between loyalty-driven incremental bookings and organic demand is methodologically contested; commercial, finance, and loyalty teams use different attribution models, producing materially different ROI figures that undermine programme investment decisions

l4_steps.name: Capture flight departure event from PSS
l4_steps.input: Passenger name record (PNR) at flight departure
l4_steps.output: Accrual trigger event posted to loyalty processing queue
l4_steps.kpi: Accrual events captured within 24h of departure ≥99%
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus Altéa departure events can be delayed during irregular ops; cancelled-then-reprotected flights generate duplicate accrual triggers requiring deduplication logic not natively supported in Altéa

l4_steps.name: Validate member account active status
l4_steps.input: Accrual trigger event with member number
l4_steps.output: Account status flag: Active / Suspended / Pending
l4_steps.kpi: Zero false-positive account suspensions per month
l4_steps.pain_point: Accounts suspended for fraud screening block legitimate accruals; reactivation SLA is 5 business days — members with pending fraud reviews miss accruals with no automatic back-posting upon clearance

l4_steps.name: Verify ticket eligibility by fare basis code
l4_steps.input: Fare basis code extracted from PNR segment
l4_steps.output: Eligible / Ineligible flag with applicable earning rate
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of ineligible fare classes (award tickets, staff travel) correctly excluded
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO fare basis eligibility mappings require quarterly refresh; stale mappings incorrectly block accruals on newly introduced fare classes until the next scheduled update cycle

l4_steps.name: Retrieve flown distance and cabin class data
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS / OAG Schedule Analyser
l4_steps.input: Validated PNR with operated flight segment
l4_steps.output: Flown distance in miles and cabin class code
l4_steps.kpi: Distance retrieval accuracy ≥99.9% vs. IATA great-circle distances
l4_steps.pain_point: Codeshare segments report operating-carrier distance rather than marketing-carrier distance; causes systematic under-accrual on partner-operated flights when the operating carrier's city pair distance is shorter than the ticketed routing

l4_steps.name: Calculate base miles using distance × fare multiplier
l4_steps.input: Flown distance, cabin class code, fare basis eligibility flag
l4_steps.output: Base miles award value
l4_steps.kpi: Base miles calculation latency <3 seconds per transaction; calculation error rate <0.01%
l4_steps.pain_point: Multiplier tables must be synchronised between Comarch Loyalty and Amadeus Altéa; version mismatch after a programme rule change causes accrual discrepancies requiring a manual batch correction job affecting tens of thousands of accounts

l4_steps.name: Apply elite tier and promotional bonus multipliers
l4_steps.system: Comarch Loyalty Management / Salesforce Marketing Cloud
l4_steps.input: Base miles value, member tier level, active campaign codes
l4_steps.output: Adjusted miles award value with bonus breakdown by source
l4_steps.kpi: Promotional miles correctly applied in ≥99.5% of eligible transactions
l4_steps.pain_point: Stacked promotions (elite tier bonus + partner co-brand card bonus + targeted campaign) can exceed programme liability caps; no automated cap enforcement exists in the current Comarch configuration — over-issuance discovered only at month-end liability review

l4_steps.name: Post miles transaction to member account ledger
l4_steps.input: Adjusted miles award value with all multipliers applied
l4_steps.output: Miles balance updated; transaction ledger entry created with timestamp
l4_steps.kpi: Miles posted within 3 business days of flight departure (IATA Loyalty Standard); batch failure rate <0.1%
l4_steps.pain_point: Batch posting jobs can fail silently under high transaction volume during peak travel seasons; reconciliation lag of up to 72h before failures are detected means members contact the call centre before the system self-corrects, driving avoidable contact volume

l4_steps.name: Evaluate qualifying miles for tier re-qualification
l4_steps.input: Updated miles balance; qualifying miles year-to-date counter
l4_steps.output: Tier status decision: Maintain / Upgrade / Downgrade candidate
l4_steps.kpi: Tier re-qualification evaluated within 24h of miles posting; tier status error rate <0.05%
l4_steps.pain_point: Qualifying miles rollover logic at the programme year boundary is hard-coded in Comarch and requires a manual configuration change each January; incorrect rollover logic has historically caused erroneous tier downgrades affecting high-value members

l4_steps.name: Send accrual confirmation notification to member
l4_steps.input: Posted transaction record from Comarch Loyalty Management
l4_steps.output: Email or push notification with miles summary and updated balance
l4_steps.kpi: Notification delivery rate ≥97%; unsubscribe rate <0.5% per campaign
l4_steps.pain_point: Multiple accrual events on the same travel day (flight segment + lounge visit + partner hotel) trigger separate notifications; no deduplication or daily digest batching in the current Salesforce journey configuration — member over-notification drives opt-outs among frequent flyers

l4_steps.name: Ingest daily partner accrual activity file
l4_steps.input: Structured partner activity file from hotel, car rental, or co-brand credit card partner
l4_steps.output: Raw partner accrual records loaded to staging table in AWS Redshift
l4_steps.kpi: Partner file ingested and schema-validated within 4h of scheduled receipt; file rejection rate <2%
l4_steps.pain_point: Partner file format inconsistencies (non-standard delimiters, missing member IDs, variant date formats) cause up to 8% record rejection rate per cycle; no automated partner notification on rejection — manual follow-up adds 1–3 day processing delay

l4_steps.name: Match partner activity records to member accounts
l4_steps.input: Validated partner accrual records from staging table
l4_steps.output: Matched transaction records with confirmed member account links
l4_steps.kpi: Member account match rate ≥95% of valid partner records within 24h of ingestion
l4_steps.pain_point: Hotel and car rental partners submit member IDs in non-standard formats (e.g., with country prefix or leading zeros stripped); no automated fuzzy-match fallback in Comarch means unmatched records queue indefinitely rather than routing to a resolution workflow

l4_steps.name: Validate miles award against partner rate card
l4_steps.input: Matched transaction with partner ID and activity type code
l4_steps.output: Validated miles award value per partner agreement terms
l4_steps.kpi: Rate card accuracy ≥99% vs. signed partner agreement; rate discrepancy resolution within 5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Partner rate card amendments effective mid-cycle are not always communicated via API update; manual rate table maintenance in Comarch lags partner notification by 3–7 days, causing systematic under- or over-accrual until the next scheduled sync

l4_steps.name: Reconcile partner-posted miles vs. billing invoice
l4_steps.input: Monthly partner billing summary and posted miles ledger from Comarch
l4_steps.output: Reconciliation variance report; approved settlement invoice
l4_steps.kpi: Monthly partner reconciliation completed within 5 business days of period close; variance <0.5% of total billed miles
l4_steps.pain_point: Partner billing files use proprietary transaction IDs that differ from loyalty system reference numbers; cross-reference mapping is maintained in a manually updated Excel file — a single point of failure that causes reconciliation delays when the file owner is unavailable

l4_steps.name: Receive and triage missing miles claim from member
l4_steps.input: Member claim submission with supporting documentation (boarding pass, receipt, transaction reference)
l4_steps.output: Claim record created with investigation status and SLA timer started
l4_steps.kpi: Missing miles claim resolved within 21 days (IATA Resolution 9984 standard); first-contact resolution rate ≥60%
l4_steps.pain_point: Members frequently submit claims without required documentation (flight coupon number, original partner receipt); incomplete claims account for ~35% of total case volume and require a second contact cycle, inflating average handle time and breaching SLA on high-case-volume days

l4_steps.name: Post manual miles adjustment for approved claims
l4_steps.input: Approved claim record with validated miles value from investigation
l4_steps.output: Manual adjustment transaction posted to member account; claim closed in Salesforce Service Cloud
l4_steps.kpi: Manual adjustments audited within 48h of posting; adjustment error rate <0.5%; high-value adjustments (>10,000 miles) require dual approval
l4_steps.pain_point: Comarch manual override permits posting to suspended or fraud-flagged accounts without a blocking control; no secondary approval gate exists for high-value adjustments — creates an audit and fraud risk that is currently mitigated only by weekly spot-check reviews rather than systematic controls

l4_steps.name: Member Initiates Redemption via Digital Channel
l4_steps.system: Airline Mobile App / Web Self-Service Portal
l4_steps.input: Member login session, desired award type (flight, ancillary, partner)
l4_steps.output: Redemption request record with member ID, award category, and travel dates
l4_steps.kpi: Digital channel redemption rate ≥85% of all award transactions
l4_steps.pain_point: Session timeout during multi-step redemption causes abandoned requests; no mid-session save capability in legacy web portals

l4_steps.name: Validate Member Account Status & Tier
l4_steps.input: Member ID from redemption request
l4_steps.output: Account eligibility flag (Active / Suspended / Frozen)
l4_steps.kpi: Account validation response time <2 seconds (99th percentile)
l4_steps.pain_point: Members with disputed fraud flags are incorrectly blocked; manual review queue SLA averages 4 business days, causing member complaints

l4_steps.name: Verify Miles Balance Sufficiency
l4_steps.input: Current miles balance, requested award miles cost
l4_steps.output: Balance sufficiency flag; shortfall amount if insufficient
l4_steps.kpi: Real-time balance accuracy ≥99.95% (no stale cache reads)
l4_steps.pain_point: Miles balance caching latency of up to 15 minutes causes members to see inflated balances post-accrual, leading to failed redemption attempts at checkout

l4_steps.name: Query Award Seat Inventory in PSS
l4_steps.input: Requested flight, cabin class, travel dates
l4_steps.output: Award availability response (available classes and seat counts)
l4_steps.kpi: Award seat search response time <3 seconds; award seat availability ≥10% of total cabin capacity on published routes
l4_steps.pain_point: Award inventory buckets are statically defined and rarely recalibrated; high-demand routes show zero award availability 6+ months out despite low commercial load

l4_steps.name: Apply Award Inventory Control Rules
l4_steps.input: Current commercial load factor, award bucket thresholds, blackout calendar
l4_steps.output: Approved or blocked award seat release decision
l4_steps.kpi: Award inventory utilisation rate ≥72% of allocated buckets per quarter
l4_steps.pain_point: Blackout date logic is manually maintained in a spreadsheet outside the RM system; discrepancies between RM rules and loyalty portal display cause member-facing availability errors

l4_steps.name: Check Partner Award Availability
l4_steps.system: NDC API Gateway / Partner Redemption API
l4_steps.input: Partner category (hotel, car hire, retail voucher), member request
l4_steps.output: Partner award catalogue response with availability and miles cost
l4_steps.kpi: Partner API availability ≥99.5% uptime; catalogue refresh latency <24 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Partner APIs use non-standard schemas; mapping failures cause 3–5% of partner redemption requests to error silently without member notification

l4_steps.name: Hold Award Seat or Partner Slot
l4_steps.input: Confirmed award availability, member session token
l4_steps.output: Provisional hold reference number (TTL: 15 minutes)
l4_steps.kpi: Hold-to-booking conversion rate ≥78%; hold timeout abandonment rate <22%
l4_steps.pain_point: 15-minute TTL is insufficient for members using screen readers or with accessibility needs; no TTL extension capability exists in the current PSS configuration

l4_steps.name: Calculate Miles Required & Applicable Taxes
l4_steps.input: Award type, cabin class, route, tier status, active promotions
l4_steps.output: Final miles cost breakdown and cash surcharge/tax amount
l4_steps.kpi: Pricing calculation accuracy 100% (zero mis-priced awards issued)
l4_steps.pain_point: Government-imposed departure taxes and carrier surcharges are inconsistently applied to award tickets; manual overrides required for certain markets increase processing time by 40%

l4_steps.name: Collect Cash Co-Pay for Taxes & Surcharges
l4_steps.input: Calculated cash amount, member payment credentials
l4_steps.output: Payment authorisation reference; receipt
l4_steps.kpi: Payment authorisation success rate ≥97.5%; fraud decline rate <0.8%
l4_steps.pain_point: PCI-DSS tokenisation scope forces redirect to external payment page, breaking the redemption flow and increasing cart abandonment by an estimated 12%

l4_steps.name: Member Confirms Award Booking
l4_steps.system: Airline Mobile App / Web Self-Service Portal
l4_steps.input: Full award summary, payment confirmation, miles cost
l4_steps.output: Member acceptance event (within 15-minute session window)
l4_steps.kpi: Confirmation completion rate ≥80% of members who reach review screen
l4_steps.pain_point: Members presented with unexpected surcharge totals at confirmation abandon at a 35% rate; no pre-checkout surcharge estimate is shown earlier in the funnel

l4_steps.name: Deduct Miles from Member Account
l4_steps.input: Member confirmation event, calculated miles cost
l4_steps.output: Updated miles balance; deduction transaction record
l4_steps.kpi: Miles deduction posting time <5 seconds; deduction error rate <0.01%
l4_steps.pain_point: Concurrent redemption requests from the same account (e.g., via app and web simultaneously) can cause double-deduction if idempotency checks are not enforced at the API layer

l4_steps.name: Issue Award Ticket or E-Voucher
l4_steps.input: Confirmed booking PNR, deduction transaction record
l4_steps.output: Electronic ticket number (ETK) or partner voucher code
l4_steps.kpi: Ticket issuance success rate ≥99.8%; issuance time <30 seconds
l4_steps.pain_point: Award tickets on interline itineraries require manual segment-by-segment ticketing in Altéa; automation gap adds 20–45 minutes per complex itinerary and scales poorly during peak redemption periods

l4_steps.name: Transmit Partner Booking via API
l4_steps.system: NDC API Gateway / Partner Redemption API
l4_steps.input: Voucher code, partner booking reference, member contact details
l4_steps.output: Partner booking confirmation reference
l4_steps.kpi: Partner booking API success rate ≥98.5%; confirmation delivery time <2 minutes
l4_steps.pain_point: Real-time partner booking APIs cover only 60% of partners; remaining 40% use batch file exchange with 24-hour confirmation lag, leaving members without instant booking confirmation

l4_steps.name: Send E-Ticket & Booking Confirmation to Member
l4_steps.input: ETK or voucher code, partner confirmation, member contact preferences
l4_steps.output: Transactional email/SMS confirmation with PNR and redemption summary
l4_steps.kpi: Confirmation delivery rate ≥99.2%; delivery time <5 minutes of ticket issuance
l4_steps.pain_point: Members who update contact preferences in the loyalty portal mid-session may receive confirmations to a stale email address due to CRM sync latency of up to 6 hours

l4_steps.name: Update Member Redemption History
l4_steps.input: Completed transaction record, ETK, partner reference
l4_steps.output: Updated member activity ledger; redemption event record
l4_steps.kpi: Ledger update latency <10 seconds; history record accuracy 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Partner redemption events written by the NDC gateway use a different transaction format than PSS award tickets; consolidation into a single view requires nightly batch job, preventing real-time statement accuracy

l4_steps.name: Reconcile Miles Deducted vs Tickets Issued
l4_steps.input: Daily miles deduction log, ticket issuance log, partner voucher log
l4_steps.output: Reconciliation report; exception list of unmatched transactions
l4_steps.kpi: Reconciliation match rate ≥99.9%; exception resolution within 2 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Ticketing system and loyalty ledger use different timestamps (UTC vs local departure time); timezone mismatch causes ~0.3% of daily transactions to appear as exceptions requiring manual investigation

l4_steps.name: Report Liability Reduction to Finance
l4_steps.input: Reconciled redemption volume, miles deducted, average CPM (cost per mile)
l4_steps.output: Loyalty liability journal entry; deferred revenue release posting
l4_steps.kpi: Monthly loyalty liability reporting accuracy ±0.5% variance vs actuals; posted within 3 business days of month-end
l4_steps.pain_point: CPM (cost per mile) used for liability valuation is updated quarterly; interim month fluctuations in redemption mix (premium vs economy) create material variance in reported liability that is not visible until quarter-end

l4_steps.name: Analyse Redemption Patterns for Programme Optimisation
l4_steps.system: Tableau / Power BI (connected to AWS Redshift)
l4_steps.input: Redemption history, award category breakdown, tier segment data
l4_steps.output: Redemption analytics dashboard; programme adjustment recommendations
l4_steps.kpi: Award seat utilisation rate ≥75%; partner redemption share ≥20% of total redemptions
l4_steps.pain_point: Redemption data from partner ecosystems arrives with 48-hour delay and inconsistent granularity; analytics dashboards cannot provide same-day programme performance visibility needed for dynamic award pricing decisions

l4_steps.name: Ingest flight activity from PSS transaction feed
l4_steps.input: Post-departure flight coupons and e-ticket transaction records
l4_steps.output: Raw activity records loaded into loyalty staging table
l4_steps.kpi: Transaction ingestion latency ≤4 hours post-departure; error rate <0.1%
l4_steps.pain_point: PSS transaction feeds use EDIFACT format; schema mismatches between Altéa versions cause silent drop of codeshare and interline segments, under-crediting elite members

l4_steps.name: Validate fare class earning eligibility vs ATPCO rules
l4_steps.input: Fare basis code and booking class from ingested transaction
l4_steps.output: Earning eligibility flag (qualifying / non-qualifying) per segment
l4_steps.kpi: Eligibility rule coverage ≥99.5% of active fare families; <0.5% manual review rate
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO fare rules update fortnightly; loyalty rule tables often lag by 1–2 cycles, causing incorrect non-qualifying flags on newly filed promotional fares and generating member complaints

l4_steps.name: Post qualifying miles/segments/spend to member ledger
l4_steps.input: Validated earning eligibility flag and segment distance/revenue data
l4_steps.output: Qualifying Miles (QM), Qualifying Segments (QS), and Qualifying Spend (QSP) posted to member account
l4_steps.kpi: Ledger posting accuracy ≥99.9%; retro-credit request rate <2% of eligible transactions
l4_steps.pain_point: Partner airline codeshare miles require a separate interline settlement file; delays of up to 72 hours in partner data delivery create visible ledger gaps that prompt unnecessary member calls to contact centre

l4_steps.name: Aggregate qualifying credits against tier thresholds
l4_steps.input: Rolling 12-month QM, QS, and QSP ledger totals per member
l4_steps.output: Tier progress score and distance-to-next-tier metric per member
l4_steps.kpi: Batch refresh cycle ≤6 hours; member progress accuracy vs ledger ±0 credits
l4_steps.pain_point: Real-time tier progress is surfaced via mobile app; Redshift batch latency causes app to show stale progress bars, triggering trust complaints from high-value members after qualifying flights

l4_steps.name: Apply partner airline and credit card earning multipliers
l4_steps.input: Base qualifying credits and active partner multiplier rules
l4_steps.output: Adjusted qualifying total inclusive of promotional and partner bonuses
l4_steps.kpi: Multiplier application accuracy ≥99.8%; promotional credit disputes <0.3% of bonus transactions
l4_steps.pain_point: Co-branded credit card spend multipliers are fed by card issuer APIs on a monthly settlement cycle; mid-month tier assessments cannot include unsettled spend, causing members to miss tier upgrades they would have earned had the spend posted on time

l4_steps.name: Flag members within 10% of next tier threshold
l4_steps.input: Tier progress score from Redshift; tier threshold configuration
l4_steps.output: Proactive tier-progress nudge email or push notification sent to member
l4_steps.kpi: Nudge email open rate ≥35%; incremental qualifying activity uplift ≥8% among nudged cohort
l4_steps.pain_point: Personalisation tokens for nudge emails pull live balance from Altéa Loyalty API; API rate limits during peak send windows cause token failures, resulting in generic messages that undermine member engagement

l4_steps.name: Assess whether tier upgrade threshold has been met
l4_steps.input: Adjusted qualifying total; tier programme threshold table
l4_steps.output: Tier upgrade trigger event or no-action record
l4_steps.kpi: Tier threshold assessment latency ≤1 hour of qualifying transaction posting; false-positive rate <0.01%
l4_steps.pain_point: Concurrent qualifying flights on the same calendar day can create race conditions in the threshold check, causing duplicate tier upgrade events that provision double benefit sets until a nightly reconciliation job corrects them

l4_steps.name: Award new tier status in Amadeus Altéa Loyalty
l4_steps.input: Tier upgrade trigger event from step 2.4
l4_steps.output: Member profile updated with new tier code and tier validity dates
l4_steps.kpi: Tier award processing time ≤30 minutes from trigger; tier award error rate <0.05%
l4_steps.pain_point: Tier validity date logic varies by programme (calendar-year vs rolling-12-month); incorrect configuration during programme rule changes has granted tier status with wrong expiry dates, requiring costly retroactive corrections

l4_steps.name: Provision upgrade coupons and lounge access in PSS
l4_steps.input: New tier code from step 3.1; benefit entitlement table per tier
l4_steps.output: Upgrade coupons (eUTCs), lounge access certificates, and priority boarding flags active in PNR
l4_steps.kpi: Benefit provisioning completion ≤2 hours of tier award; coupon redemption error rate at airport <0.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Benefit provisioning relies on Altéa OSI/SSR message injection into the PNR; check-in agents at third-party handling stations without direct Altéa access may not see provisioned benefits, causing lounge access denials and escalations

l4_steps.name: Dispatch tier upgrade congratulation and benefit summary
l4_steps.input: Tier award event; member contact preferences; benefit entitlement copy
l4_steps.output: Personalised congratulation email with new tier benefits, card dispatch confirmation, and portal link
l4_steps.kpi: Email delivery within 2 hours of tier award; delivery success rate ≥98%; unsubscribe rate <0.2%
l4_steps.pain_point: Physical elite card production is outsourced; card delivery SLA of 10 business days conflicts with member expectation of immediate tangible recognition, generating contact centre calls in the interim window

l4_steps.name: Receive upgrade request at booking or check-in gate
l4_steps.input: Member upgrade coupon or tier-based complimentary upgrade entitlement
l4_steps.output: Upgrade request queued against target cabin class inventory
l4_steps.kpi: Upgrade request capture rate ≥99% of eligible members; request queue processing time ≤60 seconds
l4_steps.pain_point: Upgrade request channels (online check-in, kiosk, agent) do not share a single priority queue; the same coupon can be presented simultaneously across channels, creating duplicate upgrade requests that consume inventory incorrectly

l4_steps.name: Check upgrade class seat inventory availability in PSS
l4_steps.input: Upgrade request; flight date/route; target cabin upgrade bucket (e.g., C class)
l4_steps.output: Inventory availability confirmation or waitlist placement decision
l4_steps.kpi: Upgrade clearance rate for top-tier members ≥70% on eligible routes; waitlist clear rate ≥50% by T-24h
l4_steps.pain_point: Upgrade inventory buckets are controlled by Revenue Management; RM teams frequently close upgrade classes on high-demand flights up to T-72h, leaving top-tier members waitlisted on routes where premium seats are visible but commercially blocked

l4_steps.name: Process upgrade rebook or manage waitlist clearance
l4_steps.input: Confirmed upgrade inventory; priority-ranked waitlist
l4_steps.output: Upgraded PNR with new cabin class; deducted upgrade coupon; or maintained waitlist record
l4_steps.kpi: Upgrade processing time ≤5 minutes at check-in; coupon deduction accuracy 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Automated upgrade engines do not always respect manual override priorities set by premium service desks for VVIP members; automated processing can displace a manually held upgrade, requiring agent correction under time pressure at the gate

l4_steps.name: Reissue boarding pass with new cabin assignment
l4_steps.input: Confirmed upgraded PNR; new seat assignment in target cabin
l4_steps.output: Reissued boarding pass with updated class of service and seat number
l4_steps.kpi: Boarding pass reissue time ≤2 minutes; boarding document error rate <0.01%
l4_steps.pain_point: Mobile boarding pass updates via Altéa's push mechanism require the member's app to be online at time of upgrade; offline devices display the original boarding pass, creating security lane discrepancies and boarding delays

l4_steps.name: Log tier dispute or competitive status match claim in CRM
l4_steps.input: Member dispute submission (missing credits, incorrect tier, status match request) with supporting documents
l4_steps.output: Case record created in Salesforce with category, priority, and SLA timer
l4_steps.kpi: Case creation time ≤5 minutes; first response SLA ≤4 business hours for elite members
l4_steps.pain_point: Status match requests from competing programme members require manual verification of competitor tier documentation; no automated data exchange with competing programmes means agents must visually verify screenshots, which are easily manipulated

l4_steps.name: Review documentation and approve or reject dispute
l4_steps.input: Case record; flight/transaction records from Altéa Loyalty; submitted evidence
l4_steps.output: Dispute resolution decision (approved / rejected) with rationale documented
l4_steps.kpi: Dispute resolution time ≤5 business days; first-contact resolution rate ≥80%; approval accuracy vs policy ≥99%
l4_steps.pain_point: Agents lack a single-screen view joining Salesforce case data with Altéa Loyalty transaction history; switching between systems to verify activity increases handle time and introduces manual transcription errors in the resolution record

l4_steps.name: Apply manual tier or credit adjustment in loyalty system
l4_steps.input: Approved dispute decision from step 5.2; adjustment quantity and type
l4_steps.output: Manual credit or tier amendment applied to member account; case closed in Salesforce
l4_steps.kpi: Adjustment posting accuracy 100%; case closure within 1 business day of approval
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual tier adjustments bypass the standard threshold assessment workflow, meaning benefit provisioning in the PSS must also be triggered manually; agents without elevated permissions cannot complete both steps, creating a handoff gap where tier is awarded but benefits are not yet active

l4_steps.name: Run end-of-qualifying-period tier review batch job
l4_steps.input: Member qualifying credit totals for the expiring programme year; tier threshold table
l4_steps.output: Tier renewal, downgrade, or extension recommendation dataset
l4_steps.kpi: Batch job completion within 4-hour overnight window; zero failed member records; data reconciliation variance <0.01%
l4_steps.pain_point: Annual batch job processes millions of member records in a single overnight window; AWS Redshift cluster scaling has historically underestimated job duration, causing batch overruns that delay morning check-in benefit reads at airports on the first day of the new programme year

l4_steps.name: Assess requalification threshold met or missed
l4_steps.input: Recommendation dataset from step 6.1; requalification threshold per tier level
l4_steps.output: Member disposition: renew at current tier / upgrade tier / downgrade tier / place on grace period
l4_steps.kpi: Requalification assessment accuracy ≥99.99%; zero incorrect downgrades of members who requalified
l4_steps.pain_point: Grace period eligibility rules (e.g., extended status for members within 500 miles of requalification) are configured manually in Altéa; rule misconfiguration during programme refreshes has incorrectly downgraded members who should have received a grace extension, resulting in high-value member attrition

l4_steps.name: Execute tier renewal, downgrade, or extension notification
l4_steps.input: Member disposition from step 6.2; communication template per tier outcome
l4_steps.output: Personalised renewal/downgrade/extension email with new tier validity, benefit summary, and re-earn guidance
l4_steps.kpi: Notification delivery within 24 hours of batch completion; downgrade appeal rate <5% among downgraded members
l4_steps.pain_point: Downgrade communications must be carefully sequenced to avoid triggering opt-outs; generic downgrade emails sent without personalised re-earn incentives have historically caused measurable NPS drops among former top-tier members who subsequently churn to competitor programmes

l4_steps.name: Capture complaint from all omni-channel sources
l4_steps.input: Customer contact via email, web form, phone, app, or social media
l4_steps.output: New case record created with source channel tag and PNR/loyalty reference
l4_steps.kpi: Case capture rate 100%; average intake time <2 min per case
l4_steps.pain_point: Fragmented channel ingestion creates duplicate cases during IROPS spikes; Sprinklr social volume can exceed 5,000 mentions/hour post-disruption, overwhelming manual deduplication

l4_steps.name: Auto-classify complaint type and urgency tier
l4_steps.input: Case text, channel, booking reference, loyalty tier flag
l4_steps.output: Complaint category tag (delay, baggage, crew, billing, accessibility), urgency tier P1–P4
l4_steps.kpi: Auto-classification accuracy ≥85%; misclassification rate <5% (validated via monthly QA sample)
l4_steps.pain_point: Multi-language free-text complaints require NLP models retrained quarterly; incorrect urgency triage causes P1 DOT-reportable cases to sit in general queue breaching 24-hour SLA

l4_steps.name: Screen for regulatory and safety escalation triggers
l4_steps.system: Salesforce Service Cloud + CAPA Tool (internal quality management)
l4_steps.input: Classified case with urgency tier
l4_steps.output: Safety flag Y/N; DOT/regulatory escalation trigger Y/N; CAPA record opened if required
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of safety-tagged cases escalated within 15 min; DOT disability/discrimination complaints acknowledged within 24 hours (Part 259 mandate)
l4_steps.pain_point: DOT Part 259 requires written response to disability and discrimination complaints within 30 days — missed SLAs expose airline to civil penalties up to $27,500 per violation per passenger

l4_steps.name: Assign case to team and set SLA clock
l4_steps.role: Case Routing Engine / Customer Care Team Lead
l4_steps.input: Complaint category, urgency tier, regulatory flag, agent availability
l4_steps.output: Case assigned to agent or specialist queue; SLA deadline set and clock started
l4_steps.kpi: First-assignment accuracy ≥92%; reassignment rate <8%; queue assignment time <5 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Staffing gaps during IROPS cause queue backlog exceeding 10x normal volume; SLA clock runs regardless of staffing levels — unmanaged queues result in mass SLA breaches during weather events

l4_steps.name: Retrieve booking and full interaction history
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS + Salesforce Service Cloud
l4_steps.input: PNR reference or loyalty number extracted from case
l4_steps.output: Full booking itinerary, prior complaint interactions, current loyalty tier status
l4_steps.kpi: History retrieval time <30 sec; data completeness ≥98% of cases with valid PNR
l4_steps.pain_point: Loyalty tier data sync between Altéa and Salesforce has a 15-min replication lag — agents may not see tier upgrades applied post-flight, causing incorrect resolution offers to premium members

l4_steps.name: Validate complaint facts against operational records
l4_steps.input: Booking history, delay codes from OCC, baggage scan log
l4_steps.output: Verified complaint facts with supporting operational evidence attached to case
l4_steps.kpi: Validation completion within 4 hours of case creation; evidence attach rate ≥95% of cases
l4_steps.pain_point: Baggage scan data in SITA WorldTracer is incomplete for interline segments handled by third-party ground handlers — evidence gaps reduce resolution quality and increase re-open rate

l4_steps.name: Code root cause category for the complaint
l4_steps.input: Verified complaint facts, operational evidence, delay reason codes
l4_steps.output: Root cause code applied (OTP failure, crew behavior, baggage mishandled, ancillary billing error, etc.)
l4_steps.kpi: Root cause coding accuracy ≥90% (validated via monthly QA review of 5% sample); uncoded case rate <2%
l4_steps.pain_point: Absence of real-time delay reason codes from OCC forces agents to use estimated codes — downstream analytics are skewed, undermining VoC programs and operational improvement targeting

l4_steps.name: Escalate complex cases to specialist team
l4_steps.role: Senior Customer Care Specialist / Legal / Safety Team
l4_steps.input: Complex case flag from root cause coding step
l4_steps.output: Case transferred to specialist queue with priority flag and investigation notes
l4_steps.kpi: Escalation acknowledgment within 2 hours; escalation rate <15% of total monthly cases
l4_steps.pain_point: Specialist queues during major IROPS reach 10x normal volume — SLA adherence for escalated cases drops below 60% during large-scale disruption events, compounding reputational damage

l4_steps.name: Determine resolution type and compensation eligibility
l4_steps.system: Salesforce Service Cloud + ATPCO Fare Rules Engine
l4_steps.input: Root cause code, customer loyalty tier, fare class, applicable regulatory entitlement (EU261, DOT)
l4_steps.output: Resolution recommendation: apology, miles award, travel voucher, cash refund, or re-accommodation
l4_steps.kpi: Resolution first-contact rate ≥65%; compensation accuracy ≥98% vs. entitlement rules
l4_steps.pain_point: EU261/2004 and DOT compensation rules differ by route and delay length — agents without automated rule-based guidance misapply entitlements, creating regulatory exposure and inconsistent customer outcomes

l4_steps.name: Post miles or issue electronic voucher compensation
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa Loyalty + Salesforce Service Cloud
l4_steps.input: Approved compensation type (miles quantity or voucher value) from step 3.1
l4_steps.output: Miles credited to loyalty account or e-voucher code issued and emailed to customer
l4_steps.kpi: Miles posting time <24 hours; voucher delivery <4 hours; posting error rate <0.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa Loyalty API throttles under post-IROPS peak load — delayed miles postings trigger a second wave of inbound contacts from customers who see no credit, effectively doubling case volume

l4_steps.name: Process cash refund via PSS and finance system
l4_steps.role: Customer Care Agent / Finance Operations Team
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS + SAP S/4HANA Finance (FI/AR)
l4_steps.input: Approved refund amount, original payment method, fare rules confirmation
l4_steps.output: Refund transaction initiated in PSS; AR credit note posted in SAP; customer confirmation sent
l4_steps.kpi: Refund processing time ≤7 business days for credit card purchases (DOT mandate); refund error rate <1%
l4_steps.pain_point: PSS-to-SAP finance integration runs nightly batch — refunds initiated late in the day risk missing the 7-day DOT credit card refund deadline, exposing the airline to enforcement action

l4_steps.name: Draft, approve, and send customer response
l4_steps.system: Salesforce Service Cloud (email template library + approval workflow)
l4_steps.input: Case facts, resolution decision, compensation confirmation
l4_steps.output: Approved response letter sent to customer via preferred channel
l4_steps.kpi: First response time ≤24 hours (P1), ≤72 hours (P2); post-response CSAT ≥4.2/5.0
l4_steps.pain_point: Single QA reviewer approving 200+ responses per day creates bottleneck — grammatical errors and inconsistent tone in templated responses damage brand perception and reduce CSAT scores

l4_steps.name: Confirm customer acceptance or re-open case
l4_steps.input: Customer reply or no-reply after 7-day post-response wait window
l4_steps.output: Case closed (accepted) or re-opened with escalation note and priority uplift
l4_steps.kpi: Re-open rate <12%; closure on first resolution ≥65%; external escalation (DOT/BBB) rate <0.5% of cases
l4_steps.pain_point: Customers escalating to DOT or BBB after case closure without prior follow-up — proactive satisfaction check within 48 hours reduces external escalation rate by approximately 30%

l4_steps.name: Log case outcome and enrich customer CRM profile
l4_steps.system: Salesforce Service Cloud + Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Closed case with full resolution details and compensation record
l4_steps.output: Updated customer interaction history; CRM profile enriched with complaint category, root cause, and resolution
l4_steps.kpi: Profile update completion rate 100%; CRM data quality score ≥95% (measured via monthly data audit)
l4_steps.pain_point: Duplicate customer profiles created from multiple booking channels (direct, OTA, GDS) result in fragmented complaint history — agents cannot see prior grievances, causing repeat-issue blind spots

l4_steps.name: Aggregate complaint data for trend analysis
l4_steps.input: Closed case export with root cause codes, compensation amounts, resolution times, and SLA outcomes
l4_steps.output: Weekly complaint trend dashboard; top-10 root cause report; SLA compliance summary
l4_steps.kpi: Dashboard refresh ≤24 hours after week close; root cause coverage ≥95% of closed cases
l4_steps.pain_point: Inconsistent root cause coding across the agent population (no mandatory controlled vocabulary enforcement) degrades analytics reliability — requires monthly recalibration training sessions to maintain ≥90% accuracy

l4_steps.name: Measure NPS and CSAT from post-resolution survey
l4_steps.input: Closed cases with valid customer email and consent flag
l4_steps.output: NPS score, CSAT score per complaint category, verbatim feedback themes
l4_steps.kpi: Survey response rate ≥15%; complaint-handling NPS ≥+30; complaint CSAT ≥4.0/5.0
l4_steps.pain_point: Survey fatigue from overlapping post-flight, post-complaint, and post-service surveys reduces response rates to <10% in high-volume periods — low sample sizes make category-level NPS statistically unreliable for operational decisions

l4_steps.name: Route VoC insights to operational improvement owners
l4_steps.role: Process Improvement Manager / VoC Program Lead
l4_steps.system: Salesforce Service Cloud + Jira (improvement backlog tracking)
l4_steps.input: Weekly trend report, NPS/CSAT data, top root causes with frequency and cost impact
l4_steps.output: Improvement action items created in Jira, assigned to owning departments (OCC, Crew, Baggage, IT); revised SLA targets where warranted
l4_steps.kpi: ≥80% of top-10 root causes have assigned improvement owner within 5 business days of report publication
l4_steps.pain_point: Customer Care produces complaint analysis but operational teams (OCC, Crew, Ground Handling) have no formal SLA to respond to VoC findings — insights-to-action loop is broken, allowing chronic root causes to persist quarter over quarter

l4_steps.name: Extract booked passenger manifest from PSS
l4_steps.input: T-96h scheduler trigger; confirmed PNR bookings
l4_steps.output: Passenger manifest with PNR, contact details, flight segments
l4_steps.kpi: Manifest extraction latency ≤15 min from trigger; data completeness ≥99.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa API rate limits during peak booking windows can delay manifest pull by 30–45 min, pushing communications outside the optimal 72h window

l4_steps.name: Enrich profiles with loyalty tier & preferences
l4_steps.input: Passenger manifest from Step 1.1; Rapid Rewards member IDs
l4_steps.output: Enriched passenger profile: loyalty tier, seat preference, meal code, language, preferred channel
l4_steps.kpi: Profile match rate ≥95% against CRM records; enrichment processing ≤10 min per 10,000 records
l4_steps.pain_point: Non-member or pseudonymous bookings via OTA channels lack Rapid Rewards linkage, resulting in generic (non-personalised) communication for ~18% of bookings

l4_steps.name: Validate communication consent & channel eligibility
l4_steps.input: Enriched passenger profiles; GDPR/CAN-SPAM opt-in records
l4_steps.output: Suppression list; approved channel map (email / SMS / push) per passenger
l4_steps.kpi: Opt-out suppression accuracy 100%; consent validation completed ≤5 min before send queue
l4_steps.pain_point: Consent records stored in multiple systems (PSS, CRM, mobile app) can be out of sync; GDPR Article 7 requires unambiguous consent — mismatch risk if unified consent hub is absent

l4_steps.name: Build personalised comms cadence schedule
l4_steps.input: Approved channel map; departure date/time per PNR
l4_steps.output: Communication schedule: T-72h, T-24h, T-4h, and day-of touchpoints per passenger
l4_steps.kpi: Schedule build time ≤20 min for full departure manifest; ≥98% of schedules created before T-72h window
l4_steps.pain_point: Multi-leg itineraries with short connections require independent cadence per leg; logic errors in connection-aware scheduling have caused duplicate or mis-timed notifications

l4_steps.name: Generate dynamic itinerary & ancillary offer content
l4_steps.input: Passenger profile; flight data (route, aircraft type, departure time, gate if assigned)
l4_steps.output: Personalised HTML/text email body; SMS template; push notification payload
l4_steps.kpi: Content personalisation token fill rate ≥99%; render error rate ≤0.1% across email clients
l4_steps.pain_point: Gate and terminal data is often unavailable at T-72h for airports operating under dynamic gate assignment (e.g., Midway MDW), forcing placeholder text that reduces perceived communication quality

l4_steps.name: Validate dynamic content against live flight data
l4_steps.input: Draft communication content; live PNR and schedule data
l4_steps.output: Validated content batch; list of records with stale data flagged for re-fetch
l4_steps.kpi: Data staleness rate ≤0.5% at send time; validation cycle ≤8 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Schedule changes filed in Altéa after content generation but before send can produce communications with incorrect departure times — requires a final data refresh check within 30 min of send

l4_steps.name: Run GDPR / CAN-SPAM compliance check on content
l4_steps.input: Validated communication content batch
l4_steps.output: Compliance-approved send batch; rejected items routed back to content team
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of sends include mandatory unsubscribe link; compliance check completion ≤5 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Transactional vs marketing classification is disputed for upsell content (e.g., ancillary offers embedded in itinerary emails); misclassification exposes airline to CAN-SPAM violation — legal review required per campaign type

l4_steps.name: Send 72h check-in invitation with OLCI link
l4_steps.input: Compliance-approved send batch; OLCI deep link from Amadeus Altéa DCS
l4_steps.output: Email / SMS / push notification delivered; delivery receipt logged
l4_steps.kpi: Email open rate ≥45%; SMS delivery rate ≥98%; OLCI click-through rate ≥35%
l4_steps.pain_point: Online check-in opens at T-24h for some fare classes (e.g., Basic Economy restrictions); sending OLCI link at T-72h for ineligible passengers creates customer confusion and misdirected contact centre calls

l4_steps.name: Deliver ancillary upsell offers — seat, baggage, lounge
l4_steps.input: Loyalty tier; current booking ancillary status from Amadeus Altéa PSS; pricing from ATPCO
l4_steps.output: Personalised offer email with real-time ancillary pricing; offer acceptance tracked in CRM
l4_steps.kpi: Ancillary revenue per communication ≥$4.50; offer acceptance rate ≥8%; unsubscribe rate ≤0.2%
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO ancillary pricing updates can lag real-time seat inventory, resulting in offers quoting prices that have since changed — requires live price validation at click-through, not at send time

l4_steps.name: Send travel readiness advisory — docs, visa, weather
l4_steps.input: Destination country; passenger nationality; IATA Travel Centre visa data; NWS / Weather API feed
l4_steps.output: Travel advisory notification including document requirements, TSA PreCheck reminder, weather summary
l4_steps.kpi: Advisory delivery ≥ T-48h before departure; advisory relevance score ≥4.2/5 in post-trip survey
l4_steps.pain_point: International routes to Mexico and Caribbean require ESTA / visa data that is sourced from IATA Travel Centre; data freshness is ±24h — incorrect requirements issued to passengers have led to denied-boarding incidents and liability claims

l4_steps.name: Confirm check-in status and deliver boarding pass
l4_steps.input: Completed OLCI session; seat assignment; SSR codes (wheelchair, UMNR, etc.)
l4_steps.output: Mobile boarding pass (PKPass / Google Wallet); check-in confirmation with seat and gate (if known)
l4_steps.kpi: Mobile boarding pass adoption rate ≥72%; boarding pass delivery latency ≤30 sec post check-in
l4_steps.pain_point: PKPass wallet integration with Altéa DCS has known compatibility gaps for codeshare itineraries — passengers on partner-operated segments occasionally receive blank boarding passes, requiring airport reprint

l4_steps.name: Monitor real-time flight status for schedule changes
l4_steps.input: Live OPS data feed from SITA AMS; ATC slot updates; weather NOTAMs via Jeppesen FliteDeck
l4_steps.output: Continuous status stream flagging delays, gate changes, cancellations per flight
l4_steps.kpi: Flight status event latency ≤2 min from OPS system to comms trigger; monitoring uptime ≥99.9%
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA AMS and Altéa PSS publish flight status updates independently; reconciliation lag between the two systems (up to 8 min) can result in duplicate or conflicting passenger notifications

l4_steps.name: Detect IROPS threshold breach and raise alert
l4_steps.input: Flight status stream from Step 4.1; IROPS threshold parameters (delay >30 min, gate change, cancellation)
l4_steps.output: IROPS event record; passenger impact list; notification trigger sent to comms platform
l4_steps.kpi: IROPS detection-to-trigger latency ≤3 min; false positive alert rate ≤1%
l4_steps.pain_point: Threshold parameters are configured statically — a 25-min delay that extends to 90 min in increments may not trigger the 30-min rule until too late, leaving passengers uninformed during the critical re-booking window

l4_steps.name: Send gate change, delay or cancellation notification
l4_steps.input: IROPS event record; passenger contact details; new gate/ETD or cancellation flag
l4_steps.output: Push/SMS/email alert delivered; delivery confirmation logged in Salesforce CRM
l4_steps.kpi: First notification delivered ≤5 min of IROPS trigger; SMS delivery rate ≥99%; passenger awareness rate ≥90% (tracked via boarding rate post-alert)
l4_steps.pain_point: Airport-side gate change displays (FIDS) and passenger SMS notifications are not synchronised — passengers often receive gate-change SMS after the FIDS has already shown the new gate, eroding trust in the notification system

l4_steps.name: Generate and deliver rebooking options for cancelled flights
l4_steps.input: Cancellation event; passenger PNR; available alternative flights; loyalty tier (for priority rebooking)
l4_steps.output: Personalised rebooking offer email/SMS with up to 3 flight alternatives; compensation voucher if applicable; self-service rebooking link
l4_steps.kpi: Rebooking offer delivered ≤10 min of cancellation confirmation; self-service rebooking rate ≥55%; contact centre deflection rate ≥40%
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa availability query during IROPS events is throttled due to simultaneous mass rebooking — alternative availability returned to passengers can be stale within 90 sec, leading to 'flight no longer available' errors at checkout and escalated call volumes

l4_steps.name: Benchmark competitor in-flight service offerings
l4_steps.input: Annual CX strategy review cycle; competitor product reports
l4_steps.output: Competitive benchmarking report with service gap analysis
l4_steps.kpi: Benchmark coverage ≥10 direct competitors; report issued within 15 working days of cycle start
l4_steps.pain_point: OAG data lacks cabin-class service detail; manual research from APEX/IFSA industry reports required, creating a 2–3 week lag in intelligence

l4_steps.name: Define cabin class service standards & sequences
l4_steps.input: Benchmarking report; brand guidelines; route profitability data from Amadeus SkyCAST
l4_steps.output: Draft cabin class service standard document (Economy / Premium Economy / Business)
l4_steps.kpi: Standards documented for 100% of cabin classes within 20 working days
l4_steps.pain_point: No dedicated service-design tooling — standards authored in Confluence with no version-controlled approval workflow, leading to unapproved drafts reaching crew training

l4_steps.name: Obtain CX board approval for service standards
l4_steps.input: Draft service standard document
l4_steps.output: Approved service standard; ServiceNow change record CR raised
l4_steps.kpi: Board approval cycle ≤10 working days; zero unapproved standards in production
l4_steps.pain_point: Multi-stakeholder approval (Inflight, Safety, Commercial, Legal) causes average 18-day delay; no SLA enforcement in ServiceNow CAB workflow

l4_steps.name: Publish service sequence manual to crew portal
l4_steps.input: Approved service standard; effective date from change record
l4_steps.output: Published service sequence manual version-controlled in FliteDeck; crew acknowledgement tracked
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of active cabin crew acknowledge new manual within 5 days of publication
l4_steps.pain_point: FliteDeck acknowledgement tracking is available for pilot documents but EFB access for cabin crew varies by aircraft type, requiring parallel paper distribution on older fleets

l4_steps.name: Design seasonal menu & beverage programme
l4_steps.input: Approved service standards; route network data; passenger dietary preference trends from Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Seasonal menu specification including SPML codes, allergen declarations, and portion specs
l4_steps.kpi: Menu refresh cycle ≤90 days; SPML coverage ≥18 dietary codes per IATA standard
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS SPML data completeness averages 62% — many passengers select meal preferences at airport rather than booking, causing last-minute galley shortfalls on long-haul sectors

l4_steps.name: Issue catering RFQ and evaluate supplier bids
l4_steps.input: Menu specification; volume forecasts from Amadeus SkyCAST; existing supplier contracts
l4_steps.output: Evaluated supplier shortlist; price per meal unit by route tier
l4_steps.kpi: RFQ response rate ≥80%; bid evaluation completed within 15 working days
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP Ariba supplier onboarding for new catering vendors averages 30 days due to food safety certification upload requirements; limits ability to switch suppliers for disrupted routes

l4_steps.name: Validate food safety and regulatory compliance
l4_steps.input: Supplier bid documentation; HACCP plans; country-specific import/export food regulations
l4_steps.output: Compliance sign-off or rejection notice per supplier; allergen matrix approved
l4_steps.kpi: Zero non-compliant meals reaching aircraft; compliance review completed ≤10 working days
l4_steps.pain_point: Vary-by-country food import regulations (e.g. USDA restrictions, EU novel food rules) cause compliance hold-ups averaging 8 days per new ingredient, delaying menu finalisation

l4_steps.name: Finalise catering contracts and upload load plans
l4_steps.system: SAP Ariba (Contract Management) + Gate Gourmet CateringIT Portal
l4_steps.input: Compliance-approved supplier shortlist; agreed pricing
l4_steps.output: Signed catering contract; galley load plans uploaded to Gate Gourmet CateringIT for route-level quantities
l4_steps.kpi: Contract executed ≥21 days before menu effective date; load plan accuracy ≥98% vs actual uplift
l4_steps.pain_point: Gate Gourmet CateringIT portal API integration with Amadeus Altéa PSS pax counts is batch-based (T-24h), not real-time — load plans cannot adjust dynamically for last-minute booking surges

l4_steps.name: Build service delivery training curriculum
l4_steps.input: Approved service sequence manual; new menu specifications; regulatory safety requirements (EASA OPS / FAR Part 121)
l4_steps.output: eLearning modules and practical assessment criteria published in Cornerstone LMS
l4_steps.kpi: Curriculum published ≥14 days before crew training cohort start; ≥90% module completion rate per cohort
l4_steps.pain_point: Cornerstone LMS integration with Jeppesen crew rostering is one-way — training completion status does not auto-block scheduling of uncertified crew, requiring manual cross-checks

l4_steps.name: Deliver in-flight service standards training to crew
l4_steps.system: Cornerstone OnDemand (LMS) + Cabin Crew Training Simulator
l4_steps.input: Training curriculum; crew roster from Jeppesen Crew Management; physical mock-up galley
l4_steps.output: Training completion records per crew member; practical simulation scores
l4_steps.kpi: Training completion ≥95% of active crew 7 days before go-live; practical assessment pass rate ≥88%
l4_steps.pain_point: Simulator availability is constrained by shared scheduling with safety/emergency training (SEP); service training often deferred to on-aircraft familiarisation flights, increasing variability

l4_steps.name: Conduct service readiness assessment and certify crew
l4_steps.system: Cornerstone OnDemand (Competency Records) + Jeppesen Crew Management
l4_steps.input: Practical assessment scores; eLearning completion certificates
l4_steps.output: Certified crew competency record; Jeppesen crew qualification flag updated
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of operating crew certified before standard go-live; re-assessment cycle ≤5 days for failures
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual update of qualification flags in Jeppesen after Cornerstone certification creates a 24–48h lag; uncertified crew can be legally rostered during the gap if not caught by manual audit

l4_steps.name: Configure galley layout and equipment specifications
l4_steps.system: AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware (MRO & Configuration Management)
l4_steps.input: Approved service standards; aircraft type galley drawings; catering load plans
l4_steps.output: Galley configuration specification per aircraft registration; AMOS configuration record updated
l4_steps.kpi: Configuration records updated for 100% of affected fleet tails ≥10 days before service go-live
l4_steps.pain_point: Fleet heterogeneity (B737-800 vs B737 MAX 8 vs B737-700 galley volumes differ by 8–12%) means single load plan cannot be applied uniformly, requiring per-subfleet configuration variants

l4_steps.name: Load galley manifest into catering management system
l4_steps.input: Per-aircraft galley configuration specs; route schedule from Amadeus SkyWORKS
l4_steps.output: Route-level galley manifest uploaded; catering uplift order generated per flight
l4_steps.kpi: Manifest upload completed ≥48h before first operated flight; uplift accuracy target ≥98%
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus SkyWORKS schedule changes (re-routes, aircraft swaps) are not automatically propagated to Gate Gourmet CateringIT — manual re-upload required within 2h of change notification to avoid mismatched uplift

l4_steps.name: Validate IFE content load and seat configuration
l4_steps.system: Panasonic Avionics eX3 Content Management System
l4_steps.input: Seasonal IFE content schedule; safety video version from Comply365; aircraft tail IFE compatibility matrix
l4_steps.output: Approved content load confirmation per tail; IFE configuration sign-off in Panasonic CMS
l4_steps.kpi: IFE content load verified on 100% of IFE-equipped tails ≥5 days before service period; zero safety video version mismatches
l4_steps.pain_point: Panasonic eX3 content load requires physical ground time per aircraft and cannot be pushed OTA to older eX1 installations; schedule compression means some tails miss the update window and carry previous season content

l4_steps.name: Execute in-flight service per approved standard
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen FliteDeck (Service Brief) + Gate Gourmet CateringIT (Manifest)
l4_steps.input: Published service sequence manual; galley manifest; pre-flight passenger count from Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Completed in-flight service; wastage and shortfall log recorded on paper/EFB
l4_steps.kpi: Service sequence adherence ≥95% per audited flights; galley shortfall rate <2% of flights
l4_steps.pain_point: No real-time digital cabin service tracking — adherence is measured through periodic audits only (sample <5% of flights), creating a large blind spot between audit cycles

l4_steps.name: Capture post-flight NPS and CSAT feedback
l4_steps.input: Completed flight; passenger email list from Amadeus Altéa PSS; post-flight survey trigger
l4_steps.output: NPS score and verbatim feedback per flight/route segment in Medallia dashboard
l4_steps.kpi: Survey response rate ≥18%; NPS target ≥45 for short-haul; ≥55 for long-haul
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS email suppression rules (opt-out, GDPR, corporate booking via Sabre GDS without passenger email) reduce survey reach by ~35%, skewing NPS samples toward direct-channel passengers

l4_steps.name: Analyse service performance metrics and complaints
l4_steps.system: Power BI (Connected to Medallia + ServiceNow + Altéa Data Warehouse)
l4_steps.input: Medallia NPS/CSAT data; ServiceNow complaint tickets; galley shortfall logs; audit scores
l4_steps.output: Monthly in-flight service performance dashboard; top 5 issue categories ranked by frequency and NPS impact
l4_steps.kpi: Dashboard published within 5 working days of month-end; complaint resolution rate ≥90% within SLA
l4_steps.pain_point: Medallia, ServiceNow, and Altéa data are held in separate systems with no automated ETL pipeline; Power BI refresh depends on manual CSV exports from Medallia, introducing 2–3 day data staleness

l4_steps.name: Identify root cause and implement service improvements
l4_steps.input: Performance dashboard; root cause analysis report; benchmarking data
l4_steps.output: Approved service improvement change record; updated service standard version in Confluence; re-entry to Step 1.2 if standard revision required
l4_steps.kpi: Root cause identified within 10 working days of threshold breach; improvement implemented within 30 days of approval
l4_steps.pain_point: Continuous improvement cycle lacks a formal feedback loop into Cornerstone LMS — identified training gaps require manual curriculum update requests, averaging 6-week lag before crew retraining is delivered

l4_steps.name: Identify post-flight survey eligible pax
l4_steps.input: Flight departure confirmation and boarded pax manifest
l4_steps.output: Eligible passenger list with contact metadata
l4_steps.kpi: Eligible pax coverage ≥ 95% of boarded passengers
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa passenger records may have missing or stale email addresses when bookings originate from OTA channels without email pass-through, reducing survey reach by up to 20%

l4_steps.name: Validate opt-in status and contact data
l4_steps.input: Eligible passenger list from Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Suppression list (opted-out / invalid email) and validated send list
l4_steps.kpi: Suppression accuracy 100% — zero survey sends to opted-out contacts
l4_steps.pain_point: GDPR and CCPA compliance requires real-time suppression list sync between Altéa loyalty database and Salesforce Marketing Cloud; sync lag of >4 hours risks regulatory breach

l4_steps.name: Generate personalised survey link and dispatch
l4_steps.input: Validated send list with flight metadata (route, cabin class, flight number)
l4_steps.output: Personalised survey email sent within 24 hours of flight arrival
l4_steps.kpi: Survey dispatch latency ≤ 24 hours post-arrival; email deliverability ≥ 97%
l4_steps.pain_point: Qualtrics dynamic survey personalisation requires clean flight-level metadata from Altéa; missing cabin class data causes generic survey routing, degrading response quality for premium cabin feedback

l4_steps.name: Monitor survey response rate by flight cohort
l4_steps.input: Dispatch log and response ingestion feed
l4_steps.output: Real-time response rate dashboard per flight/route
l4_steps.kpi: Target survey response rate ≥ 20%; industry benchmark ~15–18%
l4_steps.pain_point: Response rates on short-haul routes (<90 min) are structurally lower (8–12%) due to rapid passenger disengagement post-flight; blended NPS may over-index on long-haul sentiment

l4_steps.name: Send reminder to non-responders at 48 hours
l4_steps.input: Non-response flag from Qualtrics XM at 48-hour mark
l4_steps.output: Single reminder email dispatched to eligible non-responders
l4_steps.kpi: Reminder lift in response rate ≥ 5 percentage points; max 1 reminder per passenger
l4_steps.pain_point: Over-surveying risk: passengers who received a complaint follow-up (CX-05) or loyalty communication (CX-01) within the same 72-hour window must be suppressed from reminder sends to avoid fatigue and NPS score inflation

l4_steps.name: Validate response completeness and ingest to analytics
l4_steps.input: Raw survey responses from Qualtrics XM export
l4_steps.output: Cleaned response dataset loaded to AWS S3 data lake
l4_steps.kpi: Partial response exclusion rate ≤ 5% of total submissions; ingestion latency ≤ 1 hour
l4_steps.pain_point: Qualtrics partial completion records (pax abandoned mid-survey) can corrupt NPS scoring if included; no native auto-exclusion rule in Qualtrics XM without custom workflow configuration

l4_steps.name: Classify respondents as Promoter, Passive, or Detractor
l4_steps.input: Validated 0–10 NPS responses from AWS S3
l4_steps.output: Classified respondent list: Promoters (9–10), Passives (7–8), Detractors (0–6)
l4_steps.kpi: NPS score = (% Promoters − % Detractors); target airline industry NPS ≥ 40
l4_steps.pain_point: Qualtrics NPS calculation runs at batch rather than real-time; daily NPS score may lag 12–18 hours behind actual flight completions during peak travel periods, delaying detractor recovery initiation

l4_steps.name: Perform text analytics on verbatim comments
l4_steps.input: Open-text survey responses classified by NPS segment
l4_steps.output: Themed sentiment clusters: e.g. boarding, crew, catering, IFE, baggage
l4_steps.kpi: Auto-classification accuracy ≥ 85% vs. manual coding sample; ≤ 10% uncategorised verbatims
l4_steps.pain_point: Qualtrics Text iQ topic models require periodic retraining as language patterns evolve; stale models misclassify emerging complaint themes (e.g. NDC booking friction) into legacy categories, masking new failure drivers

l4_steps.name: Flag detractor responses and route to recovery queue
l4_steps.input: Detractor records (NPS 0–6) with verbatim themes from Qualtrics XM
l4_steps.output: Service cases created in Salesforce Service Cloud with priority tier based on score severity
l4_steps.kpi: Detractor case creation latency ≤ 4 hours from survey submission; 100% of NPS 0–3 cases created same day
l4_steps.pain_point: Qualtrics-to-Salesforce webhook integration requires stable API keys and payload schema alignment; schema drift after Qualtrics XM or Salesforce release upgrades has caused dropped detractor cases in production

l4_steps.name: Correlate NPS scores with operational performance data
l4_steps.input: NPS dataset from AWS S3 joined with OTP, delay codes, load factor from Amadeus Altéa
l4_steps.output: Correlation matrix: NPS vs. OTP, delay duration, cabin load, crew staffing
l4_steps.kpi: Correlation analysis refresh cycle ≤ 24 hours; cover ≥ 90% of surveyed flights with ops data join
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa operational data (delay codes, actual arrival times) and Qualtrics survey responses use different flight key structures (Altéa uses PNR/flight leg ID; Qualtrics uses survey metadata); cross-system join requires a maintained flight key mapping table that breaks on schedule changes

l4_steps.name: Identify systemic failure drivers and escalate
l4_steps.input: Correlation matrix and themed verbatim clusters from AWS Redshift
