l4_steps.name: Ingest weather and ATC flow constraint data
l4_steps.input: METARs, TAFs, SIGMETs, FAA TFMS/SWIM Ground Delay Programs
l4_steps.output: Weather impact overlay on network map; GDP-affected flight list
l4_steps.kpi: Weather advisory ingestion latency ≤5 min from SIGMET issue
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA TFMS GDP notifications arrive via multiple channels (NAS Status, SWIM API, phone) with no single consolidated feed — manual reconciliation required

l4_steps.name: Assess airport capacity and slot utilisation
l4_steps.input: Airport slot allocations, gate availability, ground handler capacity
l4_steps.output: Slot utilisation report; gate conflict alerts
l4_steps.kpi: Gate conflict identification ≥30 min before scheduled pushback
l4_steps.pain_point: At slot-controlled airports (LHR, JFK), late slot returns trigger IATA WASG 80:20 use-it-or-lose-it penalties — NOC must balance recovery options against slot forfeiture risk

l4_steps.name: Detect operational deviation and trigger disruption alert
l4_steps.input: Automated threshold breach: delay >15 min, ATC hold, maintenance release flag
l4_steps.output: Disruption alert ticket with affected flight list and estimated downstream cascade
l4_steps.kpi: Alert-to-triage response time ≤10 min for Severity 1 events
l4_steps.pain_point: Cairo AI cascade modelling accuracy degrades when multiple simultaneous disruptions interact — controller must validate AI-generated impact scores manually for compounding events

l4_steps.name: Classify disruption severity and operational scope
l4_steps.input: Disruption alert ticket; affected flight count; estimated delay propagation
l4_steps.output: Severity classification (S1 Network Crisis / S2 Station Event / S3 Single Flight)
l4_steps.kpi: Correct severity classification rate ≥95% vs post-event review
l4_steps.pain_point: No standardised severity matrix shared between NOC, Crew Scheduling, and Maintenance Control — classification disagreements delay activation of the correct recovery protocol

l4_steps.name: Model downstream cascade impact on network
l4_steps.input: Disruption origin flight; rotational aircraft tail assignments; crew pairings
l4_steps.output: Cascade impact map: N flights affected, estimated total delay minutes, PAX count at risk
l4_steps.kpi: Cascade model produced within 5 min of S1/S2 alert; PAX-at-risk count accuracy ±5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Aircraft tail swap history held in Jeppesen Crew and SITA AMS separately — reconciling rotational conflicts across systems requires manual data export and is error-prone at speed

l4_steps.name: Escalate network-wide crisis to senior NOC leadership
l4_steps.input: S1 severity classification; cascade impact map
l4_steps.output: Crisis bridge call initiated; senior leadership (VP Operations, VP Maintenance) notified; war room convened
l4_steps.kpi: Senior leadership notified within 15 min of S1 classification
l4_steps.pain_point: Airline-specific: post-Dec 2022 IROPS crisis, several carriers lack documented escalation runbooks — NOC managers default to ad hoc phone calls, creating coordination gaps during high-stress events

l4_steps.name: Identify available spare aircraft for recovery
l4_steps.input: Current fleet status board; maintenance release schedule; spare aircraft positions
l4_steps.output: Candidate spare aircraft list with position, range capability, and availability window
l4_steps.kpi: Spare aircraft identified within 20 min of disruption classification for S1/S2 events
l4_steps.pain_point: Unscheduled AOG maintenance removes spare aircraft without real-time update to NOC fleet board — controllers discover unavailability only when attempting to assign tail, causing recovery plan rework

l4_steps.name: Model and score recovery scenario options
l4_steps.input: Spare aircraft list; delay propagation model; crew availability matrix
l4_steps.output: Ranked recovery scenarios with cost, delay, and PAX-impact scores
l4_steps.kpi: ≥3 recovery scenarios generated per S1/S2 event; scenario scoring completed within 10 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Cairo AI optimisation is constrained by static crew legality rules embedded at implementation — dynamic FAR Part 117 duty time calculations for mixed international/domestic pairings require manual override by Crew Scheduling

l4_steps.name: Evaluate crew duty legality for recovery assignments
l4_steps.input: Proposed recovery flight assignments; crew current duty start times and rest records
l4_steps.output: Legal/illegal flag per crew pairing; compliant alternatives where required
l4_steps.kpi: Zero FAR Part 117 duty-time violations in executed recovery plan; crew legality check completed within 15 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen legality engine checks planned duties but cannot pre-validate real-time operator-initiated tail swaps — illegal assignments may only surface at sign-in, causing last-minute scrambles

l4_steps.name: Select and approve final recovery plan
l4_steps.input: Scored recovery scenarios; crew legality validation; cost approval authority
l4_steps.output: Approved recovery plan with assigned tail numbers, crew, and revised schedule
l4_steps.kpi: Recovery plan approved and published within 30 min of S1 disruption onset
l4_steps.pain_point: Financial authority thresholds for ferry flights and hotel costs are not pre-delegated to NOC duty managers — approvals requiring VP sign-off during off-peak hours introduce 30–60 min delays

l4_steps.name: Issue crew reassignment instructions to Crew Scheduling
l4_steps.input: Approved recovery plan; reserve crew roster; current crew positions
l4_steps.output: Crew reassignment notifications sent via CrewTrac; updated pairing records
l4_steps.kpi: Crew contact-and-confirm cycle completed within 20 min; reserve activation rate ≥90% first contact
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew contactability drops during off-hours — contactability SLA is not contractually mandated beyond 2-hour reserve callout window, limiting rapid IROPS response capability

l4_steps.name: Coordinate aircraft maintenance release with MCC
l4_steps.input: Recovery aircraft tail number; open deferred defects (DD) list; MEL status
l4_steps.output: Maintenance release confirmation or deferred defect deferral decision
l4_steps.kpi: Aircraft release decision issued within 30 min of MCC request for non-AOG aircraft
l4_steps.pain_point: MEL deferral decisions on borderline items require OEM (Boeing) consultation — Boeing's 24/7 technical operations line response time can reach 60+ min for complex MEL calls, blocking aircraft release

l4_steps.name: Issue gate changes and ground resource reallocation
l4_steps.input: Revised aircraft routing; gate availability; ground handler and fuelling schedules
l4_steps.output: Gate reassignment notices; revised ground service orders to handlers
l4_steps.kpi: Ground resources confirmed at revised gate ≥45 min before revised departure
l4_steps.pain_point: At contracted-handler airports, gate change notifications must be transmitted via SITA messaging — handlers operating legacy systems acknowledge with 15–30 min lag, preventing NOC from confirming readiness

l4_steps.name: Update revised schedule and flight status in Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Approved recovery plan; revised departure times; aircraft and crew assignments
l4_steps.output: Updated flight records in Altéa DCS; GDS flight status broadcast via SITA Type B messages
l4_steps.kpi: Schedule update published to GDS within 10 min of plan approval; zero discrepancies between Altéa and SITA AMS flight status
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual rescheduling in Altéa for >10 flights simultaneously requires sequential data entry — bulk SSIM import is available but requires IT ops involvement, creating a bottleneck during mass IROPS events

l4_steps.name: Trigger automated passenger rebooking workflow
l4_steps.input: Cancelled/significantly delayed flights; passenger itinerary records; rebooking rules policy
l4_steps.output: Automated rebooking confirmations sent to affected PAX via email/SMS; waitlist cleared
l4_steps.kpi: ≥85% of disrupted PAX rebooked within 2 hours of cancellation; EU261/DOT delay notification compliance 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa automated rebooking applies FIFO logic that ignores high-value loyalty tier passengers — premium PAX may be rebooked on worse itineraries than low-tier PAX unless NDC/API rules override is manually triggered

l4_steps.name: Monitor recovery execution and track plan adherence
l4_steps.input: Real-time departure/arrival feeds; crew sign-in confirmations; maintenance release updates
l4_steps.output: Recovery tracking dashboard; variance alerts when execution deviates >15 min from plan
l4_steps.kpi: Recovery plan adherence ≥80% of revised departure times met within ±15 min; total network delay minutes reduced ≥40% vs no-action baseline
l4_steps.pain_point: No unified real-time recovery adherence score exists — NOC manager must manually correlate Altéa flight status, Jeppesen crew sign-ins, and SITA AMS gate data to determine if recovery is on track

l4_steps.name: Document NOC event log and decision audit trail
l4_steps.input: Chronological decision log; communications record; final recovery outcomes
l4_steps.output: Closed NOC event ticket with full audit trail; regulatory documentation for DOT/CAA if required
l4_steps.kpi: Event documentation completed within 4 hours of network recovery; 100% of S1 events produce a formal After-Action Report
l4_steps.pain_point: Decision rationale during fast-moving IROPS is rarely captured in real time — post-event reconstruction from chat logs and ACARS data is time-consuming and incomplete, undermining root cause analysis

l4_steps.name: Monitor flight status vs published schedule
l4_steps.input: Real-time gate departure feeds, OPS messages, ACARS pushback events
l4_steps.output: Live flight status dashboard with variance-from-schedule flag
l4_steps.kpi: On-time departure (D0) ≥78%; delay detection latency <2 min of STD
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS position reports lag by 90–120 sec on older aircraft, masking initial delay onset until gate hold is already confirmed

l4_steps.name: Apply IATA delay threshold trigger rule
l4_steps.input: Actual vs scheduled departure time delta from AMS feed
l4_steps.output: Delay event record opened in Altéa OC with severity tier (Minor <15 min / Moderate 15–60 min / Severe >60 min)
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of delays ≥15 min captured within 3 min of threshold breach
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa OC severity tiers are configurable per airline but default thresholds may not align with local slot-loss rules at congested airports such as LHR or JFK

l4_steps.name: Assign IATA AHM 730 delay code to event
l4_steps.input: Initial cause report from handling agent, crew, or ATC
l4_steps.output: Primary IATA two-digit delay code + sub-code entered in Altéa OC event record
l4_steps.kpi: Delay code accuracy rate ≥94% (validated at post-ops audit); code entry within 10 min of ETD revision
l4_steps.pain_point: Controllers under workload pressure default to code 93 (unknown) or airline-internal codes; post-ops correction consumes analyst time and distorts monthly reporting

l4_steps.name: Map downstream flight propagation impact
l4_steps.input: Delay event record from Altéa OC; rotational aircraft tail number; planned schedule SSIM
l4_steps.output: Propagation impact list — all subsequent flights on same tail affected with estimated knock-on delay per flight
l4_steps.kpi: Propagation analysis completed within 5 min of delay event creation; ≥95% of knock-on delays correctly identified
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyWORKS propagation engine requires manual tail-number linkage for ad-hoc swaps executed earlier in the day; stale tail assignments cause phantom impact estimates

l4_steps.name: Check crew duty time legality under FAR Part 117
l4_steps.input: Crew pairing records, revised ETD/ETA, accumulated flight duty period (FDP) totals
l4_steps.output: Crew legality status per affected flight: Legal / At-limit / Illegal flag with exact remaining FDP minutes
l4_steps.kpi: Zero FAR Part 117 exceedances; crew illegality flag generated within 3 min of delay event propagation
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen CMS and Altéa OC use separate crew-to-flight linkage tables; sync latency of up to 8 min means early illegality flags can appear after the aircraft has already pushed

l4_steps.name: Identify passenger misconnection risk
l4_steps.input: Passenger booking itineraries with MCT data; revised inbound ETA; connecting flight boarding-complete times
l4_steps.output: At-risk passenger list with booking reference, connection flight, and protection options (next available / hotel voucher eligible)
l4_steps.kpi: Misconnect identification completed before inbound landing (≥30 min ahead); protected reaccommodation rate ≥88% same-day
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa DCS minimum connect time (MCT) tables require manual update when airports revise terminal layouts; outdated MCTs cause under- or over-protection triggering either rebooking churn or missed misconnects

l4_steps.name: Assess whether delay qualifies for EC 261 compensation
l4_steps.input: Delay magnitude; origin/destination country pair; delay cause classification (extraordinary vs controllable)
l4_steps.output: EC 261 / DOT eligibility flag per affected booking; duty-of-care obligations triggered (meal voucher, hotel, rebooking rights)
l4_steps.kpi: EC 261 eligibility flag applied within 5 min of 3-hour delay threshold; 100% of entitled passengers notified before next boarding call
l4_steps.pain_point: Extraordinary-circumstances exemption (weather, ATC) requires documented evidence within 72 hours; NOC controllers rarely capture contemporaneous ATC restriction references, leading to claims upheld in arbitration

l4_steps.name: Generate recovery options — swap, absorb, or cancel
l4_steps.input: Propagation impact list; available spare aircraft inventory; crew availability matrix from Jeppesen CMS
l4_steps.output: Ranked recovery scenario list with estimated schedule recovery time (SRT) and cost-of-delay score per option
l4_steps.kpi: ≥3 ranked scenarios generated within 10 min of escalation trigger; SRT ≤45 min for Moderate tier delays
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyWORKS recovery workspace does not natively score scenarios by total cost-of-delay; controllers rely on manual mental arithmetic, leading to suboptimal aircraft swaps that increase crew costs

l4_steps.name: Evaluate aircraft swap feasibility in SkyMAX
l4_steps.input: Candidate spare aircraft; required range and seat configuration; next-maintenance-due date from AMOS
l4_steps.output: Feasibility verdict: Swap approved / blocked (maintenance hold, wrong config, insufficient range) with reason code
l4_steps.kpi: Aircraft swap evaluation completed within 8 min; maintenance-hold conflicts identified before physical repositioning begins
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyMAX queries AMOS maintenance status via batch API with up to 15-min lag; a maintenance task opened in AMOS after the last sync can result in an illegal swap being physically initiated at the gate

l4_steps.name: Coordinate revised gate and slot with airport ops
l4_steps.system: SITA Airport Management System (AMS) + IATA SLOT coordination message (SSR/SIR)
l4_steps.input: Revised ETD; new aircraft tail; gate resource availability from AMS; slot window from airport coordinator
l4_steps.output: Confirmed gate assignment and revised slot time acknowledged by airport; updated in Altéa OC
l4_steps.kpi: Gate confirmation received ≥30 min before revised ETD; slot revision accepted at slot-controlled airports within IATA SSIM Chapter 8 tolerance window
l4_steps.pain_point: At slot-coordinated airports (Level 3), missing the 15-min retiming window forfeits the slot and forces a new slot request; Altéa OC does not automatically alert the controller when the retiming window is about to expire

l4_steps.name: Approve and lock recovery plan
l4_steps.input: Ranked recovery scenarios; crew legality confirmation from Jeppesen CMS; gate confirmation from AMS
l4_steps.output: Approved recovery plan locked in Altéa OC; task assignments dispatched to ground handling, crew, and ramp teams
l4_steps.kpi: Recovery plan approved and communicated ≥25 min before revised ETD; 0% plan revisions after lock (lock discipline metric)
l4_steps.pain_point: NOC duty managers sometimes approve a plan before crew confirmations are fully resolved, requiring a second re-plan cycle that extends the delay by an additional 20–35 min

l4_steps.name: Broadcast revised ETD to all operational stakeholders
l4_steps.system: SITA ACARS + Telex; Amadeus Altéa OC automated notification
l4_steps.input: Approved recovery plan with locked revised ETD; stakeholder distribution list (crew, ramp, catering, fuelling, ATC)
l4_steps.output: ACARS ETD revision uplink to cockpit; AMS gate board update; SMS/email alerts to ground handlers
l4_steps.kpi: ETD update reaches all stakeholders within 2 min of plan lock; 100% of downstream flights updated in Altéa OC within 5 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Catering and fuelling vendors receive notifications via separate legacy email/fax channels, not through AMS or Altéa; revision propagation to these vendors averages 12 min, risking late catering delivery that re-extends the delay

l4_steps.name: Monitor recovery execution against revised milestones
l4_steps.input: Recovery plan milestones (boarding-complete, doors-close, pushback); real-time gate event feeds
l4_steps.output: Milestone adherence scorecard updated in real time; red flag alert if any milestone slips by >5 min
l4_steps.kpi: Pushback within 3 min of revised ETD for ≥80% of recovery flights; milestone slip detection latency <90 sec
l4_steps.pain_point: AMS milestone tracking relies on manual scan events at gates with intermittent handheld scanner connectivity; at remote stands, missing scan events create false 'on-track' status until ACARS pushback message arrives

l4_steps.name: Close recovery loop and update schedule actuals
l4_steps.input: ACARS airborne message (ATD); gate actual out/off events; confirmed delay duration
l4_steps.output: Delay event record closed in Altéa OC with actual block times; downstream schedule actuals updated; SSIM actual file entry created
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of closed delay events have IATA delay code confirmed within 30 min of ATD; actual block time accuracy ±1 min vs ACARS
l4_steps.pain_point: Controllers frequently forget to close delay events after pushback under high workload; open events accumulate in Altéa OC, inflating active-delay counts and distorting NOC dashboard metrics

l4_steps.name: Aggregate delay evidence and system event logs
l4_steps.system: AWS S3 / Amazon Redshift (Operations Data Lake)
l4_steps.input: Altéa OC event records; AMS gate logs; ACARS messages; Jeppesen crew duty records; weather METAR/SIGMET archive
l4_steps.output: Consolidated delay evidence package in Redshift: one row per delay event with all contributing data sources joined
l4_steps.kpi: Evidence package assembled within 24 hours of flight ops; data completeness ≥97% (all events have linked ACARS record)
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS message archive retention policy varies by data source; some third-party handling agents purge logs after 72 hours, making post-hoc evidence reconstruction impossible for disputes filed after that window

l4_steps.name: Attribute delay causes per IATA AHM 780 methodology
l4_steps.system: Tableau (connected to Redshift delay evidence layer)
l4_steps.input: Consolidated evidence package; IATA AHM 780 attribution rules; airline-defined delay ownership matrix
l4_steps.output: Final delay attribution record: primary cause code, contributing cause codes, responsible department/vendor, accountable cost estimate
l4_steps.kpi: Attribution accuracy ≥94% (audited quarterly by Quality); attribution completed within 48 hours of event for all Severe-tier delays
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA AHM 780 assigns single-cause attribution, but most airline delays are multi-causal; forcing a single code obscures systemic issues (e.g. late catering masked as ATC when both contributed) and skews corrective action priorities

l4_steps.name: Detect systemic delay patterns across rolling 30-day window
l4_steps.input: 30-day delay attribution dataset from Redshift; threshold rules (≥3 events same root cause = systemic flag)
l4_steps.output: Systemic pattern alert: cause code, frequency, affected routes/aircraft type, responsible team, trend direction
l4_steps.kpi: Systemic patterns identified within 5 business days of 3rd occurrence; false-positive pattern rate <10%
l4_steps.pain_point: Pattern detection thresholds are set manually and rarely reviewed; low thresholds generate alert fatigue (managers ignore flags), while high thresholds allow systemic issues to accumulate for 6–8 weeks before escalation

l4_steps.name: Publish delay performance report to operations leadership
l4_steps.input: Final attribution records; systemic pattern alerts; benchmarks (OAG industry OTP data; IATA Annual Review)
l4_steps.output: Weekly delay report: OTP vs target, top-5 delay codes, cost-of-delay by category, systemic patterns open/closed, trend vs prior 4 weeks
l4_steps.kpi: Report published by 08:00 Monday; OTP data currency within 12 hours of end of reporting week
l4_steps.pain_point: Delay cost estimates in the report use average cost-per-minute assumptions (typically €80–100/min CODA benchmark) rather than actual cost data; finance does not integrate actual incremental cost from SAP FI in time for the weekly cycle

l4_steps.name: Submit delay cost attribution to Finance for accrual
l4_steps.system: SAP S/4HANA Finance (FI-CO) — Cost Centre Accounting
l4_steps.input: Final delay attribution records with responsible department; estimated cost-of-delay by category (crew, ground handling, passenger compensation, fuel burn)
l4_steps.output: Cost centre journal entries in SAP FI; EC 261 compensation accrual posted; month-end delay cost reconciliation file
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of Severe-tier delay costs accrued in SAP FI within 5 business days of event; variance between estimated and actual delay cost <15%
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP FI cost centre structure does not granularly distinguish catering vendor delays from ground handler delays; both post to generic 'Ground Services' cost centre, preventing targeted vendor SLA penalty enforcement

l4_steps.name: Monitor real-time ACARS & ACMS flight alerts
l4_steps.input: Continuous ACARS datalink messages, ACMS fault codes, crew SELCAL calls
l4_steps.output: Confirmed irregularity event record in NOC operations log
l4_steps.kpi: Alert acknowledgement within 2 minutes of ACARS receipt; 100% alert capture rate
l4_steps.pain_point: High ACARS message volume creates noise; controllers must distinguish genuine emergencies from routine fault codes without cockpit confirmation — risk of delayed response during shift handover

l4_steps.name: Classify emergency type and severity level
l4_steps.input: ACARS alert, pilot voice report via Telex/SITA ACARS or VHF relay, flight plan data
l4_steps.output: Emergency classification (Medical / Mechanical / Weather / Security / Other) and severity (Level 1–3) logged in OCC system
l4_steps.kpi: Classification completed within 5 minutes of initial alert; misclassification rate <1%
l4_steps.pain_point: Ambiguous early reports from cockpit force controllers to act on incomplete information; multi-type events (e.g. medical + mechanical) may be misclassified, delaying correct response track

l4_steps.name: Determine if full emergency declaration is required
l4_steps.input: Emergency classification, aircraft type performance limits, crew request
l4_steps.output: Go / No-Go decision for emergency declaration; Emergency Response Plan activation trigger
l4_steps.kpi: Decision latency <3 minutes from classification; 0 missed full-emergency escalations
l4_steps.pain_point: Ambiguity in Level 2 events where crew has not declared Mayday/Pan-Pan; NOC may under-declare to avoid costly ARFF standby fees, creating liability exposure if situation worsens

l4_steps.name: Identify candidate diversion airports and performance data
l4_steps.input: Aircraft current position, fuel state, emergency type, weather METARs/TAFs
l4_steps.output: Ranked list of suitable alternate airports with runway performance calculations and estimated fuel on arrival
l4_steps.kpi: Alternate identification completed within 5 minutes; fuel calculation accuracy ±50 kg
l4_steps.pain_point: Real-time runway contamination and NOTAM status not always reflected immediately in NAVBLUE; stale NOTAMs risk selecting an airport with active runway closure

l4_steps.name: Evaluate diversion airport suitability and slot availability
l4_steps.input: Candidate airport list, aircraft MTOW, runway length/PCN data, weather forecasts, slot constraints
l4_steps.output: Approved diversion airport with confirmed runway compatibility, available ground services, and weather minima
l4_steps.kpi: Evaluation complete within 4 minutes; 100% runway compatibility verified before recommendation
l4_steps.pain_point: Coordinated airports (Level 3) require slot approval that cannot be obtained in real-time during emergency — dispatcher must accept non-compliance risk and coordinate retroactively with slot coordinator

l4_steps.name: Confirm diversion decision and alternate airport selection
l4_steps.input: Dispatcher recommendation, fuel state, medical urgency (if applicable), crew preference
l4_steps.output: Confirmed diversion instruction logged in OCC; crew notified via ACARS and voice
l4_steps.kpi: Diversion instruction transmitted to crew within 10 minutes of initial alert; 0 diversions to airports with insufficient runway performance
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew and NOC may disagree on preferred alternate; without clear authority hierarchy in SOPs this creates delay — particularly when crew has elected an airport not on the approved alternate list

l4_steps.name: Coordinate ATC diversion clearance via datalink
l4_steps.input: Confirmed diversion airport, squawk code (7700/7600/7500), current ATC sector
l4_steps.output: ATC diversion clearance received; amended flight plan filed; OOOI update transmitted
l4_steps.kpi: ATC clearance obtained within 3 minutes of diversion decision; 100% amended flight plan filed within 5 minutes
l4_steps.pain_point: In non-radar oceanic airspace or remote FIRs, HF voice communication is required instead of datalink — significantly increasing coordination time and controller workload

l4_steps.name: Activate Emergency Response Plan and notify ERT
l4_steps.input: Confirmed emergency declaration, incident classification, ERP checklist
l4_steps.output: Emergency Response Team assembled; checklist activated; notification log initiated
l4_steps.kpi: ERP activation within 5 minutes of emergency declaration; 100% of required ERT contacts notified within 10 minutes
l4_steps.pain_point: ERP contact trees rely on manual phone call cascades — if primary contacts are unavailable during off-hours, escalation path is unclear and notification time degrades significantly

l4_steps.name: Alert ARFF, medical, and emergency services at diversion airport
l4_steps.input: Confirmed diversion airport, flight number, aircraft type, number of passengers, nature of emergency
l4_steps.output: ARFF category confirmed; medical standby ordered; airport operations alerted; AMS event record created
l4_steps.kpi: Diversion airport notified within 5 minutes of diversion decision; ARFF on standby confirmed ≥15 minutes before estimated landing
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA AMS interface with some regional airports is limited to telex-only — automated notification fails and NOC must resort to direct phone calls, introducing manual error and delay

l4_steps.name: Determine if hospital transfer or specialist medical support needed
l4_steps.input: Cabin crew medical report via ACARS, MedLink or equivalent in-flight medical advisory service output
l4_steps.output: EMS / ambulance request confirmed or waived; hospital pre-notification triggered if required
l4_steps.kpi: Medical severity determination within 5 minutes of crew report; EMS request placed ≥20 minutes before landing for Level 1 medical events
l4_steps.pain_point: In-flight medical advisories (e.g. MedLink) are contracted by airline but cabin crew may not initiate contact in time; late escalation reduces hospital preparation time and increases patient risk

l4_steps.name: Notify regulatory authorities per emergency event type
l4_steps.input: Emergency type, squawk code used, aircraft registration, event timeline
l4_steps.output: FAA ATC notification confirmed; NTSB/AAIB preliminary notification filed if required; airline safety officer looped in
l4_steps.kpi: Regulatory notification completed within 30 minutes of event; 100% compliance with ICAO Annex 13 / FAR Part 830 reporting timelines
l4_steps.pain_point: International diversions trigger multi-authority notification requirements (local CAA, ICAO state of registry, ICAO state of operator) — manual tracking in OCC frequently results in missed or delayed filings

l4_steps.name: Reserve gate, parking, and coordinate ground handling at diversion airport
l4_steps.input: Aircraft type, estimated arrival time, passenger count, special handling requirements
l4_steps.output: Gate or remote stand assigned; ground handling agent notified; fuel order placed if required; PRM assistance requested
l4_steps.kpi: Ground handling confirmation received ≥20 minutes before estimated landing; 100% PRM passengers pre-identified and notified to handler
l4_steps.pain_point: At outstations with no contracted ground handler, NOC must arrange ad-hoc handling at premium cost with unpredictable service levels — especially critical for widebody or heavy aircraft at small airports

l4_steps.name: Arrange immediate passenger care and amenity provision
l4_steps.input: Passenger manifest, diversion airport facilities, estimated delay duration, special needs passengers flagged
l4_steps.output: Passenger care plan activated (meals, accommodation vouchers, transport); unaccompanied minor and MEDA passengers prioritised
l4_steps.kpi: Passenger care plan communicated to diversion station within 30 minutes of landing; vouchers issued within 1 hour per EC261/DOT consumer protection requirements
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS does not automatically flag all MEDA passengers to diversion station — manual cross-check of Special Services Requests is required, creating risk of missed care for vulnerable passengers

l4_steps.name: Assess whether passengers can continue on diverted aircraft
l4_steps.input: Aircraft technical status, crew remaining duty time, fuel state, ATC slot availability, estimated delay
l4_steps.output: Go / No-Go decision to continue flight on same aircraft; if No-Go, recovery plan initiated
l4_steps.kpi: Continue / cancel decision communicated to passengers within 45 minutes of landing; 0 illegal crew departures approved
l4_steps.pain_point: Pressure from station managers and passengers to resume quickly can bias NOC toward premature Go decision before maintenance and crew legality checks are complete

l4_steps.name: Rebook affected passengers on next available services
l4_steps.input: Passenger manifest, destination, next available flight inventory, interline agreements
l4_steps.output: Rebooking confirmations issued; PNR updated; boarding passes reissued; IROPS waiver applied
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of affected passengers rebooked within 2 hours of diversion landing; involuntary reroute documented for EU261/DOT compensation tracking
l4_steps.pain_point: Disrupted inventory during IROPS means preferred rebooking flights are often sold out; interline rebooking on partner carriers requires manual ticketing if NDC agreements are not in place

l4_steps.name: Verify crew duty time legality for continued or return operations
l4_steps.input: Crew sign-on times, actual block hours flown, rest requirements under FAR Part 117 / EASA FTL
l4_steps.output: Crew legality assessment report; approved continuation or rest requirement logged
l4_steps.kpi: Legality check completed within 30 minutes of diversion landing; 0 regulatory FTL violations incurred
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen Crew Management may not have real-time position updates for diverted crew if ACARS OOOI data is delayed — manual reconciliation required, increasing error risk under time pressure

l4_steps.name: Source and position relief crew if original crew is illegal
l4_steps.input: Crew illegality flag, diversion airport location, reserve crew availability, positioning options
l4_steps.output: Relief crew identified and travel confirmed; estimated time to diversion airport logged in OCC
l4_steps.kpi: Relief crew identified within 1 hour of illegality determination; positioning confirmed within 2 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Reserve crew availability at outstations is typically zero — positioning from base requires commercial travel or ferry flight, leading to delays of 4–12 hours and potential AOG at diversion airport

l4_steps.name: Assess aircraft airworthiness and coordinate maintenance release
l4_steps.input: ACMS fault data, MEL/CDL checks, maintenance release requirements at diversion airport
l4_steps.output: Aircraft serviceability determination; maintenance work order raised if defect found; Return-to-Service sign-off or AOG declared
l4_steps.kpi: Initial airworthiness assessment within 60 minutes of landing; AMOS work order raised within 15 minutes of defect confirmation
l4_steps.pain_point: Diversion airports rarely have the airline's contracted MRO present — sourcing an approved Part 145 maintenance organisation at short notice is costly and time-consuming, frequently resulting in AOG delays exceeding 24 hours

l4_steps.name: Submit incident report and complete post-event regulatory filings
l4_steps.input: Full event timeline, ATC comms log, crew statements, maintenance findings, passenger impact data
l4_steps.output: Internal incident report filed; mandatory regulatory reports submitted (FAA MOR, ASIAS, ICAO occurrence report); lessons-learned triggered
l4_steps.kpi: Internal report completed within 24 hours; FAA Mandatory Occurrence Report filed within 72 hours per FAR Part 830; 100% of required attachments included
l4_steps.pain_point: Post-event reporting relies on manual assembly of data from multiple systems (ACARS logs, AMS, Jeppesen, AMOS) with no automated aggregation — data gaps and inconsistencies frequently require follow-up with multiple departments, delaying final filing

l4_steps.name: Verify ETOPS route approval in OpSpecs
l4_steps.input: Planned route, aircraft registration, OpSpec C057 reference
l4_steps.output: ETOPS route authorization confirmed; approved diversion time threshold recorded
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of ETOPS-routed flights pre-validated against OpSpecs before release
l4_steps.pain_point: OpSpec revisions under FAR 121.161 / ICAO Doc 10085 require 30-day authority lead time; last-minute network re-routing post-approval is operationally prohibited and forces costly re-planning

l4_steps.name: Confirm aircraft ETOPS certification level
l4_steps.input: Aircraft registration, current maintenance release status
l4_steps.output: ETOPS certification level confirmed (e.g. 120 / 180 / 240 min) and recorded against flight
l4_steps.kpi: Zero ETOPS departures without valid airworthiness certificate and ETOPS approval on record
l4_steps.pain_point: ETOPS certification can be suspended mid-rotation due to maintenance findings; AMOS aircraft status must be queried in real time — stale cache data in dispatch systems has caused near-misses on ETOPS eligibility checks

l4_steps.name: Retrieve ETOPS alternate airport weather forecasts
l4_steps.input: Planned ETOPS alternate list, estimated departure time, flight duration
l4_steps.output: TAF and METAR reports for all alternates within ETOPS diversion circle
l4_steps.kpi: Weather data currency ≤1 hour before departure; TAF coverage ≥18 hours ahead of ETP crossing
l4_steps.pain_point: Remote oceanic alternates (e.g., NFFN Nadi, PGUM Guam, BIKF Keflavik) have sparse observation networks; TAF accuracy degrades beyond 12 hours, leaving critical ETP windows with low-confidence forecasts

l4_steps.name: Validate ETOPS alternate airport operational status
l4_steps.input: Alternate airport list, current NOTAM bulletins, AIP supplements
l4_steps.output: Alternate availability confirmed, or replacement alternate identified and approved
l4_steps.kpi: 100% alternate validation completed ≥2 hours before scheduled departure
l4_steps.pain_point: NOTAM closure of a primary alternate (e.g., runway works at Honolulu's divert field) forces complete replanning; NOTAM parsing tools remain largely manual, and auto-filtering tools miss complex conditional NOTAMs issued by some Pacific island states

l4_steps.name: Calculate Equal Time Point and Point of No Return
l4_steps.input: Approved route, winds aloft model, alternate coordinates, single-engine cruise speed profile
l4_steps.output: ETP and PNR coordinates, fuel checkpoint waypoints, go/no-go decision gates embedded in OFP
l4_steps.kpi: ETP calculation within ±2 nm of independent manual cross-check; PNR fuel state verified against aircraft performance tables
l4_steps.pain_point: NAVBLUE wind model integration updates every 6 hours; stale wind data on long trans-oceanic sectors (>14 hr block) can shift ETP by up to 40 nm, materially affecting alternate fuel requirements and crew decision windows

l4_steps.name: Review ETOPS significant systems maintenance status
l4_steps.input: Aircraft tech log, ETOPS significant systems check sheet, MEL Part B (ETOPS items)
l4_steps.output: ETOPS airworthiness assessment: all significant systems serviceable or MEL-permissible deferred
l4_steps.kpi: ETOPS maintenance check completed ≥90 min before scheduled departure; zero open ETOPS-critical MEL items at release
l4_steps.pain_point: ETOPS MEL (Minimum Equipment List) items differ substantively from standard MEL — APU, dual hydraulics, FADEC, SATCOM, and fire suppression must all be assessed against ETOPS-specific criteria; staff confusion on MMEL Part B boundaries generates repeated compliance queries and delays

l4_steps.name: Obtain dual maintenance and operations ETOPS release
l4_steps.input: Completed tech log, ETOPS significant systems sign-off sheet, dispatcher release
l4_steps.output: Dual-signed ETOPS flight release stamped in aircraft tech log and ops system
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of ETOPS flights have both maintenance certification and dispatcher release before pushback
l4_steps.pain_point: Paper tech log workflows at outstations create risk of missing or illegible ETOPS-specific entries; digital tech log adoption is incomplete, and remote stations lack AMOS real-time connectivity, causing release delays of 20–45 min

l4_steps.name: Calculate ETOPS fuel requirements
l4_steps.input: ETP coordinates, alternate distances, holding requirements, single-engine fuel burn curves, ETOPS contingency rule (FAR 121 Appendix P / ICAO Annex 6)
l4_steps.output: ETOPS fuel plan: trip fuel + ETOPS reserve + contingency fuel + alternate fuel + final reserve
l4_steps.kpi: ETOPS fuel uplift within ±2% of planned quantity; zero short-fuel departures
l4_steps.pain_point: ETOPS fuel requirements stack on top of standard dispatch reserves; on maximum-range sectors the cumulative fuel obligation can impose a 3–5 tonne payload penalty, directly reducing revenue yield on high-demand routes

l4_steps.name: Validate ETOPS fuel load against MTOW constraints
l4_steps.system: NAVBLUE Flight Planning / Amadeus Altéa DCS
l4_steps.input: ETOPS fuel plan, passenger count, cargo manifest, zero-fuel weight
l4_steps.output: Approved fuel load with weight-and-balance confirmation; payload trim decision if required
l4_steps.kpi: Zero overweight departures; fuel optimised within 500 kg of minimum legal ETOPS load
l4_steps.pain_point: On peak summer rotations, ETOPS fuel combined with full passenger payload frequently pushes narrow-body aircraft to MTOW; payload trimming displaces revenue passengers and triggers downstream compensation and rebooking costs

l4_steps.name: File ETOPS-annotated ATC flight plan via AFTN
l4_steps.input: Approved ETOPS fuel plan, route with ETP waypoints, alternate airports
l4_steps.output: ATC flight plan filed with ETOPS notation in ICAO Item 18 TBE field; ACK confirmation received
l4_steps.kpi: Flight plan filed and acknowledged ≥60 min before scheduled departure; zero unacknowledged plans at departure
l4_steps.pain_point: ICAO Item 18 TBE (ETOPS) field is not consistently parsed by all regional ATC automation systems; Pacific RVSM and North Atlantic Track coordination require secondary manual validation with Shanwick / Oakland Oceanic, adding 15–30 min to filing cycle

l4_steps.name: Monitor ETOPS significant systems via ACARS / SATCOM
l4_steps.input: In-flight ACARS position reports, engine health data (EHM), crew SATCOM check-ins
l4_steps.output: Real-time ETOPS systems status log; alert flags raised for any significant system degradation
l4_steps.kpi: ACARS position report receipt ≤15 min intervals on oceanic tracks; 100% engine health message coverage
l4_steps.pain_point: HF radio dependency in ACARS dead zones (South Pacific, polar routes beyond SATCOM footprint) creates monitoring gaps of 30–60 min; aircraft without Swift Broadband (SBB) upgrade rely on VHF-only ACARS, which drops out on oceanic tracks

l4_steps.name: Update ETOPS alternate weather at ETP crossings
l4_steps.input: Inflight position reports, ETP waypoint schedule, updated TAF / SIGMET bulletins
l4_steps.output: Go / No-Go weather assessment for each alternate at projected ETP crossing time
l4_steps.kpi: Weather reassessment delivered to flight crew ≤30 min before each ETP; 100% ETP coverage on all ETOPS sectors
l4_steps.pain_point: Rapidly developing convective weather at oceanic alternates (e.g., Bermuda in Atlantic hurricane season, Midway Atoll in typhoon season) can invalidate ETOPS release post-departure; regulatory requirement to notify crew and assess divert feasibility creates a compressed decision window once the PNR is passed

l4_steps.name: Assess engine or system anomaly for divert decision
l4_steps.input: Engine health alerts, ECAM / EICAS messages reported via SATCOM, crew deviation report
l4_steps.output: Divert decision (continue to destination or proceed to ETOPS alternate); amended routing filed with ATC
l4_steps.kpi: Divert decision communicated within ≤15 min of anomaly detection; ATC re-clearance obtained within ≤20 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Dual authority model (dispatcher + PIC) under FAR 121 for ETOPS divert decisions creates communication latency; SATCOM voice quality on older long-haul narrow-body fleets is often insufficient for complex technical discussions, forcing dispatcher to rely on ACARS text exchange with limited bandwidth

l4_steps.name: Complete ETOPS post-flight operational report
l4_steps.system: AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware / Airline OpsControl
l4_steps.input: Flight data recorder summary, ACARS message logs, crew debrief notes, maintenance findings
l4_steps.output: ETOPS post-flight report compliant with FAR 121.374 / ICAO Doc 10085 Appendix; filed in ops system
l4_steps.kpi: Report filed within 24 hours of landing; 100% compliance rate on regulatory audit cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual aggregation of ACARS logs, crew debrief, and maintenance notes creates a 4–6 hour compilation burden per ETOPS flight; no automated data ingestion pipeline exists in most legacy ops platforms, making timely filing dependent on individual dispatcher diligence

l4_steps.name: Update ETOPS reliability programme and IFSD database
l4_steps.system: AMOS / Aviation Safety Action Programme (ASAP) Portal
l4_steps.input: ETOPS post-flight report, in-flight significant system events, maintenance findings, IFSD occurrences
l4_steps.output: Updated ETOPS reliability metrics report; IFSD rate trend; corrective action initiated if threshold exceeded
l4_steps.kpi: In-Flight Shutdown (IFSD) rate ≤0.02 per 1,000 engine hours (ETOPS-180 regulatory threshold); reliability report issued within 30 days of each reporting period
l4_steps.pain_point: IFSD rate trending requires cross-fleet data aggregation over a 12-month minimum window; smaller operators and new ETOPS entrants fall below the statistical significance threshold required by authorities for self-approval, creating dependency on OEM data sharing and authority-imposed restrictions

l4_steps.name: Crew sign-in and duty period validation
l4_steps.input: Scheduled report time, crew roster assignment
l4_steps.output: Validated duty start time, confirmed crew pairing
l4_steps.kpi: Sign-in completion ≥30 min prior to departure; FTL compliance 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 117 / EASA FTL limits require real-time cumulative duty tracking across time zones — late roster updates in Jeppesen Crew Management can create compliance gaps at sign-in

l4_steps.name: Validate fatigue risk and FTL compliance
l4_steps.input: Cumulative flight hours, rest period log, duty start time
l4_steps.output: FTL compliance confirmation or crew relief trigger
l4_steps.kpi: FTL violation rate <0.1% of monthly departures
l4_steps.pain_point: Fatigue Risk Management System (FRMS) data is not always integrated with real-time crew tracking; manual overrides by Crew Scheduling introduce compliance risk during IROPS

l4_steps.name: Retrieve and open crew briefing package
l4_steps.input: Flight number, date, departure station
l4_steps.output: Loaded briefing package: flight plan, weather, NOTAMs, ATIS
l4_steps.kpi: Briefing package retrieval within 2 min of sign-in; package currency ≤60 min old at review
l4_steps.pain_point: EFB synchronisation delays on congested airport Wi-Fi (especially at hub gates) can result in crews accessing stale briefing data — no automatic staleness alert in FliteDeck

l4_steps.name: Review METAR, TAF, and SIGMET reports
l4_steps.input: Current METAR, TAF for departure/en-route/destination, SIGMETs
l4_steps.output: Crew weather assessment and ceiling/visibility minima check
l4_steps.kpi: Weather briefing completed ≥20 min before STD; 100% SIGMET acknowledgement logged
l4_steps.pain_point: Rapidly evolving convective SIGMETs issued by NOAA Aviation Weather Center can be uploaded to GoDirect with 10–15 min latency — crew may depart with outdated convective picture

l4_steps.name: Assess destination and alternate minima
l4_steps.input: Terminal aerodrome forecasts, instrument approach plate minima, airline OpSpecs
l4_steps.output: Alternate airport selection and additional fuel requirement
l4_steps.kpi: Correct alternate selected per ICAO Annex 2 / FAR 121.619; fuel-to-alternate margin ≥45 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Low-visibility operations (Cat II/III) require special OpSpecs approval in FAA WebOPSS; not all airports in the network have current CAT II/III plates loaded in FliteDeck for all aircraft types

l4_steps.name: Confirm weather acceptable for planned departure
l4_steps.input: Weather assessment, crew minimums, operational limits
l4_steps.output: Go / No-Go weather decision; delay or reroute request if no-go
l4_steps.kpi: Weather-related departure decision communicated to OCC ≥15 min before STD
l4_steps.pain_point: Dispatcher and Captain may reach independent weather conclusions using different data sources (GoDirect vs airline wx feed) with no reconciliation workflow — leads to coordination delays at the gate

l4_steps.name: Review computerised flight plan and fuel load
l4_steps.input: Filed ATC flight plan, optimised route, fuel figures from Dispatch
l4_steps.output: Reviewed flight plan with crew acknowledgement
l4_steps.kpi: Flight plan review complete ≥15 min before STD; fuel uplift variance ≤2% vs planned
l4_steps.pain_point: NAVBLUE flight plan generation relies on current NOTAM and airspace restriction feeds; late TFR activations (military, VIP) can invalidate the planned route after the plan has been generated but before crew signs off

l4_steps.name: Review dispatch release for regulatory compliance
l4_steps.input: Dispatch release document, OpSpecs authorisations, fuel release
l4_steps.output: Crew review annotation; list of queries for Dispatcher
l4_steps.kpi: Dispatch release co-sign rate without amendment ≥92%; amendment resolution time ≤10 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Dispatch releases generated in NAVBLUE are not dynamically linked to MEL deferral records in Boeing Toolbox — Captain must manually cross-check deferred items against the release, increasing error risk under time pressure

l4_steps.name: Co-sign dispatch release with Dispatcher
l4_steps.input: Reviewed and agreed dispatch release
l4_steps.output: Dual-signed dispatch release (FAR 121.663 joint responsibility established)
l4_steps.kpi: Dispatch release signed ≥10 min before STD; 100% digital co-signature audit trail
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR 121.663 requires both Captain and Dispatcher to hold the release jointly — paper-based release at remote stations without NAVBLUE access creates audit trail gaps and scan-to-file delays

l4_steps.name: Review NOTAM package for departure and en-route
l4_steps.input: NOTAM filter output for departure airport, en-route waypoints, destination
l4_steps.output: Annotated NOTAM list; crew awareness of active restrictions
l4_steps.kpi: NOTAM review complete prior to departure; safety-critical NOTAMs (runway closures, ILS unserviceable) flagged 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: NOTAM volume has increased >300% since 2010 (FAA data); FliteDeck's automated filtering still surfaces 80–120 NOTAMs per flight, creating information overload and risk that critical items are missed

l4_steps.name: Review MEL and CDL deferred item list
l4_steps.input: Aircraft tail number, active MEL/CDL deferrals, maintenance logbook
l4_steps.output: Crew acceptance or rejection of aircraft with deferred items
l4_steps.kpi: MEL review completion rate 100% prior to boarding; deferral-related delays <0.5% of departures
l4_steps.pain_point: MEL records in Boeing Toolbox are updated by Maintenance Control but real-time sync to crew EFB (FliteDeck) is not guaranteed — crews may board an aircraft unaware of a late deferral logged after their briefing

l4_steps.name: Confirm airworthiness release from Maintenance
l4_steps.input: Signed aircraft logbook, maintenance release certificate
l4_steps.output: Airworthiness confirmed; aircraft released for service
l4_steps.kpi: Maintenance release issued ≥45 min before STD; 100% release traceability in AMOS
l4_steps.pain_point: Maintenance release signature workflows in AMOS require LMB engineer to physically sign the tech log — at outstations without AMOS connectivity, paper tech logs create a digitisation lag and potential duplicate entry errors

l4_steps.name: Conduct pre-flight exterior walk-around
l4_steps.input: Completed maintenance release, pre-flight checklist
l4_steps.output: Completed exterior inspection record; any defects raised
l4_steps.kpi: Walk-around completed ≥30 min before STD; defect-to-report time ≤5 min
l4_steps.pain_point: FliteDeck EFB walk-around checklists are not connected to AMOS defect recording — items found during walk-around must be re-entered manually in the aircraft tech log, creating duplication and potential omission

l4_steps.name: Confirm final weight & balance load sheet
l4_steps.input: Final passenger count, cargo weights, fuel load, trim settings
l4_steps.output: Signed load sheet; CG within envelope confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: Load sheet issued ≤15 min before STD; CG deviation from plan <0.5% MAC
l4_steps.pain_point: Last-minute passenger no-shows or late cargo add-ons require load sheet recalculation in Altéa — under the 10-min gate departure pressure window, rushed W&B recalculations increase the risk of CG errors

l4_steps.name: Obtain ATC clearance and departure slot
l4_steps.input: Filed flight plan, ATIS, ATFM slot allocation
l4_steps.output: ATC route clearance; CTOT confirmed or delay calculated
l4_steps.kpi: Clearance received ≥5 min before pushback; ATFM slot adherence ≥94%
l4_steps.pain_point: ATFM slot allocations from EUROCONTROL NMOC (or FAA EDCT in North America) are issued dynamically and can shift within the last 10 min — ACARS delivery to cockpit adds latency vs. VHF voice clearance, risking slot miss

l4_steps.name: Trigger wireless QAR data offload at gate
l4_steps.input: Aircraft weight-on-wheels signal; gate docking confirmation
l4_steps.output: Raw QAR binary file transferred to FOQA ground server
l4_steps.kpi: Offload completion within 10 min of gate arrival; flight coverage rate ≥99%
l4_steps.pain_point: WiFi connectivity gaps at remote apron stands force manual USB retrieval, adding 4–6 hr to processing queue and delaying same-day exceedance review

l4_steps.name: Validate data frame completeness and CRC integrity
l4_steps.input: Raw QAR binary file from Step 1.1
l4_steps.output: Validated flight data file or data gap report
l4_steps.kpi: Data completeness ≥98% of flight duration; frame error rate <0.1%
l4_steps.pain_point: Pre-2010 QAR units use proprietary frame formats requiring manual decoding — adds up to 2 hr per flight to the processing queue and delays exceedance detection

l4_steps.name: Ingest supplemental ACARS performance snapshots
l4_steps.input: Data gap notification from Step 1.2 or routine ACARS push
l4_steps.output: ACARS performance dataframes merged into consolidated flight record
l4_steps.kpi: ACARS data merge success rate ≥95%; gap-fill latency <30 min
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS snapshot frequency (every 10–30 min) is too coarse to reconstruct fine-grained exceedance events; oceanic airspace has no ACARS coverage, leaving gap-fill as an estimate only

l4_steps.name: Execute automated exceedance detection run
l4_steps.input: Validated and merged flight data file from Phase 1
l4_steps.output: Exceedance event list with parameter name, recorded value, threshold, and timestamp
l4_steps.kpi: Detection run completion <30 min per flight; false positive rate <5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Threshold libraries require manual calibration per aircraft type variant (e.g., 737-800 vs MAX 8 have different structural limits); miscalibration generates false positives that erode crew confidence in the FOQA programme

l4_steps.name: Classify exceedances by severity Cat A/B/C
l4_steps.input: Exceedance event list from Step 2.1
l4_steps.output: Classified exceedance report (Cat A = flight safety, Cat B = airworthiness, Cat C = crew technique)
l4_steps.kpi: Classification accuracy ≥97%; all Cat A events reviewed within 24 hr of detection
l4_steps.pain_point: IOSA audit and airline AQP programme use different category boundary definitions — maintaining dual threshold tables increases configuration error risk and complicates audit trail documentation

l4_steps.name: Escalate Cat A exceedance to Flight Safety
l4_steps.input: Cat A exceedance classification from Step 2.2
l4_steps.output: Safety investigation record opened; NOC and crew scheduling notified
l4_steps.kpi: Cat A notification delivered to Flight Safety Manager <2 hr of detection
l4_steps.pain_point: Integration between Safety Line FOQA and Intelex SMS is typically manual (CSV export/import), introducing notification latency that risks breaching 24-hour internal reporting SLAs and downstream regulatory filing windows

l4_steps.name: Extract engine performance parameters post-flight
l4_steps.input: Completed flight leg identifier; aircraft tail number
l4_steps.output: EGT margin, N1 deviation, fuel flow, vibration, and oil pressure time series per engine
l4_steps.kpi: Parameter extraction completeness ≥99.5%; processing latency <15 min post-landing
l4_steps.pain_point: GoDirect data feed latency for long-haul international operations can exceed 1 hr post-landing due to satellite link congestion, delaying trend detection for time-sensitive engine health events

l4_steps.name: Compare engine trends against MRO baseline
l4_steps.input: Engine parameter time series from Step 3.1; fleet engine health baseline in AMOS
l4_steps.output: Engine health trend report; deviation flags relative to fleet statistical baseline
l4_steps.kpi: EGT margin loss ≤1°C per flight cycle; alerts triggered at ±3σ deviation from fleet mean
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS engine baselines require manual update after each shop visit — stale baselines mask post-maintenance performance degradation and delay early warning detection of incipient failures

l4_steps.name: Raise maintenance alert for engine trend deviation
l4_steps.input: Deviation flag exceeding ±3σ threshold from Step 3.2
l4_steps.output: Corrective work order raised; borescope inspection scheduled against next available ground time
l4_steps.kpi: Maintenance alert actioned within 4 hr of detection; on-wing unplanned engine removal rate <0.05 per 1,000 flight hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Tight aircraft utilisation (≥13 hr/day on narrowbody fleets) means borescope inspections are routinely deferred due to limited ground time, allowing early-stage engine degradation to progress to AOG events

l4_steps.name: Cross-reference event with ATC and meteorological records
l4_steps.input: Flagged exceedance event from Phase 2; flight leg metadata
l4_steps.output: Contextualised event report overlaying ATC radar track, METAR/SIGMET, and PIREP data
l4_steps.kpi: Contextualisation report completed within 48 hr of event detection
l4_steps.pain_point: ATC radar data access requires a formal request to the relevant ANSP in most regions, with turnaround of 3–10 business days — delays investigation timelines and risks crew debriefing weeks after the event

l4_steps.name: Conduct de-identified ASAP crew debrief
l4_steps.input: Contextualised event report from Step 4.1; crew roster for the flight
l4_steps.output: Crew disclosure statement; event narrative; de-identified ASAP safety report
l4_steps.kpi: ASAP debrief completed within 72 hr of event detection; crew voluntary disclosure rate ≥80%
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew participation in ASAP is undermined in organisations with punitive safety cultures; legal protections for voluntary disclosures vary by jurisdiction, limiting debrief effectiveness for international crew members

l4_steps.name: Route finding to training or close investigation
l4_steps.input: Debrief outcome and root cause classification from Step 4.2
l4_steps.output: Training referral issued to LMS, or closed investigation record with corrective recommendations
l4_steps.kpi: Corrective action closure within 30 days; recurrence rate for same event type <5% within 12 months
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated integration between Intelex SMS and airline LMS platforms — manual training referral process results in tracking gaps, unverifiable completion, and repeat exceedances from the same crew pairing

l4_steps.name: Publish monthly FOQA performance dashboard
l4_steps.input: Aggregated exceedance data and KPI metrics exported from Safety Line FOQA
l4_steps.output: FOQA monthly report; fleet-level performance dashboard published to safety portal
l4_steps.kpi: Dashboard published by 5th calendar day of each month; ≥12 FOQA KPIs tracked and trended
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual data export pipeline from Safety Line FOQA to Tableau breaks with each platform version upgrade — dashboard reconciliation consumes 3–4 hr/month of analyst time on non-value-adding data plumbing

l4_steps.name: Evaluate event against mandatory SDR reporting threshold
l4_steps.input: Completed investigation record; regulatory threshold matrix (FAR 121.703, IOSA ISM)
l4_steps.output: Regulatory reporting decision memo (SDR required Y/N; ASAP report required Y/N)
l4_steps.kpi: Mandatory reporting decisions documented within 48 hr of investigation close
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR 121.703 SDR thresholds are ambiguous for software-defined exceedances such as FMS autoflight anomalies — each case requires legal review, delaying time-sensitive filings and creating regulatory exposure

l4_steps.name: Submit SDR or ASAP report to FAA
l4_steps.input: Reporting decision memo and closed investigation record from Step 5.2
l4_steps.output: Filed SDR or ASAP report; FAA confirmation number recorded in SMS
l4_steps.kpi: SDR submitted within 96 hr of discovery per FAR 121.703; ASAP report submitted within 24 hr of event
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA DrAFT portal experiences 2–3 unplanned outages per year — no automated failover submission path means airlines risk missing mandatory filing deadlines and face potential enforcement action

l4_steps.name: Archive FDR and QAR data per FAR 91.609 retention policy
l4_steps.input: Validated FDR/QAR files, investigation records, and all associated reports
l4_steps.output: Archived data objects with retention metadata tags; automated deletion schedule per regulation
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of FDR/QAR files archived within 24 hr of processing completion; retention period ≥25 hr (FDR per FAR 91.609), ≥2 yr (QAR programme data)
l4_steps.pain_point: AWS S3 lifecycle policy misconfiguration has caused premature deletion of QAR data at multiple carriers — audit trail gaps expose the airline to FAA enforcement action and inability to reconstruct accident sequences

l4_steps.name: Load ACARS datalink frequencies for planned route
l4_steps.input: Filed flight plan with route and frequency plan
l4_steps.output: ACARS datalink profile loaded for flight
l4_steps.kpi: Datalink configuration complete ≥15 min before departure
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS frequency gaps over oceanic or remote continental segments require fallback to HF voice, increasing dispatcher workload by 40%

l4_steps.name: Assign and verify SELCAL code for aircraft
l4_steps.input: Aircraft tail number, route segment with HF requirement
l4_steps.output: Confirmed SELCAL code entered in flight plan and crew briefing
l4_steps.kpi: SELCAL assignment accuracy 100%; no duplicate codes per sector
l4_steps.pain_point: SELCAL code conflicts across shared fleet pools cause missed ATC calls; manual cross-check process has no automated deconfliction in legacy ACARS ground system

l4_steps.name: Test ACARS uplink connectivity with Operations Control
l4_steps.input: Aircraft powered-on ACARS avionics, OCC datalink server status
l4_steps.output: Two-way ACARS test message acknowledged; link quality confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: Uplink test round-trip <90 seconds; link quality ≥95% message delivery
l4_steps.pain_point: Gate-to-aircraft ACARS connectivity failures affect ~3% of departures; ground crew must physically confirm avionics status with no automated alert to dispatch

l4_steps.name: Activate voice backup if ACARS uplink fails
l4_steps.input: Failed ACARS uplink test result
l4_steps.output: VHF Company frequency and phone patch number issued to crew; failure logged
l4_steps.kpi: Voice backup activation within 5 min of confirmed datalink failure
l4_steps.pain_point: Voice backup coordination relies on manual frequency lookups; no integrated fallback workflow in dispatch system creates inconsistent crew briefing quality

l4_steps.name: Transmit OUT and OFF OOOI messages via ACARS
l4_steps.input: Aircraft door close and wheels-off events from FMS
l4_steps.output: OUT/OFF timestamps transmitted to OCC and airline operations system
l4_steps.kpi: OOOI transmission latency <30 seconds of triggering event; 99.5% capture rate
l4_steps.pain_point: Automatic OOOI triggering depends on door-closure sensor accuracy; carrier-specific wiring faults on ageing narrowbodies cause delayed or missed OUT messages, distorting OTP metrics

l4_steps.name: Send initial position report and fuel state to dispatch
l4_steps.input: Departure fuel uplift, FMS waypoint sequence, ATC initial clearance
l4_steps.output: Position report with fuel on board (FOB) and cleared altitude uplinked to OCC
l4_steps.kpi: Initial report transmitted within 10 min of wheels-off
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual crew entry of FOB in FliteDeck creates transcription errors; no automated FMS-to-ACARS fuel bridge in older EFB configurations

l4_steps.name: Evaluate departure delay or route amendment requirement
l4_steps.input: ATC slot allocation, departure ATIS, updated SIGMET/AIRMET data
l4_steps.output: Decision: standard departure confirmed or amended clearance required
l4_steps.kpi: Route amendment decision issued ≥5 min before off-block when ATC delay >15 min
l4_steps.pain_point: ATC ground delay programmes (GDPs) issued with <10 min notice require simultaneous reroute and crew notification; NAVBLUE slot management tool lacks real-time GDP ingestion from FAA TFMS

l4_steps.name: Uplink revised route clearance or holding instructions
l4_steps.input: ATC revised clearance or GDP holding instruction
l4_steps.output: Amended route or holding fix uplinked and crew-acknowledged via ACARS CPDLC
l4_steps.kpi: Crew acknowledgement received within 3 min of uplink; amendment compliance 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: CPDLC message formatting errors between airline system and FAA FANS-1/A avionics create rejected uplinks requiring voice re-confirmation, adding 4–8 min average delay

l4_steps.name: Monitor automated ACARS position reports en-route
l4_steps.input: FMS periodic position reports (10–30 min intervals per route type)
l4_steps.output: Real-time flight track displayed in OCC; anomalies flagged for dispatcher review
l4_steps.kpi: Position report receipt interval ≤30 min; missed report alert within 5 min of overdue
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS position reporting gaps over North Atlantic and Pacific oceanic tracks require manual ADS-C polling; latency up to 15 min leaves dispatch with stale situational awareness

l4_steps.name: Process and acknowledge dispatch uplink messages
l4_steps.input: Weather updates, NOTAM amendments, fuel revised calculations from dispatch
l4_steps.output: Crew acknowledgement sent; updated parameters loaded in FMS as required
l4_steps.kpi: Uplink acknowledgement within 5 min for operational messages; 100% receipt confirmation
l4_steps.pain_point: High-volume uplink queues during irregular operations (IRROPs) overload crew attention; no message priority ranking in FliteDeck causes safety-critical messages to queue behind routine updates

l4_steps.name: Execute HF radio handoff for oceanic or remote operations
l4_steps.input: Oceanic entry waypoint, assigned HF frequencies from route briefing
l4_steps.output: HF contact established with Oceanic ATC or ARINC/SITA HF network
l4_steps.kpi: HF contact established within 10 min of oceanic FIR entry; first-call success rate ≥90%
l4_steps.pain_point: HF propagation variability in high-latitude routes (NAT track system) causes failed initial contacts; airlines without SATCOM-equipped fleets have no reliable backup, risking SLOP deviation reporting failures

l4_steps.name: Assess weather deviation or emergency communication need
l4_steps.input: PIREPs, SIGMET updates, crew request for deviation or emergency declaration
l4_steps.output: Decision: routine ops continue OR deviation/emergency coordination initiated
l4_steps.kpi: Dispatcher response to crew deviation request <2 min; emergency acknowledgement <1 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Weather deviation requests during oceanic segments require simultaneous ATC and OCC coordination over SATCOM and ACARS; latency in SATCOM voice degrades timely clearance issuance

l4_steps.name: Coordinate weather deviation or emergency with ATC and OCC
l4_steps.input: Crew deviation request, SIGMET polygon, alternate routing from NAVBLUE
l4_steps.output: ATC deviation clearance relayed to crew; OCC fuel and alternate analysis completed
l4_steps.kpi: Deviation clearance loop closed (crew request → ATC clearance → crew confirmation) <15 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Multi-party coordination chain (crew → dispatch → ATC → dispatch → crew) has no single-system view; handoffs via separate ACARS and voice systems create documentation gaps for post-event safety review

l4_steps.name: Receive and acknowledge D-ATIS update via datalink
l4_steps.input: Destination airport D-ATIS broadcast (IATA code, ATIS identifier letter)
l4_steps.output: Current ATIS letter confirmed in crew acknowledgement; approach brief updated
l4_steps.kpi: D-ATIS received ≥30 min before destination ETA; ATIS currency check at top of descent
l4_steps.pain_point: Airports without D-ATIS capability require VHF voice ATIS, adding crew workload; ATIS letter change between receipt and landing causes approach briefing invalidation with no automated crew alert

l4_steps.name: Transmit final ETA and fuel state to dispatch and OCC
l4_steps.input: FMS top-of-descent calculations, current FOB, ATC ETA slot
l4_steps.output: ETA and FOB report uplinked; OCC arrival planning triggered
l4_steps.kpi: ETA accuracy ±3 min versus actual on-blocks; fuel state report within 1 min of TOD
l4_steps.pain_point: FMS ETA drift in RVSM/RNP environments caused by ATC tactical vectoring is not automatically pushed to ACARS; dispatcher uses stale ETA for gate planning, causing downstream turnaround delays

l4_steps.name: Confirm destination availability with dispatch
l4_steps.input: Destination NOTAMs, RVR, field condition report, ATC ATIS status
l4_steps.output: Decision: destination available for landing OR diversion to alternate required
l4_steps.kpi: Go/no-go decision for destination communicated to crew ≥20 min before ETA
l4_steps.pain_point: NAVBLUE NOTAM integration does not ingest real-time runway contamination SNOWTAM data; dispatchers must manually cross-check ATIS and ATC PIREPs, creating decision latency in winter operations

l4_steps.name: Coordinate diversion to alternate airport if required
l4_steps.input: Diversion trigger (weather, NOTAM, fuel state), alternate airport list from flight plan
l4_steps.output: Alternate airport confirmed; revised routing, fuel check, and crew notification completed
l4_steps.kpi: Alternate airport decision and crew uplink <5 min of diversion trigger; fuel sufficient for alternate + 30 min holding confirmed
l4_steps.pain_point: Alternate airport ATIS and gate availability data not integrated in NAVBLUE; dispatcher must manually contact destination OCC and alternate airport ops, adding 8–12 min to diversion coordination loop

l4_steps.name: Download and archive ACARS message logs post-flight
l4_steps.input: Full ACARS message thread for completed flight (uplinks and downlinks)
l4_steps.output: Archived communications log stored in data lake; indexed by flight ID and date
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of ACARS logs archived within 2 hours of on-blocks; retention period ≥24 months per ICAO Annex 6
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA ACARS ground system purges raw message buffers after 72 hours; airlines without automated archive pipelines lose communications audit trails required for accident investigation and FAA inspection

l4_steps.name: Review post-flight communications for anomalies or gaps
l4_steps.input: Archived ACARS log, OOOI timestamps, dispatcher notes from flight
l4_steps.output: Anomaly report or clean-flight confirmation; flagged items routed for investigation
l4_steps.kpi: Post-flight communications review completed within 24 hours of arrival; anomaly detection rate ≥95% vs manual audit
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated anomaly detection across ACARS and voice logs; analysts manually cross-reference two separate systems, limiting review throughput to ~30 flights/analyst/day

l4_steps.name: File ATC communications deviation or irregularity report
l4_steps.input: Anomaly flag from post-flight review, dispatcher event notes
l4_steps.output: Mandatory irregularity report filed; safety management system (SMS) notification sent
l4_steps.kpi: Deviation report filed within 48 hours of event per FAR Part 121.711; 100% compliance with ASAP/ASRS voluntary reporting where applicable
l4_steps.pain_point: Dispatcher irregularity reporting workflow is disconnected from ACARS archive system; manual re-entry of message evidence into SMS creates transcription errors and delays in safety trend analysis

l4_steps.name: Receive Shipper DG Declaration & Air Waybill
l4_steps.input: Shipper's Declaration for Dangerous Goods (IATA DGR Sec 8.1.6 format), Air Waybill
l4_steps.output: DG shipment record created in cargo system with initial classification flag
l4_steps.kpi: DG acceptance processing time ≤30 min per shipment
l4_steps.pain_point: Incomplete or incorrectly completed shipper declarations are the leading cause of DG non-compliance; IATA DGR Sec 8.1.6 mandates specific formats but non-industry shippers routinely submit non-conforming documents requiring full re-inspection

l4_steps.name: Validate UN Number and Proper Shipping Name
l4_steps.system: IATA DGR e-Tool (electronic dangerous goods database)
l4_steps.input: UN number and proper shipping name from shipper's declaration
l4_steps.output: DG classification confirmed or rejected; discrepancy report if mismatch
l4_steps.kpi: Classification error rate <0.5% of DG shipments processed
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA DGR is revised annually; local DGR lookup databases at handling agents may lag the official publication by 4–8 weeks, causing classification mismatches particularly for newly added UN numbers in Class 9

l4_steps.name: Verify Packing Group, Quantity Limits & Label Compliance
l4_steps.input: Physical package inspection, shipper's declaration packing details
l4_steps.output: Packing compliance report; label and marking verification sign-off
l4_steps.kpi: DG package rejection rate for non-compliance ≤2% of DG shipments; lithium battery state-of-charge verification rate 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Lithium battery shipments (Class 9, UN3480/3481) account for >40% of DG non-compliance findings; IATA DGR Sec 3.9 requires state-of-charge ≤30% which is physically unverifiable without specialised equipment, creating acceptance risk

l4_steps.name: Check Operator Acceptance Policy & Forbidden DG List
l4_steps.input: DG classification, operator Cargo Acceptance Policy manual, forbidden items registry
l4_steps.output: Operator acceptance or rejection decision; special approval requirement flagged if applicable
l4_steps.kpi: Operator policy compliance rate 100%; forbidden item interception rate 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Individual airlines maintain forbidden DG lists that exceed IATA minimums; policy updates are not always propagated to the CargoWise rules engine in real time, creating a window where inadvertent acceptance of operator-prohibited DG is possible

l4_steps.name: Verify Aircraft Type DG Limits (PAX vs CAO)
l4_steps.input: DG class and quantity, aircraft registration, flight number
l4_steps.output: Aircraft-specific DG quantity limits confirmed per IATA DGR Table 2.3; PAX/CAO classification applied
l4_steps.kpi: Per-aircraft DG limit compliance rate 100%; last-minute aircraft swap DG re-check completion rate 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Mixed fleet operations mean PAX aircraft quantity limits are significantly more restrictive than CAO limits for the same DG class; last-minute aircraft swaps change applicable limits and require full re-validation — Altéa DCS does not automatically trigger re-check on tail number change

l4_steps.name: Validate State & Overflight DG Restrictions for Routing
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen FliteDeck (state restriction and NOTAMs database)
l4_steps.input: Flight routing waypoints, DG class, UN number, quantity
l4_steps.output: State variation compliance confirmation or routing conflict advisory
l4_steps.kpi: State restriction check completion rate 100% per DG-carrying flight; overflight violation rate 0%
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA DGR Addendum for State Variations is updated bi-annually but some states (notably China CAAC and several Middle East CAAs) impose interim restrictions not captured in the published addendum, requiring manual dispatcher lookup against state CAA circulars

l4_steps.name: Confirm Operator Approval for Restricted DG Classes
l4_steps.input: DG class requiring specific operator approval (Class 1 explosives, Class 7 radioactive, infectious substances)
l4_steps.output: Operator approval number confirmed and recorded; CAA authorisation obtained if required
l4_steps.kpi: Approval verification cycle time ≤4 hours for restricted classes; approval expiry miss rate 0%
l4_steps.pain_point: Class 7 radioactive material requires Transport Index calculations and specific CAA approvals that expire; renewal tracking at most carriers relies on manual spreadsheets with no system-enforced expiry alert in CargoWise, creating regulatory exposure under IATA DGR Sec 10.8

l4_steps.name: Assign ULD Position per DG Segregation Rules
l4_steps.input: DG class, quantity, ULD type, aircraft hold configuration, passenger manifest
l4_steps.output: DG ULD or bulk position assignment in hold; preliminary centre-of-gravity impact noted
l4_steps.kpi: DG stowage compliance rate 100%; CG deviation ≤±0.5% MAC from target
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa LoadPlanner's DG segregation module requires manual overrides when multiple incompatible DG classes are present on the same flight; there is no automated incompatibility alert in the base LoadPlanner configuration, relying entirely on load controller knowledge

l4_steps.name: Run DG Compatibility Matrix Check Across All Shipments
l4_steps.input: All DG shipments on the flight, IATA DGR Table 9.3 segregation matrix
l4_steps.output: Compatibility check result; stowage conflict report if incompatible DG classes co-located
l4_steps.kpi: Segregation non-conformance rate 0%; compatibility check cycle time ≤10 min
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA DGR Table 9.3 covers 49 hazard class combinations; Altéa LoadPlanner automates checks for only 12 primary class pairs, requiring manual cross-reference for mixed-class loads — a high-error-risk step during high-density cargo operations

l4_steps.name: Calculate Total DG Quantities vs Aircraft Hold Limits
l4_steps.input: All assigned DG ULD positions, per-hold DG limits from aircraft type profile
l4_steps.output: DG quantity compliance summary per hold compartment; net explosive mass (NEM) calculation where applicable
l4_steps.kpi: Per-hold DG limit compliance 100%; NEM calculation accuracy within ±1%
l4_steps.pain_point: Cumulative DG quantity limits per hold require aggregating across multiple individual shipments; there is no automated per-hold summation in standard Altéa LoadPlanner, exposing load controllers to arithmetic error risk on high-volume DG flights

l4_steps.name: Generate NOTOC Draft in IATA Standard Format
l4_steps.input: Confirmed DG positions, classes, UN numbers, quantities, stowage locations from load plan
l4_steps.output: Draft NOTOC (Notice to Captain) in IATA-standard format ready for dispatcher review
l4_steps.kpi: NOTOC generation time ≤15 min after load plan finalised; NOTOC accuracy rate ≥99.9%
l4_steps.pain_point: NOTOC format requirements vary by state CAA — some authorities (FAA, EASA) require additional supplementary fields beyond the IATA standard template; Altéa NOTOC templates are not always maintained to reflect the latest state-specific variants, requiring manual addenda

l4_steps.name: Dispatcher DG Load Authorization Sign-Off
l4_steps.input: DG compliance checklist, NOTOC draft, load plan, dispatcher training currency record
l4_steps.output: Signed DG load authorization record; compliance checklist archived
l4_steps.kpi: Authorization completion ≥D-45 min (45 min before departure); 100% sign-off completion rate
l4_steps.pain_point: ICAO Annex 18 and 49 CFR Part 172 require dispatchers to hold current DG recurrent training (every 24 months); expired training certificates are not always flagged in Altéa DCS against the authorising dispatcher's profile, creating a silent regulatory non-compliance risk

l4_steps.name: Transmit NOTOC to Captain via ACARS Datalink
l4_steps.system: SITA ACARS (aircraft communications and reporting system)
