l4_steps.pain_point: Analytics data latency from Jeppesen to the data warehouse (AWS Redshift) averages 6–12 hours; IROPS events skew utilisation metrics and must be manually isolated from baseline planning to avoid over-provisioning reserve pools

l4_steps.name: Extract layover schedule by station and date
l4_steps.input: Published crew pairings for 14-day rolling window
l4_steps.output: Layover demand matrix by city, date, and crew count
l4_steps.kpi: Schedule extraction latency <15 min after pairing publish
l4_steps.pain_point: Late pairing publication (T-24h or less) leaves insufficient lead time for contracted hotel vendors requiring 48-hr booking notice

l4_steps.name: Forecast hotel room demand by city
l4_steps.input: Layover demand matrix, historical IROPS uplift factors by station
l4_steps.output: City-level room demand forecast with IROPS buffer (typically +15%)
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast accuracy ≥90% vs actual bookings week-over-week
l4_steps.pain_point: IROPS surges at hub stations can exhaust all contracted room blocks within 2 hrs; forecast buffers are static and do not adjust to live weather events

l4_steps.name: Validate contracted block vs demand forecast
l4_steps.input: Room demand forecast, contracted block inventory by hotel and city
l4_steps.output: Block gap report flagging cities with coverage <95%
l4_steps.kpi: Contracted block coverage ≥95% of forecasted demand
l4_steps.pain_point: Multi-hub IROPS events simultaneously exhaust blocks across 3–5 cities; no automated cross-city reallocation mechanism exists in current system

l4_steps.name: Auto-generate hotel reservations for pairings
l4_steps.input: Approved layover schedule, contracted hotel inventory
l4_steps.output: Hotel confirmation records with room type, check-in/out times
l4_steps.kpi: Auto-booking rate ≥98% for standard layovers; zero manual entry for pairings >48 hrs out
l4_steps.pain_point: API integration gaps with major hotel chain property management systems cause duplicate booking records requiring manual reconciliation 3–4 times per week

l4_steps.name: Book ground transport for crew arrival and departure
l4_steps.input: Hotel confirmation records, scheduled flight arrival/departure times
l4_steps.output: Transport schedule with vendor assignment, vehicle type, and pickup windows
l4_steps.kpi: Transport booking confirmed ≥4 hrs before crew arrival; on-time pickup rate ≥97%
l4_steps.pain_point: Schedule changes within T-2h require emergency vendor calls; dispatch API does not support same-day amendments at 60% of outstations, forcing manual phone coordination

l4_steps.name: Validate hotel transit time vs FAR 117 rest period
l4_steps.input: Hotel address, transport time estimate, crew report time for next leg
l4_steps.output: FAR Part 117 §117.25 compliance flag per crew member
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of layovers validated against FAR Part 117 before booking confirmation
l4_steps.pain_point: Hotels beyond 30-min transport window from airport trigger rest period recalculation under §117.25; legacy hotel contracts predate this requirement and contain non-compliant properties

l4_steps.name: Monitor real-time schedule changes affecting layovers
l4_steps.input: Live flight operations feed, crew schedule update events
l4_steps.output: Change alerts for affected hotel and transport bookings
l4_steps.kpi: Change detection latency <5 min from schedule update event
l4_steps.pain_point: Dec 2022 IROPS demonstrated that cascading schedule changes overwhelm manual monitoring; automated alerting still misses secondary-effect pairings when first-order cancellation triggers re-crewing at a different station

l4_steps.name: Amend hotel and transport bookings for disruptions
l4_steps.input: Change alert with new layover city, arrival time, or cancellation flag
l4_steps.output: Amended or cancelled booking confirmations sent to hotel and transport vendor
l4_steps.kpi: Amendment completion within 30 min of schedule change notification
l4_steps.pain_point: Hotel cancellation penalty windows (typically 6-hr cutoff) generate no-show charges when flights cancel <6 hrs out; no automated penalty-waiver negotiation tool exists

l4_steps.name: Push updated crew itinerary to mobile devices
l4_steps.input: Amended booking confirmations, crew contact roster
l4_steps.output: Push notification with hotel name, address, transport pickup time, and confirmation number
l4_steps.kpi: Notification delivery rate ≥99.5%; crew acknowledgement ≥95% within 30 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew operating international outstations without cellular data roaming miss push notifications; no fallback SMS gateway for low-connectivity stations is currently integrated

l4_steps.name: Dispatch transport on actual aircraft block-in
l4_steps.input: ACARS actual gate arrival time, crew count from flight manifest
l4_steps.output: Driver dispatch instruction with ETA to gate
l4_steps.kpi: Transport wheels-rolling ≤20 min after block-in; crew at hotel ≤45 min after block-in
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS feed latency at 12% of outstations means dispatch is triggered on estimated rather than actual arrival, causing early driver arrival and standby cost or missed crew if delayed

l4_steps.name: Confirm all crew aboard transport before departure
l4_steps.input: Crew roster for arriving flight, driver headcount check
l4_steps.output: Departure confirmation or missing-crew alert
l4_steps.kpi: Crew accounting accuracy 100% before vehicle departs gate area
l4_steps.pain_point: No electronic crew manifest is scanned at transport boarding; headcount is manual and error-prone, particularly for large widebody arrivals with 12–16 crew members at international stations

l4_steps.name: Source spot-rate hotel for IROPS overflow crew
l4_steps.input: Block gap report, IROPS declaration from Network Operations Control
l4_steps.output: Spot-rate hotel bookings for overflow crew with transport coordination
l4_steps.kpi: Overflow booking confirmed <2 hrs from IROPS declaration; spot rate ≤2.5x contracted rate
l4_steps.pain_point: Current system has no real-time rate cap enforcement for spot bookings; spot-rate hotels during major IROPS events have reached 4x contracted rate with no approval gate, generating significant unplanned cost

l4_steps.name: Reconcile hotel and transport invoices to bookings
l4_steps.input: Vendor invoices, hotel and transport booking confirmation records
l4_steps.output: Matched/unmatched line items and variance report by vendor
l4_steps.kpi: Invoice-to-booking match rate ≥97%; variance items resolved within 10 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Hotel vendors routinely apply early checkout penalties and no-show charges not captured in the booking system, requiring Finance to cross-reference Crew Hotel Management System records manually for every disputed line

l4_steps.name: Generate vendor performance scorecard
l4_steps.input: Matched invoice data, crew feedback submissions, transport on-time records
l4_steps.output: Quarterly vendor scorecard covering cost compliance, service quality, and SLA adherence
l4_steps.kpi: Vendor SLA compliance ≥95%; crew accommodation satisfaction score ≥4.2 / 5.0
l4_steps.pain_point: No structured crew feedback loop exists between hotel stay and vendor management; scores rely on ad-hoc complaints submitted to Crew Control rather than systematic post-stay surveys, understating quality failures

l4_steps.name: Identify crew training requirements from profiles
l4_steps.input: Crew qualification records, regulatory expiry dates, new-hire roster
l4_steps.output: Training requirements matrix per crew member
l4_steps.kpi: Training needs identified ≥90 days before regulatory expiry for 100% of crew
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen stores expiry dates per qualification type but does not auto-generate training demand; planners must run manual extracts, creating lead-time risk when expiry windows cluster post-peak season

l4_steps.name: Build annual training schedule against roster windows
l4_steps.input: Training requirements matrix, published crew roster, training facility calendar
l4_steps.output: Draft annual training schedule with assigned cohorts and dates
l4_steps.kpi: Training schedule published ≥60 days in advance for 95% of planned events
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP SuccessFactors Learning schedule does not have a real-time read of Jeppesen roster data; integration relies on nightly batch sync, causing scheduling conflicts when roster changes are made intra-day

l4_steps.name: Validate training slot availability vs expiry window
l4_steps.input: Draft training schedule, regulatory expiry dates per crew member
l4_steps.output: Approved training schedule or rescheduled cohort
l4_steps.kpi: Zero crew members scheduled for training after regulatory expiry date
l4_steps.pain_point: Facility and simulator capacity at crew training centres frequently bottlenecks slot availability, particularly for SEP training requiring full-scale cabin mock-ups — often forces costly overtime or third-party centre bookings

l4_steps.name: Deliver SEP safety & emergency procedures training
l4_steps.input: Approved training schedule, current SEP syllabus per aircraft type, regulatory syllabus (FAR Part 121.433)
l4_steps.output: Completed SEP classroom and practical session records
l4_steps.kpi: SEP training completion rate ≥100% before regulatory expiry (FAR Part 121.433 mandatory); classroom session NPS ≥4.2/5.0
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 121.433 mandates annual SEP recurrent training; full-scale cabin mock-up availability at training centres is constrained — scheduling slippage >30 days past planned date has occurred during peak hiring periods

l4_steps.name: Conduct aircraft type-specific cabin familiarization
l4_steps.input: Aircraft configuration specs (B737-700/800/MAX 8), SEP completed status
l4_steps.output: Aircraft type familiarization sign-off per crew member
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of cabin crew type-qualified before first line assignment on that aircraft variant
l4_steps.pain_point: Fleet mix of B737-700 (-143 seats) and B737-800/MAX 8 (-175 seats) requires separate door and evacuation drills; adding MAX 8 MCAS awareness content required unplanned syllabus revision after 2019 grounding

l4_steps.name: Administer written safety knowledge assessment
l4_steps.input: Completed SEP and type familiarization sessions
l4_steps.output: Assessment score record per crew member
l4_steps.kpi: First-attempt pass rate (score ≥80%) ≥95% of cohort; average score ≥87%
l4_steps.pain_point: Assessment question bank in SAP SuccessFactors Learning is not versioned against specific regulatory revision cycles; outdated questions have appeared after FAA circular updates, requiring manual audit of question pools before each cohort

l4_steps.name: Evaluate safety assessment pass/fail and route remediation
l4_steps.input: Assessment score record
l4_steps.output: Pass certification or remedial training assignment
l4_steps.kpi: Remedial loop resolved within 14 calendar days; zero crew deployed without confirmed pass
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew who fail on first attempt require additional classroom time that displaces scheduled cohorts; no automated re-booking logic in SAP SuccessFactors Learning forces manual calendar intervention

l4_steps.name: Deliver in-flight service standards curriculum
l4_steps.input: Service standards manual (current version), brand and product updates from inflight services team
l4_steps.output: Completed service standards classroom session record
l4_steps.kpi: Service standards curriculum delivered to 100% of active cabin crew within annual training cycle; session completion rate ≥98%
l4_steps.pain_point: Inflight product changes (e.g. menu rotations, new beverage service procedures) are communicated via separate email distribution; SAP SuccessFactors Learning course content lags by 4–6 weeks, leaving a gap where crew operate on outdated standards

l4_steps.name: Train galley management and catering loading procedures
l4_steps.input: Catering loading specifications, galley configuration diagrams per aircraft type
l4_steps.output: Galley management competency sign-off
l4_steps.kpi: Galley loading error rate on line flights ≤0.5% of sectors (measured via customer complaint and inflight report data)
l4_steps.pain_point: B737-700 and B737-800 have different galley configurations; training material must be aircraft-type-specific but SAP SuccessFactors Learning course library does not enforce type-level prerequisites, allowing crew to complete wrong-type galley module

l4_steps.name: Conduct mock in-flight service drill and evaluate
l4_steps.input: Completed service standards and galley modules, cabin mock-up facility booking
l4_steps.output: Service drill evaluation scorecard per crew member
l4_steps.kpi: Drill pass rate ≥90% first attempt; average service quality score ≥3.8/5.0 on evaluation rubric
l4_steps.pain_point: Mock cabin facility time is shared with SEP drills; scheduling conflicts cause service drills to be shortened or deferred, resulting in crew entering IOE with incomplete practical service training

l4_steps.name: Assign IOE line check flights with qualified evaluator
l4_steps.input: Drill pass scorecard, evaluator availability roster, open line flight schedule
l4_steps.output: IOE pairing assignment for new or recurrent check crew
l4_steps.kpi: IOE line check flights assigned within 10 days of practical training completion for 90% of crew
l4_steps.pain_point: Qualified cabin crew evaluators (check cabin crew) are drawn from operational roster — their availability conflicts with line flying duties; Jeppesen does not distinguish check crew duty type from line duty for optimisation purposes, causing evaluator shortfalls

l4_steps.name: Conduct IOE line check observation and scoring
l4_steps.input: IOE pairing assignment, IOE evaluation form, service standards scorecard criteria
l4_steps.output: Completed IOE observation report with scored competency ratings
l4_steps.kpi: IOE report submitted within 24 hours of check flight; evaluation criteria coverage ≥100% of mandatory competency items
l4_steps.pain_point: IOE evaluation forms are completed on paper and manually entered into IBS iCrew post-flight; transcription errors and late submissions (>48 hours) have created compliance gaps identified during FAA ATOS audit cycles

l4_steps.name: Evaluate IOE line check pass/fail threshold
l4_steps.input: Completed IOE observation report, minimum competency thresholds
l4_steps.output: Line check pass certification or additional IOE assignment
l4_steps.kpi: IOE first-attempt pass rate ≥88%; crew requiring >2 IOE attempts flagged for remediation programme review
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated escalation logic when crew fail second IOE attempt; Crew Training Manager must manually initiate extended remediation, which delays qualification by 3–6 weeks and increases cost per trained crew member

l4_steps.name: Issue FAA-compliant cabin crew qualification record
l4_steps.input: IOE pass certification, safety assessment pass, all module completions
l4_steps.output: Crew qualification certificate with next-due recurrency dates
l4_steps.kpi: Qualification record issued within 48 hours of final IOE pass; zero records issued with incomplete module pre-requisites
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 121 requires the operator to maintain individual crew training records that are producible on FAA request within 24 hours; IBS iCrew record completeness depends on all upstream systems having posted — batch sync gaps with SAP SuccessFactors create producibility risk

l4_steps.name: Synchronise training records across LMS and crew system
l4_steps.input: Qualification certificate, SAP SuccessFactors Learning completion records
l4_steps.output: Reconciled crew training record in IBS iCrew and SAP SuccessFactors
l4_steps.kpi: Record reconciliation completed within 24 hours of qualification issuance; discrepancy rate between systems ≤0.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Nightly batch integration between SAP SuccessFactors Learning and IBS iCrew uses flat-file exchange without transaction-level error logging; silent failures result in qualification data appearing complete in LMS but absent in crew scheduling system, causing crew to be erroneously assigned flights

l4_steps.name: Validate FAR Part 121.433 recurrent compliance status
l4_steps.input: Reconciled crew training records, FAR Part 121.433 recurrency intervals by training type
l4_steps.output: Compliance status report — pass or non-compliant flag per crew member
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of active flying crew compliant with all FAR Part 121.433 recurrency requirements at all times; compliance dashboard accuracy ≥99.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 121.433 recurrency window calculations require tracking multiple qualification types (SEP, type, service) with different intervals; manual tracking in spreadsheets has been used as a backup when IBS iCrew reports are slow, introducing version-control risk

l4_steps.name: Apply scheduling restriction to non-compliant crew
l4_steps.input: Non-compliant crew flags from IBS iCrew compliance report
l4_steps.output: Scheduling hold applied in Jeppesen; crew notified via automated alert
l4_steps.kpi: Scheduling restriction applied within 2 hours of non-compliance flag; zero non-compliant crew assigned to revenue flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen scheduling hold must be manually applied by a crew compliance analyst — there is no automated API trigger from IBS iCrew non-compliance flags; overnight non-compliance identified after Jeppesen pairing optimiser has already run can result in non-compliant pairings requiring costly last-minute rebidding

l4_steps.name: Monitor flight disruption alerts
l4_steps.input: OTP delay/cancel alerts from airport ops or ATC; Altéa PSS flight status feed
l4_steps.output: Disruption event record opened in crew tracking system
l4_steps.kpi: Detection-to-action time ≤10 min; alert integration latency ≤5 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS and Jeppesen do not sync in real-time; 5–15 min lag in crew impact visibility causes delayed recovery initiation

l4_steps.name: Classify disruption type and scope
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen Crew Management + SITA Airport Management System (AMS)
l4_steps.input: Flight status updates, weather NOTAMs, ATC delay codes
l4_steps.output: Disruption classification record: type (delay/cancel/divert), scope (isolated/systemic), affected flight list
l4_steps.kpi: Classification accuracy ≥95%; classification time ≤5 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Weather-driven systemic disruptions affecting 50+ crew members simultaneously overwhelm manual classification; no automated severity scoring in Jeppesen

l4_steps.name: Extract affected crew roster
l4_steps.input: Disruption classification, impacted flight list
l4_steps.output: Affected crew list with current duty status, rest period elapsed, and home base
l4_steps.kpi: Roster extraction time ≤5 min; crew data accuracy ≥98%
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew position data lags if crew fail to check in via mobile app; roster inaccuracies force manual verification calls adding 10–20 min

l4_steps.name: Validate FAR Part 117 duty time status
l4_steps.input: Affected crew list; current cumulative duty times; rest period records
l4_steps.output: Compliance status matrix per crew member: legal / marginal / illegal with hours remaining
l4_steps.kpi: Duty time calculation accuracy 100%; 0 regulatory violations per post-flight audit
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 117 augmented crew provisions and cumulative fatigue risk calculations are complex; manual overrides risk non-compliance and FAA enforcement action

l4_steps.name: Check crew qualifications and type ratings
l4_steps.input: Affected crew list; aircraft types on disrupted and recovery routes
l4_steps.output: Crew qualification match matrix; list of crew with type rating mismatches
l4_steps.kpi: Qualification verification ≤3 min per crew member; 0 unqualified crew assigned
l4_steps.pain_point: Narrowbody/widebody type rating mismatches restrict recovery options on mixed fleets; qualification database refresh latency causes stale records

l4_steps.name: Identify available reserve crew resources
l4_steps.input: Reserve crew duty board; crew availability calendar; standby call-out rules (CBA)
l4_steps.output: Available reserve crew list ranked by seniority, duty legality, and base proximity
l4_steps.kpi: Reserve utilization rate ≤85% to maintain buffer; reserve call-out success rate ≥90%
l4_steps.pain_point: Reserve pool depletion during systemic weather events; seniority-driven CBA bidding limits scheduling flexibility and overrides optimizer suggestions

l4_steps.name: Run automated re-pairing optimizer
l4_steps.input: Available crew pool (legal, qualified, available); disrupted pairing list; revised flight schedule
l4_steps.output: Proposed re-pairing solution set with cost scores and legality flags
l4_steps.kpi: Optimizer run time ≤8 min; automated solution coverage ≥95% of disrupted pairings
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen optimizer produces sub-optimal solutions under tight time windows; cost parameter tuning requires experienced scheduler intervention to avoid excessive deadhead costs

l4_steps.name: Evaluate deadhead and positioning options
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen Crew Management + Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Proposed re-pairing solution; available seat inventory on required flights
l4_steps.output: Deadhead bookings confirmed or rejected; adjusted re-pairing plan with positioning costs
l4_steps.kpi: Deadhead seat availability rate ≥70%; deadhead cost per re-pairing ≤$800
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated deadhead booking integration between Jeppesen and Altéa PSS; competing passenger demand on sold-out recovery flights blocks crew positioning

l4_steps.name: Apply manual overrides for exceptional cases
l4_steps.input: Optimizer solution gaps; exceptional crew constraints (compassionate leave, training conflicts)
l4_steps.output: Manually adjusted re-pairing with override justification log and authorisation code
l4_steps.kpi: Manual override rate ≤15% of total re-pairings; override documentation compliance 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual overrides are audit-tracked by labour unions and must be defensible under CBA; pressure to minimise them conflicts with operational necessity during major disruptions

l4_steps.name: Validate full re-pairing plan legality
l4_steps.input: Final re-pairing plan including all manual overrides
l4_steps.output: Legality validation report with pass/fail per assignment and FAR Part 117 reference citations
l4_steps.kpi: 100% compliance pass rate before plan activation; 0 post-departure duty violations
l4_steps.pain_point: Real-time legality checks may not capture late-reported duty changes; crew self-reporting of off-system duty time creates hidden violations discoverable only at post-flight audit

l4_steps.name: Assess CBA cost impact and premium pay flags
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen Crew Management + SAP S/4HANA Finance (FI/CO)
l4_steps.input: Approved re-pairing plan; crew pay rules from collective bargaining agreement
l4_steps.output: Estimated re-pairing cost vs. baseline pairing cost; premium pay flags (missed trip, deadhead, min-day guarantee)
l4_steps.kpi: Re-pairing cost premium ≤$1,200 per disrupted pairing; CBA rule flag accuracy ≥98%
l4_steps.pain_point: CBA minimum-day compensation, missed connection pay, and hotel expense rules trigger unexpected premium costs not modelled in Jeppesen; finance reconciliation with SAP is manual

l4_steps.name: Notify affected crew via CrewConnect and ACARS
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen CrewConnect mobile app + Telex/SITA ACARS
l4_steps.input: Finalised re-pairing assignments; crew contact details; estimated report times
l4_steps.output: Push notifications and duty change messages delivered; crew acknowledgment timer started
l4_steps.kpi: Notification delivery rate ≥98%; crew acknowledgment within 30 min for ≥85% of assignments
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew connectivity gaps in airports without WiFi; ACARS coverage limited to airborne crew; personal device management policy inconsistency across crew bases

l4_steps.name: Confirm crew acknowledgment and acceptance
l4_steps.input: Notification delivery confirmation; crew response (accept/reject with reason code)
l4_steps.output: Confirmed duty acceptance log or rejection record with CBA reason code
l4_steps.kpi: Crew acceptance rate on first notification ≥80%; escalation rate ≤20%
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew refusals citing CBA rest-period disputes or training conflicts require union liaison review before escalation; each dispute adds 20–40 min to recovery timeline

l4_steps.name: Escalate unresolved crew assignments
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen Crew Management + airline labour relations tracking system
l4_steps.input: Non-accepted assignment records; union contact roster; operational contingency options
l4_steps.output: Escalated case record; alternative crew sourced or operational contingency activated (delay/cancel flight)
l4_steps.kpi: Escalation resolution time ≤60 min; crew replacement sourced within 90 min of escalation
l4_steps.pain_point: Union grievance procedures can extend resolution beyond the operational window; documented escalation playbooks are inconsistent across crew bases and crew categories

l4_steps.name: Monitor re-pairing execution in real-time
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen Crew Management + SITA Airport Management System (AMS)
l4_steps.input: Live flight status updates; crew check-in confirmations; gate and stand assignments
l4_steps.output: Execution status dashboard with exception flags for late crew, missed check-ins, and gate conflicts
l4_steps.kpi: Re-pairing execution compliance rate ≥92%; real-time tracking lag ≤5 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Multi-airport simultaneous disruptions create monitoring overload; a single controller may track 20+ active re-pairings with no auto-escalation in Jeppesen for critical deviations

l4_steps.name: Update crew records and close disruption event
l4_steps.input: Completed re-pairing execution log; final duty times; hotel and transport receipts
l4_steps.output: Updated crew records (cumulative duty, pay events, pairing history); disruption closure report with root cause tag
l4_steps.kpi: Record update within 2 hours of final flight completion; data accuracy ≥99.5%; pay discrepancy rate ≤0.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen-to-SAP SuccessFactors payroll integration latency causes pay discrepancies that generate crew queries and manual reconciliation effort averaging 45 min per affected pairing

l4_steps.name: Ingest ratified CBA language into rule repository
l4_steps.input: Ratified CBA document or amendment notice from union
l4_steps.output: Rule change requests logged in Jeppesen crew scheduling rule library
l4_steps.kpi: CBA rule ingestion initiated within 5 business days of ratification
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual translation of legal CBA language into Jeppesen-readable scheduling constraints requires specialist knowledge; misinterpretation of trip rig, rest augmentation, or bidding period provisions is common

l4_steps.name: Configure duty/rest limits in scheduling engine
l4_steps.input: CBA duty/rest rule change requests; FAR Part 117 regulatory minimums
l4_steps.output: Updated Jeppesen rule set with CBA contractual duty time and rest limits
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of CBA rest rules coded and tested within 10 business days of ratification
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 117 regulatory minimums and CBA contractual minimums differ by crew position (Captain vs F/O vs Flight Attendant); dual-layer rule stacking in Jeppesen increases configuration complexity and regression testing cycles

l4_steps.name: Configure premium pay triggers and trip rig rules
l4_steps.input: CBA pay schedule, premium pay provisions, trip rig and guarantee rules
l4_steps.output: Configured pay rules in SAP with all premium triggers (IROPS reassignment, hotel substitution, min-day guarantee)
l4_steps.kpi: Pay rule configuration accuracy ≥99.5%; zero retroactive pay adjustments attributable to misconfiguration in first post-implementation payroll cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: CBA premium pay provisions (e.g., reassignment pay, deadhead premium, per diem differentials) are frequently misinterpreted; configuration errors are not detected until payroll run, creating retroactive liability

l4_steps.name: Validate rule configuration against CBA source text
l4_steps.input: Configured Jeppesen scheduling rules and SAP pay rules; original CBA text
l4_steps.output: Validation sign-off memo or change request list
l4_steps.kpi: Zero CBA violations attributable to misconfiguration within 90 days of new rule deployment
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated cross-reference tooling between CBA legal article numbers and Jeppesen rule IDs; validation is entirely manual and relies on individual analyst expertise, creating key-person dependency

l4_steps.name: Run pre-publication CBA compliance scan on draft schedule
l4_steps.input: Draft pairing solution from Jeppesen optimizer
l4_steps.output: Compliance report flagging CBA rule violations by article and step number
l4_steps.kpi: Compliance scan completed ≥2 hours before schedule publication deadline; scan must cover 100% of published pairings
l4_steps.pain_point: Late schedule changes driven by aircraft swaps or demand reforecast force rescan within 30-minute windows; Jeppesen batch compliance jobs may not complete in time, leaving residual violations undetected

l4_steps.name: Adjudicate violations and determine waiver or remediation
l4_steps.input: Compliance scan violation report
l4_steps.output: Decision per violation: remediate, obtain union waiver, or escalate
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of violations resolved or formally waived before schedule publication; adjudication cycle ≤4 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Some CBA violations require mutual union agreement for waiver (e.g., minimum rest reduction below contractual floor); union contact SLAs are not always met in real-time operations, creating publication holds

l4_steps.name: Remediate non-compliant pairings or assignments
l4_steps.input: List of violations requiring remediation; available crew pool and reserve positions
l4_steps.output: Revised compliant pairings or crew assignments
l4_steps.kpi: Remediation cycle ≤90 minutes; crew coverage maintained ≥97% post-remediation
l4_steps.pain_point: Remediation options are constrained by qualified reserve availability at domicile; fixing one CBA violation can cascade into secondary violations for adjacent pairings, triggering iterative rescan loops

l4_steps.name: Monitor real-time crew duty times and rest windows
l4_steps.input: Live flight departure/arrival data; crew check-in and check-out events via ACARS
l4_steps.output: Real-time duty time dashboard; automated alerts for crews approaching CBA or FAR Part 117 limits
l4_steps.kpi: Duty limit alerts triggered ≥60 minutes before contractual limit; zero post-facto exceedances reported in monthly audit
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS data latency can delay duty-on/duty-off timestamp capture by 5–15 minutes, creating a window of undetected limit approach; iCrew alert thresholds must be manually calibrated per CBA article and crew category

l4_steps.name: Decide on duty extension or crew replacement during IROPS
l4_steps.input: Duty limit alert; flight delay status; qualified reserve availability at station
l4_steps.output: Documented decision: CBA extension invoked with crew consent, or replacement crew assigned
l4_steps.kpi: Crew replacement or extension decision made ≥45 minutes before departure; 100% of CBA waiver invocations logged with timestamp and crew consent reference
l4_steps.pain_point: CBA duty extensions require individual crew member consent; crew refusals during IROPS with no available replacement create cascading departure delays; iCrew has no automated consent-capture mechanism, exposing airline to grievance risk

l4_steps.name: Log and acknowledge crew grievance within CBA window
l4_steps.input: Written grievance submitted by crew member or union representative
l4_steps.output: Grievance case record with CBA article citation, incident timestamp, and acknowledgement sent to filer
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of grievances logged within 24 hours of receipt; formal acknowledgement delivered within CBA Step 1 filing window (typically 72 hours)
l4_steps.pain_point: CBA grievance filing windows (commonly 10–30 days from incident) require precise date/time stamping of the triggering event; SAP SuccessFactors case management is not purpose-built for CBA article-based aviation grievance workflows

l4_steps.name: Investigate grievance and retrieve corroborating data
l4_steps.input: Grievance case record; referenced duty period, flight, or pay event
l4_steps.output: Investigation dossier with duty logs, pay records, system-generated timestamps, and CBA article analysis
l4_steps.kpi: Investigation completed within CBA Step 1 response window (typically 14 calendar days); 100% data retrieval from duty records for incidents ≤24 months old
l4_steps.pain_point: Historical duty and pay records span Jeppesen, iCrew, and SAP — three separate systems with no unified query interface; cross-system data extraction for grievance investigations is manual and can take 2–5 days, compressing response timelines

l4_steps.name: Assess grievance merit and issue management response
l4_steps.input: Investigation dossier; CBA articles cited in grievance
l4_steps.output: Merit assessment and formal Step 1 management response delivered to union
l4_steps.kpi: Management response delivered within CBA Step 1 deadline 100% of the time; grievance upheld rate ≤15%
l4_steps.pain_point: Inconsistent management responses across crew domiciles create arbitration precedents that constrain future positions; absence of a centralised CBA case law repository means analysts are unaware of prior rulings on identical fact patterns

l4_steps.name: Escalate unresolved grievance to arbitration
l4_steps.input: Grievance not resolved at Steps 1–3; arbitration demand notice from union
l4_steps.output: Arbitration brief, hearing schedule confirmed, award recorded in case management system
l4_steps.kpi: Arbitration win/settlement rate ≥60%; average cost per arbitration case ≤$15,000
l4_steps.pain_point: Arbitration preparation requires multi-year historical data retrieval; poor data quality from legacy crew system migrations (pre-2023) degrades management's evidentiary position and increases settlement risk

l4_steps.name: Execute monthly CBA compliance audit across all domiciles
l4_steps.input: Prior month's schedule execution data, payroll run outputs, duty logs from iCrew
l4_steps.output: Monthly compliance dashboard showing violation rate by CBA article, crew category, and domicile
l4_steps.kpi: Audit completed by day 5 of the following month; CBA violation rate ≤0.5% of all duty periods in scope
l4_steps.pain_point: ETL pipelines aggregating data from Jeppesen, iCrew, and SAP into Redshift are fragile; data latency or pipeline failures cause the audit to miss late-adjusted duties and produce understated violation counts

l4_steps.name: Distribute compliance report to union per CBA schedule
l4_steps.input: Monthly compliance dashboard from AWS Redshift
l4_steps.output: Formatted union-facing compliance report delivered by CBA-stipulated deadline
l4_steps.kpi: Report delivered by 10th of the month 100% of the time; zero data discrepancies disputed by union within 30 days of delivery
l4_steps.pain_point: CBA may require specific tabular formats or certified audit trail attachments not natively supported by Tableau; manual reformatting prior to union delivery introduces transcription errors and reputational risk

l4_steps.name: Determine if corrective action plan is required
l4_steps.input: Monthly compliance report; union objections or formal notices if any
l4_steps.output: Corrective Action Plan (CAP) initiated or formal closure memo issued
l4_steps.kpi: CAP initiated within 5 business days of audit finding confirmation; 100% of open CAPs closed within 60 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Systemic violations (e.g., recurring pay calculation errors, scheduling rule misapplication) require IT system changes with 4–8 week lead times; union may file class grievances covering the entire affected population while the CAP is open

l4_steps.name: Trigger CBA expiry alert and negotiation readiness review
l4_steps.input: CBA expiry date calendar alert (18-month advance trigger)
l4_steps.output: Negotiation readiness checklist; data extraction scope and timeline defined
l4_steps.kpi: Negotiation preparation formally initiated ≥18 months before CBA expiry; zero missed expiry dates across all bargaining units
l4_steps.pain_point: Multiple CBAs (pilots, flight attendants, dispatchers, ground operations) carry staggered expiry dates; tracking across contracts in SAP SuccessFactors requires custom calendar configuration that is not standard in the SuccessFactors Employee Central module

l4_steps.name: Extract historical compliance and cost data for bargaining
l4_steps.input: 3-year historical duty records, grievance case data, payroll actuals, IATA peer benchmarks
l4_steps.output: Bargaining data package: cost impact modelling of proposed rule changes, violation trend analysis, peer carrier benchmarks
l4_steps.kpi: Data package completed ≥12 months before CBA expiry; benchmark dataset covers ≥5 comparable peer carriers
l4_steps.pain_point: Historical data quality degrades beyond 24 months due to crew system migrations; IATA labour cost benchmarks are published on 12–18 month lag cycles, reducing relevance of peer comparisons at the bargaining table

l4_steps.name: Validate bargaining data package for negotiation
l4_steps.input: Draft bargaining data package from Labour Analytics
l4_steps.output: Approved bargaining data package or supplemental data extraction requests
l4_steps.kpi: Data package formally approved ≥10 months before CBA expiry; zero material data gaps surfaced at the bargaining table
l4_steps.pain_point: Union may dispute the airline's data methodology or system-of-record selection; absence of a jointly agreed data framework creates credibility risk and can stall early bargaining sessions

l4_steps.name: Implement ratified CBA rules in scheduling and pay systems
l4_steps.input: Ratified new or amended CBA document; confirmed effective date
l4_steps.output: Updated Jeppesen scheduling rules and SAP pay configuration; parallel-run test results; go-live sign-off
l4_steps.kpi: System implementation completed ≥14 calendar days before CBA effective date; zero pay errors attributable to new CBA rules in first post-implementation payroll cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: CBA ratification often occurs within days of the contractual effective date, leaving insufficient time for Jeppesen rule testing cycles and SAP parallel pay run validation; compressed timelines increase risk of live-environment misconfiguration

l4_steps.name: Analyse crew headcount gap vs. demand forecast
l4_steps.input: 12-month schedule demand forecast, current crew establishment headcount by fleet and base
l4_steps.output: Headcount gap report segmented by fleet type, domicile, and class date window
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast accuracy ±5% vs. actual recruits needed; report delivered ≥10 months ahead of class date
l4_steps.pain_point: Demand forecast volatility from new route announcements and aircraft delivery slippage causes mid-cycle requisition revisions; 9–12-month type-rating lead times mean over/under-hiring is costly and hard to correct

l4_steps.name: Submit and approve crew recruitment requisition
l4_steps.input: Approved headcount gap report, budget allocation from Finance (SAP S/4HANA FI/CO)
l4_steps.output: Approved job requisition record with fleet type, domicile, target class date, and minimum qualifications
l4_steps.kpi: Requisition-to-posting cycle ≤3 business days; budget approval SLA ≤5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP SuccessFactors integration with Jeppesen Crew Management is manual; class date misalignment between HR and Training wastes simulator slots costing $5,000–$12,000 per unused FFS hour

l4_steps.name: Publish vacancy and build candidate pipeline
l4_steps.input: Approved requisition with role minimums (ATP certificate, total flight hours, type rating preferences)
l4_steps.output: Live job posting across channels; ranked candidate pipeline in ATS
l4_steps.kpi: Application-to-qualified-applicant ratio ≥15%; time-to-slate ≤21 days from posting
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR 121.436 ATP minimum (1,500 hours) creates a shallow qualified candidate pool; competition from cargo carriers and regional airlines for experienced pilots drives signing bonus inflation, increasing cost-per-hire beyond budget assumptions

l4_steps.name: Screen applications against FAR 121 ATP minimums
l4_steps.system: SAP SuccessFactors Recruiting + FAA Airmen Inquiry
l4_steps.input: Candidate application submissions; FAA Airmen Inquiry certificate data
l4_steps.output: Shortlisted candidates meeting FAR 121.436 ATP, total hours, and currency requirements
l4_steps.kpi: Screen pass rate ≥40% of qualified applicants; false-negative rate <5% on manual reviews
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual logbook hour verification is time-consuming and fraud-prone; inflated or falsified total-time entries are an industry-wide risk requiring cross-check against FAA Airmen Inquiry — no automated integration exists between ATS and FAA records

l4_steps.name: Conduct HR pre-screen video interview
l4_steps.input: Shortlisted candidate pool from application screening
l4_steps.output: Pre-screen assessment score; advance or decline decision per candidate
l4_steps.kpi: Pre-screen to assessment conversion rate ≥65%; no-show rate <10%
l4_steps.pain_point: Scheduling across time zones for international candidates and active-duty military applicants creates coordination overhead; no-show rates of 10–15% without automated two-way reminder workflows in SuccessFactors deplete pipeline faster than sourcing can replenish

l4_steps.name: Administer aptitude and psychometric assessment
l4_steps.input: Advance decision from pre-screen; candidate email invitation to assessment portal
l4_steps.output: Cognitive aptitude score, personality fit report, and composite recommendation
l4_steps.kpi: Assessment completion rate ≥90%; pass threshold ≥65th percentile on cognitive battery
l4_steps.pain_point: Hogan and Criteria Corp are not natively integrated with SAP SuccessFactors; scores must be manually uploaded, creating data-entry lag and gaps in the EEOC audit trail required for FAR Part 121 carrier compliance

l4_steps.name: Conduct simulator technical assessment — FFS Level D
l4_steps.system: CAE SimuFlite Full-Flight Simulator (FFS Level D)
l4_steps.input: Passed aptitude assessment; confirmed FFS simulator slot from training schedule
l4_steps.output: Simulator assessment gradesheet (pass / conditional / fail) per standardised evaluation form
l4_steps.kpi: First-attempt pass rate ≥75%; FFS simulator utilisation for recruiting ≥80% of booked slots
l4_steps.pain_point: FFS Level D availability is a shared constraint between line training, recurrent training, and recruiting — unplanned FFS maintenance causes candidate rescheduling and downstream class-date delays; recruiting slots are lowest priority in most carriers' FFS allocation policies

l4_steps.name: Conduct structured panel interview and make hire decision
l4_steps.input: FFS gradesheet, aptitude and psychometric scores, pre-screen interview notes
l4_steps.output: Hire or no-hire decision recorded in ATS; offer authorisation initiated
l4_steps.kpi: Offer acceptance rate ≥85%; panel-to-verbal-offer cycle ≤5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Panel scoring without a Behaviourally Anchored Rating Scale (BARS) leads to inconsistent decisions and EEO exposure; calibration sessions between Chief Pilots and HR are ad hoc, creating inter-rater reliability risk that is difficult to defend in EEOC investigations

l4_steps.name: Initiate PRIA check and criminal background screening
l4_steps.system: FAA Airmen Records Clearinghouse (ARC) + HireRight Background Screening
l4_steps.input: Conditional offer accepted; signed PRIA consent form from candidate
l4_steps.output: PRIA report (prior employer records, accident/incident history, drug and alcohol test records); criminal background check result
l4_steps.kpi: PRIA response turnaround ≤30 days (FAR 121.432 statutory deadline); background check completion ≤10 days; disqualification rate <8%
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR 121.432 PRIA requires contacting all prior aviation employers within 5 years — defunct carriers, foreign operators, and unresponsive employers can delay responses by 4–8 weeks with no regulatory enforcement mechanism, directly pushing class dates and increasing training pipeline gaps

l4_steps.name: Schedule and complete FAA Class 1 AME medical exam
l4_steps.system: FAA MedXPress + AME Network (Aviation Medical Examiner)
l4_steps.input: Candidate personal data; completed FAA Form 8500-8 submitted via MedXPress
l4_steps.output: First-Class Medical Certificate issued by AME; MedXPress submission forwarded to FAA AMCD (Aeromedical Certification Division)
l4_steps.kpi: First-class medical pass rate ≥88%; average AME scheduling lead time ≤10 days; medical disqualification identified pre-class ≥95% of cases
l4_steps.pain_point: Candidates with undisclosed conditions (ADHD, cardiovascular history) or special issuance requirements fail at this late stage, creating class fill gaps with no time to backfill; BasicMed provisions do not apply to FAR Part 121 ATP-required operations, so no alternative pathway exists

l4_steps.name: Verify right-to-work and obtain TSA security clearance
l4_steps.system: DHS E-Verify + TSA Security Threat Assessment (STA) Portal
l4_steps.input: Government-issued identity documents; completed I-9 form
l4_steps.output: E-Verify employment authorisation result; TSA STA clearance confirmation number
l4_steps.kpi: E-Verify clearance ≤3 business days; TSA STA clearance ≤21 days; I-9 compliance rate 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: TSA STA delays for candidates with extensive foreign travel history or partial name matches on government watchlists can hold class starts by 2–4 weeks; airline bears DOT liability if any revenue flying occurs before STA clears, requiring costly reallocation of training resources

l4_steps.name: Issue employment contract and confirm class date
l4_steps.input: All compliance checks passed; class date slot confirmed with Training Operations
l4_steps.output: Digitally signed employment contract; new hire record activated in HRIS; class start date confirmed to candidate and training department
l4_steps.kpi: Contract signature to class start ≥14 days buffer; offer-to-class-start cycle ≤90 days; DocuSign completion rate 100% within 3 days of issue
l4_steps.pain_point: Contract terms covering domicile preference, upgrade timelines, and training bond obligations are a primary retention lever — verbal recruiter commitments that diverge from standardised contract language drive year-1 attrition; no single system of record exists to track promises made during recruitment

l4_steps.name: Complete airline indoctrination and systems ground school
l4_steps.system: SAP SuccessFactors Learning (LMS) + Airline CBT Training Portal
l4_steps.input: Class start date; FAR Part 121 Subpart N-approved training syllabus; aircraft systems manuals
l4_steps.output: Ground school completion certificate; aircraft systems knowledge exam result (pass threshold ≥80%)
l4_steps.kpi: Ground school exam first-attempt pass rate ≥90%; dropout or withdrawal rate <5% per class
l4_steps.pain_point: CBT content revision cycles lag behind avionics Service Bulletin (SB) and procedure changes by 6–12 months; new hires learn superseded procedures during ground school and require re-briefing before IOE, increasing Check Airman workload and extending qualification timelines

l4_steps.name: Conduct type rating simulator training under AQP
l4_steps.system: CAE SimuFlite FFS Level D + LOSA Observation Software
l4_steps.input: Ground school completion certificate; FAA-approved Advanced Qualification Programme (AQP) training plan
l4_steps.output: FFS event grades per AQP curriculum; simulator training records logged per FAR 121.409
l4_steps.kpi: FFS training syllabus completion rate 100%; average event grade ≥Satisfactory on all AQP manoeuvres; FFS utilisation ≥85%
l4_steps.pain_point: AQP data management is manual at many carriers — FFS event grades recorded on paper and scanned into training records, creating audit trail gaps for FAA AAIP oversight; LOSA data capture is not standardised, reducing safety data quality for SMS programmes

l4_steps.name: Administer FAA checkride and issue type rating
l4_steps.role: FAA Designated Pilot Examiner (DPE) / AAIP Check Airman
l4_steps.system: FAA IACRA (Integrated Airman Certification and Rating Application)
l4_steps.input: Completed AQP FFS training with all events graded Satisfactory; training records package
l4_steps.output: Temporary airman certificate with type rating endorsement; IACRA application submitted to FAA Registry
l4_steps.kpi: First-attempt checkride pass rate ≥85%; temporary certificate issuance ≤2 days post-exam; permanent certificate ≤120 days per FAA Registry SLA
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA DPE availability is a systemic bottleneck — nationwide DPE shortage means checkride wait times of 2–4 weeks, delaying class graduation and IOE start; airline AAIP (Airline Aviation Training Programme) designation mitigates this but requires dedicated Check Airman capacity that competes with line operations

l4_steps.name: Complete Initial Operating Experience (IOE) line check
l4_steps.role: IOE Check Airman / New Hire First Officer
l4_steps.input: Type rating certificate on file; FAR 121.434 IOE syllabus; assigned IOE pairings in crew schedule
l4_steps.output: IOE completion sign-off by Check Airman; line check gradesheet; FAR 121 line qualification endorsed
l4_steps.kpi: IOE completion within 90 days of type rating issuance (FAR 121.434); first-attempt line check pass rate ≥90%; IOE hours per graduate ≤25 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: IOE pairing availability depends on route and equipment schedule — Jeppesen pairing optimiser does not natively prioritise IOE pairings, causing delays beyond the 90-day FAR 121.434 regulatory window; FAR Part 117 fatigue rules for Check Airmen further constrain IOE scheduling during high operational tempo periods

l4_steps.name: Activate crew qualification record and assign domicile
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen Crew Management + IBS Software iCrew
l4_steps.input: IOE sign-off documentation; type rating on file; employment contract domicile preference
l4_steps.output: Active crew qualification record in Jeppesen; domicile assignment confirmed; PBS eligibility flag set in iCrew
l4_steps.kpi: System activation within 24 hours of IOE sign-off; crew record data accuracy 100%; payroll activation lag ≤1 business day
l4_steps.pain_point: Data synchronisation between Jeppesen crew qualification records and SAP SuccessFactors payroll is manual at most carriers — activation delays cause pay errors and crew portal access failures on day 1 of line flying, generating HR ticket volume and eroding new hire confidence

l4_steps.name: Assign to initial PBS bid period and complete onboarding
l4_steps.role: Crew Planning Analyst / New Hire Pilot
l4_steps.input: Active crew qualification record; open roster positions for current bid period; onboarding task checklist
l4_steps.output: First PBS bid period assignment; completed onboarding compliance tasks (uniform fitting, airport ID, emergency equipment familiarisation, CBA acknowledgement)
l4_steps.kpi: Time from IOE completion to first revenue pairing ≤5 days; onboarding task completion rate 100% by day 30; year-1 voluntary attrition ≤8%
l4_steps.pain_point: New hires unfamiliar with Preferential Bidding System (PBS) mechanics consistently place suboptimal first bids, resulting in undesirable schedules and early attrition complaints; targeted PBS orientation reduces this but is rarely standardised in onboarding programmes, and Jeppesen CrewPlan offers no new-hire guided bidding mode

l4_steps.name: Detect Open Crew Position Requiring Deadhead
l4_steps.input: Schedule change event, crew absence report, or pairing modification trigger
l4_steps.output: Open position flag with required report time and destination station
l4_steps.kpi: Position detected within 30 min of trigger event; 95th-percentile detection latency
l4_steps.pain_point: Late notification from operations control reduces available positioning flight windows, forcing costlier interline or charter options

l4_steps.name: Calculate Deadhead Eligibility & Rest Window
l4_steps.input: Crew member duty history, block hours, and rest timestamps from pairing record
l4_steps.output: Earliest legal report time per FAR Part 117 / EASA FTL; rest compliance flag
l4_steps.kpi: 100% FAR Part 117 compliance on all deadhead assignments; 0 regulatory violations
l4_steps.pain_point: Cumulative duty and transport time ambiguity under FAR Part 117 §117.25; manual override risk when schedulers bypass system warnings under pressure

l4_steps.name: Identify Available Positioning Flight Options
l4_steps.input: Origin station, destination station, required arrival window
l4_steps.output: Ranked list of viable positioning flights with seat availability and timing feasibility
l4_steps.kpi: ≥3 routing options identified per positioning requirement; identification completed ≤15 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Limited own-metal frequency on thin or spoke routes forces interline deadheads at significantly higher cost and approval overhead

l4_steps.name: Check Own-Airline Seat Availability
l4_steps.input: Positioning flight options list, cabin inventory snapshot
l4_steps.output: Seat availability confirmation per candidate flight
l4_steps.kpi: Own-carrier deadhead utilisation rate ≥85% of all positioning trips
l4_steps.pain_point: High load factors on peak routes (>90% LF) eliminate deadhead seat inventory; conflicts arise with revenue upgrade requests in the same booking class

l4_steps.name: Request Interline or Charter Positioning
l4_steps.input: No own-carrier availability confirmed; positioning deadline and budget ceiling
l4_steps.output: Interline booking confirmation or charter request raised with vendor
l4_steps.kpi: Interline deadhead cost ≤$500 per segment average; charter approval ≤60 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Absence of interline agreements with ultra-low-cost carriers limits competitive options; charter approvals require multi-level sign-off, slowing time-critical positioning

l4_steps.name: Book Deadhead Seat & Issue Travel Document
l4_steps.input: Confirmed flight selection, crew ID and employee number
l4_steps.output: PNR booking record, crew boarding pass, travel authorisation number
l4_steps.kpi: Booking confirmed ≥4 hours before positioning flight departure; 98% booking success rate
l4_steps.pain_point: Deadhead bookings compete with upgrade inventory management; system priority rules inconsistently applied across stations, causing silent booking failures

l4_steps.name: Notify Crew of Deadhead Assignment via App
l4_steps.input: Confirmed PNR, flight details, report time, and destination duty assignment
l4_steps.output: Push notification delivered to crew mobile app; acknowledgment receipt logged
l4_steps.kpi: Crew notification issued ≥3 hours before check-in; acknowledgment rate ≥95% within 30 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Unacknowledged assignments discovered late trigger cascading delays; crew contact reliability degrades during IROPS when app server load peaks

l4_steps.name: Coordinate Priority Boarding with Departure Gate
l4_steps.input: Crew PNR, flight gate assignment, boarding time
l4_steps.output: Priority boarding flag applied to PNR; gate agent briefed on crew presence
l4_steps.kpi: Deadhead crew boarded before door close 100% of trips; 0 involuntary offloads
l4_steps.pain_point: Gate agent awareness of deadhead priority inconsistent across stations; crew offloaded during oversale situations without crew scheduling notification

l4_steps.name: Verify Crew Check-In Within Required Window
l4_steps.input: Check-in event, seat map, boarding pass issuance status
l4_steps.output: Boarding pass issued; seat confirmed; check-in timestamp logged
l4_steps.kpi: Check-in completed ≥90 min before STD (international) or ≥60 min (domestic) — 100% compliance
l4_steps.pain_point: Self-service kiosks cannot identify crew priority status; manual override at check-in desk required but not always flagged in AMS leading to seat assignment conflicts

l4_steps.name: Monitor Positioning Flight Departure Status
l4_steps.input: STD, real-time flight status feed from OAG Flight Status API
l4_steps.output: Departure alert triggered if delay ≥30 min detected against crew arrival window
l4_steps.kpi: Delay alert generated within 5 min of ATD divergence; monitoring coverage 100% of active deadheads
l4_steps.pain_point: Real-time flight status integration latency (up to 8 min) causes late crew re-planning; ATC data feed inconsistencies during high-traffic periods create false-negative alerts

l4_steps.name: Confirm Crew Boarded on Positioning Flight
l4_steps.input: Boarding scan data from gate reader
l4_steps.output: Crew-on-board confirmation record with timestamp
l4_steps.kpi: On-board confirmation received ≥15 min before block-out; 100% of tracked deadheads
l4_steps.pain_point: Boarding scan data not always relayed to crew scheduling in real time; crew off-loaded for weight-and-balance or oversale without crew scheduling notification causes undetected open positions

l4_steps.name: Confirm Crew Arrival at Destination Station
l4_steps.input: Positioning flight block-in time, crew self-report via mobile app
l4_steps.output: Arrival confirmation timestamp logged in pairing record
l4_steps.kpi: Arrival confirmed within 15 min of block-in; 100% of active positioning trips
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew app connectivity issues in remote or international airports; manual phone confirmation fallback increases coordinator workload during multi-disruption IROPS events

l4_steps.name: Validate Rest Compliance Before Activating Duty
l4_steps.input: Arrival timestamp, cumulative duty history, transport time log, FAR Part 117 rule set
l4_steps.output: Go / No-Go duty eligibility decision; compliance audit record
l4_steps.kpi: 0 FAR Part 117 violations; 100% FTL compliance audit pass rate; review completed ≤10 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Ambiguity in counting deadhead transport time against rest requirements under FAR Part 117 §117.25(d); grey-area interpretations vary by base chief pilot, creating inconsistent application

l4_steps.name: Activate Crew for Assigned Duty Pairing
l4_steps.input: Go decision from compliance check; destination duty pairing details
l4_steps.output: Crew activated in system; pairing record updated; downstream operations notified
l4_steps.kpi: Crew activation completed ≥45 min before STD of first duty leg; 98% on-time activation rate
l4_steps.pain_point: Late activations (<45 min before STD) trigger minimum connect time violations requiring re-planning; system does not auto-notify gate agents of late crew activation status

l4_steps.name: Initiate Disruption Recovery for Failed Positioning
l4_steps.input: Missed or critically delayed positioning flight; unresolved open crew position
l4_steps.output: Alternative coverage plan: standby activation, crew reassignment, or re-deadhead routing
l4_steps.kpi: Alternative solution identified within 20 min of confirmed disruption; 0 flights cancelled solely due to unresolved crew positioning failure
l4_steps.pain_point: Standby crew pool depleted during IROPS; simultaneous multi-station disruptions overwhelm scheduling coordinator capacity; re-deadhead approval chains add 30–45 min delay during peak disruption windows

l4_steps.name: Aggregate crew flight duty period records
l4_steps.input: Published rosters, completed duty reports, ACARS sign-on/sign-off logs
l4_steps.output: Crew duty history dataset; cumulative flight hours register
l4_steps.kpi: Data completeness ≥99% within 24 hrs of duty completion
l4_steps.pain_point: Missing ACARS sign-on/sign-off data during irregular ops causes duty time calculation gaps requiring manual correction in Jeppesen; sync delays post-disruption inflate analyst reconciliation workload by 30–40%

l4_steps.name: Extract simulator training completion records
l4_steps.input: Completed simulator session logs; CAE Simfinity session completion events
l4_steps.output: Training currency status per crew member; upcoming expiry alert list
l4_steps.kpi: Training record update latency ≤4 hrs post-session; record accuracy ≥99.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Third-party simulator vendor API reliability varies — CAE Simfinity batch exports rather than real-time push require overnight reconciliation; discrepancies between carrier records and CAE records require manual adjudication with vendor

l4_steps.name: Collect in-flight LOSA & IOE observation reports
l4_steps.input: Line Operational Safety Audit (LOSA) forms; Initial Operating Experience (IOE) completion records
l4_steps.output: Standardised crew observation reports; threat-and-error management (TEM) scores per crew
l4_steps.kpi: ≥2 line observations per crew member per 12-month rolling window; observation form completion rate ≥95%
l4_steps.pain_point: Check airman availability conflicts with revenue operations — scheduling a standards captain as observer removes a qualified crew member from a revenue flight; subjective scoring inconsistency across check airmen requires periodic inter-rater reliability calibration sessions (FAR Part 121.409)

l4_steps.name: Aggregate customer satisfaction scores by crew assignment
l4_steps.system: Medallia CX Platform / Amadeus Altéa PSS (crew-flight linkage)
l4_steps.input: Post-flight NPS surveys; in-flight service feedback; complaint records
l4_steps.output: Crew-attributed satisfaction scorecard; NPS and complaint rate per crew member
l4_steps.kpi: Crew-attributed NPS ≥72; cabin crew complaint rate <0.3 per 1,000 PAX
l4_steps.pain_point: Survey response rate <15% limits statistical significance at individual crew level — scores based on <5 responses are flagged as unreliable; Altéa crew-to-flight linkage requires manual reconciliation when irregular ops causes crew substitutions not captured in final manifest

l4_steps.name: Validate recurrent training compliance deadlines
l4_steps.input: Crew training currency records; FAR Part 121.433 compliance calendar; carrier AQP programme schedule
l4_steps.output: Training compliance status matrix; 30/60/90-day expiry alert distribution
l4_steps.kpi: Zero crew members operating with lapsed recurrent training; ≥30-day advance alert issued for 100% of expiring qualifications
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 121.433 recurrent training windows are crew-type specific and vary by AQP approval — Jeppesen qualification rules must be manually updated when FAA approves AQP amendments; last-minute scheduling conflicts (crew illness, irregular ops) cause near-miss compliance breaches requiring emergency simulator slots

l4_steps.name: Review proficiency check results and competency grades
l4_steps.system: CAE Simfinity Training Management / Jeppesen Crew Management
l4_steps.input: Completed proficiency check (PC) grade sheets; simulator session recordings; AQP competency unit scores
l4_steps.output: PC pass/fail determination; graded competency assessment per AQP unit; recheck scheduling flag
l4_steps.kpi: First-attempt PC pass rate ≥94%; recheck completion within 30 days of initial failure
l4_steps.pain_point: Inconsistent grading standards across check airmen require periodic inter-rater reliability audits — FAA ATOS inspectors have cited grading variance in Part 121 operator evaluations; simulator slot scarcity for MAX-type recurrent events (shared with new-entrant type rating candidates) causes recheck scheduling delays beyond the 30-day window

l4_steps.name: Verify medical certificate currency and fitness-for-duty status
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen Crew Management / CASS (Crew Authorisation & Scheduling System)
l4_steps.input: FAA First Class medical examination reports from AME; crew qualification records
l4_steps.output: Medical currency status flag per crew member; crew legal-to-fly determination
l4_steps.kpi: 100% medical certificate currency verified before scheduling assignment; zero FAR Part 61.23 violations
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA First Class medical certificate validity (12 months under age 40, 6 months over 40) requires proactive scheduling of AME appointments — AME scarcity in crew domicile cities (especially smaller hubs) causes crew members to approach expiry without confirmed exam slots; CASS medical flag propagation to Jeppesen rostering has 2–4 hr latency creating a window for illegal assignment

l4_steps.name: Assess type rating and route qualification currency
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen Crew Management / Amadeus Altéa PSS (crew qualification module)
l4_steps.input: Type rating certificates; route qualification records; recency requirements per FAR Part 121.439
l4_steps.output: Crew qualification matrix; route and fleet assignment eligibility flags
l4_steps.kpi: Qualification matrix accuracy ≥99.9%; zero illegal crew assignments attributable to qualification data error
l4_steps.pain_point: Dual-system qualification storage (Altéa holds PSS-level eligibility; Jeppesen holds operational crew management records) creates synchronisation risk — a qualification update applied in one system but not the other can result in illegal assignment; no real-time bidirectional API between Altéa and Jeppesen requires manual reconciliation after each qualification event

l4_steps.name: Compile integrated performance scorecard per crew member
l4_steps.system: AWS Redshift / Tableau (crew performance analytics dashboard)
l4_steps.input: Duty records from Jeppesen; training grades from CAE Simfinity; LOSA scores; CSAT data from Medallia; FOQA exceedance flags
l4_steps.output: Consolidated crew performance scorecard (quarterly); percentile ranking within crew category
l4_steps.kpi: Scorecard completion rate 100% within 30 days of quarter-end; data freshness ≤24 hrs from source systems
l4_steps.pain_point: Five-source ETL pipeline (Jeppesen, CAE Simfinity, Medallia, FOQA, ASAP) requires ongoing maintenance — schema changes by any vendor break ingestion pipelines; AWS Redshift refresh latency spikes during post-irregular-ops recovery periods when data volumes are 3–5× normal

l4_steps.name: Review FOQA exceedances and ASAP safety report history
l4_steps.system: FOQA (Flight Operational Quality Assurance platform) / ASAP tracking system
l4_steps.input: FOQA exceedance alert reports; ASAP self-disclosure submissions; ATC incident notifications
l4_steps.output: Safety event summary per crew member; corrective action flags; ASAP ERC review outcomes
l4_steps.kpi: FOQA exceedance rate <2.5 per 1,000 flight hours; ASAP report ERC review cycle ≤14 days
l4_steps.pain_point: ASAP programme confidentiality provisions (FAA MOU requirement) restrict sharing of individual ASAP submissions with HR performance systems — safety managers must deconflict performance use of safety data from ASAP protections to avoid chilling voluntary disclosure; FOQA data volume from 800+ aircraft requires automated triage algorithm to prioritise analyst review

l4_steps.name: Conduct formal performance appraisal interview
l4_steps.input: Compiled performance scorecard; training records summary; safety event history; prior appraisal ratings
l4_steps.output: Signed performance appraisal document; development goals for next period; performance rating
l4_steps.kpi: Appraisal completion rate ≥98% within performance period; crew satisfaction with appraisal process ≥75% (internal survey)
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP SuccessFactors has no native integration with Jeppesen Crew Management — crew performance data must be manually exported as CSV and uploaded to SuccessFactors before each appraisal cycle, creating data staleness risk; union CBA provisions (ALPA, AFA contracts) restrict appraisal content, frequency, and the use of ASAP/FOQA data in formal evaluations

l4_steps.name: Initiate Performance Improvement Plan with union review
l4_steps.input: Below-threshold performance appraisal; applicable CBA provisions; HR policy framework
l4_steps.output: Signed PIP document; action timeline with milestone dates; union representative notification
l4_steps.kpi: PIP initiation within 10 business days of appraisal decision; ≥70% PIP completion success rate (crew returns to standard performance)
l4_steps.pain_point: ALPA and AFA CBAs impose strict procedural requirements on PIP content and duration — legal review adds 5–10 business days before issuance; PIP templates must differ by crew category (captain, first officer, flight attendant) due to different contractual language, increasing HR preparation workload

l4_steps.name: Schedule targeted remedial simulator or recurrent training
l4_steps.system: CAE Simfinity (simulator booking) / Jeppesen Crew Management
l4_steps.input: PIP-specified training requirements; simulator capacity calendar; crew availability roster
l4_steps.output: Confirmed simulator training assignment; crew notification; updated Jeppesen training record
l4_steps.kpi: Remedial training scheduled within 21 days of PIP initiation; simulator slot utilisation ≥85%
l4_steps.pain_point: Q4 recurrent training demand surge (driven by anniversary-month training windows clustering in autumn) competes directly with remedial training scheduling — PIP trainees are lower-priority than regulatory recurrent events, causing delays beyond the 21-day target; CAE Simfinity booking API rate limits cause queuing delays during bulk roster update events

l4_steps.name: Monitor PIP milestone progress and conduct gate reviews
l4_steps.input: Completed training results; line observation scores; PIP milestone schedule
l4_steps.output: PIP progress report; pass/continue/escalate/terminate decision per gate
l4_steps.kpi: Gate reviews completed on schedule ≥95%; escalation decision issued within 5 business days of missed milestone
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP SuccessFactors milestone alert configuration requires manual setup per PIP — no automated trigger from Jeppesen training completion events; inconsistent documentation standards across fleet types make cross-fleet PIP outcome comparisons unreliable for HR trend analysis

l4_steps.name: Generate FAA/AQP regulatory compliance report
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen Crew Management / AWS S3 (compliance data lake)
l4_steps.input: Crew qualification records; training completion data; medical certificate currency; PC results
l4_steps.output: AQP compliance report; ATOS audit evidence package; FAA programme approval data
l4_steps.kpi: Regulatory report submission on-time rate 100%; zero FAA violation notices attributable to reporting failures
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 121 Subpart Y (AQP) reporting requires carrier-specific competency unit data formats not natively exported by Jeppesen — manual report assembly from three source systems increases error risk during FAA ATOS audit periods; AWS S3 data lake partitioning strategy for crew records requires careful schema governance to support ad-hoc FAA data requests

l4_steps.name: Update crew qualification records in PSS and crew system
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS / Jeppesen Crew Management
l4_steps.input: Completed training events; new qualifications issued; medical certificate updates; PIP outcomes
l4_steps.output: Updated qualification eligibility flags in Altéa and Jeppesen; crew scheduling restrictions lifted or applied
l4_steps.kpi: Record update latency ≤4 hrs post-qualification event; dual-system sync accuracy ≥99.99%
l4_steps.pain_point: Dual-system update requirement (Altéa + Jeppesen) with no real-time sync creates a window during which Altéa reflects updated qualification but Jeppesen does not (or vice versa), enabling an illegal crew assignment if a scheduling query is run in the lagging system during the sync gap

l4_steps.name: Archive performance records per regulatory retention policy
l4_steps.input: Performance appraisals; PIP documents; training records; safety event reports; medical records
l4_steps.output: Archived records package; retention schedule compliance confirmation; access control audit trail
l4_steps.kpi: Record archival within 5 business days of period close; zero GDPR or FAR Part 121.683 retention violations
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 121.683 requires training records retention for the duration of employment plus 1 year, while GDPR (applicable to EU crew and EU-operated routes) mandates data minimisation and right-to-erasure — these requirements conflict for international crew records and require per-jurisdiction retention rules not supported by default AWS S3 lifecycle policies

l4_steps.name: Extract completed duty periods from crew system
l4_steps.input: Flight completion signals and crew check-in/check-out events
l4_steps.output: Raw duty period records per crew member for the pay period
l4_steps.kpi: Data extraction completeness ≥99.9% of operated flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Late ACARS sign-off events or manual overrides in Jeppesen can produce duplicate or null duty records, requiring manual reconciliation before payroll can proceed

l4_steps.name: Validate actual block times against ACARS data
l4_steps.input: ACARS OUT/OFF/ON/IN timestamps for each flight leg
l4_steps.output: Validated block-hours per leg with variance flags
l4_steps.kpi: Block-time discrepancy rate <0.5% of legs per pay cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS message loss over oceanic tracks or VHF dropouts can leave gaps requiring manual entry from paper OFP, introducing audit risk

l4_steps.name: Adjudicate duty time discrepancies with crew
l4_steps.input: Flagged duty records with variance >2 minutes vs ACARS
l4_steps.output: Crew-acknowledged corrected duty record; updated in Jeppesen
l4_steps.kpi: Discrepancy resolution cycle time ≤24 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Pilots and cabin crew may contest block-time adjustments that reduce pay — disputes require union observer involvement under most CBAs, extending resolution time

l4_steps.name: Lock finalised duty records for pay period
l4_steps.input: Resolved and validated duty periods for all crew
l4_steps.output: Locked, immutable duty record set ready for pay rule application
l4_steps.kpi: Records locked ≥48 hours before payroll cut-off
l4_steps.pain_point: Late crew changes from irregular ops (IROPS) in the final days of a pay period can force record reopening, risking payroll deadline breach

l4_steps.name: Load CBA pay rules for crew category
l4_steps.input: Locked duty records; active CBA rate tables by crew category (Captain, First Officer, Flight Attendant)
l4_steps.output: Rule set applied to each crew member's records for the pay period
l4_steps.kpi: CBA rule table accuracy rate 100% (zero miscategorisation)
l4_steps.pain_point: Airlines operating multiple crew agreements (pilots vs cabin crew vs contract ground) must maintain separate rate tables in SAP SuccessFactors; version mismatches after CBA renegotiation cause systematic overpayment or underpayment

l4_steps.name: Calculate block/credit hours and per diem
l4_steps.input: Locked duty records; CBA credit-hour conversion rules; per diem rate by city-pair
l4_steps.output: Gross flight pay and per diem amounts per crew member
l4_steps.kpi: Payroll calculation variance vs manual audit sample ≤0.1%
l4_steps.pain_point: CBAs often specify credit hours that differ from actual block hours (e.g. scheduled vs actual, or minimum leg credit), requiring complex conditional logic that is error-prone when rates change mid-year

l4_steps.name: Evaluate and apply minimum-guarantee provisions
l4_steps.input: Calculated credit hours; CBA minimum monthly guarantee thresholds
l4_steps.output: Adjusted pay figure with minimum guarantee top-up applied where triggered
l4_steps.kpi: Minimum guarantee errors detected in post-payroll audit ≤0.2%
l4_steps.pain_point: IROPS-driven trip removals can drop crew below the monthly minimum guarantee, triggering a top-up that must be calculated separately from regular flight pay — SAP wage-type configuration must handle this without double-counting

l4_steps.name: Apply premiums, overrides, and special pay components
l4_steps.input: Base pay calculation; premium triggers (international, redeye, equipment type, senior position)
l4_steps.output: Fully loaded gross pay record including all CBA-mandated premium components
l4_steps.kpi: Premium application accuracy ≥99.8% validated against CBA schedule
l4_steps.pain_point: Introduction of new aircraft types (e.g. A320neo vs B737 MAX) or new international routes creates CBA premium ambiguity until Letter of Agreement (LOA) is ratified — interim pay must be tracked and retroactively corrected

l4_steps.name: Validate daily flight duty period against FAR Part 117
l4_steps.input: Finalised duty records; FAR Part 117 FDP and rest-period limit tables
l4_steps.output: Compliance status flag per duty period (Pass / Warning / Violation)
l4_steps.kpi: FAR Part 117 violation rate 0 per pay cycle; automated check coverage 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 117 FDP limits vary by time-of-day start and number of flight segments — Jeppesen rules engine requires precise configuration and must be updated whenever ICAO or FAA revises rest requirements

l4_steps.name: Check cumulative hours against 28-day and 365-day limits
l4_steps.input: Rolling 28-day and 365-day block-hour totals per crew member
l4_steps.output: Cumulative hours compliance report; breach flags for affected crew
l4_steps.kpi: Zero crew members exceeding FAR Part 117 cumulative limits (100 hrs/28 days; 1,000 hrs/365 days)
l4_steps.pain_point: Cross-border operations and wet-lease arrangements complicate cumulative tracking when hours are flown under different AOCs — hours from partner carriers may not be visible in Jeppesen without manual import

l4_steps.name: Escalate violations and trigger roster correction
l4_steps.input: Breach flags from Step 3.2; crew roster for remainder of period
l4_steps.output: Corrected roster with non-compliant crew removed from duty; compliance memo issued
l4_steps.kpi: Violation-to-resolution cycle time ≤4 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Grounding crew mid-period to cure a FAR Part 117 breach triggers crew-shortage cascades and CBA compensation obligations (deadhead pay, hotel, reassignment premiums) that add unplanned payroll cost

l4_steps.name: Approve validated hours for payroll submission
l4_steps.input: Compliance-cleared duty and hours records
l4_steps.output: Approved payroll data package signed off by Crew Pay Manager
l4_steps.kpi: Payroll approval completed ≥36 hours before payroll cut-off
l4_steps.pain_point: Approval bottleneck when a single manager owns sign-off for hundreds of crew — absence or IROPS event during cut-off window can delay entire payroll run

l4_steps.name: Transfer approved pay data to SAP SuccessFactors
l4_steps.input: Approved payroll data package from Jeppesen in SFTP/XML format
l4_steps.output: Pay records loaded into SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central Payroll wage types
l4_steps.kpi: File transfer success rate 100%; record reconciliation count match before payroll run
l4_steps.pain_point: Schema mismatches between Jeppesen export format and SAP wage-type structure require a custom integration layer — changes to either system can silently break the interface until the next payroll run

l4_steps.name: Execute payroll calculation run in SAP
