l4_steps.input: Loaded wage types; tax tables; statutory deduction rates; benefit deductions
l4_steps.output: Gross-to-net payroll results; payslip data; GL posting document
l4_steps.kpi: Payroll error log: zero critical errors; warning resolution ≤2 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Multi-state tax residency for crew who live in a different state from their crew base requires correct SAP tax-area assignment — errors create IRS compliance exposure and retroactive correction cost

l4_steps.name: Generate pay advices and post GL entries
l4_steps.input: Approved gross-to-net payroll results
l4_steps.output: Digital pay advices distributed to crew; GL postings to crew cost centres
l4_steps.kpi: Pay advice delivery within 24 hours of payroll run; GL posting error rate 0%
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew cost-centre allocation requires splitting payroll costs across multiple operational cost centres when a crew member flew for different fleets or bases in the same period — misallocation distorts fleet P&L reporting

l4_steps.name: Reconcile payroll cost vs crew operations budget
l4_steps.input: GL payroll postings; crew operations budget from SAP CO; headcount actuals
l4_steps.output: Variance report by crew category and cost centre; commentary on material variances
l4_steps.kpi: Payroll-to-budget variance explained ≥95% within 3 business days of payroll run
l4_steps.pain_point: IROPS months generate significant unbudgeted premium and minimum-guarantee costs that distort variance analysis — Finance needs a dedicated IROPS payroll variance code to separate structural from operational pay drivers

l4_steps.name: Generate crew hours utilisation and fatigue report
l4_steps.input: Finalised hours data from Jeppesen; payroll cost data from SAP S/4HANA
l4_steps.output: Monthly crew hours utilisation dashboard; fatigue risk indicator by base
l4_steps.kpi: Crew utilisation rate ≥85% of contractual hours; fatigue indicator trend published ≤5 days post-period
l4_steps.pain_point: Combining hours data from Jeppesen with cost data from SAP requires a data pipeline that must be maintained across system upgrades — ad hoc Tableau reports built on inconsistent extracts produce conflicting crew productivity figures for leadership

l4_steps.name: Archive payroll and hours records per FAA requirements
l4_steps.input: Finalised pay advices; duty records; compliance reports
l4_steps.output: Archived records retained per FAR 121.683 (24 months minimum) with audit trail
l4_steps.kpi: Record archive completeness 100%; retrieval SLA ≤4 hours for FAA audit request
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR 121.683 mandates 24-month retention for crew duty records; GDPR and state privacy laws (CCPA) impose conflicting obligations on how long certain payroll data can be held — retention policy must be reviewed with legal each year

l4_steps.name: Activate DCS flight check-in window
l4_steps.input: Flight schedule activation trigger from PSS; T-24h threshold reached
l4_steps.output: Check-in window open; flight record active in DCS with configured limits
l4_steps.kpi: Check-in window live within 2 min of scheduled T-24h open time
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa DCS activation can lag if PSS flight record contains schedule irregularity codes from prior disruption; agents must manually resolve before window opens

l4_steps.name: Transmit APIS data to government gateway
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa DCS + SITA APIS Gateway
l4_steps.input: Passenger PNR records with passport/travel document data collected at booking
l4_steps.output: APIS message transmitted to CBP (US) or destination country border authority
l4_steps.kpi: APIS transmission ≥99.5% success rate; all records sent ≥60 min pre-departure
l4_steps.pain_point: Incomplete passport data in PNR (collected via NDC or OTA) prevents automated APIS; agents must manually collect at counter, increasing queue time by avg 4 min/pax

l4_steps.name: Validate APIS clearance response from authority
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa DCS + SITA APIS Gateway
l4_steps.input: Government APIS response message (OK / Inhibit / Further Check)
l4_steps.output: Passenger flagged as cleared or held; DCS boarding permission set accordingly
l4_steps.kpi: APIS clearance rate ≥99.8%; inhibit rate <0.2% on domestic sectors
l4_steps.pain_point: CBP Inhibit responses arrive without explanation; agents must contact CBP Passenger Analysis Unit directly, causing delays of 15–45 min with no SLA guarantee

l4_steps.name: Process web/mobile self-service check-in
l4_steps.input: Passenger booking reference or e-ticket number; opens T-24h pre-departure
l4_steps.output: Mobile or PDF boarding pass issued; seat confirmed (where applicable)
l4_steps.kpi: Web/mobile check-in adoption ≥65% of pax; avg session completion <3 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa Web Check-In has limited SSR (special service request) handling — passengers requiring wheelchair, UMNR, or PETC must complete check-in at counter, reducing self-service deflection rate

l4_steps.name: Process airport kiosk check-in
l4_steps.system: SITA CUSS Kiosk + Amadeus Altéa DCS
l4_steps.input: Booking reference, e-ticket barcode scan, or passport MRZ scan
l4_steps.output: Boarding pass printed at kiosk; baggage tag receipt if bags declared
l4_steps.kpi: Kiosk transaction time ≤90 sec avg; kiosk availability ≥98.5% uptime
l4_steps.pain_point: CUSS kiosk MRZ readers degrade in high-throughput environments; passport scan failure rate >5% triggers agent-assisted queue diversion, negating kiosk capacity benefit

l4_steps.name: Counter check-in for SSR & irregular pax
l4_steps.input: Passenger queue; SSR flags (WCHR, UMNR, PETC, excess baggage, name discrepancy)
l4_steps.output: Check-in complete with SSR coded; boarding pass issued; special handling instructions added to PNR
l4_steps.kpi: Counter transaction time ≤4 min/pax; SSR coding accuracy 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa DCS SSR codes not always consumed by downstream ramp/catering systems in real time; WCHR requests can fail to appear on OCS load sheet if coded after T-45 min

l4_steps.name: Verify travel documents & eligibility to travel
l4_steps.input: Passenger passport, visa, travel document; destination entry requirements from Timatic
l4_steps.output: Document check passed or failed; boarding authorization set in DCS
l4_steps.kpi: Document check failure rate <0.5%; inadmissible pax rate <0.1% of international sector pax
l4_steps.pain_point: Timatic database lags behind real-time government policy changes (e.g., COVID-era entry requirements updated faster than Timatic refresh); airlines face deportation liability and repatriation costs averaging $3,000–$5,000 per inadmissible passenger

l4_steps.name: Issue boarding pass and confirm check-in
l4_steps.input: Completed check-in record; APIS cleared; seat assigned
l4_steps.output: Boarding pass (mobile wallet, PDF, or thermal print) with barcode; PNR status updated to HK
l4_steps.kpi: Boarding pass issuance within 30 sec of check-in completion; barcode scan success rate ≥99.9% at gate
l4_steps.pain_point: Mobile boarding pass wallet integration (Apple Wallet / Google Wallet) requires Altéa connector; third-party OTA bookings may not receive push update if itinerary changed post-check-in, causing boarding pass mismatch at gate

l4_steps.name: Accept, weigh & measure checked baggage
l4_steps.input: Passenger with checked bags at counter or self-service bag drop; ticket with baggage allowance
l4_steps.output: Bag weight/dimensions recorded in DCS; excess baggage fee calculated if applicable
l4_steps.kpi: Baggage acceptance transaction ≤90 sec; excess bag fee collection accuracy 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA BagDrop scale calibration drift causes weight discrepancies; bags near allowance threshold require re-weighing at counter, increasing queue time and creating customer disputes

l4_steps.name: Print & apply IATA 10-digit baggage tag
l4_steps.input: Accepted bag; passenger PNR with flight and destination data
l4_steps.output: IATA 10-digit bag tag printed and applied; bag record created in WorldTracer
l4_steps.kpi: Bag tag print success rate ≥99.8%; bag tag scan read rate at sortation ≥99.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa bag tag thermal print quality degrades in high-humidity airport environments; low-contrast tags fail sortation OCR/barcode readers, causing misrouting — IATA Resolution 753 tracking mandates every bag event be captured

l4_steps.name: Induct bags into EDS/TSA screening belt
l4_steps.system: Airport EDS System (TSA-operated) + SITA Baggage Reconciliation System
l4_steps.input: Tagged, accepted bags inducted at sortation entry point
l4_steps.output: Bag inducted into automated screening belt; bag status updated to 'In Screening'
l4_steps.kpi: Bag induction-to-screening time ≤15 min; EDS throughput ≥1,200 bags/hr per lane
l4_steps.pain_point: TSA EDS systems are airport authority / TSA-owned, not airline-controlled; EDS lane outages cause cascading bag delays with no airline SLA recourse — peak holiday periods see queue back-ups exceeding 45 min

l4_steps.name: Resolve EDS alarm — security secondary screening
l4_steps.role: TSA Security Officer / Baggage Services Agent
l4_steps.system: Airport EDS System + SITA Baggage Reconciliation System
l4_steps.input: EDS alarm triggered on specific bag; bag diverted to manual inspection lane
l4_steps.output: Bag cleared after manual inspection or removed from flight; BRS status updated
l4_steps.kpi: Secondary screening resolution time ≤20 min pre-departure; cleared bags ≥95% make flight
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual EDS secondary screening has no airline-controlled SLA; if passenger has already boarded, policy requires offloading all bags and re-matching — per TSA requirement — causing departure delay averaging 22 min

l4_steps.name: Open gate & configure boarding group sequence
l4_steps.system: SITA Airport Management System (AMS) + Amadeus Altéa DCS
l4_steps.input: DCS flight record with check-in close count; gate assignment from AMS
l4_steps.output: Gate screen displays boarding groups; boarding group logic configured in DCS
l4_steps.kpi: Gate open ≥35 min pre-departure; boarding group display accuracy 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Gate assignments change frequently due to aircraft swaps; SITA AMS gate change notification can lag DCS by 3–5 min, causing agents to set up at wrong gate — high at congested hubs like ATL and ORD

l4_steps.name: Assess oversale position & solicit volunteers
l4_steps.input: Check-in close count vs. aircraft capacity; upgrade waitlist; standby list
l4_steps.output: Oversale position confirmed; VDB (voluntary denied boarding) offer issued if overbooked
l4_steps.kpi: VDB offer initiated ≥25 min pre-departure; IDB (involuntary) rate <0.05 per 10,000 boarded (DOT threshold)
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa DCS overbooking display does not auto-factor no-show passengers from connecting flights until T-15 min; late confirmation of actual seat count means VDB offers are solicited unnecessarily or too late for proper compensation negotiation

l4_steps.name: Process VDB compensation & rebook denied pax
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa DCS + Airline Voucher System
l4_steps.input: Volunteer passenger confirmed for VDB; compensation amount per DOT 14 CFR Part 250
l4_steps.output: VDB compensation issued (cash/voucher/miles); pax rebooked on next available service
l4_steps.kpi: VDB compensation processing time ≤8 min; rebooking on same-day flight ≥85% of VDB cases
l4_steps.pain_point: Voucher issuance system integration with Altéa DCS is not real-time at all stations; agents at outstations must use paper vouchers subject to fraud risk and delayed reconciliation in SAP S/4HANA AR

l4_steps.name: Scan boarding passes & verify pax identity
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa DCS + SITA Gate Reader
l4_steps.input: Passenger presenting boarding pass (mobile/paper) at gate scanner
l4_steps.output: Boarding pass scanned; pax status updated to 'Boarded' in DCS; seat confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: Gate scan throughput ≥30 pax/min; scan success rate ≥99.5%; first scan read rate ≥99%
l4_steps.pain_point: Mobile boarding pass screen brightness and barcode display inconsistency (especially on cracked screens) causes scan failures; SITA gate reader firmware version mismatches with Altéa DCS on shared CUTE gates cause intermittent rejections during irregular ops re-accommodation

l4_steps.name: Perform final headcount & manifest reconciliation
l4_steps.input: Boarding complete; gate close signal; boarded pax count from DCS
l4_steps.output: Final passenger manifest reconciled; pax count confirmed against physical headcount
l4_steps.kpi: Manifest accuracy 100% (regulatory — FAR 121.693); reconciliation completed ≥5 min pre-departure
l4_steps.pain_point: Gate reader offline events (network drop at remote stands) cause boarding records to queue locally and sync after pushback begins; manifest can show in-transit counts that require captain confirmation, delaying doors-closed by 3–8 min

l4_steps.name: Transmit final load sheet & close flight in DCS
l4_steps.input: Reconciled pax count; final baggage and cargo weights; zero fuel weight from ramp
l4_steps.output: Final load sheet transmitted to cockpit via ACARS; DCS flight status set to Departed
l4_steps.kpi: Load sheet transmitted ≥3 min pre-pushback; captain acceptance acknowledgement received 100% of flights
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS OOOI message timing and load sheet transmission depend on aircraft avionics connectivity; older narrowbody aircraft without VHF ACARS datalink require VHF voice relay, increasing workload for dispatch and introducing manual transcription errors in weight & balance

l4_steps.name: Verify passenger allowance in PSS
l4_steps.input: Passenger PNR, ticket class, frequent flyer tier
l4_steps.output: Baggage allowance entitlement confirmed; excess fee notification triggered
l4_steps.kpi: Allowance lookup time ≤10 sec; fee notification accuracy ≥99%
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa allowance rules do not sync in real-time with codeshare partner PSS, forcing manual overrides and creating revenue leakage on interline itineraries

l4_steps.name: Weigh and measure baggage at counter
l4_steps.system: SITA Common Use Terminal Equipment (CUTE) with integrated scale
l4_steps.input: Passenger-presented baggage
l4_steps.output: Weight and dimension record; excess baggage charge calculated
l4_steps.kpi: Average bag acceptance time ≤90 sec per bag; scale accuracy ±0.1 kg
l4_steps.pain_point: Scale calibration drift at high-volume counters causes inconsistent weight readings; CUTE has no automated recalibration alert, so discrepancies are caught only during periodic QA audits

l4_steps.name: Collect excess baggage fees
l4_steps.input: Excess weight or piece determination from step 1.2
l4_steps.output: Fee collected and recorded in PNR; EMD (Electronic Miscellaneous Document) issued
l4_steps.kpi: Excess fee collection rate ≥98% of chargeable bags
l4_steps.pain_point: Agents waiving fees at discretion without supervisory approval triggers revenue leakage estimated at $30–50 per waived bag; Altéa has no mandatory approval workflow for fee waivers at Level 1 agent access

l4_steps.name: Print bag tag and transmit BSM
l4_steps.input: Confirmed weight, destination, passenger itinerary
l4_steps.output: IATA 10-digit barcode bag tag affixed; Baggage Source Message (BSM) transmitted to BHS and destination airport
l4_steps.kpi: BSM transmission accuracy ≥99.5%; BSM delivery to BHS ≤5 sec
l4_steps.pain_point: BSM transmission lag >30 sec to downstream stations causes missed sortation windows on tight connections; IATA Resolution 753 mandates scan tracking from this point but most carriers lack RFID at check-in, relying on barcode-only

l4_steps.name: Induct bag into automated EDS screening
l4_steps.system: Smiths Detection CTX / L3 ProVision Explosive Detection System (EDS)
l4_steps.input: Tagged bag inducted onto inline conveyor belt with BSM
l4_steps.output: Bag inducted into screening lane; screening initiated
l4_steps.kpi: Screening throughput ≥1,200 bags/hr per lane; induction reject rate ≤0.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Legacy inline EDS at secondary airports cannot handle post-pandemic capacity surge; single-lane configurations create 20–30 min queue backlogs during peak departures, directly causing departure delays

l4_steps.name: Evaluate automated threat detection result
l4_steps.system: Smiths Detection EDS console / L3 Technologies automated threat recognition (ATR)
l4_steps.input: CT scan image and ATR algorithm output
l4_steps.output: Clear or Suspect determination; bag status updated in screening system
l4_steps.kpi: Automated clear rate ≥85%; false-positive rate ≤12%
l4_steps.pain_point: CT systems generate 10–15% false-positive rates for dense consumer items (lithium batteries, laptops), driving manual inspection queues that delay affected bags by 8–15 min and disrupt sortation sequence

l4_steps.name: Conduct manual bag search and resolve status
l4_steps.system: TSA PARIS (Passenger and Baggage Reconciliation) / SITA WorldTracer
l4_steps.input: Suspect bag flagged by ATR; passenger paged if required
l4_steps.output: Cleared, held, or offloaded determination; bag status updated; airline notified
l4_steps.kpi: Manual resolution time ≤15 min per bag; offload-to-notification time ≤5 min
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated link between TSA PARIS resolution status and airline BHS sortation system; cleared bags require a manual phone call to ground ops to re-inject, introducing misrouting risk and operator dependency during irregular operations

l4_steps.name: Sort bag to destination make-up area via BHS
l4_steps.system: SITA BagManager / Airport BHS (Vanderlande BAGTRAX / Siemens automated sorter)
l4_steps.input: BSM data, flight departure time, make-up area assignment
l4_steps.output: Bag routed to correct make-up carousel or transfer belt
l4_steps.kpi: Sortation accuracy ≥99.7%; late bags to make-up ≤1% of total
l4_steps.pain_point: BHS sorter reading errors on damaged, bent, or folded barcoded bag tags cause misroutes; RFID fallback absent at most secondary airports despite IATA Resolution 753 requirement for 4-scan tracking — misrouted bags have no automated recovery path

l4_steps.name: Build ULD or loose-load baggage cart
l4_steps.input: Sorted bags arriving at make-up area; ULD build plan from load controller
l4_steps.output: Loaded ULD or baggage cart with physical manifest; weight estimate recorded
l4_steps.kpi: ULD build completion ≥30 min before scheduled departure; weight estimate variance ≤2%
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual ULD build-up has no real-time weight tracking — ramp agents estimate bag weight by handling; cumulative error causes load rebalancing at aircraft hold, adding avg 4–8 min to departure preparation

l4_steps.name: Reconcile bag count against active PAX list
l4_steps.system: SITA BagManager / Amadeus Altéa Departure Control System (DCS)
l4_steps.input: Loaded ULD manifest; active (boarded + checked-in) passenger list
l4_steps.output: Bag count confirmed or discrepancy flagged for investigation
l4_steps.kpi: Pre-load reconciliation accuracy ≥99.5%; discrepancy resolution time ≤10 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Disconnected systems between check-in (Altéa DCS) and ramp (BagManager) mean reconciliation relies on manual counts at make-up; count gaps widen at off-hub outstations with limited IT infrastructure and no dedicated ramp IT support

l4_steps.name: Transport ULDs and carts to aircraft
l4_steps.system: SITA Airport Management System (AMS) / Ramp Resource Management
l4_steps.input: Departure time, gate assignment, confirmed ULD manifest
l4_steps.output: ULDs delivered to aircraft within loading window
l4_steps.kpi: Bags at aircraft ≥25 min before scheduled departure; tug utilisation ≥80%
l4_steps.pain_point: Late gate changes (≤15 min before departure) force ULD re-routing on congested apron without automated rerouting guidance; ramp agents coordinate via radio only, causing ULD queuing conflicts and delay attribution to ground ops

l4_steps.name: Load baggage into aircraft hold per W&B plan
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen LoadPlanner / Ultramain Weight & Balance System
l4_steps.input: ULD manifest, aircraft hold configuration, W&B loading sequence
l4_steps.output: Bags loaded per load plan; hold positions recorded; loading confirmation sent to load controller
l4_steps.kpi: Hold loading complete ≥15 min before departure (D-15); W&B CG within ±1% of plan
l4_steps.pain_point: Real-time W&B updates require accurate bag weights from check-in; estimated weights (used when CUTE scales drift) increase fuel burn by 0.1–0.3% per flight and may require unplanned last-minute cargo offload to maintain CG envelope

l4_steps.name: Reconcile loaded bags and offload no-shows
l4_steps.system: SITA BagManager / Amadeus Altéa Departure Control System (DCS)
l4_steps.input: Final loaded bag count; departure passenger list (after boarding gate closes)
l4_steps.output: Load sheet signed off; no-fly bags identified and physically offloaded; NOTOC updated
l4_steps.kpi: 100% reconciliation before door closure; unaccompanied bag offload ≤10 min from identification
l4_steps.pain_point: ICAO Annex 17 requires offloading bags of passengers who check in but do not board; manual hold search for no-show bags averages 8–12 min delay per occurrence and is non-negotiable — no technology currently automates the physical search

l4_steps.name: Offload baggage from aircraft on arrival
l4_steps.system: SITA Airport Management System (AMS) / SITA BagManager
l4_steps.input: Aircraft block-in confirmation; hold manifest
l4_steps.output: All bags offloaded; scan event logged per IATA Resolution 753 4-point tracking requirement
l4_steps.kpi: First bag on belt ≤20 min from block-in (domestic); ≤25 min (international)
l4_steps.pain_point: Short-turn flights (≤45 min ground time) require simultaneous offload and inbound load operations; ramp agents coordinate only via radio with no automated sequencing tool, increasing error rate and first-bag time during high-rotation operations

l4_steps.name: Deliver bags to assigned baggage claim belt
l4_steps.system: SITA BagManager / Airport BHS claim belt controller / FIDS
l4_steps.input: Offloaded bags; belt assignment from airport ops; flight arrival data
l4_steps.output: Bags on reclaim belt; passenger belt notification displayed on FIDS
l4_steps.kpi: Last bag on belt ≤35 min from block-in; on-time belt delivery rate ≥92%
l4_steps.pain_point: Belt assignment conflicts during irregular operations (multiple delayed arrivals simultaneously) cause commingling of bags from different flights; commingling increases WorldTracer PIR filings by ~30% during IROPS windows and triggers EC 261/2004 and DOT compensation exposure

l4_steps.name: Identify and file PIR for mishandled bags
l4_steps.input: Unclaimed bags at belt; passenger self-report; gap in IATA Resolution 753 scan trail
l4_steps.output: Property Irregularity Report (PIR) filed in WorldTracer; passenger notified with file reference
l4_steps.kpi: PIR filing time ≤10 min from passenger report; mishandling rate ≤5 per 1,000 passengers (IATA industry target)
l4_steps.pain_point: Missing intermediate scans (induction, sortation, or loading) leave no audit trail for liability disputes under EC 261/2004 and DOT baggage rules; WorldTracer matching fails without a complete scan history, leaving agents unable to locate bag origin or last-seen point

l4_steps.name: Trace, recover and return mishandled baggage
l4_steps.system: SITA WorldTracer / baggage delivery partner (Deliver.com / BagsVIP)
l4_steps.input: PIR record; scan history; last-known location from BagManager
l4_steps.output: Bag located; delivery to passenger arranged; WorldTracer case closed
l4_steps.kpi: 80% of mishandled bags returned within 24 hrs; permanently lost bag rate ≤0.5 per 1,000 passengers
l4_steps.pain_point: WorldTracer matching depends on accurate IATA barcode scans; damaged tags with no RFID fallback leave bags stranded in 'no-read' queues at transfer hubs with no automated escalation workflow — cases age beyond 5-day threshold, triggering DOT delayed baggage compensation requirements

l4_steps.name: Capture Property Irregularity Report at arrival hall
l4_steps.input: Passenger complaint at baggage claim; flight arrival manifest
l4_steps.output: PIR reference number; AHL (mishandled bag) file opened in WorldTracer
l4_steps.kpi: PIR captured within 20 min of carousel clearance ≥98%
l4_steps.pain_point: High passenger volumes at hub airports cause PIR queue backlogs; agents default to paper forms that delay WorldTracer entry by 2–4 hrs

l4_steps.name: Verify PNR and bag tag details in Altéa
l4_steps.input: Passenger boarding pass or booking reference; PIR form
l4_steps.output: Confirmed bag tag number(s), itinerary, and contact details linked to PIR
l4_steps.kpi: PNR match rate ≥99.5%; missing bag tag resolved via passenger description within 15 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Passengers without digital boarding passes cannot self-serve via kiosk; paper bag tags occasionally unreadable after sortation damage

l4_steps.name: Search local carousel, offload area, and left baggage
l4_steps.input: Bag tag number; flight load manifest from BRS
l4_steps.output: Physical search result; BagManager scan log confirming whether bag was offloaded locally
l4_steps.kpi: Local recovery rate ≥35% within 30 min of PIR opening
l4_steps.pain_point: BagManager scan coverage gaps at outstations mean bags offloaded to wrong belt go undetected until next carousel audit

l4_steps.name: Assess local scan log — bag present at station?
l4_steps.input: BRS sortation scan history for bag tag
l4_steps.output: Decision: bag located locally (return immediately) or escalate to WorldTracer trace
l4_steps.kpi: Same-day resolution for locally present bags ≥95%
l4_steps.pain_point: BRS scan logs not always synchronised with WorldTracer in real time; 5–10 min latency causes duplicate PIRs

l4_steps.name: Create AHL/OHD/DPR tracing message in WorldTracer
l4_steps.input: PIR reference; confirmed bag tag, description, and itinerary
l4_steps.output: WorldTracer AHL file broadcast to all stations on itinerary; OHD files requested from origin and transit stations
l4_steps.kpi: AHL file created within 2 hrs of PIR ≥99%; OHD response from partner stations ≤4 hrs
l4_steps.pain_point: Interline itineraries with non-Altéa carriers require manual telex; SITA messaging delays to some outstations exceed 30 min

l4_steps.name: Query BRS scan history for last known bag location
l4_steps.input: Bag tag number; WorldTracer AHL reference
l4_steps.output: Chronological scan event log identifying last confirmed airport and handler
l4_steps.kpi: Last-scan data available within 5 min for ≥95% of bags with electronic tags
l4_steps.pain_point: RFID read rates vary by airport — legacy barcode-only stations provide no scan after check-in, forcing inference from load messages

l4_steps.name: Evaluate WorldTracer match within 24-hour window
l4_steps.input: AHL file; incoming OHD and FWD messages; BagJourney scan log
l4_steps.output: Match confirmed or escalation to manual canvass; WorldTracer case status updated
l4_steps.kpi: First match rate within 24 hrs ≥72% (IATA Resolution 743 target); escalation triggered <28%
l4_steps.pain_point: WorldTracer automatic matching fails when bag description is vague or bag tag damaged; human review adds 2–6 hr lag at high-volume stations

l4_steps.name: Send FWD message to station holding located bag
l4_steps.input: Confirmed bag location from WorldTracer OHD/match; passenger delivery address
l4_steps.output: FWD telex dispatched; holding station instructed to ship bag on next available service
l4_steps.kpi: FWD message sent within 30 min of match confirmation ≥98%
l4_steps.pain_point: Ground handler contracts at some outstations do not include expedite forwarding; next available flight may be 24–48 hrs away

l4_steps.name: Confirm bag shipped and track via BagJourney
l4_steps.input: FWD message acknowledgment; airway bill or rush tag number
l4_steps.output: Real-time shipment tracking record; passenger notified of estimated arrival
l4_steps.kpi: Forward shipment confirmed (scan at origin) within 4 hrs of FWD message ≥90%
l4_steps.pain_point: Rush tags issued at outstations not always scanned into BagJourney, causing blind spots until arrival at destination

l4_steps.name: Receive forwarded bag at destination and verify condition
l4_steps.input: Inbound bag with rush tag; WorldTracer FWD reference
l4_steps.output: Bag receipt confirmed in BagManager; condition noted; WorldTracer status updated to RFL (ready for delivery)
l4_steps.kpi: Bag condition documented at receipt ≥99%; damaged bags flagged for claims within 1 hr
l4_steps.pain_point: Damaged-in-transit bags generate secondary claims that delay closure; handler liability ambiguity between origin and transit stations

l4_steps.name: Contact passenger to confirm delivery preference
l4_steps.input: Passenger contact details from PNR; bag RFL status in WorldTracer
l4_steps.output: Confirmed delivery address or airport pickup slot; passenger notified via SMS/email
l4_steps.kpi: Passenger contacted within 1 hr of RFL status ≥95%; delivery preference captured ≥98%
l4_steps.pain_point: Passenger contact data in PNR frequently outdated for connecting itineraries; GDPR constraints limit use of third-party contact enrichment

l4_steps.name: Schedule courier delivery via third-party delivery API
l4_steps.input: Passenger delivery address; bag dimensions and weight; service SLA
l4_steps.output: Courier booking confirmation; tracking number shared with passenger
l4_steps.kpi: Courier dispatched within 2 hrs of passenger confirmation ≥92%; delivery within 24 hrs of dispatch ≥85%
l4_steps.pain_point: Courier API integrations vary by country — some stations revert to manual phone booking, introducing 3–5 hr delays and no tracking visibility

l4_steps.name: Confirm delivery and obtain proof of receipt
l4_steps.input: Courier delivery confirmation or passenger airport pickup signature
l4_steps.output: Proof of delivery (POD) attached to WorldTracer file; file status updated to CLO (closed)
l4_steps.kpi: POD captured and attached to WorldTracer within 24 hrs of delivery ≥99%; WorldTracer file closed within 48 hrs of delivery
l4_steps.pain_point: Paper POD at outstations not digitised, leaving WorldTracer files open and inflating delayed-bag statistics for IATA reporting

l4_steps.name: Assess interim expense claim under Montreal Convention
l4_steps.input: Passenger expense receipts; days without bag; Montreal Convention Article 19 liability schedule
l4_steps.output: Approved interim expense amount (capped at 1,288 SDR); claim reference created in SAP
l4_steps.kpi: Interim claim assessed within 48 hrs of PIR ≥90%; average claim processing time ≤5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: SDR-to-local-currency conversion rate must be applied at date of loss, not payment date — manual FX lookup creates errors in SAP FI journal entries

l4_steps.name: Process approved compensation payment via SAP Finance
l4_steps.input: Approved claim amount; passenger bank/card details; SAP vendor master record
l4_steps.output: Payment processed; remittance advice sent to passenger; WorldTracer file updated with settlement amount
l4_steps.kpi: Payment executed within 7 business days of approval ≥95%; zero unapproved payments exceeding liability cap
l4_steps.pain_point: Payments to international passengers require SWIFT transfers through SAP AP — SWIFT processing adds 3–5 business days in some corridors

l4_steps.name: Transfer unmatched bag to lost baggage storage at day 5
l4_steps.input: WorldTracer AHL file with no match after 5-day active trace; physical bag in holding area
l4_steps.output: WorldTracer status changed to STO (storage); bag catalogued with photo in WorldTracer Found Bag module
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of unmatched bags transferred to STO status by day 5; storage catalogue photo quality ≥95% usable
l4_steps.pain_point: Storage space at busy hubs is finite — airlines pay third-party warehouse fees after 10 days; uncatalogued bags cannot be matched to late-reporting passengers

l4_steps.name: Conduct extended 21-day owner identification search
l4_steps.input: STO bag record; WorldTracer auto-match; passenger-initiated trace enquiries
l4_steps.output: Owner identified and reunited (return to step 3.1) or case escalated to unclaimed disposal
l4_steps.kpi: Overall bag reunification rate within 21 days ≥97% (IATA Baggage Report benchmark); unclaimed rate <3%
l4_steps.pain_point: Passengers who do not file a PIR at the airport cannot initiate a WorldTracer search online without the original PIR reference — prevents late claims

l4_steps.name: Dispose of unclaimed bag per property regulation
l4_steps.input: Unclaimed STO bag at day 22+; local unclaimed property legislation requirements
l4_steps.output: Bag disposed (donated, auctioned, or destroyed) per local law; WorldTracer file closed with disposal notation
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of disposed bags documented with disposal method and date; zero regulatory non-compliance events
l4_steps.pain_point: Unclaimed property laws vary by country — US DOT, EU Regulation 889/2002, and individual state statutes create inconsistent disposal timelines and donation requirements

l4_steps.name: Import scheduled movements & gate inventory
l4_steps.input: SSIM schedule export, airport gate inventory with wingspan & equipment constraints
l4_steps.output: Flight movement list with time windows loaded into AMS
l4_steps.kpi: Gate plan build initiated ≥18h before day of operations; 100% of scheduled movements imported
l4_steps.pain_point: Late schedule amendments from airline ops (within T-6h) invalidate pre-built plans; no automated re-trigger of optimisation on change

l4_steps.name: Execute automated gate assignment optimisation
l4_steps.input: Flight movement list, terminal zone rules, contact-stand preference list
l4_steps.output: Draft gate assignment plan covering all scheduled movements
l4_steps.kpi: ≥92% of flights auto-assigned without manual intervention; optimisation run time <10 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Wide-body/narrow-body gate incompatibility not always captured in AMS master data — results in invalid auto-assignments requiring manual correction

l4_steps.name: Validate assignments against aircraft type constraints
l4_steps.input: Draft gate assignment plan, aircraft type per flight leg from PSS
l4_steps.output: Validated gate assignment list; flagged mismatches routed for manual resolution
l4_steps.kpi: 0 gate/aircraft-type mismatches published; validation complete ≥14h before operations day
l4_steps.pain_point: Ad-hoc aircraft swaps driven by AOG maintenance events are not always reflected in Amadeus Altéa PSS in time for gate validation cycle

l4_steps.name: Coordinate gate pre-conditioning with terminal ops
l4_steps.input: Validated gate plan, cleaning and catering subcontractor schedules
l4_steps.output: Confirmed gate readiness schedule aligned with ground handler SLAs
l4_steps.kpi: Gate confirmed ready ≥30 min before scheduled arrival; pre-conditioning exceptions <5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Cleaning and catering subcontractor SLA gaps at high-frequency turn stations cause gate hold-backs; A-CDM milestones not enforced contractually at all airports

l4_steps.name: Publish gate plan to FIDS and stakeholder systems
l4_steps.input: Confirmed gate assignment plan
l4_steps.output: Gate assignments published to passenger displays, ground handler portals, and crew bus scheduler
l4_steps.kpi: Published ≥12h before day of operations; 100% of gates reflected in FIDS within 90 seconds of publish
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA FIDS update latency (up to 90s per change batch) causes passenger confusion during rapid same-day gate changes at high-traffic terminals

l4_steps.name: Ingest real-time flight status via ACARS
l4_steps.input: ACARS block-off/estimated arrival messages, ATC slot data, weather NOTAMs
l4_steps.output: Updated ETA per inbound flight refreshed in AMS every 5 minutes
l4_steps.kpi: ETA refresh cycle ≤5 min; ETA data completeness ≥97% of active flights
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS signal dropout over oceanic routes causes ETA gaps; fallback to secondary radar feed introduces 15-min lag and degrades conflict detection accuracy

l4_steps.name: Confirm or revise gate assignments from updated ETAs
l4_steps.input: Updated ETAs, current gate occupancy status in AMS
l4_steps.output: Confirmed or revised gate assignment; conflict alert generated if overlap detected
l4_steps.kpi: Gate confirmed ≥60 min before scheduled arrival; <5% of gates reassigned day-of
l4_steps.pain_point: A single wide-body delay cascades into 3+ narrow-body gate conflicts as sequential turns are displaced — AMS does not auto-resolve cascades, requiring manual controller intervention

l4_steps.name: Notify ground handling of confirmed gate assignments
l4_steps.input: Confirmed gate assignments
l4_steps.output: Notifications dispatched to ground handler, fueller, caterer, and crew bus scheduler
l4_steps.kpi: Notification sent ≥45 min before arrival; stakeholder acknowledgement rate ≥95%
l4_steps.pain_point: Multiple ground handling subcontractors operating on different messaging platforms (SITA, WhatsApp, VHF radio) — fragmented comms increase risk of missed gate changes

l4_steps.name: Detect gate conflict from delay or early arrival
l4_steps.input: Real-time gate occupancy data, inbound ETA stream
l4_steps.output: Conflict alert with affected flight pair, overlap duration, and time to arrival
l4_steps.kpi: Conflict detected ≥45 min before arrival; 0 aircraft held on apron >15 min due to gate unavailability
l4_steps.pain_point: Default AMS conflict alerting threshold is 10 min — fails to catch rolling delay sequences that compound over a 3-hour window at hub airports

l4_steps.name: Assess remote stand and bus bridge feasibility
l4_steps.system: SITA AMS + Ground Transport Management System
l4_steps.input: Conflict alert, remote stand inventory, airside bus availability
l4_steps.output: Remote stand feasibility decision with estimated passenger transfer time
l4_steps.kpi: Decision made within 10 min of conflict detection; remote stand option assessed for 100% of conflict alerts
l4_steps.pain_point: Limited bus fleet at congested regional airports makes remote stand assignment impractical for wide-body aircraft loads; no real-time bus availability feed integrated into AMS

l4_steps.name: Execute gate swap or remote stand assignment
l4_steps.input: Feasibility decision, available contact gate or remote stand ID
l4_steps.output: Revised gate/stand assignment confirmed in AMS and pushed to all connected systems
l4_steps.kpi: Gate swap communicated to all parties within 5 min of decision; AMS record updated within 60 seconds
l4_steps.pain_point: Gate swap triggers manual re-notification to 6+ parties (handler, fueller, caterer, crew bus, security, cleaning) — no single-button broadcast in current AMS configuration

l4_steps.name: Update FIDS, departure boards, and airline mobile app
l4_steps.system: SITA FIDS + Amadeus Altéa PSS API + A-CDM Portal
l4_steps.input: Revised gate assignment from AMS
l4_steps.output: Updated passenger-facing displays and push notifications via airline mobile app
l4_steps.kpi: FIDS updated within 2 min of gate change; mobile app push notification delivered within 3 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Airline mobile app gate change notification requires a PSS API round-trip through Amadeus Altéa — up to 4-min latency under peak load causes passengers to board at wrong gate

l4_steps.name: Monitor aircraft block-on time and turnaround milestones
l4_steps.input: ACARS block-on timestamp, A-CDM turnaround milestone checklist
l4_steps.output: Real-time turnaround status dashboard with milestone completion percentage
l4_steps.kpi: Block-on captured within 2 min of actual; on-time departure (D0) ≥78%
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS block-on message can arrive up to 3 min after actual wheel-stop, distorting D0 measurement and masking genuine late-departure root causes in performance reporting

l4_steps.name: Validate all ground services complete before release
l4_steps.system: SITA AMS Turnaround Manager + Ground Handling System
l4_steps.input: Fuelling confirmation, catering upload complete, baggage loaded, cabin clean signed off
l4_steps.output: Go/No-Go decision for pushback authorisation
l4_steps.kpi: All services signed off ≥10 min before STD; late-service exception rate <3% of turns
l4_steps.pain_point: Paper-based sign-off by some catering subcontractors is not captured in AMS in real time — supervisor must chase confirmation manually, adding 5–8 min to gate release process

l4_steps.name: Authorise pushback and release gate in AMS
l4_steps.system: SITA AMS + Apron Control VHF Radio
l4_steps.input: Go clearance from all service streams, apron traffic status from Apron Control
l4_steps.output: Pushback authorisation transmitted; gate status set to Available in AMS
l4_steps.kpi: Gate released within 5 min of block-off; gate turnaround time ≤planned TAT per aircraft type
l4_steps.pain_point: Apron congestion at airports with single-taxiway layouts (common at secondary regional ports) delays pushback clearance from Apron Control, extending occupied gate time beyond planned TAT

l4_steps.name: Record and warehouse actual gate utilisation times
l4_steps.system: SITA AMS + AWS Redshift Data Warehouse
l4_steps.input: Block-on/off timestamps, gate occupancy records, planned vs. actual gate assignments
l4_steps.output: Actual vs. planned gate utilisation report loaded to Redshift
l4_steps.kpi: Data completeness ≥99% of movements; report available within 2h of operations day close
l4_steps.pain_point: AMS-to-Redshift ETL pipeline runs nightly batch — intraday utilisation analysis not available, preventing same-day corrective action on emerging gate congestion patterns

l4_steps.name: Analyse gate conflict frequency and root causes
l4_steps.input: Gate utilisation report, conflict log, delay attribution data from OTP system
l4_steps.output: Root cause analysis report with recurring conflict patterns and improvement recommendations
l4_steps.kpi: ≥80% of recurring gate conflicts identified with actionable root cause within 48h of operations day
l4_steps.pain_point: Delay root-cause data is siloed across SITA AMS, Amadeus Altéa PSS, and crew management system — manual correlation required; no automated attribution pipeline in place

l4_steps.name: Update gate constraint and master data in AMS
l4_steps.input: Root cause findings, updated aircraft type assignments, revised ground equipment specs
l4_steps.output: Updated gate constraint library effective for next scheduling cycle
l4_steps.kpi: Master data update cycle ≤7 days from change identification; 0 gate conflicts caused by stale constraint data in rolling 90-day window
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated synchronisation between airline fleet database (reflecting aircraft type changes) and AMS gate constraint tables — changes must be re-keyed manually, introducing error risk

l4_steps.name: Receive inbound flight movement data
l4_steps.input: Inbound OOOI messages and updated ETA from ACARS
l4_steps.output: Confirmed stand assignment and estimated on-block time
l4_steps.kpi: Stand assignment confirmed ≥30 min before ETA
l4_steps.pain_point: Late gate changes due to ATC slot revisions or prior turn overrun cause cascading resource conflicts — AMS does not auto-trigger GSE reallocation

l4_steps.name: Allocate ramp resources to inbound flight
l4_steps.input: Stand assignment, aircraft type, turnaround time target
l4_steps.output: GSE allocation plan (GPU, belt loaders, pushback tug, stairs/JBs)
l4_steps.kpi: Resource plan published ≥20 min before on-block; GSE utilisation ≥75%
l4_steps.pain_point: GSE availability gaps during peak banks — GroundStar planning horizon is 4 hours; sub-contracted handling agents may not sync real-time equipment status

l4_steps.name: Confirm stand readiness and brief ramp team
l4_steps.input: Incoming stand occupancy status, previous turn clearance confirmation
l4_steps.output: Stand ready flag set; ramp crew briefed on aircraft type, turn time, and special loads
l4_steps.kpi: Stand cleared ≥10 min before on-block for 95% of turns
l4_steps.pain_point: Stand conflicts when previous turn is delayed — SITA AMS does not automatically notify ramp crew of stand swap; verbal communication gaps cause missed briefings

l4_steps.name: Marshal aircraft to allocated stand
l4_steps.input: Stand ready confirmation, aircraft taxiing signal from Tower
l4_steps.output: Aircraft parked on stand with wheel position confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: On-block within 2 min of scheduled on-block time for 80% of turns
l4_steps.pain_point: Tight apron geometry at congested airports leads to proximity incidents — SITA AMS does not provide real-time apron conflict alerting; relies on manual visual clearance

l4_steps.name: Position chocks, connect GPU and air bridge
l4_steps.input: Aircraft on-block confirmation from marshaller
l4_steps.output: Chocks placed, GPU connected, aircraft on external power, air bridge docked
l4_steps.kpi: GPU connected within 3 min of on-block; APU off within 5 min of on-block
l4_steps.pain_point: APU-off compliance is monitored manually — airlines incur fuel burn penalty and noise fines if APU is left running; GroundStar task completion is self-reported, not sensor-verified

l4_steps.name: Conduct FOD check and open aircraft holds
l4_steps.input: Aircraft chocked and powered; airside safety clearance
l4_steps.output: FOD-clear certification logged; hold doors open and belt loaders positioned
l4_steps.kpi: FOD check completed within 5 min of chocking; zero FOD incidents per 10,000 turns
l4_steps.pain_point: FOD checks are paper-based at many stations — GroundStar task completion does not integrate with airside safety management system, preventing automated audit trail

l4_steps.name: Offload passenger baggage and ULDs
l4_steps.input: Offload sequence from LoadPlanner; ULD manifest from originating station
l4_steps.output: All baggage and ULDs offloaded and sorted to arrivals belt or transfer make-up area
l4_steps.kpi: First bag on belt ≤20 min after on-block; last bag ≤35 min for narrow-body
l4_steps.pain_point: ULD mismatch between manifest and physical load causes hold-up — SITA LoadPlanner relies on accurate originating station scanning; missing scan events create discrepancy exceptions requiring manual reconciliation

l4_steps.name: Offload cargo and mail per cargo manifest
l4_steps.input: Cargo manifest (AWBs, special load codes), ULD positions from LoadPlanner
l4_steps.output: Cargo offloaded to bonded shed or transfer unit; DG and live animal loads handled per IATA DGR
l4_steps.kpi: Cargo offload complete within 30 min of on-block; 100% DG loads documented per IATA DGR
l4_steps.pain_point: Dangerous goods (DG) misidentification at originating station discovered at offload — IATA DGR requires segregation but LoadPlanner DG flagging depends on shipper declaration accuracy

l4_steps.name: Perform lavatory and potable water servicing
l4_steps.input: Aircraft offload complete signal; lavatory service task assigned in GroundStar
l4_steps.output: Lavatory tanks emptied and rinsed; potable water tank filled to required level
l4_steps.kpi: Lavatory service complete within 15 min of task start; zero potable water contamination events
l4_steps.pain_point: Lavatory service vehicles (LSVs) are a single point of failure at smaller stations — delay cascades to all turns; IATA AHM 810 minimum water quality checks are manual and not digitally recorded in GroundStar

l4_steps.name: Calculate and uplift fuel per dispatch release
l4_steps.input: Fuel uplift order from dispatch release (Jeppesen FliteDeck / NAVBLUE); aircraft fuel gauges
l4_steps.output: Fuel uplifted to required quantity; fuel receipt signed and data transmitted
l4_steps.kpi: Fueling complete ≥15 min before scheduled departure; fuel quantity variance ≤50 kg vs. dispatch order
l4_steps.pain_point: Fuel density variation by temperature affects volumetric uplift — Into-Plane systems calculate in volume (litres/US gal); conversion errors between fuel slip and ACARS weight report create W&B discrepancies if not reconciled

l4_steps.name: Complete aircraft interior cleaning
l4_steps.input: Cabin cleaning task released in GroundStar after passenger deplane confirmed
l4_steps.output: Cabin cleaned, seat pockets restocked, galleys reset; cleaning sign-off in GroundStar
l4_steps.kpi: Cleaning complete within allocated turn time window; cabin cleanliness score ≥4.2/5 in post-flight survey
l4_steps.pain_point: Cleaning time is the most commonly cut activity during short turns — GroundStar task sequencing does not enforce minimum cleaning duration, and supervisors may sign off early under departure pressure

l4_steps.name: Load catering and provisioning per galley plan
l4_steps.input: Catering uplift order from catering management system; galley configuration file
l4_steps.output: All trolleys and supplies loaded to correct galley positions; catering doors secured
l4_steps.kpi: Catering loading complete ≥20 min before STD; zero missing trolley events per 1,000 turns
l4_steps.pain_point: Catering uplift errors (wrong galley, wrong count) discovered after door closure — gate-return for catering is operationally disruptive; caterers use paper manifests not integrated with Inform GroundStar task completion

l4_steps.name: Verify catering counts against flight specification
l4_steps.input: Catering delivery notes; passenger load forecast from Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Catering verification sign-off; discrepancy report raised if counts mismatch
l4_steps.kpi: Catering verification complete within 5 min of loading; discrepancy rate <0.5% of turns
l4_steps.pain_point: Passenger load changes after catering order cutoff (typically H-4) create over/under-provisioning — Amadeus Altéa PSS does not push live pax count updates to catering management system automatically

l4_steps.name: Receive final pax load and generate load plan
l4_steps.input: Final check-in closure data from Amadeus Altéa PSS; baggage weight data; cargo manifest
l4_steps.output: Load instruction report (LIR) with ULD build plan and position assignments
l4_steps.kpi: Load plan generated ≤10 min after check-in closure; load factor accuracy ±1% of actual
l4_steps.pain_point: Late passenger changes (gate adds, no-shows) after load plan generation require manual LIR revision — SITA LoadPlanner does not auto-recalculate when Altéa PSS pax count changes post-closure

l4_steps.name: Load passenger baggage per approved load plan
l4_steps.input: Approved LIR with ULD positions and weight targets per hold zone
l4_steps.output: Baggage loaded and locked in correct positions; actual weights per hold recorded in LoadPlanner
l4_steps.kpi: Baggage loaded per plan with ≤2% position deviation; loading complete ≥15 min before STD
l4_steps.pain_point: Ramp agents substitute ULD positions without updating LoadPlanner — actual vs. planned hold weights diverge, invalidating the W&B calculation and requiring a last-minute loadsheet reissue

l4_steps.name: Load outbound cargo and mail per manifest
l4_steps.input: Cargo manifest (AWBs); DG declarations; ULD build instructions from LoadPlanner
l4_steps.output: Cargo loaded per IATA ULD regulations; high-value and DG loads segregated and documented
l4_steps.kpi: Cargo loading complete ≥20 min before STD; 100% DG segregation compliance per IATA DGR
l4_steps.pain_point: Time-sensitive cargo (pharma, perishables) may miss cut-off due to late trucking delivery — SITA LoadPlanner does not integrate with off-airport cargo acceptance systems to provide early cut-off warning

l4_steps.name: Calculate final weight and balance
l4_steps.input: Final pax count and weights, actual baggage and cargo weights, fuel uplift confirmation
l4_steps.output: Final loadsheet with ZFW, TOW, CG% MAC, and trim setting
l4_steps.kpi: Loadsheet issued ≥10 min before STD; CG within certified envelope 100% of departures
l4_steps.pain_point: CG envelope violations caused by last-minute pax or cargo substitutions — SITA LoadPlanner CG alert requires manual Load Controller acknowledgement; no hard stop in system prevents issuance of out-of-envelope loadsheet

l4_steps.name: Transmit loadsheet to flight crew via ACARS
l4_steps.input: Approved final loadsheet from SITA LoadPlanner
l4_steps.output: Loadsheet transmitted and acknowledged by flight deck; printed copy retained per regulatory requirement
l4_steps.kpi: ACARS loadsheet transmission ≥8 min before STD; crew acknowledgement within 2 min
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS transmission failures at remote stations require fax or manual delivery — regulatory requirement (FAR Part 121 / EASA Ops) mandates crew receipt before departure; delays loadsheet delivery and pushes off-block

l4_steps.name: Disconnect all GSE and confirm all-clear
l4_steps.input: Doors-closed signal from cabin crew; loadsheet acknowledgement from flight deck
l4_steps.output: GPU disconnected, chocks removed, all GSE clear of aircraft; all-clear signal given to flight deck
l4_steps.kpi: All GSE cleared ≥3 min before off-block; zero FOD events during pushback phase
l4_steps.pain_point: GPU disconnect sequencing must precede APU start — uncoordinated disconnect in noisy ramp environment leads to momentary power loss events; GroundStar all-clear task is self-reported with no sensor confirmation

l4_steps.name: Coordinate pushback and engine start with ATC
l4_steps.input: All-clear confirmed; ATIS and pushback clearance from ATC via VHF
l4_steps.output: Aircraft pushed back to runway heading; engine start sequence complete; pushback crew clear
l4_steps.kpi: Off-block within 1 min of target off-block time (TOBT) for 78% of departures
l4_steps.pain_point: TOBT accuracy degrades during irregular operations — A-CDM TOBT updates from SITA AMS rely on all ground service completions being accurately logged; manual GroundStar updates lag real-time status, degrading ATC slot compliance

l4_steps.name: Define ground handling scope and service requirements
l4_steps.input: Network expansion plan, station opening schedule, incumbent contract expiry notice
l4_steps.output: Ground handling scope document covering ramp, fuelling, deicing, ULD, and cleaning
l4_steps.kpi: Scope document published within 10 business days of trigger event
l4_steps.pain_point: Scope creep when station-specific deicing or narrow-body-only ramp constraints are not captured early, leading to SLA gaps on first winter ops

l4_steps.name: Issue RFP to pre-qualified ground handlers
l4_steps.input: Approved scope document, approved vendor panel list from supplier master
l4_steps.output: Published RFP with evaluation scorecard, response deadline, and mandatory IATA SGHA annex B template
l4_steps.kpi: RFP issued within 5 business days of scope sign-off; minimum 3 qualified bidders invited
l4_steps.pain_point: Thin vendor panels at secondary airports (e.g. single-handler markets) reduce competitive tension and inflate unit rates by up to 25% vs hub markets

l4_steps.name: Evaluate vendor proposals against qualification criteria
l4_steps.input: Vendor RFP responses, IATA ISAGO audit certificates, IOSA-compliant safety declarations
l4_steps.output: Scored evaluation matrix; shortlist of 1–2 vendors approved for site audit
l4_steps.kpi: Evaluation completed within 15 business days of RFP close; minimum ISAGO score ≥ 80%
l4_steps.pain_point: ISAGO certificates from some regional handlers are expired or cover a different station than the one being contracted, requiring manual verification against IATA ISAGO registry

l4_steps.name: Conduct on-site capability and safety audit
l4_steps.input: Shortlisted vendor details, ISAGO report, audit checklist aligned to IATA AHM 810
l4_steps.output: Audit report with pass/fail rating per category; safety risk register entry in Archer GRC
l4_steps.kpi: On-site audit completed within 20 business days of shortlist; zero critical findings to proceed
l4_steps.pain_point: Handlers at code-share or alliance partner hubs may operate under local airport authority waivers that do not meet airline-specific safety standards, creating liability exposure

l4_steps.name: Negotiate SLA terms, turnaround targets, and penalty rates
l4_steps.input: Audit-cleared vendor, benchmark turnaround data from SITA Airport Management System, peer airline SLA benchmarks
l4_steps.output: Agreed SLA schedule: D0 target ≥78%, bag delivery ≤20 min, FOD check compliance 100%
l4_steps.kpi: SLA negotiation concluded within 10 business days; penalty trigger at ≥3 consecutive monthly SLA breaches
l4_steps.pain_point: Handlers resist penalty clauses tied to D0 when ATC or fuel delays (outside handler control) are not explicitly excluded in the SLA attribution model

l4_steps.name: Conduct legal and aviation safety compliance review
l4_steps.input: Draft IATA SGHA Main Agreement and Annex B, insurance certificates, local aviation authority operating permit
l4_steps.output: Legal sign-off memo; contract approved or returned with redlines
l4_steps.kpi: Legal review cycle ≤ 15 business days; zero unresolved liability caps at execution
l4_steps.pain_point: Jurisdictional variation in ground handling regulations (e.g. EU Groundhandling Directive 96/67/EC vs. FAA Part 139 requirements for US stations) extends review cycles for multi-station contracts

l4_steps.name: Execute contract and issue purchase order
l4_steps.input: Countersigned SGHA, approved budget in SAP cost centre, contract start date confirmed with station team
l4_steps.output: Executed contract stored in SAP Ariba repository; PO issued in SAP S/4HANA; vendor activated in supplier master
l4_steps.kpi: PO issued within 2 business days of contract execution; contract visible in SAP Ariba within same day
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual data re-entry when contracts are executed outside SAP Ariba (e.g. via email exchange) causes vendor master mismatches and delayed invoice matching

l4_steps.name: Register vendor in airport operations system
l4_steps.input: Executed contract, vendor contact list, station codes, service scope per aircraft type
l4_steps.output: Vendor profile active in SITA AMS with service assignments per stand and aircraft type
l4_steps.kpi: Vendor profile configured and tested in SITA AMS ≥ 5 business days before go-live
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA AMS vendor profiles are station-scoped; multi-station contracts require separate profile creation at each station, increasing setup time and risk of configuration inconsistencies

l4_steps.name: Configure KPI monitoring thresholds in performance dashboard
l4_steps.input: Contracted SLA targets, SITA AMS data feeds, Amadeus Airport Management turnaround data
l4_steps.output: Live Tableau dashboard with amber/red KPI alerts per vendor, per station, per service type
l4_steps.kpi: Dashboard live and validated against 5 historical flights before go-live; alert latency ≤ 1 hour from event
l4_steps.pain_point: Data latency between Amadeus Airport Management and Tableau can exceed 90 minutes during peak schedules, causing delayed breach detection and missed real-time intervention windows

l4_steps.name: Conduct pre-operations readiness assessment
l4_steps.input: Vendor staff roster, GSE serviceability checklist, SITA AMS profile test results, safety induction completion records
l4_steps.output: Signed go/no-go readiness certificate; open items logged in Archer GRC if any
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of vendor staff complete airline safety induction before go-live; GSE serviceability ≥ 95% on day 1
l4_steps.pain_point: High staff turnover at ground handling contractors (industry average >40% p.a.) means safety induction records in SAP SuccessFactors are frequently out of date within weeks of go-live

l4_steps.name: Ingest daily turnaround performance data from ops systems
l4_steps.input: SITA AMS event logs (chocks-on, door-open, door-close, chocks-off), ACARS timestamps, fuelling records
l4_steps.output: Validated daily performance dataset per vendor per flight sector
l4_steps.kpi: ≥ 98% of flights matched to vendor records within 24 hours; data completeness ≥ 99%
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS timestamp gaps on narrow-body short-haul sectors (sub-45-min turns) create ambiguous attribution when two ground handlers operate at adjacent stands simultaneously

l4_steps.name: Generate monthly vendor performance scorecard
l4_steps.input: 30-day aggregated performance dataset, contracted SLA thresholds, prior month scorecard for trend analysis
l4_steps.output: Vendor scorecard PDF: D0 %, bag delivery time, FOD incidents, safety events, delay attribution
l4_steps.kpi: Scorecard issued by business day 5 of following month; D0 target ≥78%, bag delivery ≤20 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Delay attribution disputes between airline and vendor are common where root-cause coding (e.g. IATA delay code 93 vs. 61) is entered by different parties, inflating apparent handler performance

l4_steps.name: Assess KPI compliance against contracted SLA thresholds
l4_steps.input: Monthly vendor scorecard, SLA penalty schedule from SAP Ariba contract record
l4_steps.output: Compliance verdict per KPI: Green (met), Amber (within cure period), Red (penalty triggered)
l4_steps.kpi: Compliance assessment completed within 2 business days of scorecard publication; penalty invoice raised within 5 days of Red verdict
l4_steps.pain_point: SLA cure periods (typically 30 days) allow repeated near-misses that never formally trigger penalties, masking systemic under-performance until a major disruption event

l4_steps.name: Issue formal performance improvement notice to vendor
l4_steps.input: Red KPI verdict, scorecard evidence, prior month trend data, contract penalty clause reference
l4_steps.output: Formal written performance improvement plan (PIP) with 30/60/90-day milestones logged in SAP Ariba
l4_steps.kpi: PIP issued within 5 business days of Red verdict; vendor root-cause response required within 10 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Ground handlers often attribute performance failures to airline-side delays (late aircraft, late pax boarding) that are poorly documented, making PIP enforcement difficult without granular ACARS evidence

l4_steps.name: Conduct annual vendor safety and compliance audit
l4_steps.input: 12-month performance data, open PIP items, ISAGO renewal status, local regulatory inspection reports
l4_steps.output: Annual audit report with risk rating (Low/Medium/High) and mandatory corrective action items
l4_steps.kpi: Annual audit completed ≥ 90 days before contract renewal date; zero High-risk open findings at renewal
l4_steps.pain_point: ISAGO audit cycles (every 2 years) do not align with annual contract reviews, creating a 12-month window where compliance status is unverified between ISAGO renewal and airline audit

l4_steps.name: Evaluate contract renewal versus re-tender decision
l4_steps.input: Annual audit report, 12-month KPI scorecard trend, market rate benchmarks, strategic station growth plan
l4_steps.output: Renewal or re-tender recommendation memo approved by VP Ground Operations
l4_steps.kpi: Decision memo issued ≥ 60 days before contract expiry; re-tender initiated if 12-month D0 average < 75%
l4_steps.pain_point: At captive single-handler airports, re-tender is not a credible threat, weakening commercial leverage and often resulting in rate increases at renewal regardless of performance history

l4_steps.name: Execute contract renewal or initiate new sourcing cycle
l4_steps.input: Approved renewal or re-tender decision memo, updated scope (if changed), revised SLA targets
l4_steps.output: Renewed contract executed in SAP Ariba OR new RFP issued back at step 1.2; vendor master updated
l4_steps.kpi: Contract renewal executed ≥ 30 days before expiry; zero lapse in contractual coverage at any station
l4_steps.pain_point: Contract lapses during re-tender transitions force reliance on month-to-month SGHA extensions at full tariff rates, increasing ground handling costs by 15–30% until new contract is executed

l4_steps.name: Retrieve Final Pax Count & Baggage Weights
l4_steps.input: Check-in closure trigger (T-30 min); APIS/DCS pax manifest
l4_steps.output: Confirmed pax count, checked-bag count, total baggage weight
l4_steps.kpi: Data retrieval completed ≤5 min after check-in close
l4_steps.pain_point: Late pax additions and standby activations in Altéa can shift total bag weights by 200–400 kg after preliminary load plan is locked, requiring full recalculation

l4_steps.name: Calculate Preliminary Weight & Balance
l4_steps.input: Pax manifest, estimated bag weights, fuel uplift from ACARS
l4_steps.output: Preliminary zero fuel weight (ZFW), centre of gravity (CG) estimate, hold allocation plan
l4_steps.kpi: Preliminary W&B issued ≤10 min after check-in close
l4_steps.pain_point: Standard passenger weight assumptions (IATA Standard Weights 2023) may under-estimate actual payload on leisure routes with heavy baggage allowances, skewing preliminary CG

l4_steps.name: Validate Dangerous Goods Declarations
l4_steps.input: Shipper's Declaration for Dangerous Goods (SHPD), NOTOC entries from cargo manifest
l4_steps.output: Validated DG NOTOC; approved or rejected DG items with segregation instructions
l4_steps.kpi: DG validation completed ≤15 min before cargo loading commences; zero IATA DGR Part 7 segregation violations
l4_steps.pain_point: Lithium battery shipments (IATA DGR Section II PI 966/967/968) increasingly misclassified by shippers; SITA DGM lacks real-time integration with courier manifest data, requiring manual cross-check

l4_steps.name: Generate Loading Instruction Report (LIR)
l4_steps.input: Approved hold allocation plan, DG segregation instructions, special cargo positions
l4_steps.output: Loading Instruction Report (LIR) specifying bay/pit assignment per item type
l4_steps.kpi: LIR issued to ramp supervisor ≤20 min before scheduled loading start
l4_steps.pain_point: Paper or tablet-based LIR distribution to ramp agents creates version-control risk; last-minute config changes (late cargo acceptance) may not reach all loading teams before loading begins

l4_steps.name: Sort & Route Checked Baggage to Make-Up Area
l4_steps.input: Baggage reconciliation data from Altéa, belt assignment from SITA AMS
l4_steps.output: Sorted baggage staged at correct make-up carousel/area for the flight
l4_steps.kpi: Baggage sortation accuracy ≥99.5%; all bags at make-up area ≥30 min before STD
l4_steps.pain_point: Interline transfer bags arriving via multiple carriers carry different barcode standards (BCBP vs legacy 10-digit); SITA BagManager reconciliation failures require manual intervention, risking late bags

l4_steps.name: Build ULD / Container per Load Plan Spec
l4_steps.input: LIR bay assignments, sorted baggage at make-up area
l4_steps.output: Loaded ULD/containers tagged with position ID and estimated weight
l4_steps.kpi: ULD build completed per LIR sequence; zero wrong-position items at loading start
l4_steps.pain_point: Wide-body aircraft use mixed ULD types (LD3, LD7, bulk) — incorrect ULD type selection delays loading due to incompatible cargo door dimensions; SITA LoadManager ULD type validation is advisory only

l4_steps.name: Weigh Completed ULD / Container
l4_steps.system: Mettler Toledo ULD Scale + SITA LoadManager
l4_steps.input: Loaded ULD on weigh platform
l4_steps.output: Actual ULD gross weight recorded in LoadManager against plan position
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of ULDs weighed before loading; weight variance vs estimate ≤±50 kg per ULD
l4_steps.pain_point: Ramp-scale calibration drift (EASA Part-145 requirement: calibration every 12 months) causes systematic weight bias accumulating across all holds; discrepancies only surfaced at final W&B stage

l4_steps.name: Confirm ULD Weight Within Structural Limit
l4_steps.input: Actual ULD weight vs aircraft structural limit per bay (from Boeing aircraft performance data)
l4_steps.output: ULD cleared for loading or redistributed; updated hold allocation if rebalancing required
l4_steps.kpi: Zero structural limit exceedances reaching the aircraft; resolution time ≤8 min per overweight ULD
l4_steps.pain_point: Aircraft type changes (e.g. A320 substituted for A321) alter bay structural limits mid-process; SITA LoadManager aircraft config library updates lag fleet changes by 24–48 hours

l4_steps.name: Confirm Ground Equipment Positioning at Aircraft
l4_steps.input: Gate assignment from SITA AMS, loading start trigger from Load Controller
l4_steps.output: Baggage loaders / hi-loaders and belt loaders confirmed in position; loading authorised
l4_steps.kpi: GSE at aircraft ≤5 min after aircraft-on-blocks; zero loading delays attributable to GSE unavailability
l4_steps.pain_point: GSE pooling across multiple handlers at shared terminals creates resource contention; SITA AMS GSE tracking relies on manual check-in, not real-time GPS — actual vs reported positions diverge during peak banks

l4_steps.name: Load Cargo Holds per LIR Bay Assignment
l4_steps.input: LIR bay assignment, loaded ULDs/bulk bags at aircraft side
l4_steps.output: Items loaded into designated holds; barcode scan confirmation per piece
l4_steps.kpi: Loading compliance with LIR ≥99%; fwd/aft hold loaded within 20 min of start for narrowbody
l4_steps.pain_point: Handheld SITA LoadManager scan confirmation step is frequently skipped during high-tempo turns; missing scan events break baggage reconciliation and create BSM (Baggage Source Message) failures reported to IATA BRS

l4_steps.name: Load Special & Priority Items per NOTOC
l4_steps.input: Approved NOTOC, special cargo labels (live animals, wet ice, perishables, human remains)
l4_steps.output: Special cargo positioned per segregation rules and NOTOC; supervisor sign-off recorded
l4_steps.kpi: 100% NOTOC items loaded in approved positions; zero segregation violations on departure
l4_steps.pain_point: Live animal loading under IATA LAR requires temperature-zone compliance — cargo hold temperature monitoring (ACARS datalink) is not available on all aircraft types, creating regulatory exposure on LAR shipments

l4_steps.name: Verify Loading Sequence Matches LIR
l4_steps.input: Scan confirmations from step 3.2, LIR bay plan
l4_steps.output: Loading conformance report — approved to proceed or discrepancy flagged for correction
l4_steps.kpi: Loading conformance check completed before any hold door closed; discrepancy resolution ≤10 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Forward CG bias risk: ramp teams load forward holds first for efficiency; deviation from LIR sequence without re-run of W&B can produce an out-of-envelope CG that is only caught at step 4.3

l4_steps.name: Record Actual Loaded Weights per Hold
l4_steps.input: Scan-confirmed item list per hold bay from step 3.4
l4_steps.output: Actual hold-by-hold weight breakdown entered in LoadManager for final W&B run
l4_steps.kpi: All hold weights entered within 5 min of loading completion
l4_steps.pain_point: Bulk-loaded items (oversized bags, strollers, wheelchairs) weighed individually at check-in but grouped in cargo manifests without piece-level tracking — cumulative weight error can exceed 100 kg on narrow-body aircraft

l4_steps.name: Compute Final ZFW, TOW & CG Position
l4_steps.system: SITA LoadManager + Boeing Aircraft Performance Tool (OPT)
l4_steps.input: Actual hold weights, confirmed fuel uplift, final pax count with no-shows applied
l4_steps.output: Final Zero Fuel Weight (ZFW), Take-Off Weight (TOW), Landing Weight (LW), and CG index value
l4_steps.kpi: Final W&B calculation completed ≤15 min before STD; TOW within ±0.5% of fuel plan
l4_steps.pain_point: Boeing OPT structural limits database must match the exact aircraft tail number's modification status (SB-tracked changes alter limits); mismatches between OPT aircraft config and actual tail configuration require manual override with engineering sign-off

l4_steps.name: Confirm CG Within Certified Envelope
l4_steps.input: Final CG index, aircraft type CG envelope limits, trim setting
l4_steps.output: CG confirmed in-envelope and stabiliser trim setting issued to crew; or rebalance instruction issued
l4_steps.kpi: CG in-envelope on first calculation ≥95% of flights; rebalance time ≤15 min when required
l4_steps.pain_point: Point-of-no-return conflict: CG rebalance after door closure requires re-opening hold, adding 10–20 min to turnaround; pressure from OCC to depart on-time leads to borderline CG positions being accepted with minimal margin

l4_steps.name: Generate & Sign Final Loadsheet
l4_steps.input: Approved ZFW, TOW, CG, trim setting; final pax/bag count
l4_steps.output: Signed final loadsheet (paper or e-loadsheet) with load controller and captain signature blocks
l4_steps.kpi: Final loadsheet generated ≥15 min before STD; e-loadsheet adoption rate target ≥80%
l4_steps.pain_point: Regulatory requirement for wet-ink captain signature on paper loadsheet persists at many airports due to incomplete e-loadsheet adoption under IATA Simplifying the Business (StB) programme; creates courier dependency and delays on remote stands

l4_steps.name: Transmit Final Loadsheet to Flight Deck via ACARS
l4_steps.input: Signed final loadsheet from SITA LoadManager
l4_steps.output: Loadsheet datalink message (LDM/CPM) received on flight deck EFB or ACARS printer
l4_steps.kpi: ACARS loadsheet delivery confirmed ≤12 min before STD; delivery failure rate <1%
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS datalink congestion during peak departure banks (multiple aircraft departing simultaneously) causes transmission delays of 3–8 min; crews on ACARS-equipped EFBs (Jeppesen FliteDeck) may not receive message before paperwork cut-off

l4_steps.name: Obtain Crew Acknowledgment of Loadsheet
l4_steps.input: Loadsheet datalink message or paper copy delivered to flight deck
l4_steps.output: Crew acknowledgment uplinked via ACARS or paper signature returned; loadsheet accepted or queried
l4_steps.kpi: Crew acknowledgment received ≥10 min before STD; query resolution ≤5 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew queries about non-standard weights (e.g. cargo-only belly loads, heavy charters) require Load Controller to re-explain figures verbally — no structured digital query-and-response workflow exists in SITA LoadManager to track queries and responses for audit trail

l4_steps.name: Issue Last-Minute Change (LMC) if Required
l4_steps.input: Post-loadsheet change trigger (late pax, offload, security-removed bag)
l4_steps.output: LMC document transmitted to crew; updated ZFW/CG confirmed within limits
l4_steps.kpi: LMC issued and acknowledged ≤7 min before pushback; LMC rate <5% of departures
l4_steps.pain_point: Security-driven offloads (unaccompanied baggage removal per IATA Resolution 753 BRS) can occur as late as T-5 min; cascading CG shift from forward-hold offload frequently triggers full W&B recalculation, compressing final clearance window to under 3 min

l4_steps.name: Close Cargo Doors & Issue Station Clearance
l4_steps.input: Crew acknowledgment confirmed, LMC resolved, all hold doors secured
l4_steps.output: Station departure clearance recorded in SITA AMS; ramp-clear signal issued to tug crew
l4_steps.kpi: Hold doors closed and ramp-clear signal issued ≥5 min before STD; on-time departure (D0) contribution ≥85%
l4_steps.pain_point: Concurrent ground activities (refuelling, catering, water service) on the same aircraft require physical clearance coordination not tracked in SITA AMS — ramp supervisors rely on verbal radio confirmation, creating safety blind spots during rushed turns

l4_steps.name: Receive IRROP alert from Operations Control Centre
l4_steps.input: OCC disruption notification (weather, ATC, mechanical, or crew IRROP)
l4_steps.output: IRROP event record opened in AMS with timestamp and flight reference
l4_steps.kpi: Alert-to-acknowledgement time ≤5 min
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA AMS alert feeds from multiple upstream systems (NOC, Jeppesen, Altéa) with inconsistent data latency, causing duplicate or conflicting IRROP triggers during high-volume disruption events

l4_steps.name: Classify disruption type and assign severity tier
l4_steps.input: IRROP alert with reason code (WX, ATC, MX, CREW, OPS)
l4_steps.output: Severity tier (Tier 1: delay <2 hrs; Tier 2: delay 2–4 hrs; Tier 3: cancellation/diversion) logged in AMS
l4_steps.kpi: Classification accuracy ≥95% (validated vs. final outcome)
l4_steps.pain_point: Mechanical IRROPs often escalate from Tier 1 to Tier 3 mid-process due to late MX diagnosis; premature low-tier classification under-triggers rebooking resources

l4_steps.name: Confirm affected flight status in Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Flight number, departure date, disruption severity tier
l4_steps.output: Flight record locked for IRROP processing; passenger count confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: Manifest retrieval time ≤2 min from alert
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS record locking conflicts when OCC and airport teams access the same flight simultaneously; requires coordinated queue management via PSS administrator role

l4_steps.name: Extract full passenger manifest for affected flight
l4_steps.input: Locked flight record in Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Full passenger manifest with PNR, contact details, connection itineraries, and ancillary services
l4_steps.kpi: Manifest extraction completeness 100% of checked-in and booked passengers
l4_steps.pain_point: Passengers booked via third-party OTAs often have incomplete contact data in Altéa, blocking automated notification and requiring manual agent outreach

l4_steps.name: Flag PRM, UM, and MAAS passengers requiring priority handling
l4_steps.input: Passenger manifest with SSR codes (WCHR, WCHC, UM, MAAS, MEDA)
l4_steps.output: Priority handling list dispatched to special assistance team and gate supervisor
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of SSR-flagged passengers identified before rebooking batch runs
l4_steps.pain_point: SSR codes entered by codeshare or interline partners are not always carried over into the operating carrier's Altéa record, creating missed-flag risk for vulnerable passengers

l4_steps.name: Determine EU261 / DOT compensation threshold applicability
l4_steps.input: Delay duration, disruption cause code, origin/destination jurisdiction, fare class
l4_steps.output: Compensation eligibility flag per passenger (EU261 / DOT Part 250 / no entitlement)
l4_steps.kpi: Eligibility determination completed before rebooking batch execution
l4_steps.pain_point: EU261 extraordinary-circumstances defence (e.g. ATC strike, severe weather) requires real-time legal review; automated rules engines in Altéa do not always capture all exemption nuances, exposing the airline to over- or under-payment

l4_steps.name: Execute automated mass rebooking via Altéa Inventory
l4_steps.input: Affected passenger manifest, compensation eligibility flags, available seat inventory on alternate flights
l4_steps.output: Automated rebooking records for ≥70% of affected passengers on next-available services
l4_steps.kpi: Auto-rebook success rate ≥70% of affected PAX; batch processing time ≤15 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Inventory availability for the rebooking window is often constrained by already-high load factors (industry avg ≥83%), forcing passengers onto flights departing 24–48 hrs later and increasing duty-of-care cost

l4_steps.name: Identify and triage rebooking conflicts and seat oversells
l4_steps.input: Mass rebooking output; oversell alerts from Altéa Inventory
l4_steps.output: Conflict list with oversell count per flight, voluntary upgrade candidates, and interline options
l4_steps.kpi: Oversell resolution time ≤30 min; upgrade/interline acceptance rate ≥60%
