l4_steps.pain_point: NRM inventory controls may auto-close cabin classes during the rebooking wave, preventing agents from placing passengers even when physical seats are available — requires temporary override authorisation from RM Analyst

l4_steps.name: Manually rebook complex and unresolvable itineraries
l4_steps.input: Conflict list from Step 3.2; interline partner availability via Sabre GDS or Travelport GDS
l4_steps.output: Confirmed alternate itinerary per complex passenger; interline endorsement where required
l4_steps.kpi: Manual rebook completion ≤60 min from conflict identification
l4_steps.pain_point: Interline rebooking requires bilateral interline agreements (IIAs); if the next-available flight is on a carrier with no IIA, agents must issue refunds rather than rebooking, increasing passenger dissatisfaction scores

l4_steps.name: Issue new boarding passes and update ancillary entitlements
l4_steps.input: Confirmed new itinerary records; pre-paid ancillaries (seat, bag, meal) on original booking
l4_steps.output: New boarding passes issued; ancillaries transferred or refund flag set
l4_steps.kpi: Boarding pass issuance ≤5 min per passenger post-rebooking confirmation
l4_steps.pain_point: Ancillary transfer from disrupted to alternate flight is not fully automated in Altéa DCS; agents manually re-enter seat selections and meal preferences, adding ~3–4 min per PNR and creating ancillary revenue leakage

l4_steps.name: Trigger automated SMS and email notifications to affected PAX
l4_steps.input: Confirmed rebooking records; passenger contact data; disruption reason code
l4_steps.output: Outbound SMS/email sent to all passengers with new itinerary details and self-service rebooking link
l4_steps.kpi: Notification delivery rate ≥95% within 10 min of rebooking confirmation
l4_steps.pain_point: Passengers with international mobile numbers often fail SMS delivery due to carrier routing gaps; email-only fallback is slower and has lower open rates during time-sensitive IRROP events

l4_steps.name: Update FIDS and gate display boards with disruption status
l4_steps.input: Disruption classification, new departure time or cancellation flag, alternate gate assignments
l4_steps.output: FIDS and gate display boards updated; PA announcement script generated for gate agents
l4_steps.kpi: FIDS update within 3 min of disruption classification confirmation
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA AMS FIDS integration with some airport authority display networks requires manual refresh at certain stations, creating information lag of 5–15 min in secondary terminals

l4_steps.name: Brief gate agents and customer service desk on disruption status
l4_steps.input: Disruption ops log from AMS; rebooking summary from Altéa
l4_steps.output: Agent briefing completed; customer service desks staffed and equipped with voucher stock
l4_steps.kpi: Agent briefing completion ≤10 min from IRROP classification
l4_steps.pain_point: High-disruption events (weather cancellations affecting 20+ flights simultaneously) overwhelm customer service desk staffing ratios — airline contingency plans often require minimum 1:50 agent-to-passenger ratio, which is rarely met in mass IRROP scenarios

l4_steps.name: Assess duty-of-care entitlements by delay duration and cause
l4_steps.input: EU261/DOT eligibility flags from Step 2.3; confirmed delay/cancellation duration
l4_steps.output: Duty-of-care entitlement matrix per passenger (meals at 2 hrs, hotel at 4 hrs overnight, transport)
l4_steps.kpi: Entitlement assessment completed within 15 min of Tier 2/3 classification
l4_steps.pain_point: EU261 duty-of-care obligations apply regardless of extraordinary-circumstances defence — airlines frequently conflate compensation exemption with duty-of-care exemption, creating regulatory exposure under EC Regulation 261/2004 Art. 9

l4_steps.name: Issue meal and hotel vouchers to entitled passengers
l4_steps.input: Duty-of-care entitlement matrix; passenger count by entitlement tier
l4_steps.output: Meal and hotel vouchers issued; voucher serial numbers logged against PNR for cost recovery
l4_steps.kpi: Voucher issuance rate ≥90% of entitled passengers within 30 min of threshold trigger
l4_steps.pain_point: Many airlines operate VMS as a standalone system disconnected from Altéa PNR records; reconciling voucher costs against individual PNRs for EU261 cost recovery requires manual matching, creating audit gaps of up to 30% unreconciled spend

l4_steps.name: Manage passenger queue flow at rebooking and check-in desks
l4_steps.input: Volume of unreboooked passengers at gate; staffing plan from AMS resource module
l4_steps.output: Queue management plan activated; overflow desks opened; escalation to airport authority if required
l4_steps.kpi: Average passenger wait time at rebooking desk ≤20 min during IRROP event
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA AMS resource scheduling module does not dynamically redeploy staff from non-disrupted gates during an IRROP event — staffing reallocation depends on supervisor radio coordination, adding 15–20 min to response time

l4_steps.name: Record disruption costs against flight and cost centre in SAP
l4_steps.input: Voucher serials, interline reissue charges, hotel invoices, overtime staffing costs
l4_steps.output: IRROP cost posting in SAP CO cost centre; accrual for EU261 claims liability
l4_steps.kpi: IRROP cost posting completed within 24 hrs of event closure
l4_steps.pain_point: Voucher costs from third-party hotel partners arrive as bulk invoices weekly, preventing real-time flight-level cost attribution in SAP CO and distorting disruption cost-per-passenger metrics

l4_steps.name: Submit EU261 / DOT compensation claims data to legal team
l4_steps.input: Eligibility flags, delay duration actuals, disruption reason code, passenger PNR list
l4_steps.output: Claims data package exported from Altéa; submitted to Legal and Customer Relations for processing
l4_steps.kpi: Claims data submitted within 48 hrs of event; EU261 response SLA ≤7 days per regulation
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO and IATA resolution frameworks for extraordinary-circumstances documentation are not standardised; each jurisdiction's CAA applies different evidence standards, requiring airline legal teams to maintain jurisdiction-specific defence packs

l4_steps.name: Generate IRROP performance report and update process KPIs
l4_steps.input: AMS event log, Altéa rebooking data, voucher costs, customer satisfaction (CSAT) scores
l4_steps.output: IRROP post-event report: rebooking rate, notification rate, avg wait time, duty-of-care compliance, cost-per-disrupted-passenger
l4_steps.kpi: Report published within 72 hrs; cost-per-disrupted-passenger target ≤$85 (industry benchmark)
l4_steps.pain_point: Data from SITA AMS, Altéa, VMS, and SAP sit in separate schemas with no native ETL integration; Tableau dashboards rely on nightly batch feeds, preventing real-time IRROP performance monitoring during the event itself

l4_steps.name: Ingest WCHR/WCHC/WCHS/WCHB SSR codes from PNR
l4_steps.input: Passenger booking request or PNR with special assistance SSR codes
l4_steps.output: SSR codes attached to PNR and transmitted to ground handling agents via SITA Type B message
l4_steps.kpi: SSR capture rate ≥99% of passengers self-identifying as requiring assistance
l4_steps.pain_point: SSR codes entered via third-party OTA bookings (Sabre/Travelport GDS) frequently omit WCHR detail level — WCHR vs WCHC vs WCHB require different staffing and equipment, forcing manual re-verification at check-in

l4_steps.name: Validate SSR codes against IATA AIRIMP definitions
l4_steps.input: SSR codes from PNR (WCHR, WCHC, WCHB, WCHS, DEAF, BLND, UMNR)
l4_steps.output: Validated or corrected SSR categorisation confirmed in PNR
l4_steps.kpi: SSR validation accuracy ≥98% completed ≥24 hours before scheduled departure
l4_steps.pain_point: WCHR (ambulatory, needs chair to/from aircraft), WCHC (immobile), WCHB (on-board transfer only), WCHS (steps only) have distinct handling requirements — conflation causes resource misallocation and DOT ACAA exposure

l4_steps.name: Flag MEDA/OXYG/LEGL cases for medical clearance
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS + MedAire Medical Clearance Portal
l4_steps.input: SSR codes including MEDA (medical case), OXYG (oxygen), LEGL (stretcher), INCAD
l4_steps.output: Medical clearance decision or deferral notice attached to PNR
l4_steps.kpi: Medical clearance decision issued ≤4 hours before departure; MEDA clearance rate tracked monthly
l4_steps.pain_point: MEDA cases require physician sign-off via MedAire or equivalent — no standardised PSS-to-medical portal API; clearance requests are manual email/phone, creating decision latency that can strand medically complex passengers

l4_steps.name: Generate special assistance manifest for flight
l4_steps.input: Finalised SSR list pushed from Amadeus Altéa PSS, flight departure schedule
l4_steps.output: Special assistance manifest: pax count by category, seat numbers, mobility device details
l4_steps.kpi: Manifest accuracy ≥97% verified at gate against actual presenting passengers
l4_steps.pain_point: Real-time SSR updates from late bookers and day-of upgrades are not always pushed from Altéa to SITA AMS — agents frequently work off stale manifests, missing newly added WCHR requests

l4_steps.name: Allocate wheelchair equipment and trained staff
l4_steps.system: SITA Airport Management System (AMS) + Workforce Management System (Jeppesen Crew Management)
l4_steps.input: Special assistance manifest, available equipment inventory, staff roster
l4_steps.output: Staff assignments confirmed, wheelchair and aisle chair allocation per flight logged in AMS
l4_steps.kpi: WCHR equipment availability ≥99.5% at departure time; staff-to-WCHR ratio ≥1:3
l4_steps.pain_point: Shared wheelchair pool across concurrent bank departures causes equipment shortfalls — no real-time IoT tracking of wheelchair/aisle chair location at most airports; agents spend 10–15 min locating equipment

l4_steps.name: Brief check-in, gate, and lounge staff on SSR pax
l4_steps.system: SITA Airport Management System (AMS) + Airline Ops Communication App
l4_steps.input: Staff duty roster, special assistance manifest, gate assignments
l4_steps.output: Pre-departure briefing confirmed, staff aware of individual passenger needs and mobility restrictions
l4_steps.kpi: Briefing completion ≥90 minutes before scheduled departure for all WCHR flights
l4_steps.pain_point: High turnover in ground handling contractor staff means briefings are the primary knowledge transfer channel — no structured digital briefing delivery to ramp contractor teams; verbal-only handoffs cause information loss at shift changes

l4_steps.name: Meet and greet passenger at curbside or check-in
l4_steps.system: SITA Airport Management System (AMS) + Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Passenger arrival at airport, WCHR manifest from Phase 2
l4_steps.output: Passenger confirmed on manifest, escort service initiated and logged in AMS
l4_steps.kpi: Meet-and-greet wait time ≤5 minutes from passenger arrival notification; missed meet rate <1%
l4_steps.pain_point: No reliable mechanism for passengers to pre-notify airport of their actual arrival time — agents use scheduled departure window as proxy, causing missed meets for passengers arriving >90 min early or late

l4_steps.name: Process priority check-in and accessible seat assignment
l4_steps.input: PNR, validated SSR category, mobility device dimensions and weight
l4_steps.output: Boarding pass issued, bulkhead or aisle seat assigned, mobility device tagged for gate-check or cargo
l4_steps.kpi: Priority check-in processing time ≤10 minutes; accessible seat assignment compliance ≥100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa seat maps do not surface DOT Part 382-mandated accessible seats (bulkhead with movable armrests) separately from general inventory — agents must manually cross-check airline accessible seating policy to avoid assigning window or obstructed seats

l4_steps.name: Escort passenger through security checkpoint
l4_steps.system: SITA Airport Management System (AMS) + TSA PreCheck / Airport Security System
l4_steps.input: Boarding pass, passenger with personal mobility device
l4_steps.output: Passenger cleared through security, mobility device screened and returned, security escort time logged
l4_steps.kpi: Security escort completion ≤20 minutes; extended screening incidents <5% of WCHR escorts
l4_steps.pain_point: TSA screening of power wheelchairs with lithium batteries (>300Wh) triggers extended secondary screening — no pre-clearance pathway between airline SSR data and TSA PreCheck; battery removal for screening adds 15–20 minutes and requires specialised TSA training

l4_steps.name: Pre-board WCHR passengers ahead of general boarding
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS (boarding control) + SITA Airport Management System (AMS)
l4_steps.input: WCHR manifest, gate assignment, boarding gate opening time
l4_steps.output: WCHR passengers boarded before general boarding commences, boarding scan logged in Altéa
l4_steps.kpi: Pre-boarding initiation ≥20 minutes before scheduled departure; WCHR pre-board completion rate ≥98%
l4_steps.pain_point: Gate changes issued via Amadeus AMS real-time updates do not automatically trigger re-dispatch of staged WCHR escort teams — agents must manually monitor FIDS for gate swaps, causing missed pre-boards when late gate changes occur

l4_steps.name: Transfer passenger to aisle chair at jet bridge threshold
l4_steps.system: SITA Airport Management System (AMS) + Airline Aisle Chair Inventory System
l4_steps.input: WCHC or WCHB passenger at gate, aisle chair staged at jet bridge
l4_steps.output: Passenger safely transferred to aisle chair and escorted to assigned seat
l4_steps.kpi: Aisle chair transfer completion ≤8 minutes per passenger; transfer injury rate 0%
l4_steps.pain_point: Narrow-body aircraft (737, A320 family) require airline-specific aisle chair dimensions — third-party ground handling company equipment is frequently incompatible; DOT Air Carrier Access Act mandates two trained staff for transfers, but solo escorts are common at smaller stations

l4_steps.name: Tag, stow, or gate-check personal mobility device
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS (baggage tagging) + SITA Baggage Reconciliation System (BRS)
l4_steps.input: Personal wheelchair, power scooter, or walker; baggage tag from check-in
l4_steps.output: Mobility device tagged, stowed gate-check or in cargo hold, recorded in SITA BRS with return location flag
l4_steps.kpi: Mobility device stow without damage ≥99.8%; aircraft-door return ≥90% of WCHC/WCHB cases
l4_steps.pain_point: Power wheelchair lithium batteries >300Wh require IATA DGR Section 3.3.1 special handling — ramp agents are not universally IATA DGR certified; battery removal adds 15–20 min dwell time and risks damage to chair electronics if improperly handled

l4_steps.name: Confirm seating, call bell, and lavatory access briefing
l4_steps.system: Aircraft Cabin Systems (IFE / Seat Control) + SITA Airport Management System (AMS)
l4_steps.input: Passenger seated, boarding in progress, pre-departure checklist
l4_steps.output: Passenger briefed on accessible IFE, call bell, and lavatory access; assistance closure logged in AMS
l4_steps.kpi: Passenger safety and accessibility briefing completion 100% before door close
l4_steps.pain_point: Single-aisle narrow-body aircraft (737-800, A320) have no onboard accessible lavatory — WCHR passengers on sectors >3 hours require a pre-departure lavatory visit; this is frequently omitted when boarding is behind schedule, resulting in DOT ACAA complaints

l4_steps.name: Transmit WCHR count and SSR detail to destination station
l4_steps.system: SITA Messaging (Type B / IATA AHM) + Amadeus Altéa PSS (SSR relay)
l4_steps.input: SSR manifest, confirmed pax list, flight ETA
l4_steps.output: LDM/PSM/IATA AHM 140 PRM advice message transmitted to destination with WCHR count and categories
l4_steps.kpi: SSR transmission to destination ≥60 minutes before ETA; message accuracy ≥99%
l4_steps.pain_point: Not all carriers use structured IATA AHM 140 (PRM advice) messaging — some destination stations rely on informal teletype or email, causing missed meet-and-greets at remote or outstations with minimal ground handling staff

l4_steps.name: Deplane WCHR passengers in coordinated sequence
l4_steps.role: Cabin Crew + Arrival Special Assistance Agent
l4_steps.system: SITA Airport Management System (AMS) + Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Aircraft at blocks-on, WCHR manifest from arrival station, aisle chair staged at jet bridge
l4_steps.output: WCHR passengers deplaned safely, arrival assistance confirmed and logged in SITA AMS
l4_steps.kpi: WCHR deplaning completion within 15 minutes of blocks-on; missed assist rate <0.5% of WCHR arrivals
l4_steps.pain_point: Remote stands (bus gates) require two-stage transfer: aisle chair → ambulift → terminal wheelchair — ambulift availability is not tracked in SITA AMS; unplanned remote stand assignments cause 20–30 min assistance delays and DOT ACAA complaint exposure

l4_steps.name: Return mobility device at aircraft door or baggage claim
l4_steps.system: SITA Baggage Reconciliation System (BRS) + SITA Airport Management System (AMS)
l4_steps.input: Tagged mobility device retrieved from cargo hold, arrival WCHR manifest
l4_steps.output: Device returned to passenger in original condition; damage inspection completed and logged
l4_steps.kpi: Device return at aircraft door ≥90% (DOT ACAA requirement); mobility device damage rate <0.1 per 1,000 devices handled
l4_steps.pain_point: DOT Air Carrier Access Act requires power wheelchair return at aircraft door — carriers routinely return at baggage claim due to cargo door sequencing constraints; each violation exposes the carrier to DOT fines of up to $35,000 per incident

l4_steps.name: Log completed assistance events in SITA AMS
l4_steps.input: Assistance completion confirmations from agents, timestamps, staff IDs
l4_steps.output: Digital event log of WCHR assistance with timestamps, pax IDs, staff IDs, and outcomes
l4_steps.kpi: Assistance event logging rate ≥99% within 30 minutes of flight departure or arrival blocks-on
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual data entry creates compliance gaps — paper-based backup processes at smaller outstations mean event logs are incomplete; data aggregation for monthly DOT Part 382 reporting requires manual reconciliation across 8–12 station formats

l4_steps.name: Audit DOT Part 382 / ACAA compliance metrics
l4_steps.system: Tableau / Power BI (Compliance Dashboard) + SITA AMS Data Export
l4_steps.input: Assistance event logs, complaint records, mobility device damage and delay reports
l4_steps.output: Monthly DOT Part 382 compliance scorecard, gap analysis, corrective action register
l4_steps.kpi: DOT ACAA complaint rate <0.5 per 10,000 passengers; mobility device damage claims <0.1%; complaint resolution within 30 days ≥95%
l4_steps.pain_point: DOT Part 382 requires individual written complaint response within 30 days — complaint tracking spans CX, legal, and ground ops with no single integrated system; manual status reconciliation between Salesforce CRM and SITA AMS takes 2–3 hours per month per station

l4_steps.name: Escalate unresolved complaints to CX and Regulatory Affairs
l4_steps.role: Customer Experience Manager / Regulatory Affairs Director
l4_steps.system: Salesforce Service Cloud (CRM) + SITA Airport Management System (AMS)
l4_steps.input: Open DOT/ACAA complaints, device damage claims, missed assist incident reports
l4_steps.output: Escalation ticket created in Salesforce, root cause analysis completed, process improvement recommendation issued
l4_steps.kpi: Complaint resolution within 30 days ≥95% (DOT Part 382 §382.155 requirement); repeat incident rate reduction target ≥20% quarter-over-quarter
l4_steps.pain_point: No direct integration between SITA AMS ground ops incident logs and Salesforce CRM — staff must manually recreate incident context in Salesforce tickets, causing information loss and duplicate investigative effort; recurring root causes (e.g. remote stand ambulift gaps) are not systematically fed back into resource planning

l4_steps.name: Pull premium passenger manifest from Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Flight departure schedule T-24h; SSR codes VIPS, MAAS, EXST
l4_steps.output: Confirmed VIP/CIP passenger list with PNRs and service flags
l4_steps.kpi: VIP list generated ≥3h before STD for 100% of flagged flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa SSR codes not consistently populated by booking agents; last-minute upgrades bypass VIP workflow trigger, causing missed service setup

l4_steps.name: Verify VIP profile, entitlements and SSRs in CRM
l4_steps.input: PNR list and SSR flags from Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Verified VIP tier, lounge entitlement, dietary/mobility needs, escort preferences
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of flagged passengers have CRM profiles verified ≥2h before STD
l4_steps.pain_point: CRM–PSS integration is batch-updated every 30 min; loyalty tier upgrades post-booking are not reflected in CRM until next sync cycle, causing entitlement disputes at lounge

l4_steps.name: Assign dedicated escort agent and ground transport
l4_steps.input: Verified VIP list, staff roster, buggy and vehicle availability in AMS
l4_steps.output: Named escort assignments and ground transport booking confirmations
l4_steps.kpi: Dedicated escort assigned ≥2h before STD for 95% of VIP departures
l4_steps.pain_point: High-volume departure banks create escort staff shortages; SITA AMS staff-allocation module is not integrated with VIP workflow, requiring manual cross-referencing

l4_steps.name: Deploy escort agent to kerb or designated arrival point
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS (mobile boarding agent app)
l4_steps.input: VIP manifest, expected arrival time, ground transport ETA
l4_steps.output: Escort agent positioned at correct terminal entry with passenger itinerary loaded
l4_steps.kpi: Escort on-station ≥15 min before passenger arrival for 95% of VIP movements
l4_steps.pain_point: No real-time kerb vehicle arrival feed from ground transport into Altéa mobile app; agents rely on manual WhatsApp coordination, introducing timing errors

l4_steps.name: Confirm passenger identity and validate service entitlement
l4_steps.input: Passenger boarding pass, frequent flyer card or government-issued ID
l4_steps.output: Identity confirmed, service tier validated, escort commences
l4_steps.kpi: Identity verification completed within 2 min of passenger contact; 100% compliance rate
l4_steps.pain_point: Offline CRM access unreliable in terminals with poor Wi-Fi coverage; agents revert to static printed lists containing stale tier and entitlement data

l4_steps.name: Escort passenger through fast-track security and immigration
l4_steps.system: Airport Authority Fast-Track Access System (TSA/CBP portal or equivalent)
l4_steps.input: Confirmed identity, valid boarding pass, fast-track access credentials
l4_steps.output: Passenger cleared security and immigration, escorted airside
l4_steps.kpi: Fast-track clearance time ≤15 min for 90% of VIP passengers
l4_steps.pain_point: Fast-track lane access controlled by third-party airport authority; VIP agents have no influence over TSA/CBP staffing levels; clearance times spike during IRROP events with no advance warning to escort team

l4_steps.name: Validate lounge entitlement and execute lounge access
l4_steps.input: Verified VIP tier, flight PNR, loyalty programme status
l4_steps.output: Lounge access granted and logged; passenger introduced to lounge host
l4_steps.kpi: Lounge access processing time ≤3 min for 95% of eligible passengers
l4_steps.pain_point: LoungeKey API is batch-synced with PSS; real-time upgrades at check-in are not reflected in lounge access rights until next sync, generating incorrect denials and reputational risk

l4_steps.name: Coordinate ground transport, buggy or mobility service
l4_steps.input: Gate assignment, STD, passenger mobility requirements from CRM
l4_steps.output: Ground buggy or wheelchair dispatched with confirmed pickup time
l4_steps.kpi: Transport dispatched ≥25 min before STD for 95% of requested VIP movements
l4_steps.pain_point: AMS ground transport module is not linked to lounge host workstations; lounge staff must radio ramp operations manually, introducing dispatch delays of 5–12 min during peak periods

l4_steps.name: Monitor flight status and trigger lounge departure alert
l4_steps.system: SITA Airport Management System (AMS) + Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Real-time departure board, gate change notifications from AMS
l4_steps.output: Departure alert issued to VIP passenger; escort confirmed at lounge door
l4_steps.kpi: Departure alert issued ≥30 min before STD for 98% of VIP departures; gate change communicated within 5 min of AMS notification
l4_steps.pain_point: Gate change notifications from AMS to lounge management system carry up to 8-min latency; during high-disruption periods VIP passengers have missed boarding calls due to undelivered gate change alerts

l4_steps.name: Set up priority boarding lane and verify gate readiness
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS (check-in and boarding module)
l4_steps.input: VIP passenger list, boarding call time, confirmed gate assignment
l4_steps.output: Priority boarding lane activated; VIP seat blocking released in Altéa
l4_steps.kpi: Priority lane ready ≥20 min before boarding call for 100% of VIP-flagged flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Gate agent allocation is driven by generic staffing schedule; premium lane setup requires a manual Altéa query for VIP passenger count — awareness is not pushed to gate agents automatically

l4_steps.name: Pre-board VIP passenger and brief cabin crew on preferences
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS (boarding scan) + Jeppesen FliteDeck (EFB ground message)
l4_steps.input: Boarding pass, VIP escorted to gate, CRM preference profile
l4_steps.output: Boarding scanned in Altéa; cabin crew briefed via FliteDeck; amenity kit pre-positioned
l4_steps.kpi: VIP pre-board completed ≥10 min before general boarding opens for 95% of applicable flights
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated CRM-to-EFB passenger profile push; escort agent must verbally relay preferences or hand-carry printed notes, creating transcription errors and missed dietary or seating requirements

l4_steps.name: Confirm VIP baggage priority-tagged and loaded in hold
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS (bag reconciliation) + SITA Baggage Reconciliation System (BRS)
l4_steps.input: VIP bag tags from check-in, ULD load plan from weight and balance system
l4_steps.output: Priority bags confirmed loaded and reconciled in SITA BRS before door close
l4_steps.kpi: VIP baggage reconciliation complete ≥10 min before aircraft door close for 100% of bags
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA BRS priority flag requires a manual scan override by ramp agent; automated priority sequencing is not enforced by baggage handling systems at most outstations, defaulting to FIFO load order

l4_steps.name: Confirm VIP boarding complete before general boarding opens
l4_steps.input: Boarding scan records, VIP count from pre-departure list
l4_steps.output: Gate agent confirmation that all VIPs are boarded; general boarding lane opened
l4_steps.kpi: VIP boarding window closed ≥5 min before general boarding for 95% of flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Tight turnaround schedules (<35 min ground time) compress the pre-board window; gate agents under pressure to open general boarding early, bypassing the VIP exclusivity window

l4_steps.name: Detect VIP disruption and escalate for priority recovery
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS + SITA Airport Management System (AMS)
l4_steps.input: Flight cancellation or delay ≥60 min notification from AMS/NOC feed
l4_steps.output: VIP disruption flag raised; supervisor notified; recovery workflow initiated
l4_steps.kpi: VIP disruption detected and escalated within 10 min of AMS notification for 100% of affected flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa IRROP rebooking tool does not auto-surface VIP tier during mass disruption; disrupted VIP passengers are queued alongside general passengers with no proactive priority identification

l4_steps.name: Rebook VIP and arrange priority hotel or lounge extension
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS + Salesforce Service Cloud
l4_steps.input: Disrupted VIP passenger list, next-available flight inventory, hotel inventory feed
l4_steps.output: Confirmed rebooking on next available flight; hotel or lounge extension voucher issued
l4_steps.kpi: VIP rebooking offered within 20 min of disruption notification for 95% of affected passengers
l4_steps.pain_point: Hotel inventory access from Altéa IRROP module is limited to contracted properties; premium passengers expecting 5-star accommodation must be manually booked outside PSS, adding 15–30 min to recovery time

l4_steps.name: Log service delivery notes and quality score in CRM
l4_steps.input: Completed service checklist, passenger feedback, any complaints or deviations noted during escort
l4_steps.output: CRM record updated with service quality score, issues flagged for relationship manager follow-up
l4_steps.kpi: CRM updated for 100% of VIP interactions within 2h of flight departure
l4_steps.pain_point: Post-departure CRM logging is manually triggered with no workflow enforcement; during high-volume operations coordinators defer or skip logging, creating gaps in VIP relationship history that affect retention and future service quality

l4_steps.name: Receive cargo booking and AWB data
l4_steps.input: Air Waybill (AWB), shipper booking request, commodity declaration
l4_steps.output: Booking record created in cargo management system
l4_steps.kpi: Acceptance processing time ≤15 min per shipment
l4_steps.pain_point: Paper-based AWBs delay IATA e-freight compliance; IATA eAWB mandate targets 100% adoption by 2026 but shipper readiness lags at ~68% globally

l4_steps.name: Validate AWB, weight, dimensions, and piece count
l4_steps.input: Physical cargo presented at acceptance counter, AWB data
l4_steps.output: Validated weight/dimension record; discrepancy notice if mismatch
l4_steps.kpi: AWB discrepancy rate ≤2%; re-weigh resolution ≤10 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Weight/dimension discrepancy between booked and actual triggers load plan recalculation in SkyMAX; late changes within 2h of STD cause cascading W&B revisions

l4_steps.name: Screen shipment for dangerous goods compliance
l4_steps.input: Commodity code, shipper's DG declaration, MSDS where applicable
l4_steps.output: DG acceptance confirmation or rejection notice with IATA DGR citation
l4_steps.kpi: Undeclared DG detection rate = 100%; DG non-compliance rejection logged within 5 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Undeclared lithium batteries and aerosols remain the #1 air cargo safety risk; IATA DGR 64th Edition tightens Section II battery limits, requiring agent retraining each Jan cycle

l4_steps.name: Submit ACAS pre-screening data for US-bound cargo
l4_steps.input: AWB data, commodity details, shipper/consignee identifiers
l4_steps.output: ACAS submission confirmation; Do Not Load (DNL) or cleared status from CBP
l4_steps.kpi: ACAS submission ≥4h before departure per 19 CFR 122.48a; CBP response latency typically <2 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Late ACAS submission or CBP DNL response with <1h to departure forces cargo offload, disrupting finalised load plan and triggering FFM amendment; no automated retry on CBP system timeout

l4_steps.name: Physically screen cargo via X-ray or ETD
l4_steps.input: Accepted and DG-cleared shipment presented at screening station
l4_steps.output: Screened cargo with TSA/TCAS security clearance label
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of cargo screened before loading per TSA 12-5 CCSF programme; throughput ≥600 kg/h per lane
l4_steps.pain_point: Dense or opaque shipments (machinery, consolidated freight) require manual ETD swab resolution, creating bottleneck at peak build-up windows (02:00–05:00 for early banks); insufficient overnight staffing at secondary airports

l4_steps.name: Assign screened cargo to flight and ULD position
l4_steps.input: Screened shipment data, aircraft load plan from load control, ULD inventory
l4_steps.output: ULD assignment record with build-up instructions and position code
l4_steps.kpi: ULD utilisation ≥85% by volume; assignment issued ≥3h before STD
l4_steps.pain_point: Last-minute passenger IRROP (flight cancellation/diversion) displaces belly cargo capacity, requiring full re-manifest of 15–40 shipments within 30 min with no automated re-optimisation tool in most legacy CMS configurations

l4_steps.name: Build ULD, palletise cargo, and apply labels
l4_steps.input: Build-up instructions, cargo, ULD/pallet, netting, and tiedown equipment
l4_steps.output: Completed ULD with IATA ULD tag, gross weight, and content manifest
l4_steps.kpi: Build-up accuracy (correct ULD manifest) ≥98%; ULD gross weight tolerance ±0.5% of declared
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual pallet build without automated real-time feed to weight-and-balance system means errors (overweight, CG shift) are only discovered at aircraft hold door, causing ramp delay averaging 18 min per incident

l4_steps.name: Generate and transmit final cargo manifest (FFM)
l4_steps.input: Completed ULD manifest records, AWB data, flight details
l4_steps.output: FFM Cargo-IMP message transmitted to destination station, customs, and ground handler
l4_steps.kpi: FFM transmitted ≥45 min before STD per IATA Cargo-IMP MSG standard; retransmission on amendment ≤5 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Integration gaps between CMS and PSS mean late passenger rebooking changes (affecting belly payload) trigger manual FFM amendments; automated reconciliation missing in non-NDC-integrated stations

l4_steps.name: Transport ULDs and bulk cargo to aircraft ramp
l4_steps.input: Ramp movement instruction, airside vehicle assignment, ULD ready notification
l4_steps.output: ULD delivered to aircraft position on time; vehicle movement logged
l4_steps.kpi: Cargo at aircraft ≥30 min before STD; ramp vehicle utilisation ≥80%
l4_steps.pain_point: Airside congestion at hub airports (multiple simultaneous narrow-body turns) causes sequencing conflicts between cargo dollies, fuel bowsers, and catering trucks; no real-time airside traffic management at most regional stations

l4_steps.name: Load cargo into aircraft hold per load instruction report
l4_steps.input: Load Instruction Report (LIR) from load control, ULDs and bulk cargo on ramp
l4_steps.output: Completed loading; signed LIR returned to load control; actual weights confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: Loading completion ≥15 min before STD; W&B CG deviation ≤2% of planned; LIR sign-off accuracy 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Bulk cargo dimension inconsistencies discovered at hold door during loading trigger manual re-sequencing; Jeppesen LoadPlanner does not auto-update when actual weights deviate >50 kg from planned, requiring crew notification and possible taxi-back

l4_steps.name: Offload cargo from arriving aircraft hold
l4_steps.input: Aircraft arrival confirmation, inbound load manifest (FWB/FFM from origin)
l4_steps.output: Offloaded ULDs and bulk cargo staged on ramp with position labels
l4_steps.kpi: ULD offload complete ≤35 min after chocks-on; bulk hold clear ≤25 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Combi aircraft and wide-body mixed-class configurations require sequential hold access, extending ground time; misrouted ULDs from origin (wrong station label) discovered only at offload, requiring urgent re-manifest and re-tender

l4_steps.name: Break down inbound ULDs and scan all pieces
l4_steps.input: Inbound ULD with origin manifest
l4_steps.output: Individual shipment scan records; discrepancy report if count/condition mismatch
l4_steps.kpi: Breakdown and scan complete ≤60 min after offload; discrepancy rate ≤1%; cargo claim initiation ≤15 min of confirmed shortage
l4_steps.pain_point: ULD damage (torn nets, cracked pallets) discovered at breakdown delays customs release and inflates cargo claims cost; CHAMP exception workflow requires manual supervisor override, adding 20–45 min to resolution when supervisor unavailable overnight

l4_steps.name: Transmit arrival notices to consignees and forwarders
l4_steps.input: Breakdown scan records, AWB consignee and notify-party contact data
l4_steps.output: Arrival Notices (ANs) transmitted via EDI/email to all notified parties
l4_steps.kpi: Arrival notice sent ≤2h after breakdown; automated AN rate ≥95% of AWBs with complete contact data
l4_steps.pain_point: Incomplete or missing consignee contact data in AWB (common with e-commerce fulfilment shipments) prevents automated notification; manual agent intervention required, increasing dwell time and risk of exceeding free storage period

l4_steps.name: File customs entry and e-manifest for inbound cargo
l4_steps.input: AWB, commodity data, commercial invoice, country of origin certificate
l4_steps.output: Customs entry filed; Movement Reference Number (MRN) or CBP release reference received
l4_steps.kpi: Customs pre-clearance filing ≥2h before aircraft arrival per EU ICS2 and CBP advance cargo rules; entry acceptance rate ≥97%
l4_steps.pain_point: Incomplete commercial invoices from e-commerce shippers (missing HS codes, undervalued goods) cause customs holds and demurrage charges; ICS2 Phase 3 (2024) adds 6-digit HS code mandate that many SME shippers are not yet compliant with

l4_steps.name: Present cargo for customs physical examination if selected
l4_steps.input: CBP or customs authority examination order; cargo held in bonded warehouse
l4_steps.output: Cargo presented at examination bay; examination result recorded
l4_steps.kpi: Cargo presented at examination bay ≤4h of exam order; examination completion ≤8h for non-complex shipments
l4_steps.pain_point: Random and targeted exam selection (10–15% of shipments at major US gateways) creates unpredictable delay and bonded storage cost; no SLA from CBP on exam completion time, causing consignee escalations and missed just-in-time delivery windows

l4_steps.name: Release and deliver cargo to consignee upon clearance
l4_steps.input: Customs release confirmation, consignee photo ID and delivery order
l4_steps.output: Signed delivery receipt; cargo released from airline/handler custody; AWB closed
l4_steps.kpi: Dwell time ≤24h for general cargo; ≤4h for perishables and pharmaceuticals (IATA CEIV Pharma benchmark); delivery receipt accuracy 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Free storage period expiry (typically 24–48h depending on carrier tariff) triggers demurrage charges averaging $0.50–$1.50/kg/day; consignee no-shows spike on weekends and public holidays without automated SMS/email reminder integration in CHAMP delivery module

l4_steps.name: Activate Winter Operations Plan via AMS
l4_steps.input: Meteorological forecast showing OAT <= +3°C or freezing precipitation expected within 2 hours
l4_steps.output: WINOPS activation notice distributed to ground crews, ramp supervisors, and flight dispatch
l4_steps.kpi: Activation lead time >= 2 hours before first affected departure; 100% crew acknowledgement within 15 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Late NOTAMs or rapidly developing weather compress the activation window; insufficient crew briefing time during sudden temperature drops leads to unprepared ground teams

l4_steps.name: Pre-Position De-icing Equipment and Brief Crews
l4_steps.input: WINOPS activation notice, flight schedule, de-icing pad/gate assignments
l4_steps.output: De-icing vehicles positioned at pad or gates; crews briefed, signed off on fluid handling procedures
l4_steps.kpi: Equipment readiness >= 30 min before first scheduled de-icing event; all crew holdover time (HOT) training current within 12 months
l4_steps.pain_point: GSE unserviceability during peak winter events reduces available truck count with no redundancy at smaller stations; crew HOT training currency lapses go undetected until seasonal activation

l4_steps.name: Confirm Fluid Inventory and Type Availability
l4_steps.input: Current fluid stock levels (Type I, II, III, IV), upcoming flight schedule, forecast storm duration
l4_steps.output: Fluid availability confirmed and logged; reorder triggered if stock < 40% of estimated daily requirement
l4_steps.kpi: Fluid stock >= 120% of estimated daily requirement; reorder threshold: 40% remaining; no event aborted due to fluid shortage
l4_steps.pain_point: Type IV fluid supply chain disruptions during extended winter events common at capacity-constrained stations; airports with limited glycol storage cannot buffer multi-day storm events

l4_steps.name: Monitor Real-Time Weather and Issue De-icing Advisory
l4_steps.input: METAR, TAF, PIREP, real-time OAT, precipitation type and rate from DTN feeds
l4_steps.output: De-icing advisory issued specifying contamination type, severity level, and recommended fluid type
l4_steps.kpi: Advisory issued within 10 min of METAR update confirming frozen precipitation; advisory accuracy vs actual ramp conditions >= 90%
l4_steps.pain_point: Rapidly changing precipitation type (freezing rain transitioning to snow) invalidates HOT mid-event; DTN update latency vs real-time ramp microclimate conditions can lead to under- or over-treatment decisions

l4_steps.name: Conduct Aircraft Contamination Walk-Around Inspection
l4_steps.system: SITA Airport Management System (AMS) — Mobile Ops Tablet
l4_steps.input: Aircraft parked at gate or de-icing pad, current weather conditions, contamination advisory
l4_steps.output: Contamination type and surface coverage documented (wings, fuselage, tail, control surfaces, sensors)
l4_steps.kpi: Inspection completed within 5 min of aircraft block-in; 100% of critical surfaces (wing leading edge, ailerons, elevator, rudder, pitot tubes) checked
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew access to tail surfaces restricted at narrow-body gates without elevated stands; time pressure from tight turnarounds causes rushed inspections that miss contamination on aft fuselage or horizontal stabiliser

l4_steps.name: Determine De-Icing Treatment Type and Fluid Selection
l4_steps.input: Contamination type (frost, snow, ice, freezing rain), OAT, precipitation rate, planned departure time
l4_steps.output: Treatment order specifying: Type I only vs. Type I + anti-icing fluid, dilution ratio, and sequence
l4_steps.kpi: Treatment type decision within 3 min of inspection completion; fluid selection compliant with SAE AMS 1424 (Type I) and AMS 1428 (Type IV) specifications
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew chiefs without current SAE HOT table training select incorrect dilution ratios, overestimating holdover time and creating latent safety risk; audit trail for treatment decision not captured in all DMS implementations

l4_steps.name: Position De-icing Vehicle and Establish Cockpit Communication
l4_steps.input: Treatment order, aircraft stand or pad assignment, vehicle positioning clearance from ramp controller
l4_steps.output: Vehicle positioned within safe working envelope; two-way communication established with flight deck; chocks and safety cones confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: Spray basket clearance >= 1 m from aircraft surface at all times; positioning complete within 3 min of vehicle arrival at stand
l4_steps.pain_point: Ramp congestion at hub airports delays vehicle access to stand; ATC-mandated de-icing pad queuing adds 15–20 min to turnaround during peak demand; inadequate ground lighting at night complicates safe vehicle positioning

l4_steps.name: Apply Type I Heated Fluid — Active Contamination Removal
l4_steps.input: Contaminated aircraft surfaces, Type I fluid heated to 60–82°C, application nozzle settings
l4_steps.output: Aircraft surfaces cleared of snow, ice, and frost; fluid volume applied and temperature at nozzle logged in DMS
l4_steps.kpi: All critical surfaces clear of contamination after Type I pass; fluid temperature >= 60°C at application point; fluid waste rate < 5% through overspray
l4_steps.pain_point: Very low OAT (<-15°C) reduces Type I heated fluid effectiveness, requiring multiple passes and extending turnaround; excessive Type I application increases glycol runoff requiring EPA/Transport Canada environmental reporting

l4_steps.name: Apply Anti-Icing Fluid (Type II/IV) for Holdover Protection
l4_steps.input: Clean aircraft surfaces confirmed, selected anti-icing fluid and dilution ratio, OAT, precipitation rate
l4_steps.output: Anti-icing fluid coat applied uniformly; application start time, volume, dilution ratio, and fluid type recorded to DMS with timestamp
l4_steps.kpi: Application completed within 3 min; fluid start time logged to second-level accuracy for HOT calculation; coating uniform per SAE AMS 1428 visual check
l4_steps.pain_point: Type IV fluid viscosity at OAT < -14°C reduces flow-off performance on wing surfaces, requiring switch to Type III or abandoning anti-icing and increasing re-treatment frequency; operators must carry multiple fluid types adding storage and logistics complexity

l4_steps.name: Calculate Holdover Time from FAA/TC Tables via EFB
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen FliteDeck (EFB — FAA/TC HOT Table Application)
l4_steps.input: Anti-icing fluid type, dilution ratio, application start time, OAT, precipitation type and rate
l4_steps.output: HOT start and end times calculated and communicated to flight crew via ACARS or verbal relay
l4_steps.kpi: HOT calculation completed within 2 min of anti-icing fluid application start; communicated to captain before pushback clearance request; zero cases of HOT communicated after pushback initiation
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA/TC HOT tables are conservative estimates; actual holdover time reduced by wind, direct sunlight, taxiway delays — flight crews must perform independent pre-departure contamination check but training and procedures vary by airline; EFB app connectivity failures force manual table lookup

l4_steps.name: Conduct Post-Application Clean Aircraft Inspection
l4_steps.system: SITA Airport Management System (AMS) — Mobile Ops Tablet
l4_steps.input: Anti-icing fluid applied, aircraft surfaces, current precipitation conditions
l4_steps.output: Clean aircraft confirmation issued or re-treatment ordered; inspection result logged with crew ID and timestamp
l4_steps.kpi: Inspection covers 100% of critical surfaces; completion within 5 min of fluid application finish; re-treatment rate < 8% of treated aircraft
l4_steps.pain_point: Inadequate ramp lighting during night ops or heavy snowfall reduces visibility for post-application inspectors; incorrect clean aircraft calls are a primary de-icing safety risk (referenced in multiple NTSB and TSB accident reports); no standardised photographic evidence requirement at most carriers

l4_steps.name: Issue De-Icing Completion Record and Transmit to Flight Crew
l4_steps.input: DMS treatment record (fluid type, volume, dilution, start/end time, HOT range), clean aircraft confirmation
l4_steps.output: De-icing completion report transmitted to flight deck via ACARS; paper copy retained for regulatory compliance per FAA AC 120-60B
l4_steps.kpi: Report transmitted >= 5 min before pushback; 100% compliance with FAA pre-takeoff contamination check communication requirement; zero ACARS transmission failures without verbal backup
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS data entry errors under time pressure cause incorrect HOT communication to crew; regional and charter operations rely on verbal communication with no digital audit trail, creating regulatory exposure; captains not trained to question HOT plausibility against observed conditions

l4_steps.name: Coordinate Pushback Within HOT Window
l4_steps.input: HOT end time, ATC ground departure sequence, aircraft readiness confirmation, tug availability
l4_steps.output: Pushback clearance issued within HOT validity window; ATC ground movement coordination confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: Departure initiated >= 5 min before HOT expiry; on-time departure rate (D0) >= 78% during active winter ops; zero aircraft departing with documented expired HOT
l4_steps.pain_point: ATC sequencing delays during high-demand winter events push departures beyond HOT expiry, requiring return to pad for costly re-treatment; airlines report 18–25 min average re-treatment penalty per aircraft during peak de-icing, cascading across the departure bank

l4_steps.name: Monitor Departure Queue for HOT Expiry and Re-Treatment Triggers
l4_steps.input: Real-time departure queue timestamps, HOT end times per aircraft, updated weather data from DTN
l4_steps.output: Re-treatment orders issued for aircraft exceeding HOT; ATC notified of delay and sequence changes
l4_steps.kpi: Re-treatment decision made >= 10 min before HOT expiry; zero aircraft cleared for takeoff with expired HOT; re-treatment throughput capacity >= scheduled de-icing volume + 20% buffer
l4_steps.pain_point: Simultaneous HOT expiry across multiple aircraft during heavy snowfall creates ramp congestion and cascading departure delays; single de-icing pad airports cannot handle re-treatment surges without significant schedule disruption; AMS does not natively flag HOT expiry without custom integration

l4_steps.name: Log De-Icing Event Data for Compliance and Performance Analysis
l4_steps.input: DMS treatment records (fluid volumes, times, tail numbers, crew IDs), HOT data, weather data, delay records
l4_steps.output: De-icing event records archived; fluid consumption and waste report generated; seasonal performance dashboard updated
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of de-icing events logged within 24 hours; fluid waste rate < 5% of applied volume; regulatory audit trail completeness >= 99.5%; glycol runoff report submitted to EPA/Transport Canada within 30 days of season-end
l4_steps.pain_point: DMS data silos prevent automated correlation with on-time performance and maintenance data, limiting root-cause analysis; EPA and Transport Canada glycol runoff reporting requirements vary by airport and add manual compliance burden; data quality issues in DMS (manual entries, missing fields) degrade seasonal analytics

l4_steps.name: Pull TSA Security Directive updates from portal
l4_steps.input: Daily TSA operational bulletin and Security Directive notifications
l4_steps.output: Updated security parameters and procedural changes for departure day
l4_steps.kpi: Directive review completion 100% by 04:00 local; zero missed directives
l4_steps.pain_point: TSA directives arrive with minimal lead time and no automated push — coordinator must manually poll the portal daily; late directives received after briefings require real-time re-briefing of ramp and gate teams

l4_steps.name: Configure Secure Flight data elements in PSS
l4_steps.input: Updated TSA directive, PNR database for day-of-departure flights
l4_steps.output: Secure Flight data fields (name, DOB, gender, redress number) enabled and validated for all active PNRs
l4_steps.kpi: Secure Flight data completeness ≥99.5% of PNRs before check-in window opens
l4_steps.pain_point: Missing Secure Flight data from OTA and indirect bookings (name misspellings, missing DOB) requires last-minute PNR remediation calls to passengers — average 4–6 incidents per hub departure bank

l4_steps.name: Verify Airport Security Program compliance readiness
l4_steps.input: TSA-approved Airport Security Program (ASP) document, staffing roster, certification records
l4_steps.output: Compliance readiness checklist signed off; uncertified staff removed from security-sensitive positions
l4_steps.kpi: ASP readiness sign-off ≥60 min before first departure; 100% rostered security staff TSA-certified
l4_steps.pain_point: High turnover at outstations leads to uncertified agents being inadvertently rostered in AOA access roles — TSA civil penalties up to $25,000 per violation; AMS roster does not flag certification expiry automatically

l4_steps.name: Transmit Secure Flight Passenger Data Records to TSA
l4_steps.input: PNR passenger name, date of birth, gender, redress number (if held)
l4_steps.output: Secure Flight data batch transmitted to TSA; transmission acknowledgement logged
l4_steps.kpi: Transmission ≥72 hours before departure for advance bookings; 100% transmitted before check-in opens for same-day bookings
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa Secure Flight module timeout during high-volume morning bank causes batch retransmission queues; TSA SLA requires 2-min response window — backlog during irregular operations extends to 15+ min, blocking boarding pass issuance

l4_steps.name: Receive Boarding Pass Print Result from TSA
l4_steps.input: TSA BPPR response codes: OK, SSSS (enhanced screening), or Inhibited (no-fly)
l4_steps.output: Boarding authorization flag applied to each PNR in Altéa; inhibited passengers flagged for escalation
l4_steps.kpi: BPPR response received within 2 min per passenger; 100% BPPR statuses resolved before check-in closes
l4_steps.pain_point: TSA BPPR 'Inhibited' status returned without explanation — agent must call TSA help desk with average hold time of 8–12 min; no case tracking integration between Altéa and TSA portal causes duplicate escalation calls

l4_steps.name: Escalate SSSS or No-Fly result to TSA liaison
l4_steps.input: SSSS or Inhibited BPPR flag from Altéa, passenger PNR details
l4_steps.output: TSA case reference number issued; SSSS passenger directed to enhanced screening lane; no-fly passenger offloaded and PNR annotated
l4_steps.kpi: SSSS coordination completed ≥45 min before departure; no-fly offload confirmed ≥30 min before departure; 100% SSSS passengers cleared or offloaded before gate close
l4_steps.pain_point: Redress number mismatches cause false positives for passengers with common names — average 3–4 false positives per week at major hubs; each requires DHS TRIP form initiation and manual TSA override, averaging 20 min per incident

l4_steps.name: Verify passenger identity document at gate
l4_steps.input: Government-issued photo ID, boarding pass scan, REAL ID enforcement flag
l4_steps.output: Identity verified and documented; boarding pass scanned; PNR boarding status updated in AMS
l4_steps.kpi: Gate document check throughput <45 sec per passenger; REAL ID non-compliance interception rate 100%; boarding completion ≥10 min before departure
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated integration between AMS ID scanner and Altéa PNR — agent must manually annotate non-compliance; inconsistent REAL ID passenger awareness creates gate-queue backlog averaging 4 min per non-compliant incident

l4_steps.name: Handle REAL ID non-compliance exception at gate
l4_steps.input: Non-compliant ID flagged at gate scan; TSA alternate acceptable ID list
l4_steps.output: Passenger offered TSA-approved alternate documents; denied boarding if no acceptable ID presented; denial documented in Altéa PNR remarks
l4_steps.kpi: REAL ID exception resolution <5 min; denied boarding documented in Altéa within 15 min of incident; zero passengers boarded without TSA-acceptable ID
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated link between AMS gate scanner and Altéa PNR creates audit gaps flagged in TSA compliance inspections; manual annotation relies on agent recall during high-throughput boarding — data quality degrades under pressure

l4_steps.name: Submit hold baggage manifest to TSA EDS screening
l4_steps.input: Checked baggage tags, weight manifest, passenger count for flight
l4_steps.output: Baggage screening manifest submitted; TSA EDS queue populated with all bag tags
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of hold bags submitted to EDS before ramp loading begins; EDS screening throughput ≥300 bags/hr at Level 1
l4_steps.pain_point: EDS machine downtime averages 4.2 hr/month per unit at busy stations; fallback to manual ETD screening reduces throughput by 60% and directly risks D0 departure delay — no automated EDS status feed into BagManager to trigger backup protocol

l4_steps.name: Execute passenger-baggage reconciliation check
l4_steps.input: Checked-in passenger list from Altéa DCS vs. boarded passenger scan list from gate
l4_steps.output: Reconciliation report: matched, unmatched, and flagged bags; departure hold issued if mismatch found
l4_steps.kpi: Reconciliation completed ≥15 min before scheduled departure; mismatched bag rate <0.1% of loaded bags
l4_steps.pain_point: Interline baggage transfers lack real-time status in BagManager — connecting bags from partner carriers are invisible to reconciliation logic; increases unaccompanied bag risk on multi-carrier itineraries handled at shared terminals

l4_steps.name: Remove and re-screen unaccompanied baggage
l4_steps.input: Unmatched bag tag identified in reconciliation report; TSA officer tasking request
l4_steps.output: Bag located, off-loaded, quarantined, and re-screened; departure hold issued; BagManager updated with off-load record
l4_steps.kpi: Unaccompanied bag off-load completed <10 min of identification; zero unaccompanied bags loaded; off-load documented 100% in BagManager
l4_steps.pain_point: Off-loading a reconciliation-mismatched bag from a loaded aircraft requires full ramp access re-coordination with TSA and averages 18-min departure delay — each incident costs approximately $8,400 in direct delay costs and downstream slot penalties at coordinated airports

l4_steps.name: Transmit eAPIS passenger manifest to CBP
l4_steps.input: PNR passport and visa data, crew manifest, flight departure details
l4_steps.output: eAPIS manifest transmitted to CBP; acknowledgement receipt logged with timestamp
l4_steps.kpi: Manifest transmitted ≥60 min before international departure per 19 CFR 122.49a; 100% transmission rate; CBP acknowledgement within 10 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Passport data OCR errors from self-service kiosks and online check-in produce CBP manifest rejections — average 2.3 passport corrections per international flight; each manual correction and CBP resubmission adds 8–10 min to pre-departure workload

l4_steps.name: Receive and action CBP pre-departure APIS response
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS + CBP eAPIS Portal
l4_steps.input: CBP per-passenger clearance or no-board response codes
l4_steps.output: No-board orders applied to PNR and flagged in Altéa; cleared passengers proceed to boarding
l4_steps.kpi: CBP no-board response processed ≤10 min of receipt; 100% no-board orders actioned before gate close
l4_steps.pain_point: CBP no-board orders occasionally arrive after gate close due to APIS processing latency — requires aircraft door reopening and coordinated offload, averaging 25-min delay and possible slot forfeiture at slot-controlled international airports (JFK, LGA, DCA, ORD)

l4_steps.name: Offload CBP no-board passenger and associated bags
l4_steps.input: CBP no-board order with passenger PNR and all associated baggage tag numbers
l4_steps.output: Passenger denied boarding; all associated bags located, off-loaded, and quarantined; CBP case number logged in Altéa PNR
l4_steps.kpi: No-board offload completed <15 min of order receipt; 100% associated baggage removed before departure; CBP case number documented in PNR
l4_steps.pain_point: Multi-segment bookings with interline bag transfers make associated baggage identification time-consuming — BagManager search limited to locally scanned bags; bags transferred from partner carriers on feeder flights are invisible, risking incomplete removal and TSA violation

l4_steps.name: Report security incident to TSA Operations Center
l4_steps.input: Incident type classification, timestamp, affected passenger PNR, witness statements, gate CCTV reference
l4_steps.output: TSA incident report filed; case reference number issued; station log updated
l4_steps.kpi: Initial report filed within 4 hours of occurrence per 49 CFR Part 1544.305; 100% incident capture with zero unreported events
l4_steps.pain_point: TSA eFile portal has no mobile interface — field agents must return to operations counter to file reports; creates reporting delays during concurrent gate incidents and documentation gaps when multiple events occur simultaneously across a departure bank

l4_steps.name: Conduct post-departure security compliance audit
l4_steps.system: SITA Airport Management System (AMS) + Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Boarding records, Secure Flight BPPR logs, BagManager reconciliation reports, ID check gate logs
l4_steps.output: Daily security compliance audit report; exception list with root-cause annotations for corrective action; submitted to airline security compliance team
l4_steps.kpi: Audit report completed within 2 hours of last departure; security exception rate <1% of daily passengers processed; 100% exceptions assigned corrective owner
l4_steps.pain_point: No unified compliance dashboard — AMS gate logs, Altéa BPPR records, and BagManager reconciliation data must be manually cross-referenced; average 45 min/day of manual report assembly per station; data format inconsistencies between systems cause reconciliation errors flagged in TSA programmatic inspections

l4_steps.name: Extract flight schedule & compute GSE demand
l4_steps.input: Inbound/outbound flight schedule, stand allocation plan, aircraft type mix
l4_steps.output: GSE demand matrix by stand, flight, and equipment type
l4_steps.kpi: GSE demand forecast accuracy ≥95% vs actual utilisation
l4_steps.pain_point: AMS schedule feeds lag 2–4 hr behind real-time slot changes; GSE demand mismatches occur at congested airports during irregular operations

l4_steps.name: Allocate GSE units to flights via AMS rules
l4_steps.input: GSE demand matrix, current GSE fleet registry with asset status
l4_steps.output: GSE-to-flight assignment schedule published to ramp supervisors
l4_steps.kpi: GSE assignment completion ≥60 min before first departure of each wave; compliance ≥95%
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual supervisor overrides bypass AMS allocation logic, creating last-minute equipment conflicts during irregular operations and peak waves

l4_steps.name: Confirm GSE serviceability against maintenance roster
l4_steps.input: GSE assignment schedule, open work orders, scheduled maintenance calendar
l4_steps.output: Confirmed serviceable GSE list; pool shortfall flag if serviceability rate below threshold
l4_steps.kpi: GSE fleet serviceability rate ≥92% at start of each operational day
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS maintenance records not always updated in real time by field technicians; apparent serviceability rates overstate actual availability, discovered only at stand

l4_steps.name: Pre-position GSE at assigned stand before block-in
l4_steps.input: Confirmed GSE assignment, inbound ETA from AMS flight information display
l4_steps.output: GSE physically staged at correct stand ≥30 min before block-in
l4_steps.kpi: On-stand pre-positioning compliance ≥95% of turns; late positioning incidents ≤2% per month
l4_steps.pain_point: GPS-based GSE telematics not universally deployed; manual radio check-in introduces positioning errors during peak waves, causing stand conflicts

l4_steps.name: Conduct pre-use walk-around inspection per IATA AHM 913
l4_steps.input: IATA AHM 913 inspection checklist, equipment logbook from prior shift
l4_steps.output: Completed pre-use inspection record; pass/fail status logged in Ramco
l4_steps.kpi: Pre-use inspection completion rate 100%; open defects from prior shift actioned before use
l4_steps.pain_point: Inspection checklist compliance drops during early-morning wave peaks; IATA AHM 913 requires 100% completion but enforcement is manual and shift-dependent

l4_steps.name: Validate GPU/ACU electrical output and hose integrity
l4_steps.input: Pre-use inspection pass record, GPU/ACU test equipment readings
l4_steps.output: Voltage/frequency validation report; unit cleared or grounded
l4_steps.kpi: GPU/ACU pre-use pass rate ≥98%; voltage within ±2% of 115V AC / 400 Hz spec
l4_steps.pain_point: Aging GPU units exhibit voltage fluctuations not detected by manual test protocols; risk of avionics damage if aircraft switched from APU to non-compliant ground power

l4_steps.name: Connect GPU and switch aircraft to ground power on block-in
l4_steps.input: Block-in confirmation from AMS, GPU readiness status
l4_steps.output: Aircraft on external ground power; APU shutdown initiated by flight crew
l4_steps.kpi: Aircraft on ground power within 3 min of block-in; APU shutdown compliance ≥90% of turns
l4_steps.pain_point: Ground power connection delays extend APU run time; each additional minute of APU operation costs ~$12–15 in fuel and increases CO₂ emissions beyond CORSIA allowances

l4_steps.name: Deploy belt loaders and baggage tractors for cargo transfer
l4_steps.input: ULD/baggage load plan from departure control system, belt loader assignment
l4_steps.output: Belt loaders and tractors positioned and operational at aircraft doors
l4_steps.kpi: Belt loader/tractor on-stand on-time rate ≥95%; FOD incidents attributable to GSE ≤0 per quarter
l4_steps.pain_point: Belt loader height mis-calibration causes FOD risk and potential cargo damage; no automated alignment verification in SITA AMS — relies on ramp agent visual check

l4_steps.name: Position fueling equipment and coordinate refueling start
l4_steps.input: Fuel uplift order from flight dispatch, fueling equipment availability status
l4_steps.output: Fuel truck or hydrant dispenser positioned; refueling sequence initiated
l4_steps.kpi: Fueling equipment on-stand within 10 min of block-in; fueling completion ≥15 min before STD
l4_steps.pain_point: Fueling equipment scheduling not integrated with AMS turnaround timer; manual coordination via radio introduces sequencing delays that cascade to departure time

l4_steps.name: Log GSE defect in maintenance system with fault code
l4_steps.input: Observed defect during or after turnaround, equipment ID and location
l4_steps.output: Defect record with fault code, severity, and timestamp in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: Defect logged within 15 min of identification; compliance ≥98%; zero unlogged defects on end-of-day fleet check
l4_steps.pain_point: Field staff reluctant to log minor defects fearing shift-end paperwork burden; systematic under-reporting creates hidden fleet degradation trends undetected until failure

l4_steps.name: Assess safety criticality and ground unit if required
l4_steps.input: Defect record, safety-criticality matrix (airline-proprietary), regulatory requirements
l4_steps.output: Safety classification (critical / non-critical); out-of-service tag issued for critical units
l4_steps.kpi: Safety-critical GSE grounded within 30 min of defect identification; zero safety-critical units operated beyond grounding threshold
l4_steps.pain_point: No standardised IATA or ICAO safety-criticality matrix for GSE defects; airlines use proprietary criteria, creating inconsistency during auditor spot-checks and insurance reviews

l4_steps.name: Execute corrective maintenance and post-repair check
l4_steps.input: Work order from AMOS, spare parts from stores, OEM repair manual
l4_steps.output: Repaired GSE unit with completed work order; post-repair serviceability test result
l4_steps.kpi: Corrective maintenance turnaround time ≤4 hr for critical GSE; ≤24 hr for non-critical; first-time fix rate ≥85%
l4_steps.pain_point: Spare parts availability for aging diesel GSE (10+ yr pushback tugs, belt loaders) declining as OEMs shift to electric-only product lines; repair lead times increasing 30–60 days

l4_steps.name: Update GSE fleet availability status in AMS
l4_steps.input: Work order closure in AMOS, post-repair serviceability confirmation
l4_steps.output: GSE unit status updated to 'Serviceable' in AMS fleet registry
l4_steps.kpi: Fleet availability status updated within 1 hr of repair closure; AMS–AMOS sync accuracy ≥99%
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA AMS availability flags not automatically synced from AMOS work order closure; manual dual-entry required, introducing status lag and risk of re-assigning grounded units

l4_steps.name: Compile monthly GSE utilisation and MTBF KPIs
l4_steps.input: AMOS maintenance history, AMS utilisation logs, defect register extract
l4_steps.output: Monthly GSE performance dashboard: MTBF, downtime rate, utilisation by equipment class
l4_steps.kpi: GSE MTBF ≥500 operating hr; fleet downtime rate ≤3%; dashboard published by 5th of each month
l4_steps.pain_point: GSE telematics data not consistently ingested into Tableau; units lacking IoT sensors require manual log extraction, creating fleet visibility gaps in the monthly KPI pack

l4_steps.name: Assess fleet adequacy and identify replacement candidates
l4_steps.input: GSE performance dashboard, asset age register, peak-demand utilisation ratios
l4_steps.output: Fleet adequacy assessment; list of assets recommended for replacement or disposal
l4_steps.kpi: Fleet adequacy ratio ≥1.2× peak demand; assets beyond 10-yr economic life flagged for replacement within next budget cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: Capital expenditure approval for GSE replacement requires 12–18 month lead time via SAP Ariba; aging fleet regularly operates beyond economic life, increasing failure risk and MRO cost

l4_steps.name: Initiate GSE procurement or lease request via SAP Ariba
l4_steps.input: Approved fleet replacement list, capital budget allocation, airport authority concession terms
l4_steps.output: Purchase requisition or lease agreement raised in SAP Ariba; vendor shortlist for tender
l4_steps.kpi: Procurement lead time ≤90 days for standard GSE; ≤180 days for electric/specialist units
l4_steps.pain_point: Airport authority GSE concession agreements at certain airports restrict airline-owned equipment, requiring third-party GSE sourcing at higher cost and lower operational control

l4_steps.name: Extract gate event data from AMS
l4_steps.input: Scheduled reporting period close (daily/weekly trigger)
l4_steps.output: Raw gate event log: block-in, block-out, stand assignment, delays
l4_steps.kpi: Data extraction latency ≤15 min after period close
l4_steps.pain_point: AMS event timestamps may be entered manually by ramp agents, introducing ±3 min inaccuracies that distort D0 calculations; no auto-capture at many regional stations

l4_steps.name: Pull ACARS turnaround event timestamps
l4_steps.input: AMS gate event log from step 1.1
l4_steps.output: ACARS-corroborated block times: chocks-on, door-open, door-close, push-back
l4_steps.kpi: ACARS coverage ≥95% of narrowbody turns at hub stations
l4_steps.pain_point: Regional and outstations with older ground equipment may have ACARS downlink gaps; fallback to manual log creates 5–8% data voids that inflate reported OTP

l4_steps.name: Ingest baggage handling data from BRS
l4_steps.input: Baggage reconciliation system (BRS) export for the period
l4_steps.output: Baggage mishandling records: late bags, wrong-loaded, offloaded, damaged
l4_steps.kpi: WorldTracer file ingestion success rate ≥99%
l4_steps.pain_point: WorldTracer data latency at transborder stations (US/Canada/Mexico) can exceed 4 hours due to customs hold scanning delays, making same-day reporting unreliable

l4_steps.name: Validate data completeness across all stations
l4_steps.input: Merged AMS, ACARS, and WorldTracer datasets loaded to Redshift staging schema
l4_steps.output: Data quality report: missing records flagged, coverage % per station
l4_steps.kpi: Data completeness ≥98% of operated flights before KPI run proceeds
l4_steps.pain_point: Redshift ingestion pipelines from SITA AMS rely on SFTP batch files; file delivery failures at outstations can silently drop entire station's data from the reporting run

l4_steps.name: Calculate D0 and D15 on-time departure metrics
l4_steps.input: Validated gate event dataset from phase 1
l4_steps.output: D0 and D15 departure performance % per station, per fleet type, per hour-of-day
l4_steps.kpi: System-wide D0 ≥78%; D15 ≥88% (IATA AHM 810 standard)
l4_steps.pain_point: Carrier-caused vs. non-carrier delay classification is applied post-hoc via delay codes entered by agents — code 93 (ATC) vs code 15 (late aircraft) misclassification inflates ground ops performance metrics

l4_steps.name: Compute gate and stand utilisation rate
l4_steps.input: Stand assignment and block-time data from AMS
l4_steps.output: Gate utilisation % per stand per day; peak-hour congestion index per station
l4_steps.kpi: Gate utilisation target ≥72% at primary hub gates; congestion index <1.2 at peak
l4_steps.pain_point: AMS stand assignment data does not reflect real-time remote-stand tows, causing gate utilisation to be overstated for aerobridged stands and understated for remote apron positions

l4_steps.name: Calculate baggage mishandling and delivery KPIs
l4_steps.input: Baggage mishandling records from step 1.3; passenger boarding counts from Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Mishandled baggage rate per 1,000 passengers; average delivery-to-belt time (minutes)
l4_steps.kpi: Mishandled bag rate ≤3.5 per 1,000 pax (IATA World Baggage Report benchmark); first-bag-to-belt ≤20 min
l4_steps.pain_point: WorldTracer only captures reported mishandled bags; unreported incidents (bag on wrong belt, passenger retrieves wrong bag) are invisible to the KPI, creating systematic under-reporting at busy stations

l4_steps.name: Assess computed KPIs against threshold rules
l4_steps.input: Computed KPI values from steps 2.1–2.3; threshold configuration table in Redshift
l4_steps.output: KPI status flags: Green / Amber / Red per metric per station
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of KPI metrics receive a RAG status within 30 min of data validation
l4_steps.pain_point: Threshold rules are stored as hardcoded SQL in Redshift procedures; changes require a DBA ticket and 48-hour change-management approval — preventing rapid threshold adjustment during irregular ops (IROPS) periods

l4_steps.name: Build station scorecard dashboard in Tableau
l4_steps.input: RAG-flagged KPI dataset published to Tableau Server data source
l4_steps.output: Interactive station scorecard: D0/D15, gate util, bag KPIs, trend sparklines per station
l4_steps.kpi: Scorecard refresh latency ≤60 min after reporting period close
l4_steps.pain_point: Tableau Server extract refresh contention at period close (multiple dashboards refreshing simultaneously) causes 30–90 min delays in scorecard availability, frustrating station managers on early shifts

l4_steps.name: Identify underperforming stations via threshold alerts
l4_steps.input: Published station scorecard with RAG flags
l4_steps.output: Underperformer shortlist: stations with ≥2 Red KPIs or single critical-metric Red flag
l4_steps.kpi: Underperformer identification completed within 2 hours of scorecard publication
l4_steps.pain_point: Alert logic in Tableau uses static thresholds that do not account for seasonal demand variation — stations operating above-plan capacity in peak periods are incorrectly flagged Red, creating alert fatigue

l4_steps.name: Conduct root cause drill-down for Red-flagged stations
l4_steps.input: Underperformer shortlist; flight-level delay code breakdown from Redshift
l4_steps.output: Root cause classification: staffing, equipment, aircraft late-in, ATC, weather, process
l4_steps.kpi: Root cause assigned for ≥90% of Red-flagged stations within 4 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Delay code data quality (entered by ramp agents under time pressure) is insufficient for reliable root cause analysis — IATA AHM delay code 15 (late aircraft arrival) frequently masks ground-caused delays

l4_steps.name: Issue performance improvement notice to station manager
l4_steps.input: Root cause classification and supporting KPI evidence from step 3.3
l4_steps.output: Performance Improvement Notice (PIN) with specific KPI targets and 30-day remediation timeline
l4_steps.kpi: PIN issued within 24 hours of Red-flag identification for stations with ground-caused root cause
l4_steps.pain_point: PINs are issued via email with no structured tracking system — follow-up compliance is manual, leading to 40% of PINs having no documented station response within the 30-day window

l4_steps.name: Assess whether VP Ground Ops escalation is required
l4_steps.input: Station KPI trend data; PIN issuance history; escalation threshold ruleset
l4_steps.output: Escalation decision: escalate to VP Ground Ops or manage at performance manager level
l4_steps.kpi: Escalation decision made within 48 hours of Red-flag identification
l4_steps.pain_point: Escalation thresholds are not codified — decisions rely on individual manager judgement, leading to inconsistent escalation behaviour across regions and delayed VP awareness of systemic station failures

l4_steps.name: Brief VP Ground Ops with station performance summary
l4_steps.input: Escalated station performance package: KPI trend, root cause, PIN history, remediation plan
l4_steps.output: VP decision: resource reallocation, contractor review, or formal station audit trigger
l4_steps.kpi: VP briefing delivered within 72 hours of escalation trigger
l4_steps.pain_point: VP briefing packs are manually compiled from Tableau exports and email threads — no single-source-of-truth system means briefing preparation takes 4–6 hours and version mismatches occur between analyst and manager copies

l4_steps.name: Publish daily ops performance briefing
l4_steps.input: Overnight KPI computation run; previous-day baseline
l4_steps.output: Daily Ops Briefing email/dashboard: top-5 KPI movers, Red-flag summary, delay code distribution
l4_steps.kpi: Daily briefing distributed by 07:00 local time at each hub station
l4_steps.pain_point: Tableau Server scheduled subscription emails require SMTP relay through corporate IT — relay outages (averaging 2 per month) cause delayed or failed briefing delivery with no automatic retry or fallback channel

l4_steps.name: Distribute weekly station scorecard to station managers
l4_steps.input: 7-day rolling KPI dataset; prior week scorecard for trend comparison
l4_steps.output: Weekly scorecard PDF distributed to station managers and regional directors
l4_steps.kpi: Weekly scorecard delivered every Monday by 09:00 local hub time
l4_steps.pain_point: Scorecard distribution list is maintained manually in a shared Excel file — personnel changes at stations result in stale distribution lists, with outgoing managers receiving reports and replacement managers missing them for up to 4 weeks

l4_steps.name: Submit monthly KPI report to senior leadership
l4_steps.input: Monthly KPI summary from Redshift; incident log from AMS; financial impact data from SAP S/4HANA Finance
l4_steps.output: Monthly Ground Ops Performance Report: trend charts, YoY comparison, cost-of-poor-quality estimate
l4_steps.kpi: Monthly report submitted to SVP Operations by the 5th calendar day of the following month
l4_steps.pain_point: Integrating financial cost data from SAP S/4HANA with operational KPI data from Redshift requires a manual reconciliation step — no automated connector exists between operational and financial data layers

l4_steps.name: Analyse 13-week rolling performance trends
l4_steps.input: 13-week historical KPI dataset from Redshift; seasonality index from Amadeus SkyCAST
l4_steps.output: Trend analysis report: directional KPI movement, seasonal-adjusted performance, benchmark gap
l4_steps.kpi: Trend analysis completed quarterly; covers 100% of hub and focus-city stations
l4_steps.pain_point: Seasonal demand data from Amadeus SkyCAST is available to network planning but not integrated into the ground ops reporting layer — analysts apply manual seasonality adjustments based on prior-year data, introducing estimation error

l4_steps.name: Review and update KPI targets in BI platform
l4_steps.input: 13-week trend report; benchmark data from IATA AHM and Airport Council International (ACI)
l4_steps.output: Updated KPI threshold configuration approved and published to Tableau data source; change log entry
l4_steps.kpi: KPI targets reviewed at minimum quarterly; changes approved within 5 business days of review
