l4_steps.kpi: Shipment uplift confirmed < 3 hours of part readiness; ETA accuracy ± 30 minutes for 90% of AOG shipments
l4_steps.pain_point: Same-day AOG courier capacity from remote OEM/distributor locations is limited; belly-freight dependencies on airline own schedule may add 6–12 hours versus charter courier option, but cost approval thresholds slow decision

l4_steps.name: Execute repair or LRU replacement per AMM
l4_steps.input: Serviceable part with traceability docs, approved AMM task card, tooling calibration records
l4_steps.output: Repair or replacement completed; work order in-progress record updated in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: Task execution time within ± 20% of AMM estimated man-hours for 80% of LRU replacements
l4_steps.pain_point: Tooling calibration records held in a separate AMOS tooling sub-module are not always linked to the active task card; engineers must manually verify calibration status, adding 10–15 min per specialist tool

l4_steps.name: Perform functional test and duplicate inspection
l4_steps.input: Completed repair, applicable AMM functional test procedure, BITE / ground test equipment
l4_steps.output: Functional test result recorded; duplicate inspection sign-off completed in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: Functional test pass rate ≥ 97% first attempt; zero releases without mandatory duplicate inspection where required by AMM
l4_steps.pain_point: At minimum-staffed outstations only one LAME may be on duty; duplicate inspection requirement cannot be fulfilled locally, forcing a flight-to-base or ferry-for-maintenance decision which adds hours to disruption

l4_steps.name: Issue Certificate of Release to Service (CRS)
l4_steps.system: AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware (CRS / Tech Log module)
l4_steps.input: Completed work order, functional test results, duplicate inspection sign-off, airworthiness confirmation
l4_steps.output: Signed CRS issued in AMOS; aircraft tech log updated; aircraft returned to airworthy state
l4_steps.kpi: CRS issued < 30 minutes of functional test pass; zero CRS issued against open critical defects
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS user authorisation matrix must reflect the certifying engineer's current type rating and licence scope; expired or incorrectly scoped authorisations are not always flagged at CRS sign-off, creating a regulatory compliance gap (CAR 145)

l4_steps.name: Update tech log, delay code, and disruption report
l4_steps.input: Closed work order, CRS, actual off-block time vs scheduled
l4_steps.output: IATA delay code recorded, passenger disruption cost captured, AOG event closed in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: Delay code accuracy ≥ 98% (audited quarterly); disruption report filed within 2 hours of aircraft departure
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA AHM 780 delay codes for technical events require judgment calls that are inconsistently applied across MCC shifts; downstream performance analytics are therefore unreliable for root cause trending

l4_steps.name: Trigger reliability review for recurring defect
l4_steps.input: AOG event record, defect history for same ATA chapter and aircraft registration
l4_steps.output: Reliability alert raised if defect recurrence threshold exceeded; engineering investigation initiated
l4_steps.kpi: Recurring defect detection rate ≥ 95% within 3 occurrences; RCA report issued within 10 working days
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS reliability trending requires consistent ATA coding across events; MCC coding variance (see step 6.1) means recurring defects are mis-binned into different ATA sub-chapters, masking the recurrence pattern and delaying corrective action

l4_steps.name: Identify MRO capability gap requiring outsourcing
l4_steps.input: Maintenance program review, fleet capacity utilisation report
l4_steps.output: Outsourcing requirement specification with scope and timeline
l4_steps.kpi: Vendor qualification cycle ≤90 days from gap identification
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS capability mapping not always current; manual gap analysis against maintenance program is error-prone and reliant on engineering judgement rather than system-generated flags

l4_steps.name: Issue RFQ to approved vendor shortlist via Ariba
l4_steps.input: Outsourcing requirement specification, current Approved Vendor List
l4_steps.output: RFQ package distributed to shortlisted MRO vendors
l4_steps.kpi: RFQ response rate ≥80% of invited vendors within 14 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Limited pool of EASA Part-145 / FAA-approved vendors for narrowbody heavy checks creates market concentration risk and limits competitive pricing leverage

l4_steps.name: Evaluate vendor Part-145 approval and capability
l4_steps.system: AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware (Vendor Management module)
l4_steps.input: Vendor qualification submissions, FAA/EASA Part-145 approval certificates
l4_steps.output: Approved Vendor List (AVL) update with capability ratings
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of selected vendors hold current EASA Part-145 or FAA Part-145 approval at time of contract award
l4_steps.pain_point: Approval expiry tracking in AMOS requires manual certificate uploads; no automated feed from FAA AIRS or EASA EAMR — expired approvals may go undetected until audit

l4_steps.name: Define MRO work scope and SLA requirements
l4_steps.input: Aircraft maintenance program, fleet maintenance schedule, maintenance history
l4_steps.output: Maintenance work scope document, draft SLA with TAT and quality KPIs
l4_steps.kpi: Work scope completeness score ≥95% (no unplanned post-induction scope additions attributable to pre-induction planning gaps)
l4_steps.pain_point: Scope creep during heavy checks when undocumented corrosion or structural findings emerge; AMOS work orders not pre-linked to vendor contracts, making scope-change traceability manual

l4_steps.name: Negotiate contract terms, pricing, and TAT commitments
l4_steps.input: Draft SLA, vendor commercial proposals, industry man-hour benchmarks
l4_steps.output: Signed MRO contract with TAT commitments, penalty clauses, and AWF pricing schedule
l4_steps.kpi: C-check contract TAT ≤35 days; man-hour rate within ±5% of OAG/industry benchmark
l4_steps.pain_point: Negotiating fixed-price contracts with variable scope (structural findings, AD compliance work) leads to post-check cost disputes; penalty clauses rarely enforced due to vendor dependency

l4_steps.name: Load signed contract into SAP Ariba and AMOS
l4_steps.system: SAP Ariba + AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware
l4_steps.input: Signed MRO contract, approved work scope
l4_steps.output: Active vendor contract record in both SAP Ariba and AMOS with linked work orders
l4_steps.kpi: Contract data entry accuracy 100%; dual-system load completed within 2 business days of signature
l4_steps.pain_point: Dual manual entry into SAP Ariba and AMOS creates synchronisation risk; contract amendments frequently update only one system, causing PO/work-order mismatches that surface at invoice reconciliation

l4_steps.name: Release aircraft to MRO vendor for scheduled induction
l4_steps.input: Signed maintenance work order, aircraft airworthiness release, ferry flight plan
l4_steps.output: Aircraft handover documentation, work package issued to vendor
l4_steps.kpi: On-time aircraft delivery to MRO station ≥95%; handover documentation completeness 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Late aircraft delivery to MRO station (due to operational delays or AOG diversions) disrupts vendor slot allocation and triggers liquidated damages clauses; AMOS does not automatically flag operational conflicts with maintenance slot windows

l4_steps.name: Monitor in-shop progress against TAT milestones
l4_steps.system: AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware (Work Order tracking)
l4_steps.input: Work package milestones, daily shop visit reports from vendor
l4_steps.output: Daily progress reports, milestone deviation flags in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: Milestone adherence ≥90%; TAT variance ≤±10% of contracted schedule at mid-check review
l4_steps.pain_point: Real-time visibility into vendor shop-floor status is absent in AMOS without a Resident Technical Representative on-site; no direct system-to-system integration between airline AMOS and most third-party MRO AMOS instances

l4_steps.name: Approve additional work findings (AWF) change orders
l4_steps.system: AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware + SAP Ariba (Change Order)
l4_steps.input: Vendor non-routine finding report, structural inspection results, AD/SB compliance requirement
l4_steps.output: Approved change order, updated work scope and cost estimate
l4_steps.kpi: AWF approval turnaround ≤4 hours to avoid vendor shop-floor downtime
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS change order approval workflow requires multiple sign-off tiers; delays in AWF approval are a leading cause of TAT overrun in heavy maintenance — vendors charge idle-time fees while awaiting airline decisions

l4_steps.name: Collect vendor scorecard data after work completion
l4_steps.system: AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware + Tableau / Power BI
l4_steps.input: Completed work orders, TAT records, defect escapes, rework events, invoice data
l4_steps.output: Vendor performance scorecard with TAT, quality, and cost dimensions
l4_steps.kpi: On-time delivery ≥92%; rework rate ≤2%; defect escape rate (post-C-of-R finding) ≤0.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Scorecard data is manually aggregated from AMOS work orders and SAP cost postings; no automated vendor KPI dashboard — quarterly scorecard preparation takes 3–5 days of analyst effort

l4_steps.name: Conduct formal quarterly vendor performance review
l4_steps.system: Tableau / Power BI (dashboards from AWS Redshift)
l4_steps.input: Vendor performance scorecard, SLA benchmarks, prior-quarter action items
l4_steps.output: Performance review minutes, corrective action plan if SLA threshold breached
l4_steps.kpi: Quarterly performance reviews completed 100% on schedule; SLA compliance rating reported within ±5% confidence interval
l4_steps.pain_point: Vendors frequently dispute scorecard data citing their own internal metrics; absence of shared system-to-system data exchange creates reconciliation disputes that delay corrective action by 30–60 days

l4_steps.name: Issue corrective action request (CAR) for SLA breach
l4_steps.input: Failed performance review record, documented defect or delay pattern
l4_steps.output: Formal CAR with 30-day vendor response requirement, root cause analysis template
l4_steps.kpi: CAR vendor response rate 100% within 30 days; repeat findings reduced ≥50% within two subsequent work packages
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS Quality module CAR tracking provides no vendor portal access; all CAR follow-up is conducted via email outside the system, creating an unauditable correspondence trail for EASA Part-CAMO findings

l4_steps.name: Review and validate MRO vendor invoices (3-way match)
l4_steps.system: SAP S/4HANA Finance (FI/CO) + AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware
l4_steps.input: Vendor invoice, completed AMOS work order, SAP Ariba PO, approved change orders
l4_steps.output: Invoice approval or dispute flag with line-item variance detail
l4_steps.kpi: 3-way match success rate ≥98%; invoice dispute resolution ≤15 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: 3-way match between AMOS work order, SAP Ariba PO, and vendor invoice frequently fails because AWF change orders are not captured in the original PO — each failure requires manual re-match across two systems

l4_steps.name: Process vendor payment and post maintenance cost allocation
l4_steps.input: Approved invoice, aircraft registration / cost centre mapping
l4_steps.output: Payment instruction, maintenance cost posted to aircraft-level cost centre
l4_steps.kpi: Payment within contracted net-30 terms ≥95%; cost allocation accuracy 100% at aircraft registration level
l4_steps.pain_point: Aircraft cost centre mapping in SAP must align with AMOS aircraft registration codes; registration mismatches (e.g., wet-lease aircraft with swapped tails) cause fleet maintenance cost reporting errors that distort unit cost analysis

l4_steps.name: Evaluate contract renewal vs. re-tender decision
l4_steps.input: Aggregated vendor scorecard (12-month), market pricing benchmarks, contract expiry calendar
l4_steps.output: Renewal recommendation or re-tender decision brief for leadership sign-off
l4_steps.kpi: Renewal or re-tender decision completed ≥90 days before contract expiry; benchmark pricing variance ≤8% from renewed rate
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP Ariba does not proactively alert on contract expiry approaching 90-day threshold; contracts default to auto-rollover at existing rates, forfeiting leverage — market benchmark data requires manual sourcing from OAG or industry surveys

l4_steps.name: Execute contract close-out or new-vendor transition
l4_steps.role: Technical Services Manager + Procurement Specialist — MRO
l4_steps.system: AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware + SAP Ariba
l4_steps.input: Renewal or re-tender decision, new vendor qualification record (if transitioning)
l4_steps.output: Closed-out contract record, active new vendor contract, knowledge transfer documentation
l4_steps.kpi: Vendor transition completed with zero AOG events attributable to transition gap; transition plan signed off ≥60 days before go-live
l4_steps.pain_point: Transitioning open AMOS work orders from outgoing to incoming vendor is a manual process with no system-supported migration wizard; open AWF items and warranty claims risk being orphaned during handover

l4_steps.name: Generate rolling parts demand forecast
l4_steps.input: Scheduled maintenance plan, fleet utilisation forecast, historical consumption rates
l4_steps.output: 12-month rolling parts demand forecast by ATA chapter
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast accuracy ≥85% vs actual consumption over rolling 90-day window
l4_steps.pain_point: Unplanned AOG events and fleet configuration changes (e.g. new aircraft sub-type) invalidate historical consumption rates in AMOS, requiring manual demand model adjustment

l4_steps.name: Calculate reorder points and min/max stock levels
l4_steps.input: Demand forecast, supplier lead times, criticality classification, safety stock policy
l4_steps.output: Updated min/max parameters and reorder point thresholds per part number in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: Stock-out rate <2% for rotables; <5% for expendables on a rolling 30-day basis
l4_steps.pain_point: Lead time variability from OEM suppliers (Boeing, CFM International) causes chronic stock-out events on critical LRUs; AMOS safety stock calculations do not automatically adjust for supplier performance deviations

l4_steps.name: Classify parts by criticality — AOG, Critical, Routine
l4_steps.input: ATA chapter structure, MEL/CDL requirements, historical AOG event data
l4_steps.output: Part criticality classification list; MEL-linked parts flagged as AOG or Critical in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of MEL-linked part numbers classified as AOG or Critical within AMOS
l4_steps.pain_point: MEL revision cycles (typically bi-annual) require manual reclassification in AMOS — no automated sync between regulatory MEL amendments and AMOS part master records

l4_steps.name: Identify approved vendors from Qualified Supplier List
l4_steps.input: Part number, OEM manufacturer P/N, criticality classification, QSL in SAP Ariba
l4_steps.output: Approved vendor shortlist with lead times, pricing history, and performance scores
l4_steps.kpi: ≥2 approved vendors per critical part number; QSL review completed annually
l4_steps.pain_point: Single-source OEM-proprietary parts (Boeing BFE components) leave airline exposed to supply chain disruption; SAP Ariba vendor master requires manual synchronisation with AMOS parts database — discrepancies cause PO rejections

l4_steps.name: Issue RFQ or generate purchase order to vendor
l4_steps.input: Approved vendor shortlist, demand quantity, required delivery date, budget authorisation
l4_steps.output: RFQ responses evaluated and ranked, or confirmed purchase order issued in SAP
l4_steps.kpi: PO issuance within 4h of demand trigger for AOG parts; within 5 business days for routine replenishment
l4_steps.pain_point: AOG parts require emergency PO bypass of standard SAP approval workflow — manual workarounds create audit trail gaps and increase risk of duplicate orders and unapproved spend

l4_steps.name: Validate airworthiness documentation from vendor
l4_steps.input: Vendor-supplied FAA Form 8130-3 or EASA Form 1, Certificate of Conformance
l4_steps.output: Airworthiness documentation approval or rejection recorded in AMOS; non-conformances raised
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of incoming parts accompanied by valid, traceable airworthiness release documentation
l4_steps.pain_point: Counterfeit parts risk from non-OEM surplus suppliers; AMOS lacks automated verification against FAA/EASA airworthiness database — manual cross-check is time-consuming and error-prone during high-volume receiving periods

l4_steps.name: Receive shipment and verify against purchase order
l4_steps.input: Inbound shipment, purchase order, vendor packing list, airworthiness documentation
l4_steps.output: Goods receipt confirmation; quantity and part number discrepancies logged in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: Receiving accuracy ≥99.5% (quantity and P/N match vs PO) on monthly cycle count
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated EDI integration with most parts suppliers requires manual goods receipt entry in AMOS, increasing keying errors; shipping damage from non-compliant vendor packaging not identified until unboxing

l4_steps.name: Perform incoming quality inspection on received parts
l4_steps.input: Received parts, airworthiness docs, incoming inspection checklist, part specification
l4_steps.output: Inspection serviceability tag applied (green = serviceable, red = unserviceable); AMOS inspection record
l4_steps.kpi: Incoming inspection completed within 4h for AOG-classified parts; within 48h for routine parts
l4_steps.pain_point: Inspector availability is a bottleneck during peak maintenance periods (C-check inductions); shelf-life controlled items (seals, O-rings, tyres) may expire during inspection backlog if not prioritised

l4_steps.name: Record serviceable parts into AMOS inventory
l4_steps.input: Inspection-passed part, green serviceability tag, airworthiness documents
l4_steps.output: Part record created in AMOS inventory with bin location, serial/batch number, and financial value
l4_steps.kpi: Inventory record accuracy ≥99.8% validated by quarterly AMOS cycle count
l4_steps.pain_point: Dual-entry requirement between AMOS (inventory) and SAP S/4HANA (financial asset register) for rotable parts creates reconciliation overhead; serial number capture omissions cause rotable tracking gaps during part-swap events

l4_steps.name: Store parts per specification and regulatory requirements
l4_steps.input: Part storage requirements (temperature, humidity, ESD sensitivity, hazmat classification)
l4_steps.output: Part physically located in compliant bin; AMOS bin location and storage condition record updated
l4_steps.kpi: Storage compliance audit pass rate ≥98% at monthly internal stores inspection
l4_steps.pain_point: Constrained line station stores lead to inadequate segregation of serviceable and unserviceable parts; ESD-sensitive avionics LRUs improperly stored in non-ESD zones cause latent damage not detectable at installation

l4_steps.name: Monitor shelf-life and time-controlled items for expiry
l4_steps.input: AMOS shelf-life alert reports, part batch/lot expiry dates, storage duration logs
l4_steps.output: Shelf-life exception report; near-expiry parts flagged in AMOS for priority issue or disposal
l4_steps.kpi: Zero serviceable parts issued or installed past expiry date; shelf-life compliance rate 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS shelf-life alerts require manual acknowledgement — items can expire unnoticed during high workload periods; system does not automatically quarantine parts on expiry date without manual configuration per part class

l4_steps.name: Issue parts against approved maintenance work orders
l4_steps.input: Approved work order part request, technician pick ticket, maintenance task card
l4_steps.output: Parts issued and consumption recorded against work order; AMOS inventory decremented
l4_steps.kpi: Pick accuracy ≥99.5%; parts issue turnaround <30 min for AOG work orders
l4_steps.pain_point: Approved alternate part number substitution (when requested P/N is unavailable) requires real-time engineering authority approval — delays issue when engineers are unavailable on shift, potentially extending AOG ground time

l4_steps.name: Trigger reorder when stock breaches reorder point
l4_steps.input: AMOS stock level alert (below reorder point threshold)
l4_steps.output: Purchase requisition auto-generated and transmitted to SAP Ariba for PO processing
l4_steps.kpi: Reorder trigger-to-PO issuance lead time <2 business days for routine; <4h for critical-classified parts
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS-to-SAP Ariba integration operates on overnight batch synchronisation — same-day reorder triggers do not generate POs until next business day, requiring manual intervention for critical stock-outs

l4_steps.name: Identify and segregate unserviceable and surplus parts
l4_steps.input: Periodic inventory review output, unserviceable tags, surplus stock report from AMOS
l4_steps.output: Unserviceable and surplus parts list with recommended disposition (repair, return, or scrap)
l4_steps.kpi: Unserviceable inventory disposition completed within 90 days of unserviceable tagging
l4_steps.pain_point: Accumulation of unserviceable rotables awaiting shop repair decisions ties up significant working capital; AMOS has no automated escalation for aged unserviceable items — management visibility relies on manual report generation

l4_steps.name: Process disposal, scrap, or vendor return with credit
l4_steps.input: Disposition decision, unserviceable part, vendor return authorisation (VRA), warranty claim documentation
l4_steps.output: Credit note or scrap record; rotable asset removed from AMOS inventory and SAP asset register
l4_steps.kpi: Vendor return credit recovery ≥90% of part value for in-warranty components; scrap processing completed within 30 days of disposition decision
l4_steps.pain_point: Warranty claim processing with OEMs (Boeing, CFM) averages 45–90 days; manual credit note reconciliation between AMOS and SAP Accounts Payable leads to write-off errors and unrecovered warranty value

l4_steps.name: Initiate structural damage finding report
l4_steps.input: Visual inspection finding, C-check opening discrepancy, or SRM-triggered inspection requirement
l4_steps.output: Damage Finding Report (DFR) with location, area, and initial severity classification
l4_steps.kpi: DFR opened within 2 hours of discovery; 100% of findings logged before repair initiation
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual damage measurement and paper sketches introduce transcription errors when uploaded to AMOS; no integrated photo capture workflow forces separate file attachment steps

l4_steps.name: Define NDT method and inspection scope
l4_steps.input: Damage Finding Report, Aircraft Structural Repair Manual (SRM) Chapter 51, airframe area access card
l4_steps.output: NDT Work Instruction specifying method (UT, ET, RT, PT, MT), zone boundary, and acceptance criteria
l4_steps.kpi: NDT scope defined within 4 hours of DFR; SRM chapter referenced on 100% of instructions
l4_steps.pain_point: Boeing Toolbox revision currency lag — SRM updates from Boeing Service Bulletins (SBs) can trail physical publication by 30–60 days, risking use of superseded acceptance limits

l4_steps.name: Evaluate damage against SRM allowable limits
l4_steps.input: NDT Work Instruction, SRM allowable damage limits, measured damage dimensions
l4_steps.output: Disposition decision: within limits (proceed to NDT), beyond limits (escalate to engineering)
l4_steps.kpi: Disposition decision issued within 8 hours of DFR for non-AOG; 100% of beyond-limit findings escalated same shift
l4_steps.pain_point: Ambiguous SRM allowable tables for compound damage (multiple adjacent findings) require engineering judgement; misclassification risk if junior structures engineers make disposition calls without Level III review

l4_steps.name: Submit damage for engineering disposition review
l4_steps.input: Beyond-limits damage finding, DFR with measurements, photographs, and SRM chapter reference
l4_steps.output: Engineering Disposition Request (EDR) submitted to Structures Engineering queue
l4_steps.kpi: EDR submitted within 2 hours of beyond-limits determination; completeness score ≥95% (all required fields populated)
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS EDR workflow does not integrate directly with OEM damage disposition portals (Boeing SRM Online); engineers must duplicate data entry across two systems, increasing cycle time and error risk

l4_steps.name: Evaluate repair options against approved engineering data
l4_steps.input: Engineering Disposition Request, SRM Chapter 51/53/57, applicable Airworthiness Directives (ADs), fleet history for recurring damage patterns
l4_steps.output: Repair scheme selection: SRM standard repair, SRM alternative repair, or DER-designed repair
l4_steps.kpi: Engineering disposition issued within 24 hours for non-AOG; 100% of dispositions reference specific SRM paragraph or approved data source
l4_steps.pain_point: Recurring structural damage at frame stations may indicate systemic fatigue or corrosion issues not captured in individual DFRs; lack of fleet-level damage trending in Boeing Toolbox means repeat repairs go undetected without manual cross-referencing

l4_steps.name: Determine if OEM or DER engineering order is required
l4_steps.input: Repair scheme assessment, FAA DER authority scope, airline DER/ODA delegation matrix
l4_steps.output: Decision: issue in-house Structural Repair Order (SRO) or submit to Boeing/OEM for Engineering Order (EO)
l4_steps.kpi: OEM referral decision made within 4 hours of disposition review; 0 instances of in-house repair where OEM EO was required by AD or AWL
l4_steps.pain_point: Airlines with limited ODA (Organization Designation Authorization) scope must route repairs to Boeing, incurring 5–15 business day lead times that drive AOG extensions; DER authority matrix not always current in AMOS, causing avoidable OEM referrals

l4_steps.name: Issue Structural Repair Order and material requirements
l4_steps.input: Approved repair scheme (SRM, in-house EO, or OEM EO), DFR, parts availability from stores
l4_steps.output: Structural Repair Order (SRO) with step-by-step instructions, material list (alloys, fasteners, sealants), tooling requirements, and inspector hold points
l4_steps.kpi: SRO issued within 2 hours of disposition approval; material list completeness ≥98% (no unplanned AOG parts requests during repair)
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS material reservation does not lock AOG-priority alloy sheet stock, allowing concurrent heavy-check work orders to consume materials needed for structural repairs, causing unplanned procurement delays

l4_steps.name: Assign certified NDT Level II/III inspector to task
l4_steps.input: NDT Work Instruction, inspector qualification matrix (NAS410 / EN4179 certifications), shift roster
l4_steps.output: Inspector assignment confirmed; qualification verified against required NDT method and aircraft type
l4_steps.kpi: Inspector assigned within 1 hour of work instruction release; 100% of assignments verified against NAS410 certification currency
l4_steps.pain_point: NDT Level II/III certifications require 24-month renewal (NAS410); gaps in recency tracking within AMOS qualification module mean expired or method-restricted inspectors may be assigned without automated block, creating FAA Part 145 compliance exposure

l4_steps.name: Execute NDT inspection per approved work instruction
l4_steps.system: Olympus OmniScan (UT/PAUT) integrated with AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware
l4_steps.input: NDT Work Instruction, calibration standards, aircraft access (panels removed, surface prepared), ambient condition log (temperature, humidity)
l4_steps.output: Raw NDT data file, calibration record, inspection coverage map, preliminary indication report
l4_steps.kpi: Coverage rate ≥100% of defined zone (no uninspected area); calibration performed every 4 hours or per shift change; scan data archived within 30 minutes of inspection completion
l4_steps.pain_point: Phased-array UT (PAUT) equipment data files (Olympus OmniScan .evo format) are not natively ingestible by AMOS, requiring manual transcription of indication sizes and locations — primary source of sizing errors reported in ASIAS NDT occurrence database

l4_steps.name: Assess NDT findings against work instruction acceptance criteria
l4_steps.input: NDT indication report, acceptance criteria from SRM or EO, prior repair history at location
l4_steps.output: Accept / reject determination; if additional damage found beyond initial scope, updated DFR issued
l4_steps.kpi: Level III review completed within 4 hours of inspection; 0 indications accepted beyond SRM limits without engineering sign-off
l4_steps.pain_point: Secondary damage found during NDT (e.g., cracking beyond a corrosion blister) resets the engineering disposition cycle, adding 24–72 hours to check schedule with no pre-planned buffer in most C-check work packages

l4_steps.name: Archive NDT findings and close NDT work card
l4_steps.input: Accepted NDT indication report, calibration records, coverage maps, inspector sign-off
l4_steps.output: Closed NDT work card with digital signature; scan data archived to aircraft records in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: Work card closed within 2 hours of Level III acceptance; 100% of scan data files attached to aircraft serial number record
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS document storage size limits (per-record attachment caps) require off-system archiving of large PAUT data files to network shares, breaking single-source traceability and complicating FAA audit responses

l4_steps.name: Procure certified repair materials and special fasteners
l4_steps.system: SAP S/4HANA Finance (FI/CO) integrated with AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware
l4_steps.input: Structural Repair Order material list, stores inventory status, certified material certifications (Mill Certs, C of C)
l4_steps.output: Issued materials kitted and delivered to work stand; material traceability records (batch numbers, C of C) linked to SRO in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: Material kitting completed within 4 hours of SRO release for planned repairs; 100% of issued materials have traceable Certificate of Conformance
l4_steps.pain_point: High-strength aluminium alloy sheet (2024-T3, 7075-T6) and titanium fasteners have long procurement lead times (8–16 weeks); inadequate buffer stock planning in SAP MRP causes AOG parts requests that extend check TAT by 3–5 days

l4_steps.name: Execute structural repair per approved Structural Repair Order
l4_steps.input: Structural Repair Order, approved engineering data (SRM/EO), issued materials, calibrated tooling (torque wrenches, drill jigs)
l4_steps.output: Completed repair with installed doublers/patches/fasteners per SRO specifications
l4_steps.kpi: Repair step completion sign-off within SRO-defined sequence; 0 out-of-sequence step completions; fastener installation torque within ±10% of SRM specification
l4_steps.pain_point: Complex composite-to-metal bonded repairs require temperature-controlled adhesive curing (120°C bond-line) with limited cure oven capacity during peak C-check input; scheduling conflicts with concurrent composites repairs delay structural repair cycle by 12–24 hours

l4_steps.name: Verify repair dimensions and load path restoration
l4_steps.input: Completed repair assembly, SRO dimensional tolerances, engineering drawing, calibrated measurement tools
l4_steps.output: Dimensional check record; pass/fail determination; rework instruction issued if out of tolerance
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of SRO-defined hold points signed before next step begins; dimensional non-conformance rate <2% of structural repair work orders
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS hold-point enforcement relies on inspector discipline — system allows step sign-off without prior hold-point completion if sequences are not correctly locked, enabling inadvertent bypass of critical structural inspection gates

l4_steps.name: Apply corrosion inhibitor and sealant compound
l4_steps.input: Approved repair with completed dimensional check, SRM-specified sealant (PR-1422, EC-776), surface preparation requirements
l4_steps.output: Sealed repair with corrosion protection applied; sealant cure time logged; area prepared for final NDT verification
l4_steps.kpi: Sealant applied within 30 minutes of surface preparation (ASTM D1002 open-time limit); cure time logged per batch number; 100% coverage of faying surfaces per SRM specification
l4_steps.pain_point: Sealant pot-life management under hangar temperature variations (summer: 35°C+) accelerates cure and reduces workable window; inadequate ambient monitoring in maintenance hangars leads to sealant application beyond open-time limits, requiring removal and rework

l4_steps.name: Perform post-repair NDT verification scan
l4_steps.system: Olympus OmniScan (UT/PAUT) integrated with AMOS by Swiss AviationSoftware
l4_steps.input: Completed sealed repair, post-repair NDT Work Instruction, original pre-repair baseline scan data for comparison
l4_steps.output: Post-repair NDT report confirming no sub-surface anomalies, fastener hole integrity, and bondline continuity
l4_steps.kpi: Post-repair scan coverage ≥100% of repair footprint + 25mm margin; indication-free result confirmed on 100% of primary structural repairs before inspector sign-off
l4_steps.pain_point: Sealant application over fastener rows reduces PAUT coupling effectiveness, causing near-surface dead zones that may mask shallow cracking at fastener holes; no airline-standardised post-sealant scan procedure in SRM forces ad-hoc method selection by NDT Level III

l4_steps.name: Quality inspector independent review and dual sign-off
l4_steps.input: Completed SRO work card, NDT pre- and post-repair reports, material traceability records, dimensional check records, engineering EO or SRM reference
l4_steps.output: Quality release stamp on SRO; airworthiness release authorisation issued or corrective action required
l4_steps.kpi: Independent QA review completed within 4 hours of last work card sign-off; QA deficiency rate <1% of released structural repair work orders
l4_steps.pain_point: Dual-sign requirements under FAR Part 145 and EASA Part-145 mandate independent inspection, but AMOS does not prevent the original mechanic from also serving as the independent inspector if role segregation is not enforced at the user account level — a recurring finding in FAA Part 145 audits

l4_steps.name: Verify documentation completeness and regulatory compliance
l4_steps.input: Closed SRO with all work cards, NDT reports, material certs, dimensional records, engineer EO sign-off, QA release stamp
l4_steps.output: Documentation compliance check result; return to service approval issued or documentation deficiency log created for correction
l4_steps.kpi: Documentation review completed within 2 hours of QA release; 0 aircraft released to service with open documentation deficiencies
l4_steps.pain_point: Structural repairs subject to Airworthiness Limitation (AWL) items require recurring inspection intervals to be loaded into AMOS task scheduling at time of repair closure — failure to create the repeat task results in missed mandatory AWL inspections, a critical safety and Part 121 compliance failure

l4_steps.name: Update airworthiness records and issue RTS authorisation
l4_steps.input: Approved documentation package, recurring inspection task creation confirmation (if AWL-driven), aircraft maintenance record
l4_steps.output: Aircraft maintenance record updated; Structural Repair Register entry created; FAA Form 337 (if DER repair) filed; Return to Service (RTS) authorisation signed
l4_steps.kpi: RTS issued within 1 hour of documentation approval; 100% of DER repairs accompanied by filed FAA Form 337 within 8 hours of RTS; AWL recurring tasks created and confirmed in AMOS for 100% of limit-item repairs
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA Form 337 electronic filing via FAA ACAIS portal is not integrated with AMOS, requiring manual data re-entry and introducing 2–4 hour delays at peak check closure periods; lost or misfiled 337s create airworthiness record gaps that require costly FAA coordination to resolve

l4_steps.name: Receive and log AD/SB notice into tracking system
l4_steps.input: FAA AD Federal Register notice or OEM Service Bulletin release
l4_steps.output: Applicability assessment report with fleet impact analysis
l4_steps.kpi: AD applicability assessment completed within 3 business days of issuance; 100% of ADs logged
l4_steps.pain_point: AD applicability across mixed fleet configurations (different mod states, AFMS revisions) requires manual cross-check in CAMP — no automated fleet-wide applicability filter exists, creating missed-applicability risk on large fleets

l4_steps.name: Assess compliance deadline and work priority flag
l4_steps.input: Applicability assessment report, AD/SB compliance timeframe, flight-hours and cycles data
l4_steps.output: Compliance deadline schedule, priority classification (EAD / mandatory / optional)
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of mandatory ADs scheduled before compliance deadline; 0% AD overrun rate
l4_steps.pain_point: Short-fuse Emergency ADs (EADs) compress planning windows to less than 48 hours, forcing AOG-level priority and displacing planned line maintenance events across multiple stations

l4_steps.name: Determine mandatory vs. optional modification track
l4_steps.input: AD/SB classification, compliance deadline, cost-benefit analysis for optional SBs
l4_steps.output: Work authorization decision: mandatory track (expedite) or optional track (standard planning)
l4_steps.kpi: Mandatory ADs never exceed compliance deadline — 0% regulatory non-compliance rate
l4_steps.pain_point: Optional SBs reclassified as mandatory mid-stream (e.g., OEM safety recommendation upgrade) force reprioritization and resource reallocation from already-scheduled maintenance events

l4_steps.name: Develop Engineering Order from OEM technical data
l4_steps.input: Approved SB/AD task data, AMM chapter reference, IPC part numbers
l4_steps.output: Engineering Order (EO) with task card, materials list, and tooling requirements
l4_steps.kpi: EO development cycle 5 business days for standard modifications; 2 days for emergency ADs
l4_steps.pain_point: Boeing TechConnect access latency and AMM revision currency issues cause engineers to reference outdated task data — no automated revision alert in AMOS when OEM documentation is superseded post-EO creation

l4_steps.name: Classify modification as major or minor alteration
l4_steps.system: FAA FSIMS (Flight Standards Information Management System)
l4_steps.input: Engineering Order draft, modification scope and system criticality assessment
l4_steps.output: Major/minor alteration determination per FAR Part 43 Appendix A; DER involvement decision
l4_steps.kpi: Major/minor determination documented within 1 business day of EO draft completion; 0% misclassification findings on FAA audits
l4_steps.pain_point: Major vs. minor alteration boundary under FAR Part 43 Appendix A is subjective for novel avionics integrations — misclassification exposes the airline to FAA enforcement action and certificate action during oversight audits

l4_steps.name: Submit Engineering Order to CAMO for formal approval
l4_steps.input: Completed EO with DER determination, SB copy, applicability data, materials list
l4_steps.output: CAMO-approved EO, released work order number in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: CAMO EO approval turnaround 2 business days for standard modifications; same-day for EADs
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS approval workflow does not enforce mandatory attachment validation (SB copy, applicability data), allowing incomplete EOs to route to the shop floor and cause mid-task holds for missing documentation

l4_steps.name: Raise parts requisition for avionics LRUs and consumables
l4_steps.input: Approved EO materials list, IPC part numbers, supplier approved vendor list (AVL)
l4_steps.output: Purchase order or stores issue request for LRUs, connectors, wire, and consumables
l4_steps.kpi: Parts availability confirmed 72 hours before scheduled modification slot; on-time parts availability rate 95%
l4_steps.pain_point: Avionics LRU lead times from OEM-approved suppliers (Honeywell, Collins Aerospace) can reach 60–90 days — long-range parts planning is rarely executed because modification scheduling is reactive, creating AOG parts shortages

l4_steps.name: Verify parts serviceability, traceability, and shelf-life
l4_steps.input: Parts received from stores or supplier, FAA Form 8130-3 / EASA Form 1 certificates
l4_steps.output: Go/No-Go decision for scheduled modification slot; quarantine order if parts rejected
l4_steps.kpi: Parts shortage-driven deferral rate 5% of avionics work orders; counterfeit parts detection — 0 unapproved parts reaching aircraft
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS parts provenance tracking does not automate FAA AC 21-29D traceability chain verification for avionics LRUs — manual document review required, and counterfeit avionics parts remain an active industry risk (FAA SUP-04 flag)

l4_steps.name: Reserve hangar bay, tooling, and technician staffing
l4_steps.input: Approved EO, parts availability confirmation, aircraft schedule and induction date
l4_steps.output: Confirmed maintenance event: hangar bay, specialized avionics tooling, staffing plan, and ground support equipment reservation
l4_steps.kpi: Avionics modification slot utilization 85%; aircraft out-of-service time within 10% of planned duration
l4_steps.pain_point: Avionics modifications requiring simultaneous avionics and airframe access create hangar bay scheduling conflicts, particularly when consolidated with heavy check inputs — bay and lift equipment contention causes schedule slippage

l4_steps.name: Remove existing avionics LRU and prepare installation zone
l4_steps.input: Approved EO task card, aircraft inducted into maintenance bay, tooling issued
l4_steps.output: Removed LRU tagged with part number, serial number, and removal date; cleared and inspected installation area
l4_steps.kpi: LRU removal and serviceable tagging completed per AMM procedure; 0 FOD events per modification event
l4_steps.pain_point: Trax task card completion tracking is not real-time on the hangar floor — supervisors rely on end-of-shift paper sign-offs that delay discrepancy identification and extend aircraft ground time

l4_steps.name: Install avionics modification per EO and AMM procedure
l4_steps.input: Approved EO, new LRU with FAA Form 8130-3, wiring diagram, torque specifications
l4_steps.output: Installed avionics component with completed installation task card; connector and harness photographs
l4_steps.kpi: Installation rework rate 2% of avionics work orders; first-time quality rate 98%
l4_steps.pain_point: Wire harness modifications on older aircraft encounter undocumented prior non-standard SB wiring deviations not reflected in current AMM diagrams — creates FOD risk and requires unplanned engineering investigation, extending aircraft down time

l4_steps.name: Inspect wiring integrity, bonding, and HIRF protection
l4_steps.input: Completed wiring installation, bonding resistance test results, HIRF test equipment readings
l4_steps.output: Wiring inspection pass/fail determination; rework order issued if failed
l4_steps.kpi: Wiring inspection pass rate 96% first pass; rework cycle 4 hours; 0 HIRF non-conformances at release
l4_steps.pain_point: HIRF and lightning protection bonding measurements require specialized test equipment not always available at line stations — deferred compliance testing creates a safety gap and requires ferry flight restrictions until verified

l4_steps.name: Load approved avionics software and update configuration data
l4_steps.input: Approved software part number, Loadable Software Aircraft Part (LSAP) list, aircraft data loader
l4_steps.output: Confirmed software load complete; post-load configuration report with part number and version verification
l4_steps.kpi: Software load completion without error within 2 hours; LSAP compatibility verified against aircraft CDS 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: LSAP version mismatches between aircraft Configuration Deviation Sheet (CDS) maintained in CAMP and the physical installed state cause rejected loads — manual CDS reconciliation is error-prone during high-tempo fleet-wide software campaigns

l4_steps.name: Execute functional ground test per approved test procedure
l4_steps.input: Completed modification, aircraft on ground power unit, approved test procedure and acceptance criteria
l4_steps.output: Functional test report with pass/fail for each test parameter; BITE fault code log
l4_steps.kpi: Avionics ground test pass rate 94% first run; 0 open safety-of-flight defects at release
l4_steps.pain_point: BITE test coverage on older avionics line-replaceable units may not fully exercise the modification scope — supplemental manual test procedures are required but not always linked in AMOS task cards, creating coverage gaps discovered only during flight test

l4_steps.name: Evaluate test results against acceptance criteria
l4_steps.input: Functional test report, BITE fault codes, acceptance criteria from EO and AMM
l4_steps.output: Airworthiness determination: proceed to release or raise defect work order for rework
l4_steps.kpi: Discrepancy rate at final test 4%; 0 open safety-of-flight items at time of release
l4_steps.pain_point: Test acceptance criteria for modified systems sometimes reference superseded test procedures — AMOS and Trax do not flag document revision status at time of test sign-off, allowing outdated acceptance limits to be applied to new configurations

l4_steps.name: Complete maintenance release and regulatory documentation
l4_steps.input: Completed task cards, functional test report, DER approval (if major alteration), FAA Form 8130-3
l4_steps.output: Signed maintenance release; FAA Form 337 filed for major alterations; updated aircraft log entry
l4_steps.kpi: Maintenance release documentation completeness 100% before aircraft release; FAA Form 337 filed within 30 days of major alteration completion
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA Form 337 filing for major alterations is a paper-plus-digital hybrid process in FAA FSIMS with no automated submission confirmation — missed or late filings are only discovered during FAA Principal Inspector audits, exposing the operator to civil penalty

l4_steps.name: Update aircraft configuration records and return to service
l4_steps.input: Signed maintenance release, EO closure, modification documentation package
l4_steps.output: Updated aircraft status in CAMP (mod state, AFMS revision, AD compliance record); aircraft released to operations
l4_steps.kpi: Configuration record update completed within 24 hours of maintenance release; CAMP mod state accuracy 99.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: CAMP Systems configuration record updates for multi-LRU modifications require manual entry of each modified item — bulk update capability is absent, creating data entry backlog during fleet-wide AD compliance campaigns and increasing the risk of mod state discrepancies between CAMP and physical aircraft

l4_steps.name: Compile CAMO annual audit programme
l4_steps.input: Regulatory calendar (EASA Part-CAMO / FAR Part 145), contracted MRO provider list, prior audit cycle dates
l4_steps.output: Approved annual audit schedule with provider assignments and due dates
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of Part-145 approved providers audited within 24-month cycle; schedule published ≥60 days before Q1
l4_steps.pain_point: MRO provider network spans 15+ stations; manual calendar alignment in spreadsheets leads to audit gaps when contracts are added mid-year without AMOS notification trigger

l4_steps.name: Risk-score providers using performance data
l4_steps.input: Historical finding rates, open CAR age, repeat finding history, on-time delivery metrics from AMOS
l4_steps.output: Provider risk ranking matrix (High / Medium / Low) with scoring rationale
l4_steps.kpi: Risk model refresh completed ≤5 business days after each completed audit; High-risk providers flagged within 48 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Reliability data is siloed across AMOS and airline OTP systems; manual data extraction introduces 1–2 week lag that distorts risk scores

l4_steps.name: Determine if expedited audit is required
l4_steps.input: Provider risk score, occurrence reports filed against provider, regulatory authority safety bulletins
l4_steps.output: Audit priority decision: standard schedule maintained or expedited audit triggered
l4_steps.kpi: Expedited audit commenced within 10 business days of trigger event; 0 High-risk providers left unaudited >6 months
l4_steps.pain_point: EASA/FAA safety bulletins arrive via email with no automated AMOS integration; manual triage by QA Manager creates response-time variability

l4_steps.name: Retrieve prior audit findings and open CARs
l4_steps.input: Provider ID, audit history reference, open Corrective Action Request (CAR) log
l4_steps.output: Prior finding summary report with CAR status (open / overdue / closed)
l4_steps.kpi: CAR retrieval completed within 1 business day; zero open Level 1 CARs permitted before new audit commences
l4_steps.pain_point: Legacy AMOS implementations store CAR evidence as unstructured PDF attachments; keyword search across >500 CARs per provider is unreliable without structured data entry discipline

l4_steps.name: Generate compliance checklist from Part-145 requirements
l4_steps.input: EASA Part-145 / FAR 145 regulatory requirements, airline-specific MOE (Maintenance Organisation Exposition), prior non-conformances
l4_steps.output: Structured audit checklist with regulatory reference codes and prior finding flags
l4_steps.kpi: Checklist covers 100% of applicable regulatory subparts; prior repeat-finding items tagged for enhanced scrutiny
l4_steps.pain_point: EASA AMC amendments (e.g. 2022 Part-CAMO revision) require manual checklist updates; no automated regulatory change management feed into AMOS checklist library

l4_steps.name: Issue formal pre-audit notification to provider
l4_steps.input: Approved audit schedule, checklist scope, lead auditor assignment
l4_steps.output: Pre-audit notification letter with scope, dates, document request list transmitted to Part-145 provider
l4_steps.kpi: Notification issued ≥14 calendar days before audit start; document request acknowledgement received within 5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Some third-party MRO stations (particularly overseas line stations) acknowledge notifications informally via WhatsApp rather than through AMOS supplier portal, creating audit-trail gaps

l4_steps.name: Confirm provider readiness and document receipt
l4_steps.input: Pre-audit document submission from provider (MOE, personnel licences, equipment calibration records, training records)
l4_steps.output: Readiness confirmation or audit postponement decision
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of requested documents received and reviewed before audit day 1; postponement rate <10% of scheduled audits
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS document portal upload limits (50 MB per file) cause providers to split calibration certificate packages across multiple uploads, increasing pre-audit review time by 30–40%

l4_steps.name: Conduct opening meeting and confirm audit scope
l4_steps.input: Audit checklist, attendee list (provider Accountable Manager, QA lead, production planning), pre-audit findings
l4_steps.output: Signed scope-confirmation record; audit log opened in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: Opening meeting completed within 1 hour; scope agreed and documented before hangar/records access begins
l4_steps.pain_point: Remote line stations (e.g. outstation MRO) conduct opening meetings via video call; AMOS audit log does not capture video-session metadata, creating traceability gaps for regulatory inspectors

l4_steps.name: Audit technical records for airworthiness compliance
l4_steps.input: Aircraft technical logbooks, Airworthiness Directive (AD) compliance records, component removal/installation logs, deferred defect register
l4_steps.output: Records audit worksheet with compliance status per AD/SB and identified discrepancies
l4_steps.kpi: AD compliance rate ≥99.5% across sampled aircraft tail numbers; zero unaddressed mandatory ADs permitted
l4_steps.pain_point: CAMP airworthiness data is not always synchronised with provider's AMOS work-order records in real time; delta between systems causes false AD non-compliance flags requiring manual reconciliation

l4_steps.name: Inspect maintenance facilities, tooling, and personnel
l4_steps.input: Tooling calibration register, Part-66 licence currency list, hangar environment records (FOD control logs, lighting/temperature)
l4_steps.output: Facilities inspection record with pass/fail status per checklist item
l4_steps.kpi: Tooling calibration current for ≥99% of items sampled; zero expired Part-66 licences on active maintenance staff
l4_steps.pain_point: Calibration certificates managed in provider's local spreadsheet rather than AMOS; discrepancies between paper records and AMOS calibration register are a recurring Level 2 finding

l4_steps.name: Classify findings and identify Level 1 safety issues
l4_steps.input: Completed audit checklist, records worksheet, facilities inspection record
l4_steps.output: Preliminary finding classification (Level 1 / Level 2 / Level 3) entered in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: All findings classified within 4 hours of audit completion; Level 1 findings notified to Accountable Manager within 2 hours of identification
l4_steps.pain_point: EASA Level 1 / Level 2 classification criteria have grey areas (e.g. incomplete but not falsified records); inconsistent classification between auditors increases provider dispute rate and regulatory risk

l4_steps.name: Issue stop-work notice or immediate CAR for Level 1
l4_steps.input: Level 1 finding record, regulatory authority contact details, affected aircraft tail numbers
l4_steps.output: Formal stop-work notice or immediate CAR issued; regulatory authority notified within 24 hours per EASA Part-CAMO M.B.902
l4_steps.kpi: Regulatory authority notification within 24 hours of Level 1 finding; stop-work enforced within 2 hours on affected task
l4_steps.pain_point: Stop-work authority at outstations requires on-call Accountable Manager approval; out-of-hours time-zone issues cause average 4-hour delay in Level 1 stop-work enforcement at overseas stations

l4_steps.name: Finalise audit report and issue CARs to provider
l4_steps.input: Classified finding list, provider Accountable Manager details, regulatory references per finding
l4_steps.output: Signed audit report and numbered CARs issued to provider within 5 business days of audit close
l4_steps.kpi: Audit report issued within 5 business days; CAR numbering 100% traceable to audit report section
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS CAR module does not auto-populate regulatory reference citations; auditors manually copy EASA AMC text, introducing transcription errors that providers use to dispute finding validity

l4_steps.name: Review and accept or reject provider CAP response
l4_steps.input: Provider Corrective Action Plan (CAP) with root-cause analysis, containment action, corrective action, preventive action, and target completion dates
l4_steps.output: CAP acceptance or rejection with specific deficiency comments returned to provider
l4_steps.kpi: CAP response received from provider within 10 business days (Level 1) / 30 days (Level 2); first-submission acceptance rate ≥75%
l4_steps.pain_point: Providers frequently submit '5-Why' root-cause analyses that misidentify systemic causes as individual errors, leading to repeat findings in subsequent audits; AMOS has no CAP quality scoring mechanism

l4_steps.name: Track CAP implementation and verify closure evidence
l4_steps.input: Accepted CAP with milestone dates, provider evidence submissions (revised procedures, training records, calibration certificates)
l4_steps.output: CAR closure record with verified evidence reference; overdue CARs escalated to Accountable Manager
l4_steps.kpi: CAR on-time closure rate ≥90%; zero Level 1 CARs open beyond 30 days; Level 2 CARs closed within 90 days
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS CAR closure workflow requires Accountable Manager digital signature but does not enforce two-person review; single-reviewer closure of Level 1 CARs has been flagged in EASA SAFA audits as a systemic gap

l4_steps.name: Monitor fleet-wide AD and SB compliance status
l4_steps.input: FAA/EASA AD feeds, Boeing Service Bulletin library, current aircraft maintenance status from AMOS
l4_steps.output: AD/SB compliance dashboard with next-due dates and overdue alerts by tail number
l4_steps.kpi: AD compliance rate ≥99.9% at fleet level; zero aircraft operated with overdue mandatory ADs; SB incorporation decisions documented within 30 days of issue
l4_steps.pain_point: CAMP receives FAA AD feeds automatically but EASA ADs require manual import from EASA e-Rules portal; 24–72 hour lag creates window where a newly effective EASA AD is not yet reflected in CAMP, risking inadvertent non-compliance

l4_steps.name: Analyse reliability programme outputs for adverse trends
l4_steps.input: PIREP/MAREP data from AMOS, component removal rates, in-flight shutdown rates, delay/cancellation codes, industry benchmark data (IATA MCTM)
l4_steps.output: Monthly reliability report with control chart trend analysis and alert flag list
l4_steps.kpi: Reliability report published by 5th working day of each month; alert threshold breach investigated within 10 business days; IFSD rate ≤0.02 per 1,000 engine hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Delay/cancellation codes entered by operations staff often misclassify maintenance-caused events as ATC or weather; data quality issues in AMOS cause reliability metrics to undercount maintenance-driven disruptions

l4_steps.name: Submit mandatory occurrence reports to regulator
l4_steps.system: ECCAIRS 2 (European Coordination Centre for Accident and Incident Reporting Systems)
l4_steps.input: Occurrence reports from maintenance crews, AMOS defect records, CAMO safety investigation findings
l4_steps.output: Mandatory occurrence report (MOR) submitted to EASA / national CAA within 72 hours per Regulation (EU) 376/2014; ASRS report filed for US operations
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of reportable occurrences submitted within 72-hour regulatory deadline; MOR rejection rate <2%; follow-up investigation reports submitted within 30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: ECCAIRS 2 taxonomy (≥1,800 occurrence categories) is complex; front-line reporters default to generic codes, reducing data quality for safety trend analysis across the European aviation safety database

l4_steps.name: Extract historical MRO spend from SAP S/4HANA
l4_steps.input: Prior-year actuals, cost centre hierarchy, work order history
l4_steps.output: 3-year MRO spend baseline by category (line, heavy, components, engines)
l4_steps.kpi: Baseline accuracy ≥98% vs audited actuals
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS work order costs and SAP cost centres may not be fully reconciled if interface mappings were altered during AMOS upgrades, producing baseline gaps

l4_steps.name: Validate cost centre structure for MRO domains
l4_steps.input: Chart of accounts, maintenance cost centre master data
l4_steps.output: Validated cost centre tree mapped to AMOS task-card categories
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of AMOS work order types mapped to SAP cost centre before budget lock
l4_steps.pain_point: New regulatory requirements (EASA Part-145, FAR Part 145) occasionally introduce new work-scope categories with no corresponding SAP cost centre, delaying budget submission

l4_steps.name: Set annual MRO budget targets by category
l4_steps.input: Baseline spend, fleet plan, planned utilisation hours, escalation indices
l4_steps.output: Approved annual MRO budget with monthly phasing per cost centre
l4_steps.kpi: Budget submission on time (T-60 days before fiscal year start)
l4_steps.pain_point: Fleet utilisation assumptions from Amadeus SkyWORKS schedule plan may diverge from finance model, requiring manual reconciliation loop between Planning and Engineering

l4_steps.name: Record labour and material costs to work orders
l4_steps.input: Signed-off task cards, parts consumption records, technician time sheets
l4_steps.output: Costed work orders with labour hours, part numbers, and unit prices
l4_steps.kpi: Work order cost closure within 48 hours of task completion; <2% late-closure rate
l4_steps.pain_point: Technician time entries in AMOS depend on line-station connectivity; remote outstations with poor VPN links accumulate backlog of uncosted work orders, distorting weekly cost reports

l4_steps.name: Allocate vendor costs to work orders via SAP Ariba
l4_steps.input: PO line items for outsourced maintenance, AMOS work order references
l4_steps.output: Work orders with vendor cost allocations and PO cross-references
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of vendor POs linked to a work order before invoice approval
l4_steps.pain_point: Ad-hoc AOG purchases placed verbally and backed by emergency POs are frequently missing work order references, requiring retrospective allocation that delays month-end close by 3–5 days

l4_steps.name: Validate work order cost allocation completeness
l4_steps.input: Open and closed work orders for the reporting period
l4_steps.output: Allocation validation report; unallocated cost exception list
l4_steps.kpi: ≤1% of period spend unallocated at month-end close
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS does not enforce mandatory cost-centre fields on all work order types; engineering change orders may slip through without allocation flags

l4_steps.name: Receive and register vendor invoices in SAP Ariba
l4_steps.input: Vendor invoice (PDF/EDI), purchase order number, goods receipt note
l4_steps.output: Registered invoice with PO and GRN cross-references in SAP Ariba
l4_steps.kpi: Invoice registration within 24 hours of receipt; e-invoice adoption ≥70% of MRO vendors
l4_steps.pain_point: Many smaller MRO vendors (especially AOG parts suppliers) still submit paper invoices or non-standard PDF formats; manual data entry introduces keying errors that fail automated matching

l4_steps.name: Execute 3-way match: PO vs GRN vs invoice
l4_steps.input: Registered invoice, SAP Ariba PO, AMOS goods receipt note
l4_steps.output: 3-way match result: matched, price variance, or quantity variance
l4_steps.kpi: First-pass 3-way match success rate ≥85%; invoice cycle time ≤10 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Component exchange transactions (core returns) create credit/debit timing mismatches between AMOS goods receipt and vendor invoice, routinely failing automated matching and requiring manual intervention

l4_steps.name: Validate invoice scope against approved work order
l4_steps.input: 3-way match result, approved work scope from AMOS work order
l4_steps.output: Invoice approval decision: approved, disputed, or escalated
l4_steps.kpi: Invoice dispute rate ≤5% of total MRO invoices per month
l4_steps.pain_point: Vendors frequently invoice for additional scope discovered during shop visits (beyond approved estimate), and contracts that lack not-to-exceed clauses result in uncontrolled cost escalation; AMOS scope change workflow is not always enforced before additional work begins

l4_steps.name: Post approved vendor invoices in SAP AP
l4_steps.input: Approved invoice from MRO Contract Manager
l4_steps.output: Posted AP document; payment scheduled per vendor payment terms
l4_steps.kpi: On-time payment rate ≥95%; early payment discount capture ≥80% where applicable
l4_steps.pain_point: Payment terms negotiated in SAP Ariba contracts are not always replicated accurately in SAP vendor master, resulting in missed early-payment discounts and occasional late-payment penalties

l4_steps.name: Extract cost and utilisation data for KPI calculation
l4_steps.input: AMOS work order actuals, SAP cost postings, flight operations utilisation data
l4_steps.output: Consolidated MRO cost and utilisation dataset in Redshift analytics schema
l4_steps.kpi: Data pipeline refresh completed by Day 3 of month following reporting period
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS and SAP use different fiscal period boundaries; the one-day offset between AMOS maintenance close and SAP financial close creates period-boundary mismatches that require manual correction macros in the ETL pipeline

l4_steps.name: Calculate CPFH, cost-per-cycle and maintenance cost ratio
l4_steps.input: Consolidated cost dataset, fleet utilisation hours and cycles from Jeppesen FliteDeck
l4_steps.output: KPI scorecard: CPFH by fleet type, CPD, maintenance cost as % of total operating cost
l4_steps.kpi: CPFH variance vs budget ≤±5%; maintenance cost ratio ≤15% of total operating cost
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen FliteDeck flight data is updated at block-off; last-minute flight diversions or technical returns can shift utilisation hours after the KPI snapshot has been taken, requiring a restatement process

l4_steps.name: Publish KPI dashboard to Power BI for stakeholders
l4_steps.input: KPI scorecard dataset from Redshift
l4_steps.output: Published Power BI dashboard with trend lines, budget vs actual, and drill-through by vendor
l4_steps.kpi: Dashboard published by Day 5 of the following month; stakeholder satisfaction score ≥4/5
l4_steps.pain_point: Row-level security in Power BI requires separate maintenance when new vendor contracts are onboarded; security configuration delays occasionally result in vendors seeing each other's cost data

l4_steps.name: Review KPIs against thresholds and alert on breaches
l4_steps.input: Published KPI dashboard, approved threshold parameters
l4_steps.output: KPI status: Green / Amber / Red per metric; variance alert issued for Amber/Red items
l4_steps.kpi: All Red-threshold KPIs reviewed and actioned within 5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Threshold parameters are set at contract signing and rarely reviewed; fleet age progression and inflationary pressures mean legacy thresholds become misleading benchmarks that suppress appropriate escalation

l4_steps.name: Conduct root-cause analysis for cost overruns
l4_steps.input: Variance alert, work order drill-through from Power BI, vendor invoice details
l4_steps.output: Root-cause analysis report identifying driver of overrun (scope, price, volume, mix)
l4_steps.kpi: Root-cause report issued within 10 business days of period close
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS work order comments are free-text with no structured categorisation, making automated root-cause clustering difficult; analysts must manually review hundreds of work orders to isolate systemic issues

l4_steps.name: Issue corrective action plan and assign owners
l4_steps.input: Root-cause analysis report, budget variance magnitude
l4_steps.output: Corrective action plan (CAP) with owner, action, and target completion date
l4_steps.kpi: CAP issued within 5 business days of root-cause sign-off; ≥80% of CAP actions closed on time
l4_steps.pain_point: No dedicated CAP tracking module in AMOS or SAP; action tracking is managed in spreadsheets, causing loss of accountability and making it difficult to evidence closure during EASA audits

l4_steps.name: Update rolling MRO cost forecast in SAP CO
l4_steps.input: Approved CAP, revised cost assumptions, updated utilisation forecast from Amadeus SkyWORKS
l4_steps.output: Revised rolling 12-month MRO cost forecast posted in SAP Controlling
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast accuracy (latest estimate vs actual at year-end) ≤±3%
l4_steps.pain_point: Utilisation forecast from Amadeus SkyWORKS is updated weekly but SAP CO planning cycles are monthly; mid-month schedule revisions (e.g. aircraft AOG grounding) are not reflected until next month's forecast, inflating CPFH variances

l4_steps.name: Prepare monthly MRO cost report for leadership
l4_steps.input: Finalised KPI dashboard, CAP status, forecast update
l4_steps.output: Executive MRO Cost Report (PDF): actuals, budget variance, CPFH trend, top 5 vendor spend
l4_steps.kpi: Report distributed by Day 7 of following month to CFO, VP Engineering, and CEO
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual narrative writing for executive commentary is time-consuming; inconsistent framing between monthly reports reduces readability and makes period-over-period trend comparison difficult

l4_steps.name: Detect Warranty-Eligible Maintenance Event
l4_steps.input: Unscheduled removal, component failure report, or shop finding in AMOS
l4_steps.output: Potential warranty event flag on work order
l4_steps.kpi: Warranty event capture rate ≥95% of eligible removals
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS warranty flag relies on manual technician input; missed flags cause unrecoverable cost leakage when discovery exceeds OEM claim window (typically 90 days)

l4_steps.name: Validate Warranty Coverage Against OEM Contract
l4_steps.input: Component part number, serial number, date of manufacture, hours/cycles on wing
l4_steps.output: Coverage determination: in-scope / out-of-scope with contract reference
l4_steps.kpi: Coverage determination completed within 2 business days of event flag
l4_steps.pain_point: OEM warranty terms scattered across multiple Ariba contract line items; exclusions for airline-induced damage (e.g. FOD, corrosion) frequently disputed without clear documented threshold

l4_steps.name: Confirm Component Airworthiness History
l4_steps.input: Component serial number, operator-applied ADs, service bulletins, repair history
l4_steps.output: Airworthiness history extract confirming no owner-induced damage voiding coverage
l4_steps.kpi: History pull completed within 1 business day
l4_steps.pain_point: CAMP component records can have gaps when aircraft are acquired from lessors or third-party MROs; incomplete records lead to OEM claim rejection citing unverifiable maintenance history

l4_steps.name: Gather Supporting Work Orders and Borescope Evidence
l4_steps.input: AMOS work order, shop finding report, borescope images, QA sign-off records
l4_steps.output: Documentation package: work orders, photographs, tear-down report
l4_steps.kpi: Documentation pack assembled within 5 business days of removal
l4_steps.pain_point: Borescope images stored outside AMOS in file shares; retrieval is manual and inconsistent — OEMs (CFM, Pratt & Whitney) require image sets in specific DPI/format standards or reject claims on technical grounds

l4_steps.name: Assess Documentation Completeness Against OEM Checklist
l4_steps.input: OEM warranty submission checklist, assembled documentation package
l4_steps.output: Gap list or complete sign-off for claim package
l4_steps.kpi: First-time claim submission completeness rate ≥88%
l4_steps.pain_point: Each OEM (Airbus, CFM, Honeywell, Collins Aerospace) has different checklist formats and portal requirements; maintaining current versions of each OEM's checklist is a manual process with no automated update feed

l4_steps.name: Build Formal Warranty Claim Package
l4_steps.input: Complete documentation set, contract reference, estimated recovery value
l4_steps.output: Formal warranty claim dossier with cover letter and cost quantification
l4_steps.kpi: Claim value accuracy within ±5% of final settlement
l4_steps.pain_point: Labour rate and material cost calculations reference SAP actuals — discrepancies between AMOS work order cost codes and SAP cost centres cause reconciliation errors that delay settlement

l4_steps.name: Submit Claim via OEM Vendor Portal
l4_steps.input: Completed claim dossier, OEM-specific portal credentials, part return authorisation (if required)
l4_steps.output: Claim reference number and submission confirmation from OEM portal
l4_steps.kpi: Claim submitted within 30 days of component removal (OEM SLA compliance)
l4_steps.pain_point: OEM portals (Airbus WSC, CFM TEAM, Honeywell MyAerospace) each have unique interfaces; no API integration with AMOS/Ramco means double-entry and high rework rate (~25%) for portal validation errors

l4_steps.name: Register Claim in Warranty Tracking Register
l4_steps.input: OEM claim reference, submission date, recovery value estimate, OEM SLA deadline
l4_steps.output: Warranty claim record with status, owner, and SLA timer in AMOS
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of submitted claims logged within same business day
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS warranty module not universally adopted — some analysts maintain parallel spreadsheet trackers creating version drift and missed follow-up triggers

l4_steps.name: Monitor Claim Status and Escalate on SLA Breach
l4_steps.input: AMOS SLA timer alerts, OEM portal status updates
l4_steps.output: Escalation email or updated status flag if OEM response overdue
l4_steps.kpi: OEM response within 30-day SLA for standard claims; escalation triggered within 5 days of breach
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS SLA alerting requires manual daily review; no automated push notification to account managers — high-value claims (>$50K) routinely age past SLA without escalation

l4_steps.name: Review OEM Assessment and Determination
l4_steps.input: OEM written determination (accept / partial accept / reject), technical rationale
l4_steps.output: Internal review memo: accepted amount vs. claimed amount, variance analysis
l4_steps.kpi: Claim acceptance rate ≥70% of submitted value
l4_steps.pain_point: OEMs commonly invoke exclusion clauses (FAR Part 43 compliance gaps, improper storage, FOD) with limited technical substantiation — airline burden of proof is high and legal recourse under IATA ATA Spec 200 is slow

l4_steps.name: Escalate Disputed Claims to Commercial Team
l4_steps.input: Rejected or partially accepted claim, OEM determination letter, original contract terms
l4_steps.output: Formal dispute letter or escalation to OEM account executive via Ariba correspondence log
l4_steps.kpi: Dispute initiated within 10 business days of unsatisfactory determination
l4_steps.pain_point: Airlines with smaller fleets or lower OEM spend have limited commercial leverage — Boeing and CFM prioritise high-volume operators; dispute resolution timelines can exceed 180 days for turbine-module claims

l4_steps.name: Prepare Technical Counter-Evidence Package
l4_steps.input: OEM rejection rationale, component maintenance records, AD compliance evidence
l4_steps.output: Counter-evidence dossier with supplementary airworthiness and compliance data
l4_steps.kpi: Counter-evidence submitted within 15 business days of dispute initiation
l4_steps.pain_point: AD compliance records in CAMP may not cross-reference superseded bulletins; if OEM cites a service bulletin the airline cannot prove was complied with, the claim is unrecoverable

l4_steps.name: Process Approved Warranty Credit or Replacement Part
l4_steps.input: OEM approval letter, credit note or replacement part despatch notice
l4_steps.output: SAP credit memo posted to vendor account; or goods receipt for replacement component
l4_steps.kpi: Credit posted within 5 business days of OEM approval; replacement part receipted against correct maintenance order
l4_steps.pain_point: OEM credit notes issued in vendor's currency (USD, EUR) — FX timing differences between AMOS claim valuation and SAP posting date create unexplained P&L variance in MRO cost accounts

l4_steps.name: Close Claim and Update Warranty Register
l4_steps.input: SAP credit memo number or replacement goods receipt, final settlement amount
l4_steps.output: AMOS warranty record closed with actual recovery value, settlement date, and variance note
l4_steps.kpi: Claim closure within 3 business days of financial settlement; register accuracy ≥99%
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS closure step is often skipped when analysts are under workload pressure — open claim backlog inflates apparent recovery pipeline and distorts management reporting

l4_steps.name: Generate Warranty Recovery KPI Dashboard
l4_steps.input: AMOS warranty register export, SAP credit memo data, claim age data
l4_steps.output: Monthly warranty KPI report: recovery rate, claim cycle time, rejection rate by OEM
l4_steps.kpi: Report published by 5th business day of each month; warranty recovery rate ≥3.5% of total MRO spend
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS-to-Tableau data pipeline is batch-refresh (T+1); real-time claim status not visible to Finance — monthly accruals for outstanding claims are estimated manually and frequently restated

l4_steps.name: Analyse Claim Patterns and Trigger Vendor Review
l4_steps.input: 12-month warranty claim dataset, component reliability data, OEM rejection rate trends
l4_steps.output: Vendor performance scorecard; recommendation for contract renegotiation or supplier change
l4_steps.kpi: Vendor review completed annually; rejection rate per OEM <15%; repeat claim rate on same part number <5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Warranty rejection patterns (e.g. systemic CFM LEAP defect series) are not automatically correlated with fleet reliability data in Redshift — root cause identification requires manual cross-referencing across three systems

l4_steps.name: Initiate annual planning cycle in SAP S/4HANA
l4_steps.input: Board-approved strategic plan, prior-year close confirmation
l4_steps.output: Planning calendar with milestones and owner assignments
l4_steps.kpi: Planning cycle launched ≥12 weeks before fiscal year-end
l4_steps.pain_point: Misalignment between network planning schedule (Amadeus SkyWORKS) and finance calendar delays capacity cost assumptions by 2–3 weeks

l4_steps.name: Extract prior-year actuals from SAP FI/CO
l4_steps.input: Year-end close completion flag in SAP
l4_steps.output: Actuals data set by cost centre, profit centre, and GL account
l4_steps.kpi: Actuals extraction completed within 3 business days of year-end close
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual reclassification of intercompany recharges between airline OpCo and MRO subsidiary inflates cost centre variances by up to 8%

l4_steps.name: Pull macro & fuel price assumptions
l4_steps.input: Spot fuel prices, FX forwards, GDP and CPI consensus forecasts
l4_steps.output: Approved macro assumption set (fuel, FX, inflation) for planning year
l4_steps.kpi: Fuel price assumption reviewed against IATA Jet Fuel Monitor within ±5% of market consensus
l4_steps.pain_point: Jet fuel price volatility (±40% year-on-year) makes fixed planning assumptions obsolete within Q1; no direct feed from Bloomberg into SAP BPC requiring manual re-entry

l4_steps.name: CFO review and approval of planning assumptions
l4_steps.input: Macro assumption pack from Treasury, strategic volume targets from Network Planning
l4_steps.output: Approved assumption sign-off memo published to all budget owners
l4_steps.kpi: Assumptions approved and published within 5 business days of Treasury submission
l4_steps.pain_point: Late delivery of network capacity plan from Amadeus SkyMAX optimisation run blocks CFO sign-off; fleet assignment iterations can extend 2+ weeks past planning calendar

l4_steps.name: Distribute budget templates via SAP BPC
l4_steps.input: Approved planning assumptions, prior-year actuals, approved headcount baseline
l4_steps.output: Pre-populated budget input templates distributed to 40+ cost centre managers
l4_steps.kpi: Templates distributed within 2 business days of assumption approval
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP BPC template version conflicts when cost centre hierarchy changes mid-cycle (e.g., post-restructuring) cause data submission errors requiring IT intervention

l4_steps.name: Departments enter cost centre budgets in SAP BPC
l4_steps.input: Distributed budget templates, departmental headcount plan
l4_steps.output: Departmental P&L budget and headcount plan submitted in SAP BPC
