l4_steps.kpi: On-time submission rate ≥90% of cost centres by stated deadline
l4_steps.pain_point: Operational departments (Ground Ops, Crew Planning) lack financial modelling skills; submissions frequently contain formula errors, requiring FP&A rework averaging 3 days per cycle

l4_steps.name: Validate completeness of departmental submissions
l4_steps.input: All departmental budget submissions in SAP BPC
l4_steps.output: Submission completeness report; escalation notices to overdue cost centres
l4_steps.kpi: 100% submission completeness achieved before consolidation window opens
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated reminder workflow in SAP BPC; FP&A team manually tracks submissions via spreadsheet, introducing version control risk

l4_steps.name: Validate headcount budget vs SAP SuccessFactors plan
l4_steps.input: Departmental headcount submissions, approved establishment file from SuccessFactors
l4_steps.output: Reconciled headcount budget with variance commentary for exceptions >5 FTE
l4_steps.kpi: Headcount variance between BPC submission and SuccessFactors plan ≤2% at department level
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP SuccessFactors and SAP BPC do not share a live integration; headcount data exported via flat-file weekly, causing stale data when departments submit after the extract cut-off

l4_steps.name: Validate capex requests against fleet and route plan
l4_steps.input: Departmental capex bids, Amadeus SkyMAX fleet assignment output, Boeing delivery schedule
l4_steps.output: Approved capex budget list with project codes assigned in SAP CO
l4_steps.kpi: Capex budget total reconciled to strategic fleet plan within ±2% variance
l4_steps.pain_point: Boeing 737 MAX delivery slippages (historically 6–18 months) invalidate fleet-linked capex budgets; no automated feed from Boeing delivery portal into SAP CO requiring manual re-phasing

l4_steps.name: Consolidate full P&L, cash flow, and balance sheet
l4_steps.input: All validated departmental budgets and capex lists
l4_steps.output: Consolidated airline-level budget P&L, cash flow statement, and balance sheet
l4_steps.kpi: Consolidation completed within 3 business days of submission deadline
l4_steps.pain_point: Intercompany eliminations between airline, MRO entity, and loyalty programme require manual journal entries in SAP BPC; risk of double-counting revenue estimated at 1–2% of group revenue

l4_steps.name: Assess consolidated budget vs EBITDAR target
l4_steps.input: Consolidated budget P&L, Board-approved EBITDAR target range
l4_steps.output: Gap analysis report: budget EBITDAR vs target with sensitivity scenarios
l4_steps.kpi: EBITDAR margin target ≥15% on consolidated airline revenue
l4_steps.pain_point: Fuel and labour costs (>65% of OPEX) are largely non-discretionary; gap closure options are limited and CFO pressure to cut maintenance capex risks AOG rate increases in Y+1

l4_steps.name: Issue cut targets and iterate with cost centres
l4_steps.input: EBITDAR gap analysis, CFO direction on cost reduction quantum
l4_steps.output: Revised departmental budget targets distributed; resubmission timeline set
l4_steps.kpi: Resubmission cycle completed within 5 business days of cut target issuance
l4_steps.pain_point: Repeated iteration loops (average 2.3 rounds per cycle) extend the planning calendar into operational freeze windows, increasing risk of budget being published after the fiscal year has started

l4_steps.name: Reconcile fuel hedge positions with treasury model
l4_steps.input: Confirmed fuel hedge book from Treasury, consolidated fuel volume budget from Operations
l4_steps.output: Hedged and unhedged fuel cost budget with sensitivity at ±10% fuel price
l4_steps.kpi: Hedge coverage ratio target ≥50% of planned fuel consumption for next 12 months
l4_steps.pain_point: Fuel hedging positions managed in Bloomberg are not natively visible in SAP BPC; hedge P&L impact must be manually bridged, introducing a reporting lag of up to 5 business days

l4_steps.name: Prepare executive budget pack for Board presentation
l4_steps.input: Approved consolidated budget, sensitivity scenarios, prior-year comparison
l4_steps.output: Board budget pack: executive summary, key metrics dashboard, risk narrative
l4_steps.kpi: Board pack delivered ≥5 business days before Finance Committee meeting
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual export of SAP BPC data into Tableau introduces version risk; FP&A teams maintain parallel Excel models that diverge from SAP BPC source of truth, undermining data integrity

l4_steps.name: Present budget to Board Finance Committee
l4_steps.input: Executive budget pack, audit committee pre-read, external auditor sign-off
l4_steps.output: Board meeting minutes with approval resolution or revision instructions
l4_steps.kpi: Board approval obtained at first presentation in ≥75% of annual cycles
l4_steps.pain_point: Board members may request scenario re-runs (e.g., different fuel assumptions) that SAP BPC cannot perform live in the board room; delays approval by 1–2 weeks

l4_steps.name: Lock approved budget baseline in SAP BPC and SAP CO
l4_steps.input: Board approval resolution, final budget version in SAP BPC
l4_steps.output: Locked budget version in SAP BPC; approved cost centre budgets released to SAP CO for actuals comparison
l4_steps.kpi: Budget locked and released to SAP CO within 3 business days of Board approval
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP BPC version locking does not prevent ad-hoc manual adjustments via SAP CO cost centre planning; shadow budgets maintained by operations managers erode single-source-of-truth discipline

l4_steps.name: Generate monthly actuals vs budget variance report
l4_steps.input: Monthly close actuals from SAP FI, locked budget baseline from SAP BPC
l4_steps.output: Monthly management accounts pack with variance commentary by cost centre
l4_steps.kpi: Management accounts published within 5 business days of month-end close
l4_steps.pain_point: Month-end close extended by late Accounts Payable accruals from MRO vendors (average 3–4 day delay post month-end); delays variance reporting and triggers reforecast discussions without complete data

l4_steps.name: Assess variance against materiality threshold
l4_steps.input: Monthly variance report, materiality threshold (±5% revenue or ±$2M EBITDAR)
l4_steps.output: Variance assessment decision: maintain budget or trigger rolling reforecast
l4_steps.kpi: Reforecast trigger decision made within 2 business days of management accounts publication
l4_steps.pain_point: Absence of a formal materiality policy means reforecast decisions are made ad-hoc; in fuel price spike scenarios (e.g., geopolitical events), Finance may be 6–8 weeks behind market reality

l4_steps.name: Execute rolling reforecast and update SAP BPC
l4_steps.input: Latest actuals, revised macro assumptions, updated capacity plan from Amadeus SkyCAST
l4_steps.output: Updated 12-month rolling forecast published in SAP BPC; variance to original budget flagged
l4_steps.kpi: Rolling reforecast cycle completed within 10 business days of trigger; forecast accuracy ≤3% vs subsequent actuals
l4_steps.pain_point: Revenue reforecast requires Amadeus NRM booking-curve data that is not available in SAP BPC; FP&A manually requests extracts from Revenue Management team, adding 2–3 day dependency

l4_steps.name: Maintain cost centre hierarchy in SAP CO
l4_steps.input: Approved organisational structure and departmental headcount plan
l4_steps.output: Cost centre master data with hierarchy nodes aligned to P&L structure
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of cost centres mapped to a valid profit centre before period open
l4_steps.pain_point: Organisational restructures (e.g. new MRO subsidiary, alliance JV) require manual CO hierarchy redesign; no automated sync from SAP SuccessFactors org chart

l4_steps.name: Load approved budget baseline into SAP CO
l4_steps.input: Board-approved annual budget locked in SAP BPC
l4_steps.output: Cost centre plan versions activated in SAP CO for current fiscal year
l4_steps.kpi: Budget upload completed ≤3 business days after board approval
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual mapping required between SAP BPC planning dimensions and SAP CO cost element groups; version mismatch causes reforecast figures to overwrite locked baseline

l4_steps.name: Configure activity types and internal activity rates
l4_steps.input: Planned cost centre volumes (flight hours, maintenance man-hours, FTE counts)
l4_steps.output: Validated activity type rates for internal cost transfers (e.g. $/flight-hour, $/MHR)
l4_steps.kpi: Activity rate variance vs prior year ≤5%; all rates signed off by Finance Director
l4_steps.pain_point: Flight-hour activity rates must be reconciled against Jeppesen crew pairing outputs; late crew schedule changes invalidate planned rate calculations after period open

l4_steps.name: Capture direct cost postings via SAP FI/MM
l4_steps.input: Supplier invoices, purchase orders, and expense reports from SAP Concur
l4_steps.output: Verified FI document postings assigned to correct cost centres and cost elements
l4_steps.kpi: Invoice processing cycle time ≤2 days; <0.5% posting error rate per period
l4_steps.pain_point: Aircraft fuel invoices from multi-supplier contracts require manual cost element split between line maintenance and flight operations cost centres; no automated split rule in standard SAP MM

l4_steps.name: Run periodic assessment cycles for indirect costs
l4_steps.input: Closed FI period with all direct postings; allocation cycle configuration
l4_steps.output: Indirect costs distributed from sender cost centres (IT, HR, Finance) to receiver cost centres
l4_steps.kpi: Assessment cycle runtime ≤4 hours; 100% of sender cost centre balances zeroed after cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: IT infrastructure costs shared across 20+ airline business units require quarterly review of allocation keys; stale keys from pre-cloud migration era overallocate to legacy data centre cost centres

l4_steps.name: Settle maintenance work orders to cost objects
l4_steps.input: Completed maintenance work orders with labour, parts, and subcontract costs
l4_steps.output: Settled maintenance costs transferred from AMOS work orders to SAP CO cost centres or internal orders
l4_steps.kpi: Work order settlement rate ≥98% within 5 business days of task completion
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS-to-SAP CO integration relies on batch interface; late settlement of heavy maintenance C-checks causes significant under-absorption variances in MRO cost centres at period-end

l4_steps.name: Validate allocation cycles balanced to zero
l4_steps.input: Completed assessment and settlement cycle results
l4_steps.output: Period-close sign-off confirmation; unallocated balance report
l4_steps.kpi: Unallocated balance <$1,000 (rounding tolerance) per sender cost centre after cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: Incorrect sender/receiver split factors from ad-hoc project cost centres prevent full balance clearance; requires manual journal workaround which bypasses standard CO cycle logic

l4_steps.name: Extract flight-level unit costs from SAP CO-PA
l4_steps.input: Settled cost centre and order actuals; flight schedule from Amadeus SkyWORKS
l4_steps.output: Per-flight cost breakdown by cost element (fuel, crew, maintenance, fees, overhead)
l4_steps.kpi: CASM (Cost per Available Seat Mile) calculated for 100% of operated flights within 48 hours of period close
l4_steps.pain_point: CO-PA account-based model requires manual derivation rules for mapping operational cost drivers (tail number, route) to profitability segments; missing derivation rules create blank segment records that distort CASM calculations

l4_steps.name: Join revenue and capacity data via AWS Redshift
l4_steps.input: Passenger revenue from Amadeus Altéa PSS; ancillary revenue from booking engine; ASM/RPM from Amadeus SkyWORKS
l4_steps.output: Integrated flight-level dataset combining cost, revenue, and capacity metrics
l4_steps.kpi: Data pipeline latency ≤6 hours after period close; revenue reconciliation variance vs FI ledger <0.1%
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus Altéa proration logic for interline and codeshare itineraries produces estimated revenue splits; actuals are only available after IATA BSP settlement (30-day lag), creating provisional revenue figures in monthly management accounts

l4_steps.name: Calculate CASM, RASM, and contribution margin
l4_steps.input: Integrated flight-level dataset from AWS Redshift
l4_steps.output: Route-level and fleet-type profitability scorecard (CASM, RASM, load factor, contribution margin $/seat)
l4_steps.kpi: Network contribution margin ≥18% of total revenue; CASM ex-fuel ≤8.5¢
l4_steps.pain_point: Allocation of fleet ownership costs (depreciation, lessor rentals) to routes requires arbitrary ASM-based split; aircraft utilisation swings caused by irregular operations distort per-route cost benchmarks

l4_steps.name: Flag underperforming routes for network review
l4_steps.input: Route profitability scorecard; minimum profitability threshold (CFO-approved)
l4_steps.output: Route watch-list submitted to Network Planning for schedule review in Amadeus SkySYM
l4_steps.kpi: Routes with contribution margin <5% for 3 consecutive months escalated within 5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Seasonal routes and new route ramp-up periods require judgement-based exclusion from watch-list; absence of a formal ramp-up tolerance policy leads to premature escalation of viable long-term routes

l4_steps.name: Run budget vs actuals comparison in SAP BPC
l4_steps.input: Locked budget baseline; period actuals loaded from SAP S/4HANA FI/CO
l4_steps.output: Variance report by cost centre, cost element, and P&L line
l4_steps.kpi: Variance report published ≤4 business days after period close
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP BPC data model refresh from S/4HANA requires nightly batch job; ad-hoc reforecasts during the period create multiple BPC plan versions that are difficult to reconcile with the locked baseline

l4_steps.name: Classify and quantify material variances by type
l4_steps.input: Variance report; cost centre manager commentary submitted via email or SharePoint
l4_steps.output: Variance classification register (price variance, volume variance, mix variance, one-off items)
l4_steps.kpi: ≥90% of variances >$50K classified and explained within 5 business days of period close
l4_steps.pain_point: Fuel price variances require decomposition into volume, price, and hedge settlement components; hedge P&L is recorded in a separate SAP FI treasury module with no direct CO linkage, requiring manual reconciliation

l4_steps.name: Determine if variance requires CFO escalation
l4_steps.input: Classified variance register; materiality thresholds approved by CFO
l4_steps.output: Escalation decision: CFO notified within 24 hours if threshold breached
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of variances exceeding $500K or 10% of cost centre budget escalated within 24 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Materiality thresholds are static (set at year-start) and do not adjust for mid-year reforecast changes; cost centres that received budget cuts become hypersensitive to small nominal variances

l4_steps.name: Conduct root-cause analysis with cost centre managers
l4_steps.input: Escalated variance items; cost centre transaction drill-down from SAP CO
l4_steps.output: Root-cause analysis memo; corrective action plan with owner and due date
l4_steps.kpi: Root-cause memo issued within 3 business days of escalation trigger
l4_steps.pain_point: Operational cost centre managers (e.g. Maintenance Base, Ground Ops) have limited SAP CO access and rely on Finance to extract drill-down data; information asymmetry delays variance explanation by 2–3 days

l4_steps.name: Compile monthly management accounts pack
l4_steps.input: Variance analysis, route profitability scorecard, corrective action plans
l4_steps.output: Monthly management accounts pack (P&L, cost bridge, KPI dashboard, CFO narrative)
l4_steps.kpi: Management pack distributed to CFO and ExCo ≤6 business days after period close
l4_steps.pain_point: Management pack relies on manual Excel consolidation of Tableau outputs, SAP BPC variance reports, and treasury hedge commentary; multi-source assembly creates version control risk and delays when any single source is late

l4_steps.name: Issue cost reduction directives to business units
l4_steps.input: Approved cost control decisions from CFO review of management pack
l4_steps.output: Revised cost centre spending authorities; updated BPC reforecast with reduction targets
l4_steps.kpi: Cost reduction directives issued within 2 business days of ExCo approval
l4_steps.pain_point: Spending authority changes require SAP CO cost centre budget updates AND updates to SAP Ariba procurement approval hierarchies; the two systems are not integrated, so purchasing limits frequently lag behind finance decisions

l4_steps.name: Trigger rolling reforecast cycle in SAP BPC
l4_steps.input: Cost reduction directives; updated fuel price and capacity assumptions
l4_steps.output: Revised full-year forecast published in SAP BPC; new CASM and EBITDAR outlook circulated
l4_steps.kpi: Rolling reforecast completed and published ≤10 business days after period close
l4_steps.pain_point: Mid-year capacity changes (aircraft AOG events, network schedule revisions from Amadeus SkyWORKS) invalidate the ASM base used for CASM forecasting; reforecasts become stale within days if not linked to live schedule data

l4_steps.name: Ingest daily BSP/ARC ticket sales data feed
l4_steps.input: IATA BSP Interactive Sales Report (ISR) file; ARC TicketExpress settlement file
l4_steps.output: Raw ticket coupon dataset loaded to revenue accounting staging area
l4_steps.kpi: File ingestion success rate ≥99.5%; processing time <2 hours after BSP file drop
l4_steps.pain_point: BSP file format differences across IATA billing regions (e.g. BSP-Americas vs BSP-Europe) cause parsing errors for non-standard fare constructions; legacy ASCII flat-file format has no structured error reporting

l4_steps.name: Match ticket coupons against PSS booking records
l4_steps.input: Raw coupon dataset from step 1.1; Altéa booking and coupon status records
l4_steps.output: Matched/unmatched coupon reconciliation report
l4_steps.kpi: Automated coupon match rate ≥97%; unmatched coupons backlog <3% of daily volume
l4_steps.pain_point: PNR purge cycle (typically 90 days post-departure) removes booking records before interline billing arrives, causing match failures for delayed interline invoices; no automated re-match queue

l4_steps.name: Apply ATPCO fare basis code validation
l4_steps.input: Matched coupons with fare basis codes from step 1.2
l4_steps.output: Validated fare constructions; flagged error report for non-compliant coupons
l4_steps.kpi: Fare validation error rate <1% of total coupons processed; validation completed within 4 hours of ingestion
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO fare filing publication lag (up to 48 hours after filing) means recently-sold fares may not yet appear in validation tables, generating false-positive errors on new fare products launched during peak sale windows

l4_steps.name: Resolve coupon validation exceptions
l4_steps.input: Flagged exceptions from steps 1.2 and 1.3; fare construction rules; Altéa reissue records
l4_steps.output: Resolved exception log; adjusted coupon records cleared for proration
l4_steps.kpi: Exception resolution within 5 business days; exception backlog <500 coupons at any time
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual exception handling volume spikes after IROP events when re-issued tickets carry non-standard fare constructions and waiver codes not recognised by the revenue accounting system; resolution requires coordination with airport and contact centre teams

l4_steps.name: Calculate interline revenue proration
l4_steps.input: Validated interline coupons; IATA Resolution 850e proration rules; bilateral proration agreements
l4_steps.output: Prorated revenue splits per operating carrier segment; interline billing receivables
l4_steps.kpi: Proration processing completed within T+3 calendar days; interline dispute rate <2% of prorated billings
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA Resolution 850e proration formula conflicts with bilaterally-negotiated prorate agreements for specific carrier pairs; manual overrides are required and not fully auditable within REVERA, creating reconciliation risk

l4_steps.name: Apply ASC 606 revenue recognition rules
l4_steps.input: Prorated revenue data from step 2.1; flight departure confirmation records from Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Revenue recognition schedule; deferred revenue journal entries for untravelled portions
l4_steps.kpi: Deferred revenue posting accuracy ≥99.9% of ticket value; period-end deferred revenue balance reconciled within T+5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Ancillary revenue bundling (e.g. seat upgrade + checked bag + base fare sold as one fare family) requires performance obligation disaggregation under ASC 606 Topic 606; the revenue accounting subledger does not support multi-element arrangement splitting natively, requiring manual journal overrides

l4_steps.name: Process EMD ancillary and ancillary revenue
l4_steps.input: Electronic Miscellaneous Document (EMD-A and EMD-S) records; ancillary sales data from direct channel
l4_steps.output: Ancillary revenue postings by product category; EMD redemption log
l4_steps.kpi: EMD-to-revenue match rate ≥98%; ancillary revenue posted within T+2 days of service delivery date
l4_steps.pain_point: EMD-A (associated, tied to flight coupon) vs EMD-S (standalone, sold independently) misclassification causes ancillary revenue to be booked to incorrect income lines; the distinction is not enforced at point of sale by all booking channels

l4_steps.name: Reconcile BSP billing memo vs internal records
l4_steps.input: IATA BSP billing memo for the settlement period; internal validated coupon dataset from Phase 1
l4_steps.output: Reconciliation variance report; list of net billing differences by agency and fare code
l4_steps.kpi: Net billing variance <0.1% of total settlement amount; reconciliation completed within T+1 business day of BSP memo receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: Currency conversion timing differences between the BSP billing date and the internal booking date create systematic variances in markets with volatile FX rates (e.g. ARS, TRY, EGP); IATA BSP Link applies the exchange rate at billing date, not booking date

l4_steps.name: Raise Agency Debit Memos for billing discrepancies
l4_steps.input: Reconciliation variances from step 3.1 exceeding tolerance; agency IATA codes and billing references
l4_steps.output: Agency Debit Memo (ADM) or Agency Credit Memo (ACM) records filed in IATA BSP Link
l4_steps.kpi: ADM filed within IATA 15-day filing deadline; ADM acceptance rate by agencies ≥85% within 30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA BSP Link ADM filing requires exact citation of the IATA resolution code authorising the ADM; incorrect or missing resolution citations cause automatic rejection, restarting the 15-day clock and risking write-off if the deadline cannot be met on re-submission

l4_steps.name: Approve and submit BSP settlement payment
l4_steps.input: Reconciled net BSP settlement amount; IATA bank account details; dual-approval workflow
l4_steps.output: Approved payment batch instruction; bank transfer confirmation to IATA clearing account
l4_steps.kpi: Payment submitted on BSP settlement value date with zero late-payment penalties; settlement accuracy 100% of approved net amount
l4_steps.pain_point: Dual-approval workflow between Revenue Accounting and Treasury creates a bottleneck when approvers are unavailable on the BSP settlement date; SAP S/4HANA workflow does not support time-sensitive escalation routing to backup approvers

l4_steps.name: Confirm BSP settlement receipt and archive
l4_steps.input: Bank MT940 payment confirmation; IATA settlement acknowledgement
l4_steps.output: Closed billing period record; settlement archive with audit trail
l4_steps.kpi: Settlement confirmation archived within 24 hours of IATA acknowledgement; audit trail completeness 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA BSP Link does not provide real-time payment confirmation; reconciliation relies on bank MT940 SWIFT message feeds which may lag by 1 business day, leaving the settlement status in IATA BSP Link as 'pending' and triggering false escalation alerts

l4_steps.name: Post revenue journal entries to SAP General Ledger
l4_steps.input: Recognised revenue data; proration outputs; ancillary postings; deferred revenue adjustments
l4_steps.output: Posted journal entries; GL revenue accounts updated with passenger and ancillary revenue
l4_steps.kpi: Automated posting rate ≥95% of journal lines; manual journals <5%; posting completed within T+2 business days of period end
l4_steps.pain_point: Revenue accounting system to SAP interface uses scheduled batch file transfer; if a batch fails mid-run, partial postings create out-of-balance GL entries requiring manual reversal journals and repost, delaying period close

l4_steps.name: Perform revenue GL account reconciliation
l4_steps.input: Posted SAP GL balances; subledger data from Mercator REVERA Revenue Accounting
l4_steps.output: Signed-off account reconciliation with variance commentary; open items list
l4_steps.kpi: All revenue GL accounts reconciled within T+5 business days of month end; unexplained open items <$50,000 aggregate
l4_steps.pain_point: High volume of open items from ongoing interline billing disputes strains the reconciliation process; open item ageing is not automatically surfaced in BlackLine, requiring manual export and pivot analysis, often pushing sign-off past the T+5 target

l4_steps.name: Generate revenue reports and close accounting period
l4_steps.input: Reconciled SAP GL balances; management reporting templates; prior-period comparatives
l4_steps.output: Revenue flash report delivered to CFO; accounting period locked in SAP S/4HANA
l4_steps.kpi: Revenue flash report delivered to CFO within T+3 business days of period end; period close completed by T+7 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Parallel month-end close activities (cost accounting, payroll, procurement AP) contend for SAP period-close resources; lock conflicts on shared profit centre and cost centre objects delay period close when multiple finance teams post simultaneously

l4_steps.name: Extract operational demand forecast from schedule system
l4_steps.input: Published 12-month flight schedule, SSIM export
l4_steps.output: Flight volume and frequency forecast by department
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast accuracy ≥90% vs actuals at 6-month horizon
l4_steps.pain_point: Schedule changes in SkyWORKS are not auto-pushed to HR systems; manual re-extract required after each revision cycle, causing stale inputs to the workforce model

l4_steps.name: Model staffing ratios by role and operational area
l4_steps.input: Flight frequency forecast, historical headcount-to-output ratios
l4_steps.output: Staffing ratio model by department (ops, cabin crew, ground handling, corporate)
l4_steps.kpi: Ratio deviation ≤5% vs prior year actuals
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 117 duty-time limits constrain crew FTE ratios and are not natively modelled in SuccessFactors; manual adjustments required for each schedule scenario

l4_steps.name: Overlay attrition and turnover projections
l4_steps.input: 3-year attrition history, exit survey data, retirement eligibility register
l4_steps.output: Attrition-adjusted headcount gap model by role and grade
l4_steps.kpi: Attrition forecast accuracy ±2pp vs 12-month rolling actuals
l4_steps.pain_point: Pilot attrition is volatile due to competitor hiring campaigns and Boeing MAX delivery schedule; SuccessFactors demographic model does not ingest external labour market signals

l4_steps.name: Assess certification and type rating requirements
l4_steps.input: Current workforce certification register, planned route and fleet expansions
l4_steps.output: Certification gap analysis covering type ratings, check airmen, and licensed dispatchers
l4_steps.kpi: Zero FAA/EASA non-compliance findings at annual audit
l4_steps.pain_point: 737 MAX type rating lead times of 9–12 months create long procurement cycles; late identification of gaps forces expensive contractor or wet-lease cover

l4_steps.name: Consolidate departmental headcount requests
l4_steps.input: Departmental business plans, headcount request forms
l4_steps.output: Consolidated headcount demand register by department and grade
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of headcount requests submitted via SuccessFactors (zero shadow-spreadsheet submissions)
l4_steps.pain_point: Ground operations departments routinely bypass SuccessFactors and submit requests by email, causing reconciliation delays of 3–5 business days

l4_steps.name: Validate requests against approved operational plan
l4_steps.input: Consolidated headcount demand register, approved flight schedule
l4_steps.output: Validated headcount demand list with business justification scores
l4_steps.kpi: Validation cycle completed ≤5 business days from submission close
l4_steps.pain_point: Schedule volatility during irregular operations invalidates demand validation within weeks of submission; no automated re-trigger exists in SuccessFactors when SkyWORKS schedule changes

l4_steps.name: Run base, upside, and downside scenario models
l4_steps.input: Validated demand list, three schedule scenarios from Amadeus SkySYM
l4_steps.output: Three-scenario headcount model with FTE count and loaded cost estimate per scenario
l4_steps.kpi: Scenario model delivered ≤10 business days from schedule freeze date
l4_steps.pain_point: Custom ETL between AWS Redshift and SuccessFactors introduces 24-hour data latency, reducing scenario responsiveness during rapid schedule changes

l4_steps.name: Submit headcount plan for financial cost review
l4_steps.input: Three-scenario headcount model with FTE cost estimate
l4_steps.output: Headcount cost impact loaded into cost-centre budget in SAP CO
l4_steps.kpi: Headcount cost submission completed ≤2 weeks before annual budget lock date
l4_steps.pain_point: Mid-year headcount additions require supplemental budget approval; SAP CO cost-centre realignment for new positions is manual and error-prone when org structures change

l4_steps.name: Obtain finance approval for headcount envelope
l4_steps.input: Headcount cost model, approved OPEX budget by cost centre
l4_steps.output: Approved or rejected headcount envelope per department with approved FTE ceiling
l4_steps.kpi: Approval decision returned ≤10 business days of submission
l4_steps.pain_point: Executive approval cycles extend by 4–6 weeks during periods of financial pressure such as fuel price spikes, delaying time-to-hire for safety-critical roles

l4_steps.name: Revise and lock headcount plan per finance decision
l4_steps.input: Finance approval decision with department-level adjustments
l4_steps.output: Revised and version-locked headcount plan published to all HR Business Partners
l4_steps.kpi: Revised plan published within 3 business days of finance approval
l4_steps.pain_point: Version control in SuccessFactors Workforce Planning is limited; multiple revision cycles create confusion between HR and Finance on which version constitutes the locked baseline

l4_steps.name: Create approved position records in HRIS
l4_steps.input: Locked headcount plan with approved FTE ceiling by department
l4_steps.output: Approved position records in Employee Central with cost centre, grade, org unit, and FTE flag
l4_steps.kpi: Position creation within 2 business days of plan lock; 100% data quality pass on mandatory fields
l4_steps.pain_point: Employee Central position management requires manual org chart updates that are time-consuming for large cohort hires such as seasonal cabin crew intakes of 200+ headcount

l4_steps.name: Trigger recruitment workflow per approved position
l4_steps.input: Approved position records from Employee Central
l4_steps.output: Job requisitions opened in SuccessFactors Recruiting; JDs published to careers portal
l4_steps.kpi: Time-to-open requisition ≤1 business day; 100% of requisitions linked to an approved position record
l4_steps.pain_point: Pilot and licensed dispatcher requisitions require FAA/EASA qualification screening criteria not pre-built in SuccessFactors Recruiting templates, causing manual customisation per role

l4_steps.name: Confirm headcount actuals against plan at point of hire
l4_steps.input: Offer accepted and onboarding record created in Employee Central
l4_steps.output: Headcount actuals updated; remaining open-position count reconciled to approved ceiling
l4_steps.kpi: Headcount actuals vs plan variance ≤3% at each quarter-end
l4_steps.pain_point: Backfill hires for unexpected attrition routinely consume approved new-hire slots, distorting the plan vs actual comparison and masking net headcount growth

l4_steps.name: Publish monthly headcount actuals vs plan dashboard
l4_steps.input: Live headcount data from Employee Central, open requisition aging report
l4_steps.output: Monthly headcount dashboard showing actuals vs plan, attrition rate, and open-requisition aging
l4_steps.kpi: Dashboard published by Day 5 of each month; plan variance flagged automatically if >5%
l4_steps.pain_point: SuccessFactors People Analytics runs on prior-day data; same-day joiners and leavers in high-volume ops departments are missed, understating attrition in real-time views

l4_steps.name: Conduct mid-year headcount reforecast
l4_steps.input: YTD actuals, updated H2 flight schedule from SkyWORKS, revised attrition forecast
l4_steps.output: Mid-year headcount reforecast with gap-to-plan analysis and recommended actions
l4_steps.kpi: Reforecast submitted ≤15 business days after H1 close; all variances >3% documented with root cause
l4_steps.pain_point: Mid-year schedule changes by Network Planning in SkyWORKS are not automatically signalled to HR, so workforce reforecasts are often triggered 4–6 weeks late

l4_steps.name: Escalate critical headcount gaps to executive committee
l4_steps.input: Reforecast gap analysis exceeding ±5% of plan, operational risk register
l4_steps.output: ExCo escalation report with options: revised hiring authority, freeze, or contractor cover; decision recorded
l4_steps.kpi: Escalation report presented within 5 business days of trigger; resolution decision returned ≤10 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Airline operational staffing shortfalls for pilots and licensed dispatchers carry regulatory consequences under FAR Part 121; delayed escalation has resulted in AOG situations and DOT scrutiny

l4_steps.name: Review headcount plan and identify vacancy
l4_steps.input: Annual headcount plan, attrition report, operational demand signal
l4_steps.output: Approved headcount request with cost centre and FTE count
l4_steps.kpi: Requisition-to-plan alignment rate ≥95%; headcount request raised within 5 business days of vacancy identification
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP SuccessFactors Workforce Planning module is not integrated with crew scheduling or flight operations staffing models — frontline vacancy data (pilots, cabin crew) must be manually cross-referenced, causing 5–10 day lag in requisition initiation

l4_steps.name: Create and submit job requisition
l4_steps.input: Approved headcount request, job description template library
l4_steps.output: Job requisition record with grade, salary band, required certifications, and target start date
l4_steps.kpi: Requisition submitted within 3 business days of headcount approval
l4_steps.pain_point: Job description templates in SAP SuccessFactors are frequently outdated for technical aviation roles (avionics technician, line maintenance engineer) — manual SME review adds 2–4 days to requisition creation

l4_steps.name: Approve requisition and confirm budget
l4_steps.system: SAP SuccessFactors Recruiting / SAP S/4HANA Finance (FI/CO)
l4_steps.input: Submitted job requisition, departmental FTE budget report from SAP S/4HANA
l4_steps.output: Approved requisition with confirmed cost centre and salary band ceiling
l4_steps.kpi: Approval cycle time ≤3 business days; 100% of approved requisitions within sanctioned FTE budget
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP S/4HANA Finance month-end close (3-day window) freezes cost centre commitments — operational hiring requisitions submitted during close are delayed, disrupting crew and maintenance staffing timelines

l4_steps.name: Post vacancy to internal and external channels
l4_steps.system: SAP SuccessFactors Career Site / LinkedIn Job Slots / Indeed
l4_steps.input: Approved requisition; internal mobility policy (minimum 5-day internal posting window)
l4_steps.output: Live job posting across internal portal and external job boards; application tracking link active
l4_steps.kpi: Internal application rate ≥20% for non-entry-level roles; posting live within 1 business day of requisition approval
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP SuccessFactors Career Site apply-flow is not mobile-optimised — pilot and cabin crew candidates applying via mobile devices report high abandonment rates, reducing application conversion vs. competitor portals

l4_steps.name: Source passive candidates via direct outreach
l4_steps.system: LinkedIn Recruiter / Avjobs Aviation Job Board
l4_steps.input: Role requirements, skills profile, talent pool database in SAP SuccessFactors
l4_steps.output: Shortlisted passive candidate profiles with initial interest confirmation
l4_steps.kpi: Passive candidate pipeline of ≥3 qualified prospects per requisition within 10 business days of posting
l4_steps.pain_point: Global commercial pilot shortage (ICAO forecasts 50,000+ deficit by 2030) makes passive sourcing for ATP-rated First Officers intensely competitive — response rates on LinkedIn Recruiter InMail for pilot roles average <15%, well below the 35% cross-industry benchmark

l4_steps.name: Assess pipeline adequacy and decide sourcing strategy
l4_steps.input: Number of qualified applicants vs. minimum threshold (5 per requisition)
l4_steps.output: Go/no-go decision: proceed to screening or extend sourcing window / engage recruitment agency
l4_steps.kpi: Minimum 5 qualified applicants before screening commences; agency engagement escalation rate ≤15% of requisitions
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP SuccessFactors does not enforce a preferred supplier list for recruitment agencies — when pipeline fails, hiring managers independently engage agencies at non-negotiated rates, inflating cost-per-hire for technical roles by 30–50%

l4_steps.name: Automated ATS screening and shortlisting
l4_steps.input: All submitted applications against minimum qualification criteria
l4_steps.output: Ranked shortlist of candidates meeting mandatory requirements
l4_steps.kpi: ATS screen-to-shortlist ratio ≤5:1; screening completed within 2 business days of application close
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP SuccessFactors AI screening does not recognise FAA-standard licence abbreviations (ATP, A&P, IA) and ICAO type rating codes — qualified pilot and maintenance candidates are incorrectly filtered out, requiring manual review of up to 30% of rejections

l4_steps.name: Conduct telephone or video pre-screen interview
l4_steps.input: ATS-generated shortlist; structured pre-screen question guide
l4_steps.output: Completed pre-screen scorecard per candidate; advance or reject recommendation
l4_steps.kpi: Pre-screen completed within 5 business days of shortlisting; candidate pass rate 50–70%
l4_steps.pain_point: HireVue asynchronous video interviews have significantly lower engagement rates with experienced pilot and senior maintenance candidates who expect direct recruiter interaction — completion rates for these cohorts are 20–25% below junior role benchmarks

l4_steps.name: Administer role-specific skills and aptitude assessments
l4_steps.system: Criteria Corp (cognitive/aptitude) / SHL (technical assessment) / CAE SimuFlite (pilot simulator check)
l4_steps.input: Pre-screen pass list; role-specific assessment battery defined by HR and technical SMEs
l4_steps.output: Assessment scores; simulator evaluation report for pilot roles; advance/reject per candidate
l4_steps.kpi: Assessment completion rate ≥85%; cognitive benchmark score ≥65th percentile for technical roles; pilot sim check pass rate reported within 5 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Simulator assessment slots at CAE and FlightSafety International facilities cost $3,000–$5,000 per candidate and must be booked 4–6 weeks in advance — scheduling constraints extend pilot time-to-hire by 3–6 weeks vs. non-technical roles

l4_steps.name: Review assessments and finalise interview shortlist
l4_steps.input: Assessment scores, pre-screen scorecards, technical SME evaluation notes
l4_steps.output: Approved interview shortlist of 3–5 candidates per role with documented rationale
l4_steps.kpi: Interview shortlist delivered to hiring manager within 3 business days of assessment completion
l4_steps.pain_point: Inconsistent scoring rubrics across business units in SAP SuccessFactors create EEOC/OFCCP audit risk — selection decisions for cabin crew base hiring lack standardised documentation, exposing the airline to disparate impact claims

l4_steps.name: Schedule panel interviews and notify participants
l4_steps.system: SAP SuccessFactors Recruiting / Microsoft Outlook (calendar integration)
l4_steps.input: Approved interview shortlist; panel interviewer availability
l4_steps.output: Confirmed interview schedule; candidate and interviewer calendar invitations with structured guide
l4_steps.kpi: Interviews scheduled within 5 business days of shortlist approval; candidate no-show rate ≤5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Outlook-to-SuccessFactors calendar sync fails for interviewers on crew scheduling systems — operational disruptions (IROPS, maintenance delays) cause same-day cancellations that are not automatically reflected in SuccessFactors, requiring manual rescheduling

l4_steps.name: Conduct structured panel interviews
l4_steps.role: Hiring Manager / HR Business Partner / Technical SME
l4_steps.system: SAP SuccessFactors Recruiting (interview guide and scorecard)
l4_steps.input: Competency framework, structured interview guide, candidate application and assessment results
l4_steps.output: Completed interview scorecard per panellist per candidate
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of interviews completed with documented scorecards; inter-rater reliability ≥0.70 (Krippendorff's alpha)
l4_steps.pain_point: Operational interviewers (crew planning managers, maintenance supervisors) frequently bypass SAP SuccessFactors scorecard entry citing system complexity — undocumented decisions create material gaps in EEOC record-keeping required for airlines with federal contracts

l4_steps.name: Debrief panel, rank candidates, and select preferred hire
l4_steps.input: Completed scorecards, assessment results, reference check summaries
l4_steps.output: Selected candidate with documented rationale; ranked reserve list for offer decline scenario
l4_steps.kpi: Debrief completed within 2 business days of final interview; offer decline reserve conversion rate ≥60%
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP SuccessFactors does not support structured calibration sessions for multi-site roles — regional hiring panels for cabin crew bases (e.g., BWI vs. MDW) use inconsistent evaluation norms, creating equity and compliance risk

l4_steps.name: Generate and extend conditional offer letter
l4_steps.input: Selection decision, approved salary band, confirmed start date
l4_steps.output: Digitally signed conditional offer letter with pre-employment conditions stated
l4_steps.kpi: Offer extended within 2 business days of selection decision; offer acceptance rate ≥85%
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP SuccessFactors salary band guardrails block above-band offers without a formal exception workflow — for experienced First Officers and A&P mechanics competing with legacy carrier packages (Delta, United), the exception approval cycle (5–7 days) causes candidate drop-off to competitors

l4_steps.name: Initiate background check and FAA PRIA records request
l4_steps.input: Signed offer letter; candidate consent form; FAA PRIA release authorisation (for pilot roles)
l4_steps.output: Background check clearance report; PRIA records request submitted and tracked
l4_steps.kpi: Background check completed within 7 business days; FAA PRIA response within 30 days (statutory maximum); 100% compliance with Air Carrier Access Act record-keeping
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA PRIA requests for internationally certified pilots (JAA/EASA licence holders converting to FAA ATP) require manual coordination with foreign civil aviation authorities — average response time is 45–60 days vs. the 30-day statutory target, blocking hire completion

l4_steps.name: Conduct DOT-mandated drug and alcohol screening
l4_steps.input: Offer acceptance confirmation; DOT 49 CFR Part 40 pre-employment testing requirement for safety-sensitive roles
l4_steps.output: MRO-verified drug test result (pass/fail); test documentation retained per DOT 5-year record requirement
l4_steps.kpi: Drug screen specimen collected within 3 business days of offer acceptance; 100% compliance rate for safety-sensitive roles (pilots, cabin crew, dispatchers, mechanics)
l4_steps.pain_point: DOT 49 CFR Part 40 requires direct-observation collection for certain re-hire categories — the LabCorp DOT collector network has limited presence in smaller airline base cities (ISP, BDL, MHT), requiring candidates to travel, causing 2–5 day delays and candidate attrition

l4_steps.name: Verify licences, certificates, and medical fitness
l4_steps.role: Talent Acquisition Specialist / Crew Compliance Officer
l4_steps.system: FAA IACRA (Integrated Airman Certification and Rating Application) / SAP SuccessFactors Document Management
l4_steps.input: Pilot: ATP certificate, type ratings, Class 1 FAA medical; Cabin crew: FAA initial certification; Tech ops: FAA A&P and IA licence
l4_steps.output: Verified credential record stored in SAP SuccessFactors employee file; compliance sign-off from Crew Compliance
l4_steps.kpi: 100% credential verification completed before Day 1; zero compliance exceptions at FAA CHDO audit; credential expiry alerts configured in SuccessFactors
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA IACRA public lookup does not have an API integration with SAP SuccessFactors — credential data must be manually transcribed, creating data entry error risk; errors discovered at FAA Certificate Holding District Office (CHDO) audit result in regulatory corrective action

l4_steps.name: Create employee record and provision system access
l4_steps.role: HR Operations Specialist / IT Service Desk
l4_steps.system: SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central / ServiceNow (IT provisioning workflow)
l4_steps.input: Cleared pre-employment checks; confirmed start date and role
l4_steps.output: Active employee record in SAP SuccessFactors; network credentials and role-based system access granted via ServiceNow
l4_steps.kpi: System access provisioned and verified by 08:00 on Day 1; first-day access failure rate ≤1%
l4_steps.pain_point: ServiceNow-to-SuccessFactors integration triggers provisioning only on a nightly batch — new hire records created less than 48 hours before the start date miss the batch window and arrive on Day 1 without access, requiring manual IT escalation that averages 4–6 hours to resolve

l4_steps.name: Enrol new hire in orientation and mandatory training
l4_steps.role: HR Operations Specialist / Learning & Development Coordinator
l4_steps.input: Active employee record; role-specific training curriculum; FAA-required initial training schedule for safety-sensitive roles
l4_steps.output: Training assignments confirmed in LMS; Initial Operating Experience (IOE) scheduled for pilots; emergency procedures training scheduled for cabin crew; A&P recurrency training enrolled for maintenance technicians
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of mandatory Day-1 training assignments loaded before start date; regulatory training completion ≥95% within first 30 days; zero FAA compliance exceptions at training audit
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP SuccessFactors LMS does not auto-assign FAA-required recurrent training curricula (FAR Part 121 initial, emergency equipment, CRM) when a new employee record is created for safety-sensitive roles — manual curriculum assignment is required and is frequently missed during high-volume new hire cohorts, creating FAA Part 121 compliance gaps

l4_steps.name: Aggregate regulatory & mandatory training requirements
l4_steps.system: IATA Training Portal / SAP SuccessFactors Learning
l4_steps.input: IATA DGR annual revision, FAA/EASA regulatory updates, IOSA audit findings, SMS programme requirements
l4_steps.output: Mandatory Training Requirements Matrix with regulatory source, frequency, and in-scope role mapping
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of regulatory training requirements identified and documented before quarter start; zero missed mandates in IOSA audit
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA, EASA, IATA, and TSA issue requirement updates on different annual cycles; manual reconciliation across portals creates risk of missed mandates — no single regulatory feed integrated into SuccessFactors

l4_steps.name: Conduct skills gap analysis from performance data
l4_steps.input: Annual performance review scores, succession planning gaps, strategic workforce plan, job architecture from SAP SuccessFactors HR
l4_steps.output: Skills Gap Report by department and role family; prioritised development needs list
l4_steps.kpi: Skills gap assessment completed for ≥95% of active employees annually; report delivered within 15 business days of performance cycle close
l4_steps.pain_point: SuccessFactors competency model requires manual alignment to airline-specific roles (e.g. load planner, NOC analyst, ramp lead) — generic competency libraries do not map cleanly, creating data quality issues in gap reports

l4_steps.name: Prioritise and approve Annual Training Plan with budget
l4_steps.system: SAP SuccessFactors Learning (Development Plan) / SAP S/4HANA Finance (CO)
l4_steps.input: Skills Gap Report, Mandatory Training Matrix, HR cost centre budget envelope from SAP CO, headcount plan
l4_steps.output: Approved Annual Training Plan with budget allocation by programme, delivery modality, and cost centre
l4_steps.kpi: Training plan approved and published ≥30 days before programme year start; budget variance vs plan ≤10% at year end
l4_steps.pain_point: Airlines routinely cut L&D budgets during cost reduction cycles, forcing de-prioritisation of non-mandatory development programmes — no systematic ROI-based prioritisation framework to defend discretionary spend

l4_steps.name: Define learning objectives and delivery modality
l4_steps.input: Approved Annual Training Plan, SME interviews, regulatory content guidelines, prior completion and effectiveness data
l4_steps.output: Course Design Document specifying learning objectives, modality (eLearning/ILT/blended/simulator), duration, and assessment approach
l4_steps.kpi: Course Design Document reviewed and approved by SME within 10 business days of initiation; 100% of safety-critical courses include knowledge assessment
l4_steps.pain_point: Simulator availability for ground handling, security procedures, and emergency response is constrained at hub airports — scheduling simulator-based courses conflicts with operational training blocks managed outside the LMS

l4_steps.name: Schedule sessions and assign instructors or facilitators
l4_steps.input: Course Design Document, certified instructor roster, facility and simulator availability calendar
l4_steps.output: Published training schedule in SuccessFactors with calendar invites; instructor assignments confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: Training schedule published ≥21 days before first session; instructor utilisation ≥75%; session cancellation rate <8%
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew and operations staff scheduling conflicts with irregular shift patterns require manual override in SuccessFactors — the system cannot natively read crew rosters from Jeppesen Crew Management, forcing coordinators to reconcile two systems manually

l4_steps.name: Assign mandatory courses to employee learning plans
l4_steps.input: Mandatory Training Requirements Matrix, employee role and position data from SAP SuccessFactors HR, training plan approval
l4_steps.output: Learning plans assigned to all in-scope employees; automated enrollment notifications triggered; due dates set per regulatory frequency
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of mandatory course assignments completed within 3 business days of plan approval; zero employees in regulated roles without an active learning plan
l4_steps.pain_point: Role-based assignment rules break when employees hold dual positions (e.g. part-time ground agent and check-in agent) — SuccessFactors assigns duplicate curricula generating confusion and inflated non-completion statistics

l4_steps.name: Develop or procure course content
l4_steps.input: Approved Course Design Document, SME subject matter input, IATA DGR manuals, airline SOPs
l4_steps.output: Draft eLearning modules in SCORM 1.2 or xAPI format, or facilitator guide and slide deck for ILT delivery
l4_steps.kpi: First draft delivered within 15 business days for standard module; IATA DGR annual update content delivered by 15 November each year for January 1 effective date
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations update annually effective January 1 — content must be revised, reviewed, and republished before year-end; production timelines frequently slip, exposing the airline to regulatory non-compliance in early January

l4_steps.name: Conduct SME, legal, and regulatory review of content
l4_steps.role: Subject Matter Expert / Regulatory Affairs / Quality Assurance
l4_steps.input: Draft eLearning module or facilitator guide submitted for review
l4_steps.output: Reviewed and annotated content with documented SME sign-off; revision log; final approved version
l4_steps.kpi: SME review cycle completed within 10 business days; maximum 2 review iterations before escalation; 0 regulatory accuracy findings post-publish
l4_steps.pain_point: Safety, Security, Legal, and Compliance must all sign off on regulated content (SMS, security awareness, DGR) — parallel review is not natively supported in SharePoint, causing sequential bottlenecks that extend review cycles to 4+ weeks

l4_steps.name: Publish approved content to LMS with version control
l4_steps.input: Approved SCORM/xAPI package or facilitator guide; version number; effective date
l4_steps.output: Published and versioned course in SuccessFactors; prior version archived; release notes documented
l4_steps.kpi: Content published to LMS within 3 business days of final approval; zero broken SCORM packages at publish verified by smoke test; prior version archived within 24 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: SuccessFactors Learning SCORM player has known compatibility issues with Articulate Storyline 360 output — testing is required for every new module; intermittent xAPI completion tracking failures result in learners receiving no credit despite completing the course

l4_steps.name: Deliver training via eLearning, ILT, or virtual session
l4_steps.system: SAP SuccessFactors Learning / Microsoft Teams (virtual ILT)
l4_steps.input: Published course in SuccessFactors, scheduled session, learner enrollment notification
l4_steps.output: Completed training session; assessment scores recorded; attendance roster captured
l4_steps.kpi: ILT and virtual session attendance rate ≥90%; eLearning completion rate ≥85% within assigned window; assessment pass rate ≥80% on first attempt for safety-critical courses
l4_steps.pain_point: Ops, ramp, and ground staff have limited computer access during shifts — eLearning completion rates for front-line employees are significantly lower (≈55%) than corporate staff; SAP SuccessFactors mobile app experience is poor, limiting shift-based self-paced completion

l4_steps.name: Record and validate completions and certification expiry
l4_steps.input: Completion records, automated eLearning scores, attendance rosters from ILT sessions
l4_steps.output: Completion certificates issued; learner transcripts updated; certification expiry dates and renewal reminders set
l4_steps.kpi: Completion records updated in LMS within 24 hours of session end; 100% of regulated certifications tracked with accurate expiry dates; zero missing records identified in IOSA audit
l4_steps.pain_point: Simulator, hands-on safety drills, and recurrent training sessions rely on paper attendance rosters that require manual data entry into SuccessFactors — transcription errors in certification dates create compliance audit risk; no digital signature capture for paper-based sessions

l4_steps.name: Identify, classify, and escalate non-completions
l4_steps.role: L&D Compliance Analyst / HR Business Partner
l4_steps.input: Overdue training report from SuccessFactors automated compliance dashboard; employee leave and absence data
l4_steps.output: Escalation notifications to line managers; approved re-enrollment actions; documented reason for non-completion
l4_steps.kpi: Mandatory training overdue rate <5% at any point in time; escalation triggered within 2 business days of due date breach; re-enrollment completed within 5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Automated escalation rules in SuccessFactors cannot distinguish between non-completion due to approved leave, LOA, or medical absence versus genuine non-compliance — over-escalation creates manager noise and erodes trust in the compliance reporting process

l4_steps.name: Generate regulatory compliance training reports for audit
l4_steps.system: SAP SuccessFactors Learning (Analytics) / SAP Analytics Cloud
l4_steps.input: Completion records, certification data, regulatory training matrix, audit schedule
l4_steps.output: Compliance dashboard; audit-ready training records export by regulator (FAA, TSA, IATA IOSA); period-end compliance rate report
l4_steps.kpi: Compliance reporting available within 5 business days of period close; 0 findings related to training records in FAA, TSA, or IATA IOSA audits; mandatory training completion rate ≥98% across all regulated roles
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA IOSA audits require evidence of training completion by role across all regulated functions — standard SuccessFactors reports are insufficient for multi-regulator submissions; custom report configuration is required for each audit cycle and is not maintained between audits

l4_steps.name: Evaluate training effectiveness and calculate ROI
l4_steps.role: L&D Business Partner / People Analytics Analyst
l4_steps.system: SAP SuccessFactors Learning (Survey) / SAP Analytics Cloud
l4_steps.input: Post-training satisfaction surveys (Kirkpatrick L1), knowledge retention test results (L2), 90-day performance review data, operational KPI baselines
l4_steps.output: Training Effectiveness Report (Kirkpatrick L1–L4); ROI calculation for investment-significant programmes; curriculum improvement recommendations for next planning cycle
l4_steps.kpi: Post-training satisfaction score (L1) ≥4.0 out of 5.0; knowledge retention test pass rate (L2) ≥80%; L3 behaviour change measurement completed for all leadership and safety programmes within 90 days of delivery
l4_steps.pain_point: Kirkpatrick L3/L4 effectiveness measurement requires correlation of training completion data with operational performance metrics (on-time rates, safety incident frequency, customer satisfaction scores) — data resides in SuccessFactors, SITA AMS, safety management databases, and AWS Redshift with no automated linkage, making ROI calculation manual and time-consuming

l4_steps.name: Monitor CBA amendable date and trigger opening
l4_steps.input: Current CBA contract dates, calendar alert at 180-day threshold
l4_steps.output: Opening trigger memo; formal Section 6 notice preparation initiated
l4_steps.kpi: Opening notice filed ≥180 days before CBA amendable date; 100% of contracts tracked in SuccessFactors
l4_steps.pain_point: Under the Railway Labour Act (RLA), contracts do not expire — they become 'amendable'; status quo obligation means outdated terms can persist indefinitely if airline fails to file timely, freezing modernisation of scheduling systems and work rules

l4_steps.name: Benchmark labour costs against peer carriers
l4_steps.input: Current pay scales from SAP SuccessFactors; DOT Form 41 peer carrier filings; IATA airline cost data
l4_steps.output: Labour cost benchmarking report (cost gap vs. Delta, United, American, Southwest)
l4_steps.kpi: Data currency ≤90 days old; peer set covers ≥5 major carriers; report delivered ≥150 days before amendable date
l4_steps.pain_point: DOT Form 41 labour cost data is lagged 6–12 months; actual competitor total compensation packages (profit sharing, equity, per diem) are often not disclosed until SEC filings or union leaks, skewing benchmark modelling

l4_steps.name: Model financial impact of proposed contract changes
l4_steps.input: Benchmarking report; current headcount, pay grades, and FTE data from SAP SuccessFactors
l4_steps.output: Financial impact model with ≥5 pay scenarios, NPV over contract term, and cost-per-ASM sensitivity analysis
l4_steps.kpi: Model covers ≥5 scenarios; labour cost projection accuracy within ±2% of actuals at year-end; model delivered 120 days before amendable date
l4_steps.pain_point: Multi-year contract costing requires fuel price and ASM growth assumptions that are highly uncertain; modelling errors >5% have triggered mid-contract re-opening demands and resulted in $100M+ unbudgeted labour cost overruns at major US carriers

l4_steps.name: Form cross-functional management negotiating team
l4_steps.role: Chief People Officer / VP Labour Relations
l4_steps.input: Board/CEO negotiation parameters; legal counsel engagement; financial model from Step 1.3
l4_steps.output: Negotiation team charter; defined mandate authority limits; war-room SharePoint site stood up
l4_steps.kpi: Team constituted ≥120 days before target opening session; team includes Legal, Finance, Operations, and HR representation
l4_steps.pain_point: Conflicting priorities between Operations (scheduling flexibility), Finance (cost ceiling), and HR (retention) create an incoherent management position; union negotiators routinely exploit internal inconsistencies to extract additional concessions worth 1–3% of contract value

l4_steps.name: Develop management opening proposals and costing
l4_steps.input: Benchmarking report; financial model; operational requirements from Flight Operations and Crew Planning
l4_steps.output: Management opening proposal document with article-by-article positions; cost envelope per article
l4_steps.kpi: Proposal reviewed by outside labour counsel within 10 business days; FAR Part 117 and ICAO fatigue regulation compliance verified for all scheduling provisions
l4_steps.pain_point: Airline ops constraints (FAR Part 117 rest rules, ICAO fatigue regulations, irregular operations pay) must be precisely reflected in scheduling and duty-time contract language; ambiguous drafting creates compliance liability and exposes carrier to FAA enforcement action

l4_steps.name: Obtain board approval of negotiation mandate
l4_steps.input: Draft opening proposal; financial model with cost ceiling; outside counsel legal review sign-off
l4_steps.output: Board-approved negotiation mandate with cost ceiling and fall-back positions
l4_steps.kpi: Mandate approved before first bargaining session; cost ceiling grounded in verified FI/CO labour cost baseline
l4_steps.pain_point: Boards often set unrealistic cost ceilings based on prior-cycle assumptions or competitor announcements rather than current market data; mid-negotiation mandate revisions require additional board sessions, causing 3–6 month delays and signalling weakness to union

l4_steps.name: File Section 6 notice and open formal bargaining
l4_steps.input: Board-approved management proposal; union's Section 6 notice received
l4_steps.output: Bargaining docket opened in NMB portal; first session date confirmed; ground rules agreed
l4_steps.kpi: First bargaining session convened within 30 days of mutual Section 6 notice exchange
l4_steps.pain_point: Under the RLA status quo obligation, the airline cannot unilaterally change rates, rules, or working conditions during negotiations — a perpetual obligation that incentivises union delay tactics, with some RLA negotiations running 5–10 years before resolution

l4_steps.name: Conduct iterative proposal exchange and counter-proposals
l4_steps.role: Labour Relations Manager / Union Bargaining Committee
l4_steps.input: Opening proposals from both parties; session minutes; ground rules agreement
l4_steps.output: Redlined contract drafts per session; session tracker; consolidated open items log
l4_steps.kpi: Open items log reduced by ≥10% per bargaining month; no previously agreed article reopened without written consent of both parties
l4_steps.pain_point: Aviation-specific provisions (deadhead travel standards, hotel quality tiers, irregular operation pay triggers, open-time bidding rules) generate 60–80 contested articles that resist quick resolution; pattern bargaining pressures from other carriers complicate single-carrier negotiations

l4_steps.name: Track tentative agreements and maintain open issues log
l4_steps.input: Session minutes; articles agreed (TA) and disputed articles from each bargaining session
l4_steps.output: TA log (articles agreed with effective dates); open issues register with union and management positions per article
l4_steps.kpi: TA log updated within 24 hours of each session; open issues register shared with both parties within 48 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Without a structured tracker, previously agreed articles get reopened through 'linked bargaining' tactics, extending negotiations by 3–6 months; several major US airline negotiations have collapsed at the TA stage due to tracking failures

l4_steps.name: Assess bargaining progress and declare impasse if warranted
l4_steps.input: Open issues register; session count; timeline vs. target; financial model thresholds
l4_steps.output: Impasse declaration to NMB, or continued bargaining directive with revised target milestones
l4_steps.kpi: ≥75% of articles TA'd before NMB referral; target contract duration ≤24 months from opening notice to ratification
l4_steps.pain_point: The 2022–2024 US pilot shortage dramatically increased union leverage, extending pilot contract negotiations by 18+ months beyond historical norms; airlines that delayed impasse declarations lost scheduling certainty during peak summer hiring and capacity planning cycles

l4_steps.name: Request NMB mediation and establish case docket
l4_steps.input: Impasse declaration; unresolved articles list with positions documented
l4_steps.output: NMB case docket opened; assigned mediator confirmed; first mediated session scheduled
l4_steps.kpi: NMB application filed within 5 business days of impasse declaration; first mediated session convened within 45 days of NMB acceptance
l4_steps.pain_point: NMB mediation under the RLA is open-ended with no statutory time limit; airlines have been in NMB mediation for 3–7 years, making 5-year fleet planning, pilot hiring targets, and network capacity decisions highly uncertain throughout

l4_steps.name: Conduct NMB-mediated bargaining and resolve open articles
l4_steps.role: VP Labour Relations / NMB Mediator / Union President
l4_steps.input: NMB mediator briefing package; remaining open articles; financial parameters
l4_steps.output: Additional TAs on mediated articles; mediator recommendations; or NMB proffer of arbitration if impasse persists
l4_steps.kpi: Open articles reduced by ≥50% within 90 days of mediation start; full TA reached before proffer of arbitration where possible
l4_steps.pain_point: NMB proffer of arbitration triggers a mandatory 30-day cooling-off period after which 'self-help' (strikes, lockouts, unilateral change) becomes legal — the resulting operational and reputational risk has cost airlines $500M–$2B in market cap losses within 48 hours of strike announcements

l4_steps.name: Draft and execute full tentative agreement
l4_steps.role: Labour Relations Manager / Legal Counsel / Union Bargaining Committee
l4_steps.input: All TAs from bargaining and mediation sessions; mediator-brokered language; financial model final scenario
l4_steps.output: Fully executed tentative agreement document (all articles); implementation date schedule
l4_steps.kpi: Legal review completed within 15 business days; zero unresolved ambiguous provisions; implementation timeline agreed before union ratification vote
l4_steps.pain_point: Ambiguous contract language in scheduling system provisions (e.g. how crew management software generates open-time offers, or how irregular ops pay is calculated from ACARS data) becomes the primary source of grievances within 90 days of implementation, driving arbitration costs

l4_steps.name: Conduct union membership ratification vote
l4_steps.input: Signed TA; union member roster from SAP SuccessFactors; voting eligibility rules
l4_steps.output: Ratification vote result (pass/fail with percentage); formal ratification notice to management
l4_steps.kpi: Voter turnout ≥60%; ratification threshold >50% of votes cast per union bylaws; result certified within 5 business days of vote close
l4_steps.pain_point: Failed ratification votes (e.g. American Airlines pilot TA rejected in 2023 requiring renegotiation) delay implementation by 6–18 months, trigger stock price decline of 3–8%, and force management back to bargaining with a weakened position and increased union expectations

l4_steps.name: Implement ratified agreement in HR and payroll systems
l4_steps.input: Ratified agreement with effective dates; retroactive pay calculation if amendable date predates ratification
l4_steps.output: Updated pay scales, work rules, and benefits configurations in SuccessFactors; payroll cutover completed; retro pay processed
l4_steps.kpi: All pay changes live within 30 days of ratification; retroactive pay (if applicable) paid within 60 days; payroll error rate <0.1% of affected employees
l4_steps.pain_point: Complex retroactive pay calculations (back pay owed from amendable date, potentially 1–4 years prior, to thousands of employees) require manual reconciliation when SAP SuccessFactors lacks a native retro-pay engine for custom union pay scales, creating $10M+ reconciliation risk

l4_steps.name: Distribute contract and conduct manager training
l4_steps.role: Labour Relations Manager / HR Business Partners
l4_steps.input: Final executed contract; implementation guidelines; manager briefing deck
l4_steps.output: Contract published to employee self-service portal; manager training completion records in SAP SuccessFactors LMS
l4_steps.kpi: Contract accessible to 100% of covered employees within 14 days of ratification; ≥90% of frontline managers trained within 30 days; training completion tracked in SuccessFactors LMS
l4_steps.pain_point: Inconsistent manager interpretation of new scheduling provisions and irregular ops pay rules is the primary source of early grievances post-ratification; structured manager briefing has been shown to reduce first-year grievance rate by ~30% at comparable carriers

l4_steps.name: Monitor grievance filings and manage compliance
l4_steps.role: Labour Relations Coordinator / HR Business Partners
l4_steps.input: Employee or union grievance filings; relevant contract provisions; prior arbitration precedents
l4_steps.output: Grievance case log; Step 1/2/3 resolution decisions; arbitration referrals with legal brief
l4_steps.kpi: Step 1 grievance response within 10 business days; ≥70% of grievances resolved at Step 1 or 2 without arbitration; arbitration spend <$500K per year per contract group
l4_steps.pain_point: Accumulation of unresolved grievances — particularly around scheduling systems and irregular ops — creates a poisoned industrial relations climate entering the next contract cycle, amplifying union leverage; airlines with >500 open grievances at amendable date face 15–25% higher settlement premiums

l4_steps.name: Monitor Altéa PSS platform availability
l4_steps.input: Real-time telemetry from Amadeus Altéa hosting environment
l4_steps.output: Availability dashboard; automated alert triggers on SLA breach
l4_steps.kpi: PSS availability ≥99.95% (Amadeus contractual SLA); P1 alert threshold <99.9%
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa is hosted on Amadeus shared infrastructure — airline has limited visibility into underlying platform health; alerts may lag actual degradation by 2–3 minutes during peak booking windows

l4_steps.name: Execute daily Altéa module health checks
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa DCS / Amadeus Service Hub
l4_steps.input: Scheduled daily runbook; prior incident tickets; check-in profile inventory
l4_steps.output: Health check report; open defect log with severity classification
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of critical Altéa modules checked daily; zero unchecked P1 defects at day-start
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa DCS health check scripts are not fully automated — manual verification of check-in profile activation is required per airport, creating risk of missed misconfigurations before morning peak operations

l4_steps.name: Assess PSS capacity against booking surge forecast
l4_steps.input: Demand forecast from SkyCAST; current PSS TPS (transactions per second) baseline
l4_steps.output: Capacity risk assessment; Amadeus capacity uplift request if threshold breached
l4_steps.kpi: PSS transaction throughput ≥3,000 TPS at peak; platform headroom ≥20% above forecast peak
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus Altéa operates on shared cloud tenancy; requesting capacity uplift requires 72-hour lead time, creating exposure during unexpected IROPS-driven booking surges

l4_steps.name: Log PSS change request in ITSM
l4_steps.input: Business enhancement request or Amadeus scheduled release notification
l4_steps.output: Change request (CR) record with impact assessment template; priority classification
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of PSS changes logged in ServiceNow before implementation; backlog reviewed weekly; zero untracked production changes
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus imposes mandatory maintenance windows for Altéa upgrades (typically 02:00–05:00 local) that may conflict with overnight red-eye operations — airline has limited ability to defer mandatory platform upgrades

l4_steps.name: Conduct PSS change impact assessment
l4_steps.input: Change request record; Altéa module dependency map; active integration inventory
l4_steps.output: Impact assessment document; list of affected downstream systems (DCS, FFP, GDS feeds, CUTE, APIS)
l4_steps.kpi: Impact assessment completed within 3 business days of CR submission; zero unassessed downstream touchpoints at CAB submission
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS has 40+ integrated touchpoints (GDS, CUTE, APIS, FFP, payment gateway) — full dependency mapping is not maintained in a single CMDB, making impact assessment error-prone and time-consuming

l4_steps.name: Present PSS change to Change Advisory Board
l4_steps.input: Impact assessment; test plan; rollback procedure; maintenance window request
l4_steps.output: CAB approval decision; approved maintenance window slot; emergency change flag if urgent
l4_steps.kpi: CAB first-pass approval rate for standard PSS changes ≥85%; emergency changes <5% of total PSS change volume
l4_steps.pain_point: CAB cycle runs weekly — urgent commercial changes (e.g. new fare class activation before a sale launch) may miss the cycle, forcing the emergency change process which bypasses full regression testing

l4_steps.name: Deploy PSS configuration or patch to production
l4_steps.input: CAB-approved CR record; deployment runbook; rollback script; maintenance window confirmation
l4_steps.output: Deployed configuration or patch; CR status updated to Implemented in ServiceNow
l4_steps.kpi: Deployment success rate ≥98%; rollback execution ≤15 minutes if triggered; zero unplanned outages from PSS deployments
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus Altéa configuration deployment does not support blue-green or canary rollout — changes go live for all users simultaneously, making partial rollback impossible without full revert to prior state

l4_steps.name: Execute post-deployment validation and UAT sign-off
l4_steps.role: PSS QA Engineer / Business UAT Lead
l4_steps.input: Deployment confirmation; test scripts; acceptance criteria from business owner
l4_steps.output: UAT sign-off document; CR closed or rollback initiated with RCA
l4_steps.kpi: UAT sign-off within 4 hours of deployment; defect escape rate from PSS releases <2%; rollback decision within 30 minutes of failed gate
l4_steps.pain_point: Post-deployment testing in production relies on live bookings — synthetic transaction testing is limited in Altéa, meaning edge-case itinerary defects (multi-segment codeshares, redemption bookings) only surface with real passenger data

l4_steps.name: Detect and triage PSS service degradation
l4_steps.input: Automated Datadog alert; call centre escalation; airport operations degradation report
l4_steps.output: ServiceNow incident ticket; initial severity classification (P1–P4)
l4_steps.kpi: Mean time to detect (MTTD) ≤5 minutes; P1 incidents triaged within 10 minutes of detection
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa degradation often manifests downstream (slow check-in, booking errors) before the root Altéa API layer raises an alert — false-negative monitoring gaps cause delayed triage during initial incident stages, especially during network-wide IROPS

l4_steps.name: Engage Amadeus emergency support bridge for P1
l4_steps.input: P1 incident ticket; Amadeus SLA escalation threshold (>15 min outage); executive notification list
l4_steps.output: Active Amadeus support bridge; incident war room established; executive notifications dispatched
l4_steps.kpi: Amadeus P1 bridge engagement ≤15 minutes of incident declaration; executive notification ≤20 minutes; Amadeus MTTR for P1 platform incidents ≤60 minutes (SLA)
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus Altéa support tiers vary by contract — airlines without Premium SLA tiers experience slower engineer response; SLA contract review is annual and cannot flex responsively during high-impact IROPS events

l4_steps.name: Activate PSS failover or CUTE operational workaround
l4_steps.role: Airport Systems Manager / DCS Operations Lead
l4_steps.input: P1 incident active; failover runbook; CUTE offline check-in procedures; pre-staged passenger manifests
l4_steps.output: Workaround activated (CUTE local mode or paper boarding pass fallback); passenger impact report
l4_steps.kpi: Workaround activation ≤20 minutes from P1 declaration; zero flights missed due to check-in system failure under CUTE local mode
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA CUTE local mode requires pre-staged passenger data synced from PSS — if the outage occurs outside the 90-minute DCS data-push window before departure, CUTE offline mode cannot function and manual processing is required

l4_steps.name: Conduct post-incident review and log problem record
l4_steps.input: Closed P1/P2 incident ticket; incident timeline; Amadeus root cause report
l4_steps.output: Problem record; root cause analysis (RCA) document; permanent fix backlog item in ServiceNow
l4_steps.kpi: RCA completed within 5 business days of P1 resolution; permanent fix scheduled within 30 days for recurring incidents; zero repeat P1s from same root cause within 90 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus contractual RCA turnaround for Altéa platform-layer incidents is 10 business days — airline-side problem records cannot be closed until vendor RCA is received, creating SLA breaches in ITSM management reporting

l4_steps.name: Monitor GDS and NDC API message volumes
