l4_steps.input: Real-time GDS/NDC feed metrics; booking volume baseline; channel-level transaction logs
l4_steps.output: Integration health dashboard; anomaly alerts per GDS channel (Sabre, Travelport, Amadeus GDS)
l4_steps.kpi: GDS message success rate ≥99.5% per channel; NDC API response time ≤500ms (p95); zero unmonitored distribution channels
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS partners (Sabre GDS, Travelport GDS, Amadeus GDS) operate independent switching infrastructure — airline-side monitoring cannot definitively distinguish PSS degradation from GDS-side issues without per-channel telemetry, leading to mis-attribution of booking failures and delayed escalation

l4_steps.name: Validate APIS/PNR submission to government systems
l4_steps.role: Government Compliance Analyst / PSS Data Engineer
l4_steps.input: Booked PNR data; departure manifest; CBP/TSA APIS API endpoints; schedule change notifications
l4_steps.output: APIS transmission confirmation log; error report for failed or incomplete submissions
l4_steps.kpi: APIS advance notification success rate ≥99.9% (US CBP mandate); failed submissions resolved ≥4 hours before scheduled departure
l4_steps.pain_point: US CBP requires APIS transmission ≥60 minutes before departure for international flights — last-minute schedule changes or codeshare segment additions can break APIS data completeness, triggering regulatory penalties up to $5,000 per violation

l4_steps.name: Maintain PSS-to-CUTE/CUSS airport integration
l4_steps.input: Check-in agent workstation logs; CUTE connectivity reports; DCS profile configuration
l4_steps.output: Updated CUTE profile configuration; resolved connectivity tickets; DCS sync confirmation
l4_steps.kpi: CUTE check-in uptime ≥99.8% across all outstations; DCS profile sync errors <0.1% of daily transactions
l4_steps.pain_point: Airline operates at 100+ airports, each with varying CUTE software versions and local airport IT ownership — PSS DCS profile updates do not auto-propagate to all CUTE endpoints simultaneously, creating version drift that causes check-in failures during Altéa upgrades

l4_steps.name: Execute quarterly PCI-DSS scope review for PSS
l4_steps.system: Qualys / Amadeus Altéa Payment Gateway Integration
l4_steps.input: PCI-DSS v4.0 assessment checklist; PSS payment processing scope diagram; prior audit findings
l4_steps.output: PCI scope review report; remediation backlog items; updated scope diagram
l4_steps.kpi: PCI-DSS assessment completed quarterly; zero P1 findings at annual QSA audit; tokenization coverage ≥100% of card-present transactions
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus Altéa integrates with multiple payment processors (Worldpay, Adyen) via PSS middleware — PCI scope boundaries shift with each integration update, and Amadeus does not consistently publish advance notice of scope-impacting Altéa upgrades

l4_steps.name: Conduct PSS user access recertification
l4_steps.role: IT Security Analyst / PSS Access Control Owner
l4_steps.input: Quarterly access review schedule; Altéa role inventory; leaver/mover report from SAP SuccessFactors
l4_steps.output: Recertified access matrix; deprovisioned orphaned accounts; audit evidence package for SOX
l4_steps.kpi: Access review completed within 10 business days of cycle start; orphaned account remediation ≤24 hours of identification; privileged Altéa accounts reviewed monthly
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus Altéa user provisioning is managed in a separate identity silo from corporate Azure AD — SSO federation is partial, meaning leavers deprovisioned in Okta may retain active Altéa sessions until manual sync runs, creating SOX and GDPR compliance exposure

l4_steps.name: Ingest threat intelligence feeds
l4_steps.system: SITA Cybersecurity Services / ISAC Aviation AISAC feed
l4_steps.input: Aviation ISAC threat bulletins, CISA alerts, commercial CTI feeds
l4_steps.output: Normalised IOC set (IPs, domains, hashes) loaded into SIEM
l4_steps.kpi: Feed ingestion latency ≤15 min from publication; IOC coverage ≥95% of subscribed feeds
l4_steps.pain_point: Aviation ISAC feed cadence is irregular; manual triage required when SITA portal and Microsoft Sentinel connector versions diverge after platform updates

l4_steps.name: Monitor SIEM for security anomalies
l4_steps.input: Log streams from Amadeus Altéa PSS, AWS Security Hub, Palo Alto NGFW, endpoint telemetry
l4_steps.output: Security alerts queue; anomaly tickets auto-created in ServiceNow Security Operations
l4_steps.kpi: Mean time to detect (MTTD) ≤4 hrs for high-severity events; alert queue SLA acknowledgement ≤15 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus Altéa PSS syslog format requires custom parser; parser breaks on Altéa quarterly patch releases causing 2–6 hr blind-spot windows

l4_steps.name: Correlate IOCs and assess threat credibility
l4_steps.system: Microsoft Sentinel / Palo Alto Cortex XSOAR
l4_steps.input: Raw SIEM alerts, enriched IOCs from threat intel feeds
l4_steps.output: Threat credibility score; escalation decision to vulnerability management or incident triage
l4_steps.kpi: False positive rate ≤12% on high-severity alerts; IOC correlation throughput ≥500 indicators/hr
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS connection endpoints (Sabre, Travelport, Amadeus GDS) generate high IOC overlap with legitimate partner traffic, inflating false-positive rates

l4_steps.name: Schedule and execute authenticated vulnerability scan
l4_steps.input: Asset inventory from AWS Security Hub and ServiceNow CMDB; approved scan windows
l4_steps.output: Vulnerability report with CVSS scores, affected asset list, and CVE references
l4_steps.kpi: Scan coverage ≥98% of in-scope assets per cycle; scan cycle ≤7 days for internet-facing assets
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew management AWS-hosted system requires coordinated scan windows with Crew Ops to avoid disrupting real-time crew tracking; missed windows extend exposure

l4_steps.name: Prioritise vulnerabilities by CVSS and asset criticality
l4_steps.input: Raw vulnerability report, asset criticality tiers from CMDB
l4_steps.output: Risk-ranked remediation backlog with SLA targets (P1–P4) in ServiceNow
l4_steps.kpi: P1 (CVSS ≥9.0) remediation SLA ≤24 hrs; P2 (CVSS 7.0–8.9) ≤7 days; mean vulnerability age ≤30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Jeppesen FliteDeck EFB tablets are classified airline OT; patches require Boeing approval and airline maintenance sign-off, extending P2 remediation to 45+ days

l4_steps.name: Execute patch deployment or emergency remediation
l4_steps.system: ServiceNow Security Operations / AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager
l4_steps.input: Approved remediation backlog item, change request from ServiceNow CAB
l4_steps.output: Patched asset record, vulnerability closure confirmation in Tenable.io
l4_steps.kpi: Patch success rate ≥99% without service disruption; emergency patch deployment ≤4 hrs for P1
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus Altéa PSS patching requires Amadeus vendor coordination and PSS freeze window; unilateral patching risks PSS instability affecting booking and check-in functions

l4_steps.name: Classify and triage incoming security alert
l4_steps.input: Alert from Microsoft Sentinel or CrowdStrike Falcon EDR
l4_steps.output: Initial triage record with classification (malware, phishing, insider, DDoS, etc.) and severity P1–P4
l4_steps.kpi: Triage completion ≤15 min for P1/P2; analyst throughput ≥20 alerts/hr per Tier-1 analyst
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC API Gateway traffic is high-volume JSON; DDoS patterns targeting NDC endpoints are difficult to distinguish from legitimate agency booking bursts without airline-specific baselines

l4_steps.name: Validate alert as true or false positive
l4_steps.input: Triage record, endpoint telemetry, network flow logs from Palo Alto NGFW
l4_steps.output: Confirmed true/false positive determination; false positives closed with tuning note
l4_steps.kpi: True positive confirmation rate ≥88%; false positive closure with tuning update ≤2 hrs
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA ACARS messages traversing legacy ground-to-air links generate unusual encoding patterns that trigger EDR heuristics; suppression rules require SITA vendor input to avoid masking real threats

l4_steps.name: Assign incident owner and escalate to IR team
l4_steps.input: Confirmed true positive with severity, initial classification
l4_steps.output: Incident ticket assigned to IR owner; P1 bridge call initiated; CISO notified for P1
l4_steps.kpi: P1 escalation to IR team ≤30 min from true positive confirmation; IR lead acknowledgement ≤15 min
l4_steps.pain_point: On-call rotation gaps during irregular flight operations (e.g., irregular operations recovery periods) delay P1 escalation when SOC team is simultaneously supporting NOC cyber requests

l4_steps.name: Activate incident response playbook
l4_steps.input: Incident ticket, threat classification, affected asset list
l4_steps.output: Active XSOAR playbook run with assigned task steps; war room opened in collaboration tool
l4_steps.kpi: Playbook activation ≤5 min of IR lead assignment; playbook coverage ≥95% of known threat categories
l4_steps.pain_point: Airline-specific playbooks for PSS compromise and GDS channel manipulation are not included in XSOAR out-of-box content library; custom playbooks require quarterly review to stay current with Amadeus Altéa version changes

l4_steps.name: Isolate affected endpoints and network segments
l4_steps.input: Confirmed affected asset list from XSOAR playbook
l4_steps.output: Isolated hosts (network contain via CrowdStrike); VLAN quarantine applied via Palo Alto policy push
l4_steps.kpi: Containment time ≤1 hr for P1; mean time to contain (MTTC) ≤2 hrs across all incidents
l4_steps.pain_point: AWS-hosted crew management system cannot be hard-isolated without triggering crew tracking outage; partial isolation (egress block only) leaves lateral movement risk

l4_steps.name: Assess OT or avionics system involvement
l4_steps.system: ServiceNow Security Operations / Tenable OT Security
l4_steps.input: Affected asset CMDB records, network topology map, CrowdStrike telemetry
l4_steps.output: OT/avionics scope determination; regulatory notification trigger decision
l4_steps.kpi: OT scope assessment completion ≤30 min of containment; 100% of OT-involved incidents flagged for TSA notification within required window
l4_steps.pain_point: EFB (Jeppesen FliteDeck) tablets on aircraft are in a grey zone between IT and OT asset classification; incident scope determination requires coordination between IT Security, Flight Operations, and Boeing technical representatives

l4_steps.name: Notify TSA and CISA per cybersecurity directive SD-04C
l4_steps.system: TSA Cybersecurity Reporting Portal / ServiceNow GRC
l4_steps.input: OT/avionics involvement confirmation, incident severity, timeline of events
l4_steps.output: TSA notification submitted within 24 hrs; CISA report filed; log preserved in ServiceNow GRC
l4_steps.kpi: TSA notification compliance: 100% on-time within 24-hr regulatory window; zero overdue reports
l4_steps.pain_point: TSA SD-04C reporting thresholds are ambiguous for incidents affecting systems that touch both IT and airline-operated networks (e.g., airport check-in kiosks on shared infrastructure); legal review adds time

l4_steps.name: Eradicate threat and preserve digital evidence
l4_steps.input: Isolated systems, threat actor TTPs, XSOAR playbook eradication task
l4_steps.output: Cleaned endpoints, forensic image stored in AWS S3 evidence bucket with chain of custody
l4_steps.kpi: Evidence collection completeness ≥99% of affected hosts; eradication verified by CrowdStrike scan before re-entry to network
l4_steps.pain_point: Volatile memory forensics on Amadeus Altéa reservation servers requires PSS vendor coordination; uncoordinated memory acquisition risks PSS process interruption affecting live bookings

l4_steps.name: Restore systems from clean validated backup
l4_steps.input: Eradication sign-off, approved recovery runbook, last known-good backup snapshot
l4_steps.output: Restored system instance, recovery validation test results, change record closed in ServiceNow
l4_steps.kpi: RTO ≤4 hrs for P1 critical systems (PSS, crew system); RPO ≤1 hr for tier-1 systems
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus Altéa PSS restoration must be sequenced with Amadeus Altéa operations team in Madrid; time zone dependency and vendor SLA of 4-hr response means RTO targets are at risk for overnight incidents

l4_steps.name: Conduct post-incident review and root cause analysis
l4_steps.input: Incident timeline, XSOAR playbook run log, forensic evidence summary
l4_steps.output: Post-incident review (PIR) report with RCA, timeline, and ≥3 action items in ServiceNow
l4_steps.kpi: PIR completion ≤5 business days for P1; 100% of action items assigned with due date; action item closure rate ≥85% within 30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Airline operational disruption pressure (irregular operations recovery) competes with PIR scheduling; PIR action items for systemic GDS security gaps are deprioritised against commercial recovery objectives

l4_steps.name: Update controls, playbooks, and threat detection rules
l4_steps.system: Microsoft Sentinel / Palo Alto Cortex XSOAR / Tenable.io
l4_steps.input: PIR action items, new threat actor TTPs identified during incident
l4_steps.output: Updated Sentinel detection rules, revised XSOAR playbooks, new Tenable scan policies; changes logged in ServiceNow GRC
l4_steps.kpi: Detection rule update deployment ≤48 hrs of PIR sign-off; XSOAR playbook coverage improvement measured per PIR cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: Sentinel custom rules for Amadeus Altéa and Sabre GDS log formats must be regression-tested against production log samples after every rule update; lack of a dedicated security staging environment increases change risk

l4_steps.name: Capture data source requirements from business
l4_steps.input: Business analytics request or new system onboarding
l4_steps.output: Data source specification document with SLA and refresh frequency
l4_steps.kpi: Requirements captured within 5 business days of request; ≥90% completeness score
l4_steps.pain_point: Airline ops systems (Amadeus Altéa, Jeppesen) use proprietary APIs with limited documentation, causing specification rework

l4_steps.name: Assess source API availability and schema
l4_steps.input: Data source specification document
l4_steps.output: Schema discovery report; connector feasibility assessment
l4_steps.kpi: Schema discovery completed within 2 days; 100% of fields documented
l4_steps.pain_point: PSS and crew management systems use batch SFTP exports rather than real-time APIs, creating up to 24-hour data latency for operational dashboards

l4_steps.name: Configure AWS Glue ETL connectors
l4_steps.input: Schema discovery report; source credentials in AWS Secrets Manager
l4_steps.output: Parameterised Glue job with incremental load logic
l4_steps.kpi: Connector build time ≤3 days; incremental load latency ≤15 min for streaming sources
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS feed formats (Sabre, Travelport) change without advance notice, breaking Glue jobs and requiring emergency patching during revenue-critical periods

l4_steps.name: Ingest raw data to S3 landing zone
l4_steps.input: Source system data via Glue job or Kinesis Data Streams
l4_steps.output: Raw partitioned Parquet files in S3 landing zone with ingestion timestamp
l4_steps.kpi: Pipeline success rate ≥99.5% per month; P99 ingestion latency ≤30 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus Altéa PNR change events generate burst loads during irregular operations (IROPs), overwhelming Kinesis shards and causing data loss if auto-scaling is not pre-configured

l4_steps.name: Execute automated data quality checks
l4_steps.input: Raw data files in S3 landing zone
l4_steps.output: DQ scorecard with row counts, null rates, freshness, schema drift alerts
l4_steps.kpi: DQ check coverage ≥95% of all active datasets; anomaly detection P95 latency ≤10 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Flight operations feeds contain mission-critical fields (flight status, delay codes) where a single null cascades into incorrect OTP reporting to DOT, creating regulatory exposure

l4_steps.name: Quarantine and triage DQ failures
l4_steps.input: DQ failure alert from Monte Carlo
l4_steps.output: Quarantine record in S3 rejected zone; Jira ticket auto-created for source team
l4_steps.kpi: P1 DQ incidents triaged within 1 hour; resolution SLA ≤4 hours for operational data domains
l4_steps.pain_point: Crew system data gaps post-irregular ops (mirrors Dec 2022 SkySolver failure pattern) create silent DQ failures where crew assignment data appears complete but contains stale records

l4_steps.name: Register and classify dataset in data catalog
l4_steps.input: Validated dataset; DQ scorecard
l4_steps.output: Catalog entry with business glossary linkage, data owner, lineage graph, and retention policy
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of production datasets catalogued within 1 sprint of go-live; lineage coverage ≥80% of governed domains
l4_steps.pain_point: High analyst turnover means undocumented datasets proliferate; teams build duplicate pipelines for the same source, wasting engineering capacity and creating inconsistent metrics

l4_steps.name: Apply PII masking and access controls
l4_steps.input: Dataset classification from Collibra; GDPR/CCPA data subject inventory
l4_steps.output: Masked/tokenised dataset in governed S3 zone; IAM policy attached to dataset
l4_steps.kpi: PII detection coverage ≥99% of passenger-facing domains; zero unmasked PII in non-production environments
l4_steps.pain_point: Rapid Rewards member data flows through multiple systems (Altéa, Redshift, Tableau); inconsistent masking across environments has previously caused PII exposure in analytics sandboxes

l4_steps.name: Develop dbt transformation models
l4_steps.input: Governed raw data in S3; dimensional modelling spec from data product owner
l4_steps.output: dbt models (staging → intermediate → mart layers); compiled SQL lineage DAG
l4_steps.kpi: dbt model test pass rate ≥98%; model execution time within agreed SLA per domain (e.g. revenue mart ≤20 min)
l4_steps.pain_point: Fare and revenue data from ATPCO and Amadeus NRM use airline-specific tariff codes that require complex lookup logic; errors in fare basis decoding produce materially wrong yield reports

l4_steps.name: Run dbt model tests and schema validation
l4_steps.input: dbt model compilation output
l4_steps.output: Test results report; row count reconciliation against source
l4_steps.kpi: Zero undetected primary-key duplicates in mart layer; row count variance ≤0.1% vs source
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus SkyWORKS schedule changes (flight adds/cancels) generate late-arriving facts that cause mart row count mismatches, failing dbt tests and blocking downstream dashboards

l4_steps.name: Load transformed data to Redshift data warehouse
l4_steps.input: Validated dbt mart tables in S3; COPY manifest
l4_steps.output: Populated Redshift dimensional schema with distribution and sort keys optimised
l4_steps.kpi: Load job SLA: ≤60 min for daily full refresh; query P90 response time ≤5 s on standard analyst workloads
l4_steps.pain_point: Redshift cluster concurrency limits cause query queuing during peak morning reporting windows (06:00–09:00 local), when ops, revenue, and finance teams all run simultaneous heavy queries

l4_steps.name: Design and build Tableau analytics dashboards
l4_steps.input: Redshift mart tables; stakeholder wireframe sign-off
l4_steps.output: Tableau workbook with certified data source and row-level security filters
l4_steps.kpi: Dashboard load time ≤8 s on standard extract; certified data source reuse rate ≥60% across dashboards
l4_steps.pain_point: Business users bypass certified data sources and connect directly to raw Redshift tables, creating metric discrepancies between dashboards and eroding trust in analytics outputs

l4_steps.name: Obtain stakeholder sign-off on dashboard accuracy
l4_steps.input: Published Tableau dashboard (UAT environment); reconciliation against source system report
l4_steps.output: Signed acceptance document; dashboard promoted to production Tableau Server
l4_steps.kpi: UAT cycle ≤5 business days; zero P1 metric errors post-production release
l4_steps.pain_point: Revenue management teams use Amadeus NRM as system of record for yield metrics; divergence between NRM native reports and Tableau (caused by time-zone offsets in fact tables) leads to sign-off delays

l4_steps.name: Publish self-service data products to analytics portal
l4_steps.input: Certified Tableau dashboards; approved dbt mart definitions
l4_steps.output: Published data product with SLA, owner, lineage, and Collibra catalog linkage
l4_steps.kpi: Data product NPS ≥7/10 in quarterly survey; product adoption ≥80% of target business unit within 30 days of launch
l4_steps.pain_point: Lack of a self-service data marketplace means analyst requests are routed to the data engineering backlog, creating queue times of 4–8 weeks for straightforward data access needs

l4_steps.name: Monitor pipeline health and SLA compliance
l4_steps.input: Airflow DAG run metrics; Glue job logs; Redshift query performance insights
l4_steps.output: Real-time pipeline health dashboard; automated SLA breach alerts to PagerDuty
l4_steps.kpi: Pipeline SLA breach rate ≤0.5% per month; mean time to detect (MTTD) ≤5 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Airflow MWAA auto-scaling lags during IROP events when flight data ingestion volume spikes 3–5× baseline, causing cascading DAG failures and delayed operational reporting to the NOC

l4_steps.name: Manage Redshift cluster capacity and cost governance
l4_steps.input: Monthly Redshift usage report; query advisor recommendations
l4_steps.output: Rightsizing recommendation; reserved instance purchase plan; cluster scaling action
l4_steps.kpi: Redshift cost per TB processed ≤$25; month-over-month cost variance ≤10%; idle cluster time ≤5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Ad-hoc analyst queries with full table scans on unoptimised Redshift tables generate runaway costs; lack of workload management (WLM) queues allows single queries to consume entire cluster resources

l4_steps.name: Execute platform incident response and root-cause analysis
l4_steps.input: SLA breach alert from CloudWatch; user-reported data outage
l4_steps.output: Incident resolution; post-mortem report in Confluence; pipeline fix deployed via CI/CD
l4_steps.kpi: MTTR for P1 data outages ≤2 hours; post-mortem completed within 48 hours; recurrence rate ≤10% for resolved incidents
l4_steps.pain_point: Data platform incidents during irregular operations (when analytics are most needed by NOC and Revenue) cannot be deprioritised, but on-call rosters are understaffed relative to the criticality of the platform

l4_steps.name: Capture and validate sourcing requirement
l4_steps.input: Purchase requisition or strategic sourcing request from business unit
l4_steps.output: Validated sourcing request with spend category code and business justification
l4_steps.kpi: Sourcing request processed within 2 business days of submission
l4_steps.pain_point: Airlines carry highly fragmented procurement across MRO, IT, fuel, catering, and ground handling — category ownership disputes between Finance and Operations delay sourcing initiation by 3–7 days on average

l4_steps.name: Conduct spend analysis and category benchmarking
l4_steps.system: SAP S/4HANA Finance (FI/CO) + SAP Ariba Analytics
l4_steps.input: Validated sourcing request, historical PO data from SAP S/4HANA
l4_steps.output: Category spend cube, supplier concentration report, year-on-year variance analysis
l4_steps.kpi: Spend data coverage ≥95% of addressable spend in category; analysis completed within 3 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Fuel, MRO, and ground handling spend frequently sits in legacy cost centers not yet mapped to SAP Ariba Analytics, creating data blind spots that understate category spend by up to 20%

l4_steps.name: Assess supply market and regulatory landscape
l4_steps.system: SAP Ariba Supplier Risk + Dun & Bradstreet Direct+
l4_steps.input: Category spend cube, procurement policy, FAA/DOT regulatory requirements
l4_steps.output: Market assessment report with supplier landscape map and regulatory constraint summary
l4_steps.kpi: Market assessment completed within 5 business days; ≥3 qualified alternative suppliers identified per category
l4_steps.pain_point: Aviation-specific supplier pools (e.g. FAA Part 145 repair stations, EASA-approved MRO shops) are narrow — market power asymmetry severely constrains negotiation leverage; fewer than 3 qualified suppliers in many technical categories

l4_steps.name: Define sourcing strategy and evaluation scorecard
l4_steps.input: Market assessment report, category strategy template, stakeholder requirements
l4_steps.output: Approved sourcing strategy document with weighted evaluation scorecard (technical, commercial, risk)
l4_steps.kpi: Stakeholder sign-off on strategy within 3 business days; evaluation criteria weighted and approved prior to RFx issuance
l4_steps.pain_point: Flight Operations and Maintenance stakeholders frequently bypass procurement to negotiate directly with preferred vendors, undermining competitive process integrity and creating maverick spend exposure

l4_steps.name: Build and issue RFI/RFP/RFQ package to suppliers
l4_steps.input: Sourcing strategy, technical specification from business unit, approved supplier invitation list
l4_steps.output: Published RFx with Q&A forum, supplier NDA, and submission deadline; ≥5 qualified suppliers invited
l4_steps.kpi: RFP issued within 5 business days of strategy approval; minimum 5 qualified suppliers invited per event
l4_steps.pain_point: Aviation technical specifications for avionics components and GSE routinely contain ITAR/EAR export control clauses requiring Legal pre-clearance — this delays RFP issuance by 3–10 business days and is not tracked within standard Ariba Sourcing workflow

l4_steps.name: Manage supplier Q&A period and receive proposals
l4_steps.input: Published RFx, supplier clarification queries, potential addenda
l4_steps.output: Clarification addenda issued to all bidders; sealed supplier proposals received in Ariba
l4_steps.kpi: Proposal submission rate ≥60% of invited suppliers; addenda issued to all bidders within 24 hours of Q&A close
l4_steps.pain_point: RFx deadline extensions to accommodate late supplier queries inflate sourcing cycle time by 5–15 days; SAP Ariba version-lock on RFP documents can prevent late addenda from being distributed to all bidders simultaneously, creating legal exposure

l4_steps.name: Score proposals against weighted evaluation criteria
l4_steps.role: Evaluation Committee (Category Manager, BU Technical Lead, Finance)
l4_steps.input: Sealed supplier proposals, approved evaluation scorecard
l4_steps.output: Ranked vendor shortlist with technical and commercial composite scores
l4_steps.kpi: Scoring completed within 5 business days of proposal deadline; inter-evaluator score variance <15% per criterion
l4_steps.pain_point: Technical evaluators from Flight Operations and MRO departments frequently lack procurement training, producing non-compliant scoring narratives that expose the airline to bid protest risk and require rework cycles

l4_steps.name: Conduct vendor due diligence and financial health check
l4_steps.system: SAP Ariba Supplier Risk + Dun & Bradstreet Direct+
l4_steps.input: Shortlisted vendor list from scoring output
l4_steps.output: Supplier risk profile covering financial stability, ESG standing, and regulatory compliance status
l4_steps.kpi: Due diligence completed within 3 business days; zero unresolved critical risk flags at award recommendation stage
l4_steps.pain_point: Post-pandemic supply chain fragility means key MRO and GSE suppliers carry elevated debt loads — D&B Paydex scores alone are insufficient for FAA-regulated suppliers, which also require manual verification of current FAA Repair Station Certificate (Form 8310-3) validity

l4_steps.name: Conduct best-and-final-offer (BAFO) round
l4_steps.input: Shortlisted vendors, scoring results, commercial baseline pricing
l4_steps.output: BAFO submissions from shortlisted vendors, updated commercial comparison matrix
l4_steps.kpi: Cost reduction vs. baseline ≥8% for competitive categories; BAFO round completed within 5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Fuel hedging contracts and aircraft wet-lease negotiations require Treasury and Legal involvement that is not modelled in standard Ariba BAFO workflows — offline negotiation tracks create version control issues and audit trail gaps

l4_steps.name: Prepare award recommendation and obtain DOA approval
l4_steps.system: SAP Ariba Procurement (Approval workflow) + SAP S/4HANA Finance
l4_steps.input: BAFO results, evaluation summary, Delegation of Authority (DOA) matrix
l4_steps.output: Award recommendation memo with financial impact analysis; spend authority approval obtained per DOA tier
l4_steps.kpi: Approval obtained within 2 business days for contracts within CPO authority; 100% of awards documented against DOA matrix
l4_steps.pain_point: Multi-tier DOA matrices mean large MRO or IT contracts frequently require Board-level approval, creating 10–20-day bottlenecks when procurement timeline is driven by AOG (Aircraft on Ground) operational urgency

l4_steps.name: Draft, negotiate, and execute vendor contract
l4_steps.input: Award recommendation, standard contract templates, BAFO final submission
l4_steps.output: Fully executed contract with SLAs, liability caps, termination clauses, and insurance requirements
l4_steps.kpi: Contract execution within 10 business days of award; ≤2 redline round-trips on standard contract terms
l4_steps.pain_point: Aviation-specific indemnity clauses (hull and liability coverage requirements for ground handlers, hangar keepers liability) routinely stall negotiations — the airline's aviation contract template library in SAP Ariba Contracts is often outdated versus current IATA Ground Handling Agreement (IGHA 2013) standards

l4_steps.name: Activate vendor master record in SAP S/4HANA
l4_steps.system: SAP Ariba Contracts + SAP S/4HANA Finance (Vendor Master)
l4_steps.input: Executed contract with payment terms, banking details, and tax classification
l4_steps.output: Active vendor master record in SAP S/4HANA; contract record linked in SAP Ariba Contracts
l4_steps.kpi: Vendor master activated within 1 business day of contract execution; 100% contract data accuracy confirmed in Ariba Contracts
l4_steps.pain_point: Duplicate vendor master entries in SAP S/4HANA (created by decentralised AP teams across hub stations without central Ariba governance) cause payment routing errors and complicate spend reporting; MDM cleanse required for ~15% of new vendor activations

l4_steps.name: Execute vendor onboarding and EDI/API integration test
l4_steps.system: SAP Ariba Supply Chain Collaboration + EDI/API Gateway
l4_steps.input: Activated vendor master, executed contract, integration specification
l4_steps.output: Completed onboarding checklist; EDI/API test results confirming PO and invoice transaction accuracy
l4_steps.kpi: Onboarding completed within 10 business days of contract activation; EDI transaction error rate <1% in test phase
l4_steps.pain_point: MRO suppliers (FAA Part 145 repair stations) and smaller catering vendors often lack EDI/API capability — manual PO and invoice processing inflates error rate and extends AOG parts procurement lead times by 24–48 hours

l4_steps.name: Establish vendor KPI scorecard and SLA baseline
l4_steps.system: SAP Ariba Supplier Performance Management + Tableau
l4_steps.input: Executed contract SLAs, historical baseline data where available, operations KPI definitions
l4_steps.output: Published vendor scorecard template; KPI dashboard live in Tableau for operational stakeholder visibility
l4_steps.kpi: Vendor scorecard published within 5 business days of go-live; ≥90% of contracted SLA fields populated at baseline
l4_steps.pain_point: Procurement and Flight Operations use conflicting KPI definitions for vendor performance (procurement measures on-time delivery; Ops measures AOG-free rate) — SAP Ariba SPM module is not configured to capture operations-driven SLAs, requiring manual Tableau overlays that are inconsistently maintained

l4_steps.name: Conduct 90-day post-award performance review
l4_steps.system: SAP Ariba Supplier Performance Management + Tableau
l4_steps.input: Vendor scorecard, invoice data, delivery records, and incident logs from first 90 days
l4_steps.output: Post-award review report; corrective action plan (CAP) issued if SLA threshold not met
l4_steps.kpi: 90-day review completed on schedule for 100% of strategic vendors; vendor SLA achievement ≥85% at 90-day gate
l4_steps.pain_point: High-volume catering and GSE contracts rarely receive structured 90-day reviews due to Category Manager bandwidth constraints — performance issues compound undetected until contract renewal, entrenching underperforming vendors and increasing switching costs

l4_steps.name: Extract fuel volume forecast from flight schedule
l4_steps.input: Approved flight schedule (SSIM), fleet assignment by station
l4_steps.output: Station-level fuel volume forecast (US gallons by month, 12-month horizon)
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast accuracy ≥95% vs actual uplift volume at month-end
l4_steps.pain_point: Schedule changes post-freeze invalidate fuel pre-purchases with no automated re-forecast trigger in SkyWORKS; manual rework required for each schedule revision

l4_steps.name: Model price scenarios and set hedging target
l4_steps.input: Fuel volume forecast, Platts jet fuel spot prices, 12-month forward curve
l4_steps.output: Hedge ratio recommendation (% of forward volume), scenario P&L analysis
l4_steps.kpi: Hedge ratio within board-approved policy band of 30–70% of forward 12-month volume
l4_steps.pain_point: Jet fuel crack spread volatility (2022: +180% YoY) can force hedge ratio outside approved bands requiring board escalation; no automated alert in OpenLink Endur

l4_steps.name: Submit annual fuel budget to Finance
l4_steps.input: Approved volume forecast, hedged price scenarios, prior-year actuals
l4_steps.output: Approved fuel OPEX budget by cost centre and quarter
l4_steps.kpi: Budget variance ≤±5% vs actual fuel cost at year-end
l4_steps.pain_point: Annual budget locked in Q4 but jet fuel prices move daily; SAP CO-PA budget version does not auto-update with market rate changes, causing stale variance reporting throughout the year

l4_steps.name: Evaluate and qualify fuel suppliers by station
l4_steps.input: Station list, ICAO airport codes, DEF STAN 91-091 quality standards, supplier capability submissions
l4_steps.output: Approved supplier register by airport with qualification status
l4_steps.kpi: ≥2 qualified suppliers at every Tier-1 hub; 100% supplier compliance with ASTM D1655 specification
l4_steps.pain_point: Remote and international stations frequently have a single into-plane agent with no qualified alternative; supply disruption at these stations forces flight hold with no automated contingency in SAP Ariba

l4_steps.name: Issue RFQ and evaluate competitive fuel bids
l4_steps.input: Volume forecast by station, approved supplier register, pricing reference (Platts Jet A)
l4_steps.output: Scored bid comparison matrix, recommended award by station
l4_steps.kpi: RFQ cycle time ≤21 calendar days; minimum 3 bids received per major hub station
l4_steps.pain_point: Fuel suppliers submit non-standard pricing structures (flat-rate, index-linked, spot differential) making direct price comparison difficult; no normalisation tool in SAP Ariba Sourcing for jet fuel indices

l4_steps.name: Negotiate and execute fuel supply agreement
l4_steps.input: Bid comparison matrix, legal terms template, approved supplier, volume commitments
l4_steps.output: Signed fuel supply agreement (price formula, volume commitment, quality specs, liability caps)
l4_steps.kpi: Contract coverage ≥90% of annual volume; contract execution ≤30 days from award decision
l4_steps.pain_point: Into-plane agent contracts are separate from fuel supply contracts at most airports — coordinating two parallel contract cycles per station doubles procurement workload and creates liability gap periods

l4_steps.name: Generate daily fuel uplift orders from flight ops
l4_steps.input: Day-of flight plan (Jeppesen FliteDeck), fuel release quantities, tankering policy parameters
l4_steps.output: Fuel uplift orders by flight number and station for next 24 hours
l4_steps.kpi: Order accuracy ≥99.5% (uplift quantity within ±2% of flight plan requirement); order generation completed ≥4 hours before first departure
l4_steps.pain_point: Tankering decisions require real-time station price feed integration with FuelPlus; feed latency of 2–6 hours causes suboptimal tankering recommendations and missed cost-saving windows

l4_steps.name: Evaluate tankering opportunity vs payload penalty
l4_steps.input: Station fuel price differentials, aircraft weight/balance constraints (MTOW), cost-per-seat-mile model
l4_steps.output: Tankering go/no-go decision with estimated cost saving per flight
l4_steps.kpi: Tankering savings ≥$0.01/US gallon average across network; zero overweight departure events attributable to tankering
l4_steps.pain_point: Boeing 737 MAX 8 MTOW constraints limit tankering payload trade-off on high-load routes; FuelPlus does not automatically model per-aircraft-variant weight limits, requiring manual override by dispatcher

l4_steps.name: Execute purchase order and payment authorisation
l4_steps.system: SAP Ariba (Purchase Orders) + SAP S/4HANA Finance (AP)
l4_steps.input: Approved uplift orders, active supply contract reference, station fuel card limits
l4_steps.output: Confirmed PO, EFT payment instruction or fuel card charge authorisation
l4_steps.kpi: PO-to-supplier-confirmation cycle ≤4 hours for same-day uplifts; zero declined fuel card transactions
l4_steps.pain_point: International stations use Air BP or Shell Aviation fuel cards with daily spending limits that are frequently exceeded during irregular operations; no real-time limit monitoring integrated with SAP Ariba

l4_steps.name: Monitor real-time fuel delivery at departure gate
l4_steps.input: Fuel truck arrival notification, loadsheet, flight plan fuel quantity (block fuel + reserve)
l4_steps.output: Uplift completion confirmation, fuel density and quantity record (litres and kg)
l4_steps.kpi: Fuelling completion ≥30 minutes before scheduled departure; zero misfuel incidents
l4_steps.pain_point: ACARS delivery confirmations are occasionally lost or delayed at high-traffic hub stations; manual phone backup creates audit trail gaps that complicate invoice reconciliation and incident investigation

l4_steps.name: Validate fuel quality certificate at delivery
l4_steps.input: Fuel delivery note, batch certificate of analysis, DEF STAN 91-091 / ASTM D1655 spec sheet
l4_steps.output: Approved fuel release certificate or hold notice with reason code
l4_steps.kpi: 100% batch documentation compliance before uplift; zero fuel contamination incidents per year
l4_steps.pain_point: API gravity and water content test results take 2–4 hours at some stations — aircraft may be fuelled before final QC sign-off is recorded, creating regulatory exposure under EASA Part-M and FAA AC 43-12A

l4_steps.name: Manage fuel shortage or delivery failure exception
l4_steps.input: Shortage notification from into-plane agent, alternate supplier register, flight departure window
l4_steps.output: Emergency fuel order confirmation or flight departure hold decision with ATC notification
l4_steps.kpi: Shortage resolution ≤45 minutes; zero flight cancellations attributable to fuel unavailability
l4_steps.pain_point: At single-supplier airports there is no fallback into-plane agent; shortage forces a weight-limited departure or flight hold with no automated contingency order workflow in FuelPlus — manual station calls required

l4_steps.name: 3-way match fuel invoice to uplift and PO
l4_steps.input: Supplier invoice, FuelPlus uplift record, approved PO
l4_steps.output: Matched invoice cleared for payment or discrepancy flag with reason
l4_steps.kpi: Automated 3-way match rate ≥97%; discrepancy identification within 2 business days of invoice receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: Into-plane agents invoice using different unit conventions (US gallons, litres, imperial gallons) with varying density references; unit conversion errors are the primary cause of auto-match failures and require manual correction

l4_steps.name: Resolve invoice discrepancy with fuel supplier
l4_steps.input: Discrepancy report, original supplier invoice, FuelPlus uplift records, PO
l4_steps.output: Approved credit note or revised invoice accepted into SAP FI-AP
l4_steps.kpi: Discrepancy recovery rate ≥95% within 30 days; average credit recovery ≥$0.005/gallon on disputed volume
l4_steps.pain_point: International suppliers dispute density conversion differences citing local regulatory standards — no standard IATA API gravity reference is integrated into the SAP Ariba supplier collaboration workflow, prolonging resolution cycles

l4_steps.name: Process approved fuel payment and post to GL
l4_steps.input: Approved invoice, contract payment terms, supplier bank details, FX daily rate
l4_steps.output: Payment run confirmation, GL posting to Fuel OPEX cost centre
l4_steps.kpi: On-time payment rate ≥98% per contract terms; zero duplicate payment incidents per quarter
l4_steps.pain_point: Multi-currency fuel payments (USD, EUR, GBP, AED) require daily FX rate updates in SAP — rate feed lag of 1–2 days creates accounting timing differences vs actual bank settlement, generating reconciling items in period-end close

l4_steps.name: Mark-to-market hedge positions and test effectiveness
l4_steps.input: Platts jet fuel spot price, 12-month forward curve, open hedge position register
l4_steps.output: Daily MTM P&L report, hedge effectiveness ratio (prospective and retrospective)
l4_steps.kpi: Hedge effectiveness ≥80% (IFRS 9 hedge accounting qualification threshold); MTM report delivered by 09:00 each trading day
l4_steps.pain_point: IFRS 9 hedge accounting requires both prospective and retrospective effectiveness testing — OpenLink Endur configuration requires quarterly recertification by external auditor; any system upgrade risks de-qualifying existing hedges

l4_steps.name: Report fuel cost per ASM to senior leadership
l4_steps.input: Monthly uplift actuals (FuelPlus), invoice data (SAP FI-AP), hedge P&L (OpenLink), budget (SAP CO-PA)
l4_steps.output: Fuel cost per available seat mile (CASM) report, budget variance analysis, rolling 12-month forecast
l4_steps.kpi: Fuel CASM ≤$0.055; variance report published within 5 business days of month-end close
l4_steps.pain_point: Flight-level fuel cost attribution requires a data join between FuelPlus uplift records and SkyWORKS ASM data with no automated ETL pipeline — monthly manual extract and reconciliation takes 2–3 FTE days and introduces version control risk

l4_steps.name: Extract aircraft parts demand from MRO system
l4_steps.input: Scheduled maintenance work orders, AD compliance calendar, historical consumption rates
l4_steps.output: Parts demand list by ATA chapter, quantity, and required-by date
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast accuracy ≥92% (actual vs planned consumption within 30-day window)
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS demand signals are not always linked to long-range MRO event schedules, causing reactive spot-buy procurement that inflates unit cost by 20–40%

l4_steps.name: Run inventory replenishment forecast in SAP MM
l4_steps.input: Current stock levels, reorder points, safety stock parameters, open POs
l4_steps.output: MRP exception report highlighting below-safety-stock and slow-moving items
l4_steps.kpi: Stockout rate ≤1.5% of demand events; safety stock coverage ≥14 days for AOG-critical parts
l4_steps.pain_point: Safety stock parameters are manually maintained and rarely updated when fleet mix changes (e.g. introduction of new variant), leading to chronic under-stocking of variant-specific parts

l4_steps.name: Review reorder triggers and approve requisition list
l4_steps.input: MRP exception report, open purchase requisitions
l4_steps.output: Approved purchase requisition batch or rejection with revised parameters
l4_steps.kpi: Requisition approval cycle time ≤4 hours for AOG-critical parts; ≤48 hours standard
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual approval queues during shift changes cause delayed AOG responses; no automated escalation when AOG-flagged requisitions remain unactioned beyond 1 hour

l4_steps.name: Create material requisition and attach technical specs
l4_steps.input: Approved purchase requisition, part number, ATA chapter, airworthiness standard (FAR/CS-25)
l4_steps.output: Sourcing-ready requisition with part description, quantity, required-by date, and certification requirements
l4_steps.kpi: Requisition completeness rate ≥98% (no return-for-correction by procurement)
l4_steps.pain_point: Part number supersession data from Boeing Toolbox is not auto-synced to SAP Ariba, causing requisitions for obsolete P/Ns that vendors cannot supply

l4_steps.name: Verify part source against Approved Vendor List
l4_steps.input: Material requisition, part number, ATA chapter
l4_steps.output: Shortlist of AVL-qualified vendors for the specific part
l4_steps.kpi: AVL coverage ≥95% of recurring part numbers; AVL review cycle ≤12 months per vendor
l4_steps.pain_point: AVL is maintained in SAP Ariba but not automatically cross-checked against FAA ASAP (Aviation Supplier Accreditation Program) suspension lists, creating compliance exposure

l4_steps.name: Validate airworthiness certification for each vendor
l4_steps.input: Vendor list, part number, applicable airworthiness directive (AD) status
l4_steps.output: Certification status decision — FAA Form 8130-3 or EASA Form 1 confirmed valid or rejected
l4_steps.kpi: Certificate validation cycle ≤2 hours; zero parts accepted without valid airworthiness release document
l4_steps.pain_point: Counterfeit parts risk is elevated for high-demand Boeing 737 consumables; manual certificate checks against FAA ACSEP database are time-intensive and inconsistently applied across stations

l4_steps.name: Issue RFQ to certified vendors via SAP Ariba
l4_steps.input: Certified vendor shortlist, technical specifications, required-by date, quantity
l4_steps.output: RFQ event published to vendors with response deadline
l4_steps.kpi: RFQ response rate ≥80% from invited vendors; RFQ-to-quote cycle ≤24 hours for standard parts, ≤4 hours for AOG
l4_steps.pain_point: AOG events require verbal quotes followed by retroactive PO creation, bypassing SAP Ariba controls and creating audit gaps under FAR Part 145 supplier documentation requirements

l4_steps.name: Evaluate vendor bids on price, lead time, and certs
l4_steps.input: Vendor quote responses including price, lead time, certification documents, warranty terms
l4_steps.output: Bid evaluation scorecard; recommended vendor selection
l4_steps.kpi: Negotiated savings vs. list price ≥8% on non-contracted parts; lead time commitment variance ≤10%
l4_steps.pain_point: Lowest-price selection without lead time weighting frequently results in late deliveries that trigger AOG events; no automated score weighting enforced in SAP Ariba evaluation templates

l4_steps.name: Create purchase order with full part traceability data
l4_steps.input: Approved vendor selection, quote reference, requisition number, delivery address
l4_steps.output: Draft PO with line items, unit price, delivery terms (INCOTERMS), and cert requirements
l4_steps.kpi: PO first-time-right rate ≥97% (no revision required post-vendor acknowledgement)
l4_steps.pain_point: INCOTERMS and hazardous material shipping codes (IATA DGR compliance for rotable parts containing hydraulic fluid) are manually entered, leading to customs clearance delays at international stations

l4_steps.name: Route PO through financial approval workflow
l4_steps.input: Draft PO, cost centre, budget availability check result
l4_steps.output: Approved or rejected PO with approval audit trail
l4_steps.kpi: PO approval cycle ≤1 business day for values ≤$50K; ≤4 hours for AOG regardless of value
l4_steps.pain_point: Approval delegation matrices in SAP FI/CO are not updated when managers are on leave, causing approval bottlenecks that delay AOG resolutions beyond IATA AHM 730 target resolution windows

l4_steps.name: Transmit approved PO and confirm vendor acknowledgement
l4_steps.input: Approved PO, vendor contact details
l4_steps.output: Vendor-acknowledged PO with confirmed delivery date and tracking reference
l4_steps.kpi: Vendor acknowledgement receipt ≤4 hours of PO transmission; acknowledgement rate ≥99%
l4_steps.pain_point: Some MRO and rotables vendors still require fax or email PO transmission; SAP Ariba supplier portal adoption is ~70%, leaving 30% of POs outside automated acknowledgement tracking

l4_steps.name: Receive parts shipment and verify packing list
l4_steps.input: Inbound shipment, vendor packing list, PO reference
l4_steps.output: Goods receipt draft with quantity discrepancy flag if applicable
l4_steps.kpi: Receiving dock processing time ≤2 hours per shipment; quantity accuracy ≥99.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: AOG parts shipped via freight forwarder sometimes arrive without correct customs clearance documentation at non-hub stations, causing hold delays that negate the benefit of expedited shipping

l4_steps.name: Validate airworthiness release documents on receipt
l4_steps.input: Physical parts, FAA 8130-3 or EASA Form 1, manufacturer C of C, batch/lot traceability records
l4_steps.output: Documentation validation decision — accept, quarantine, or return to vendor
l4_steps.kpi: Documentation rejection rate ≤0.5% of line items received; zero parts accepted with missing trace-back documentation
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS certificate module does not validate 8130-3 document numbers against FAA online registry in real time; manual spot-checks miss approximately 3% of certificate anomalies per internal audit

l4_steps.name: Perform incoming quality inspection per IPC criteria
l4_steps.input: Physical parts, Illustrated Parts Catalog (IPC) criteria, AMM serviceable limits
l4_steps.output: Inspection finding report; parts tagged Serviceable, Unserviceable, or Suspect Unapproved
l4_steps.kpi: Incoming inspection pass rate ≥99.2%; suspect unapproved parts reported to FAA per AC 21-29D within 24 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Tooling calibration records required for dimensional inspection are tracked in a separate CMMS that is not integrated with AMOS, creating manual cross-reference steps that slow AOG part acceptance

l4_steps.name: Accept serviceable parts to bonded stores or quarantine
l4_steps.input: Inspection finding report, serviceable tag, bin location assignment
l4_steps.output: Parts stocked in correct bin with full traceability record in AMOS; quarantine log updated for rejects
l4_steps.kpi: Bin accuracy rate ≥99.8%; quarantine disposition completed within 5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Bin location data in AMOS does not sync with warehouse management in SAP MM in real time, requiring nightly batch jobs that cause daytime inventory location discrepancies at high-volume line stations

l4_steps.name: Post goods receipt and update inventory in SAP MM
l4_steps.input: Accepted parts list, quantity, bin location, PO reference
l4_steps.output: GR document posted; inventory updated; open PO quantity reduced
l4_steps.kpi: GR posting lag ≤4 hours from physical acceptance; GR accuracy rate ≥99.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Back-dated GR postings to correct receiving errors distort accrual reporting in SAP FI/CO and trigger SOX compliance flags during month-end close

l4_steps.name: Execute 3-way invoice match and approve payment
l4_steps.input: Vendor invoice, PO, goods receipt document
l4_steps.output: Matched and approved invoice posted for payment; discrepancy log raised if match fails
l4_steps.kpi: 3-way match auto-approval rate ≥85%; invoice-to-payment cycle ≤30 days net; dispute resolution ≤10 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Vendor invoices often include freight and handling surcharges not captured on the original PO, causing systematic 3-way match failures for ~12% of parts invoices and manual intervention by AP

l4_steps.name: Update vendor performance scorecard and close PO
l4_steps.input: Delivery performance data, quality inspection results, invoice accuracy record, lead time variance
l4_steps.output: Vendor scorecard updated; PO closed in SAP Ariba; AVL status flagged for review if score < threshold
l4_steps.kpi: Vendor scorecard completion rate ≥95% per quarter; suppliers scoring <70/100 reviewed for AVL status within 30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Scorecard data is manually compiled from AMOS, SAP MM, and SAP FI/CO with no automated feed; quarterly compilation takes 3–5 days and is often deprioritised during AOG-heavy periods, reducing scorecard coverage below 60%

l4_steps.name: Capture safety occurrence report
l4_steps.input: Observed hazard, incident, near-miss, or unsafe condition
l4_steps.output: Safety occurrence record with initial classification and timestamp
l4_steps.kpi: Report submission rate ≥95% of known occurrences within 24 hrs
l4_steps.pain_point: Anonymous voluntary reporting culture varies by crew base; under-reporting persists in stations without dedicated Safety Officers

l4_steps.name: Classify report type & severity tier
l4_steps.input: Raw occurrence record from Step 1.1
l4_steps.output: Classified report: incident / hazard / near-miss / accident with initial severity tier (1–5)
l4_steps.kpi: Classification accuracy ≥98% validated at quarterly QA review
l4_steps.pain_point: Inconsistent severity tier assignment across regions; IQSMS taxonomy not always aligned with ICAO Annex 13 definitions

l4_steps.name: Determine mandatory regulatory reporting threshold
l4_steps.input: Classified occurrence record, FAR Part 830 / ICAO Annex 13 criteria matrix
l4_steps.output: Reporting decision: mandatory FAA/NTSB notification required (Y/N)
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of mandatory reports filed within regulatory deadlines (2 hrs / 10 days per FAR 830)
l4_steps.pain_point: Threshold ambiguity for ground damage events under FAR 830.5; legal and safety teams misalign on what constitutes 'substantial damage'

l4_steps.name: Submit voluntary report to ASAP/NASA ASRS
l4_steps.input: Non-mandatory occurrence classified in Step 1.2
l4_steps.output: ASRS report number; ASAP event record filed with ASAP ERC (Event Review Committee)
l4_steps.kpi: ASAP programme participation rate ≥80% of eligible workforce
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA AC 120-66B ASAP MOU must be current; if MOU lapses, regulatory protection for reporters is void — high legal exposure

l4_steps.name: Initiate mandatory FAA/NTSB notification
l4_steps.input: Mandatory reporting decision from Step 1.3; occurrence facts
l4_steps.output: FAA/NTSB preliminary notification; ASIAS occurrence record; internal hold placed on aircraft/evidence
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of NTSB immediate notifications within 2 hrs of accident (FAR 830.5)
l4_steps.pain_point: Coordination latency between Operations Control and Safety when event occurs overnight; on-call Director of Safety pager escalation path not always followed

l4_steps.name: Assign risk probability & severity matrix score
l4_steps.input: Classified occurrence record; ICAO SMS risk matrix template
l4_steps.output: Risk index score (probability 1–5 × severity 1–5); initial risk colour: green/amber/red
l4_steps.kpi: Risk assessments completed within 48 hrs of report receipt for Tier 1–2 events
l4_steps.pain_point: Risk matrix calibration is subjective; two analysts rating same event can produce divergent scores without standardised anchor examples in IQSMS

l4_steps.name: Validate risk score at Safety Review Board
l4_steps.input: Risk index score from Step 2.1; FOQA data (if flight event)
l4_steps.output: Validated risk rating; escalation decision for red-rated risks
l4_steps.kpi: Safety Review Board convenes within 5 business days for red-rated risks
l4_steps.pain_point: Board quorum requires VP-level attendees; scheduling conflicts delay review for high-severity events; FOQA data retrieval from Teledyne SSFDR takes 48–72 hrs

l4_steps.name: Accept low risk & assign monitoring SPI
l4_steps.input: Green-rated risk from Step 2.2
l4_steps.output: Safety Performance Indicator (SPI) assigned; monitoring threshold set in Tableau
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of accepted risks assigned at least one SPI within 5 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Tableau Safety BI dashboard is manually updated monthly; real-time SPI trending not available — latent risks may not surface until next board review

l4_steps.name: Initiate formal safety investigation
l4_steps.input: Escalated red/amber risk from Step 2.2; preliminary event facts
l4_steps.output: Investigation plan: scope, team, evidence list, timeline; IQSMS investigation record opened
l4_steps.kpi: Investigation plan issued within 24 hrs of escalation for Tier 1 events
l4_steps.pain_point: Investigator availability limited at outstations; company investigators are also line employees — release from duty requires crew scheduling coordination with Jeppesen Crew Management

l4_steps.name: Gather evidence including FOQA flight data
l4_steps.input: Flight identifier, tail number, date/time; investigation plan from Step 3.1
l4_steps.output: QAR/FOQA data extract; CVR/FDR preservation request (if applicable); witness statements in IQSMS
l4_steps.kpi: FOQA data retrieved within 72 hrs for flight-related events
l4_steps.pain_point: CVR/FDR data automatically overwritten after 30 days — late reporting of incidents frequently results in lost recorder data; preservation requests must be issued same day

l4_steps.name: Perform root cause analysis using bowtie/5-Whys
l4_steps.input: Evidence package from Step 3.2; FOQA data; witness statements
l4_steps.output: Root cause statement; contributing factors list; bowtie barriers analysis in IQSMS
l4_steps.kpi: Root cause identified for ≥90% of Tier 1 investigations within 30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Bowtie analysis tool within IQSMS lacks integration with operational data — investigators manually cross-reference FOQA exports, increasing analysis time by 30–40%

l4_steps.name: Document investigation findings & close investigation
l4_steps.input: Root cause and contributing factors from Step 3.3
l4_steps.output: Final investigation report; linked corrective action records; report published in IQSMS
l4_steps.kpi: Investigation report issued within 60 days for Tier 1; 30 days for Tier 2
l4_steps.pain_point: Regulatory review of investigation reports by FAA/NTSB (if MOU-governed) can impose revisions — internal report may need to be amended post-publication, creating version control issues

l4_steps.name: Develop safety risk controls & mitigations
l4_steps.input: Investigation report from Step 3.4; risk residual score
l4_steps.output: Risk control plan: engineering controls, procedural changes, training interventions; residual risk target score
l4_steps.kpi: Risk residual score reduced to green (≤4) for ≥95% of Tier 1 events post-mitigation
l4_steps.pain_point: Procedural changes require FOM/GOM amendment workflow through Standards & Compliance — average revision cycle is 45–60 days, leaving residual risk unmitigated in the interim

l4_steps.name: Assign corrective action owners & due dates
l4_steps.input: Risk control plan from Step 4.1
l4_steps.output: Corrective action tasks assigned in IQSMS with responsible owner, priority, and target close date
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of corrective actions have named owner and due date within 5 days of investigation closure
l4_steps.pain_point: Cross-departmental corrective actions (e.g. Maintenance + Ops) lack shared accountability — IQSMS task ownership model does not enforce escalation when due dates slip

l4_steps.name: Verify corrective action effectiveness
l4_steps.input: Closed corrective action records; post-implementation SPI data from Tableau
l4_steps.output: Effectiveness verification record; risk formally closed or re-opened if recurrence detected
l4_steps.kpi: Corrective action on-time closure rate ≥85%; recurrence rate for closed risks <5% within 12 months
l4_steps.pain_point: Effectiveness verification relies on SPI trend analysis over 6–12 months — impatient leadership pressure to close risks prematurely inflates 'green' status without sufficient data

l4_steps.name: Track safety performance indicators vs targets
l4_steps.input: SPI data feeds from IQSMS, FOQA, ASAP, ASRS aggregation
l4_steps.output: Monthly SPI scorecard: accident rate, serious incident rate, FOQA exceedance rate, ASAP report volume
l4_steps.kpi: Accident rate: 0 per year; Serious incident rate ≤0.3 per 100,000 flights; FOQA exceedance rate ≤1.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: FOQA data pipeline from Teledyne SSFDR to Tableau requires manual CSV export — automated API integration not yet implemented, causing 5–10 day data lag

l4_steps.name: Publish monthly safety performance report to executives
l4_steps.input: SPI scorecard from Step 5.1; corrective action status from IQSMS
l4_steps.output: Executive safety performance report distributed via SharePoint; board safety committee briefing deck
l4_steps.kpi: Monthly report published by 10th of following month; 100% board safety committee attendance
l4_steps.pain_point: Board-level safety committee may lack aviation SMS expertise — safety reporting must translate technical SPI data into business risk language; skills gap in governance layer

l4_steps.name: Conduct scheduled SMS internal audit
l4_steps.input: FAA AC 120-92B SMS framework; annual audit schedule; previous audit findings
l4_steps.output: Audit findings report; non-conformances raised in IQSMS; corrective action requests issued
l4_steps.kpi: Annual SMS audit completion rate 100%; critical non-conformances closed within 30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA AC 120-92B SMS requirements for Part 121 carriers are currently voluntary — without mandate, audit rigour is inconsistent and funding for SMS programme competes with operational priorities

l4_steps.name: Submit mandatory occurrence reports to FAA ASIAS
l4_steps.input: Mandatory occurrence records from Steps 1.3 and 1.5; Service Difficulty Reports (SDRs) from Maintenance
l4_steps.output: ASIAS submission receipts; SDR filings; MOR (Malfunction or Defect Report) records archived
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of SDRs filed within 3 days of discovery (FAR 121.703); zero overdue mandatory reports
l4_steps.pain_point: SDR filing workflow spans Maintenance and Safety departments — coordination gaps between AMOS MRO system and IQSMS mean some defects are resolved without triggering the SDR filing check

l4_steps.name: Subscribe to FAA rulemaking & ICAO SARPs updates
l4_steps.input: FAA NPRM publications, ICAO amendment cycles, DOT safety directives
l4_steps.output: Regulatory watch list with effective dates and applicability flags
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of applicable NPRMs captured within 5 business days of publication
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA issues 300+ NPRMs per year; manual triage against 14 CFR Part 119/121 scope causes missed applicability deadlines without automated rule-matching

l4_steps.name: Classify regulatory change by AOC impact category
l4_steps.input: Regulatory watch list, current Operations Specifications (OpSpecs) baseline
l4_steps.output: Impact classification: Critical / Significant / Administrative; assigned owner and deadline
l4_steps.kpi: Classification completed within 3 business days of receipt; ≥95% accuracy validated by VP Safety review
l4_steps.pain_point: 14 CFR Part 121 overlaps with Part 91, Part 135, and ICAO Annex 6 — misclassification risk is high for carriers operating international routes under bilateral agreements

l4_steps.name: Determine material impact on AOC or OpSpecs conditions
l4_steps.input: Impact classification, current OpSpecs (OpSpec A, B, C, D series)
l4_steps.output: Go/no-go decision: initiate gap assessment or log as no-action required
l4_steps.kpi: Decision documented within 2 business days; 0 unreviewed critical items older than 5 days
l4_steps.pain_point: OpSpecs are issued at aircraft-type level — a single Boeing 737 MAX amendment may trigger parallel OpSpec revisions across A002, B036, and D085 series, each requiring separate FAA FSDO concurrence

l4_steps.name: Conduct OpSpecs gap analysis against new regulation
l4_steps.input: Applicable regulatory change, current approved OpSpecs, Operations Manual
l4_steps.output: Gap analysis report with non-compliant clauses, affected flight types, and remediation scope
l4_steps.kpi: Gap analysis completed ≥30 days before regulation effective date for non-emergency rules
l4_steps.pain_point: WebOPSS does not provide automated diff between existing OpSpecs and new regulatory text — analysts must perform manual line-by-line comparison across 100+ OpSpec paragraphs, consuming 40+ analyst-hours per major rule change

l4_steps.name: Review fleet type ratings and pilot training compliance
l4_steps.input: Gap analysis report, approved Training Specifications (TRSpecs), FAR Part 121 Subpart N/O
l4_steps.output: Training compliance matrix: current vs. required qualification levels by aircraft type and route
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of pilots current on type rating within 24-month recurrent cycle; 0 flights dispatched with lapsed qualification
l4_steps.pain_point: Introduction of new flight deck technology (e.g., Boeing 737 MAX MCAS differences training) requires FSDO-approved training programme amendments before revenue flying — timeline mismatch with aircraft delivery schedules creates capacity risk

l4_steps.name: Identify non-compliance gaps and remediation requirements
l4_steps.input: Gap analysis report, training compliance matrix, airworthiness directives (ADs) list
l4_steps.output: Non-compliance register with risk severity rating (Critical / High / Medium / Low)
l4_steps.kpi: Zero Critical-rated gaps open beyond 30 days; High-rated gaps resolved within 90 days
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA Airworthiness Directives issued via AD registry may conflict with manufacturer service bulletin schedules — carriers must negotiate alternate means of compliance (AMOC) approval which averages 6–18 months with FAA Aircraft Certification Office

l4_steps.name: Develop and approve corrective action plan (CAP)
l4_steps.input: Non-compliance register, resource constraints, budget from SAP S/4HANA Finance
l4_steps.output: Board-approved CAP with milestones, accountable owners, and target closure dates
l4_steps.kpi: CAP approved by VP Safety within 10 business days of gap identification; milestone adherence ≥90%
l4_steps.pain_point: CAP funding competes with capital allocation cycles — safety-driven OpEx spend cannot be deferred but lacks the revenue justification framework used for commercial projects, creating budget approval delays

l4_steps.name: Prepare AOC amendment or OpSpecs revision package
l4_steps.input: Approved CAP, draft revised OpSpecs, supporting technical documentation
l4_steps.output: Complete FAA amendment package: Form 8900-1, revised OpSpec paragraphs, supporting data
l4_steps.kpi: Package completeness score ≥95% on first submission (measured by FAA deficiency rate); zero incomplete submissions
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA Form 8900-1 and WebOPSS data entry does not validate cross-references between OpSpec series — errors discovered during FSDO review require full resubmission and add 4–8 weeks to approval timeline

l4_steps.name: Submit amendment package to FAA FSDO via WebOPSS
l4_steps.input: Completed amendment package, principal operations inspector (POI) contact
l4_steps.output: FAA submission confirmation number; amendment tracking record opened in ARMS
l4_steps.kpi: Submission made ≥60 days before effective date for Major amendments; ≥30 days for Minor
l4_steps.pain_point: WebOPSS portal has documented uptime issues during peak submission periods (e.g., end-of-year deadline rush); carriers with sole-source FSDO assignment have no alternative submission channel if POI is on extended leave

l4_steps.name: Respond to FAA requests for additional information
l4_steps.input: FAA deficiency notice or Request for Additional Information (RAI)
l4_steps.output: Supplemental data package; revised submission if OpSpec text changes required
l4_steps.kpi: RAI response submitted within 10 business days of receipt; first-response resolution rate ≥75%
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA POI reviewer rotation means institutional knowledge of airline-specific OpSpecs is lost — new POI may re-open previously resolved items, causing amendment cycles to restart and exceeding planned compliance timelines

l4_steps.name: Receive, validate, and file approved OpSpecs revision
l4_steps.input: FAA-approved OpSpecs revision notification
l4_steps.output: Updated OpSpecs filed in controlled document repository; affected departments notified
l4_steps.kpi: Distribution to operational departments within 24 hours of FAA approval; acknowledgement receipt rate 100% within 48 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: OpSpecs revisions must be cascaded to Dispatch, Crew Training, Maintenance, and Ground Ops simultaneously — document management systems (SharePoint) lack mandatory-read workflow enforcement, creating compliance traceability gaps

l4_steps.name: Conduct periodic SMS internal compliance audit
l4_steps.input: Annual audit schedule, ICAO Doc 9859 SMS framework, 14 CFR §119.65 requirements
l4_steps.output: Internal audit report with findings, risk ratings, and corrective action recommendations
l4_steps.kpi: 4 SMS audits completed per year; critical findings closed within 30 days; audit coverage ≥100% of SMS components annually
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA requires SMS programmes to demonstrate safety performance improvement over time (AC 120-92B) — carriers using spreadsheet-based audit tracking cannot produce trend evidence required for IOSA (IATA Operational Safety Audit) recertification

l4_steps.name: Analyse FOQA safety performance indicators against thresholds
l4_steps.input: Flight recorder data feeds, airline-defined safety performance indicator (SPI) thresholds
l4_steps.output: SPI dashboard report: exceedance counts, trend analysis, risk-ranked event list
l4_steps.kpi: FOQA data capture rate ≥99.5% of revenue flights; SPI exceedance rate <0.5 per 1,000 flights for high-severity events
l4_steps.pain_point: FOQA data volumes from 800+ daily flights generate 2TB+ per month — without automated anomaly detection (e.g., Palantir Aviation Safety), manual analyst review creates a 4–6 week lag between exceedance event and corrective action initiation

l4_steps.name: File ASAP or VDRP voluntary safety disclosure report
l4_steps.role: Pilot / Dispatcher / Aviation Safety Action Program (ASAP) Manager
l4_steps.system: FAA Aviation Safety Action Program (ASAP) Portal
l4_steps.input: SPI threshold breach, pilot self-disclosure, or near-miss event report
l4_steps.output: ASAP Event Review Committee (ERC) report; corrective action recommendation to FAA
l4_steps.kpi: ASAP report submission within 24 hours of event identification; ERC review completed within 30 days; 0 reports rejected for lateness
l4_steps.pain_point: ASAP programme confidentiality protections (14 CFR §13.401) conflict with labour contract grievance procedures — ambiguity over which events qualify for ASAP immunity vs. disciplinary action suppresses voluntary disclosure rates, undermining SMS effectiveness

l4_steps.name: Update MEL, Operations Manual, and training materials
l4_steps.input: Approved OpSpecs revision, AD compliance status, ASAP corrective actions
l4_steps.output: Revised MEL amendments, updated Operations Manual sections, EFB content pushed to fleet tablets
l4_steps.kpi: MEL and Ops Manual updates published within 5 business days of OpSpecs approval; EFB content sync to 100% of fleet devices within 24 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: MEL amendment cycle requires simultaneous approval from airline, Boeing (MMEL source), and FAA — three-party review adds 60–120 days per amendment, creating temporary deferred maintenance item backlogs that inflate maintenance cost and aircraft availability risk

l4_steps.name: Track and report compliance costs against regulatory budget
l4_steps.input: CAP milestones, training programme costs, audit fees, legal advisory costs
l4_steps.output: Regulatory compliance cost report by OpSpec category; variance analysis vs. annual budget
l4_steps.kpi: Regulatory compliance budget variance ≤5% quarterly; cost-per-amendment tracked and benchmarked annually
l4_steps.pain_point: Regulatory compliance costs are scattered across Safety, Legal, Crew Training, and Maintenance cost centres in SAP — absence of a dedicated regulatory compliance WBS element prevents accurate total-cost-of-compliance reporting required by board audit committees

l4_steps.name: Archive compliance records and close regulatory cycle
l4_steps.input: Approved OpSpecs, audit reports, ASAP ERC decisions, CAP closure evidence
l4_steps.output: Compliance cycle closure report; archived records indexed for 7-year retention per 14 CFR §121.380
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of compliance records archived within 5 business days of cycle close; retrieval time for auditor requests ≤1 business day
l4_steps.pain_point: 14 CFR §121.380 mandates 7-year retention for most compliance records, but GDPR and state privacy laws impose conflicting deletion requirements for records containing crew personal data — dual-obligation conflict requires manual legal review for each retention decision

l4_steps.name: Review Flight Schedule
l4_steps.input: New flight schedule or changes in existing schedule
l4_steps.output: Updated flight schedule details
l4_steps.kpi: On-time performance (OTP) rate > 85%
l4_steps.pain_point: Inaccurate flight schedules leading to fuel mismanagement

l4_steps.name: Analyze Weather Conditions
l4_steps.input: Flight route and date
l4_steps.output: Weather forecast report
l4_steps.kpi: Weather-related delays < 5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Unexpected weather conditions affecting fuel consumption

l4_steps.name: Determine Base Fuel Requirement
l4_steps.input: Flight details, aircraft type, and destination
l4_steps.output: Base fuel requirement report
l4_steps.kpi: Fuel efficiency index > 1.2
l4_steps.pain_point: Over/under-fueling leading to increased costs

l4_steps.name: Calculate Uplift Factor
l4_steps.input: Base fuel requirement, weather forecast, and historical data
l4_steps.output: Uplift factor report
l4_steps.kpi: Uplift accuracy within ±5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Incorrect uplift calculation resulting in safety or cost issues

l4_steps.name: Optimize Fuel Policy
l4_steps.input: Uplift factor, fuel prices, and operational costs
l4_steps.output: Optimized fuel policy report
l4_steps.kpi: Fuel cost savings > 2%
l4_steps.pain_point: Inefficient fuel policies leading to higher operational expenses

l4_steps.name: Allocate Fuel for Each Flight
l4_steps.input: Optimized fuel policy and flight details
l4_steps.output: Flight-specific fuel allocation report
l4_steps.kpi: Fuel allocation accuracy > 95%
l4_steps.pain_point: Incorrect fuel allocation causing delays or safety risks

l4_steps.name: Monitor Fuel Usage During Flight
l4_steps.input: Live flight data and pre-planned route
l4_steps.output: Fuel usage monitoring report
l4_steps.kpi: Real-time fuel consumption tracking accuracy > 90%
l4_steps.pain_point: Lack of real-time monitoring leading to unexpected fuel shortages

l4_steps.name: Adjust Fuel Uplift Based on Real-Time Data
l4_steps.input: Real-time fuel usage data and pre-planned uplift
l4_steps.output: Adjusted uplift factor report
l4_steps.kpi: Uplift adjustment accuracy > 80%
l4_steps.pain_point: Inability to adjust uplift in real-time affecting safety or costs

l4_steps.name: Review Post-Flight Fuel Report
l4_steps.input: Post-flight fuel data and flight details
l4_steps.output: Post-flight analysis report
l4_steps.kpi: Post-flight fuel accuracy > 98%
l4_steps.pain_point: Inaccurate post-flight reports leading to incorrect future planning

l4_steps.name: Update Historical Data with New Information
l4_steps.input: Post-flight analysis report and historical data
l4_steps.output: Updated historical fuel database
l4_steps.kpi: Historical data accuracy > 95%
l4_steps.pain_point: Outdated historical data affecting future planning

l4_steps.name: Review and Approve Final Fuel Policy
l4_steps.input: Optimized fuel policy report, uplift factor report, and post-flight analysis report
l4_steps.output: Approved fuel policy document
l4_steps.kpi: Policy approval time < 2 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Delayed policy approvals impacting operational efficiency

l4_steps.name: Communicate Final Fuel Policy to Crews
l4_steps.input: Approved fuel policy document and flight details
l4_steps.output: Crew communication report
l4_steps.kpi: Crew communication accuracy > 98%
l4_steps.pain_point: Poor crew communication leading to operational errors

l4_steps.name: Monitor Compliance with Fuel Policy
l4_steps.input: Fuel usage data and approved fuel policy
l4_steps.output: Compliance report
l4_steps.kpi: Compliance rate > 98%
l4_steps.pain_point: Non-compliance with fuel policies leading to safety risks or fines

l4_steps.name: Update Fuel Policy Documentation
l4_steps.input: Approved fuel policy document and historical data
l4_steps.output: Updated fuel policy documentation
l4_steps.kpi: Documentation update accuracy > 95%
l4_steps.pain_point: Outdated documentation affecting future planning
